🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (5.6.9 → 8.0.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion

Impact

PROXY protocol support for Puma was added in version 5.5.0.

When PROXY protocol v1 support is enabled, Puma reads incoming bytes into an internal buffer. It waits for "\r\n" to determine whether a PROXY v1 line is present. If an attacker opens a TCP connection and continuously sends bytes without CRLF, Puma keeps appending to this pre-parse buffer.

This can cause unbounded in-process memory growth and additional CPU cost from repeatedly scanning the growing buffer for CRLF. A single, unauthenticated TCP connection can drive significant memory growth and may cause process/container OOM or degraded availability.

Only Puma servers using the following non-default config are affected:

   set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

author: ecommeanblvd
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the Order Operations / Fulfillment module (`/f/fulfillment`). When a Shopify order syncs, it creates a **line-level** ops record, checks MEAN warehouse stock by SKU, shows **shelf/floor** for in-stock lines and flags out-of-stock lines as "cần đặt brand", then runs the in-stock path **pick → pack → ship** (decrementing stock). Includes a manual warehouse-inventory management page.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-order-ops-fulfillment-phase1-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-08-order-ops-fulfillment-phase1.md`

### What's included
- **Schema** (4 tables): `warehouse_inventory`, `order_fulfillment`, `order_fulfillment_lines`, `order_fulfillment_events` + 2 enums (migrations 0038–0040).
- **Pure logic** (`features/fulfillment/logic.ts`, 17 unit tests): `checkStock`, `rollupOrderStatus`, `canTransitionLine`.
- **Server actions** (transaction-safe): `checkStockForOrder` (reserve + `FOR UPDATE` lock), `markLine`/`markOrder` (atomic pick/pack/ship with stock decrement), warehouse upsert/adjust, RBAC-gated backfill.
- **Re-sync safety**: fulfillment lines keyed by the **stable `shopifyLineId`** (not the volatile internal order-line id, which is delete+reinserted each sync) → progress survives order updates.
- **UI**: worklist, per-order detail (per-line location + pick/pack/ship), warehouse management. Nav item gated by `view_fulfillment`.
- **RBAC**: `view_fulfillment` / `manage_fulfillment` / `manage_warehouse`.

### Review-driven fixes (final code review)
- `recomputeRollup` moved **inside** the transaction (no torn order status under concurrency).
- `markOrder` made a **single atomic transaction**.
- `FOR UPDATE` lock on inventory rows (no double-reserve across concurrent checks).
- Release path keyed by `warehouseInventoryId`.
- **CHECK constraints** `qty_on_hand >= 0`, `qty_reserved >= 0`.

### Known follow-ups (not blocking Phase 1)
- ⚠️ **Tooling debt**: `drizzle-kit generate` currently fails ("0039_snapshot.json malformed") because migration 0039 was hand-authored. DB + `drizzle-kit migrate` are correct, but the snapshot chain under `db/migrations/meta/` needs repair before the next generate. *Recommend fixing before Phase 2.*
- Stock check is **on-demand** (the "Check lại tồn" button), not auto-run on order create — sensible since auto-checking 5,100 orders against an empty warehouse would just mark all out-of-stock.
- Stale fulfillment lines (a line removed from an order on re-sync) are not pruned and their reservation isn't released — acceptable for Phase 1, worth a follow-up.

### Deferred to later phases
Phase 2 (route orders to brand via MMP), Phase 3 (production-time metafields + ship-by + CX email), Phase 4 (delivered tracking + 30-day return window + auto-complete).

## Test Plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx vitest run features/fulfillment lib/nav.test.ts` — 23 pass
- [x] Backfill created 5,100 ops records; worklist + detail queries verified against staging
- [ ] Manual: add a warehouse SKU matching a real order line, open the order, confirm in-stock shows kệ/tầng + out-of-stock shows "Cần đặt brand", mark a line picked → on-hand decrements, rollup updates

## Summary

- `crawl()` and `find_link()` gain five new verifier parameters: `verify_destination`, `verify_threshold`, `fetch_result_content`, `max_result_bytes`, `result_to_file`
- Four new streaming events emitted per crawl: `GoalPreprocessed`, `LinksRanked`, `CandidatesExtracted`, `DestinationVerificationFailed`
- `DefaultDestinationVerifier` called for every model-confirmed candidate; rejected candidates emit `DestinationVerificationFailed` and do not appear in `result_urls`
- `CrawlResult` gains `verified_candidates`, `result_contents`, `failure_mode`, `goal_context`; `CrawlComplete` gains `failure_mode` and `goal_context`
- `FailureMode.ALL_CANDIDATES_REJECTED` set when verifier rejects all model-confirmed candidates
- `engine_support.py` extended with `_check_result()` (provenance + answer-gate), `_make_links_ranked`, `_run_extractor`, `_verify_candidate`, `_content_metadata`, `_build_crawl_result`; `engine.py` stays under the 600-line cap (583 lines)
- All existing tests updated: navigation tests pass `verify_destination="off"` to isolate from the verifier; T-27 event-sequence test updated to assert `GoalPreprocessed`, `LinksRanked`, `CandidatesExtracted`

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → 782 passed, 0 failed
- [ ] `wc -l charlotte/core/engine.py` → ≤ 600
- [ ] Review `GoalPreprocessed` is the second event after `CrawlStarted`

body:
Upgrade lodash and form-data to fix code injection via template imports and HTTP parameter pollution vulnerabilities.
✅ Code not affected by breaking changes.
✅ No breaking changes affect this codebase. The codebase only uses `lodash.get()` method (in `src/App.js`), which is not affected by any of the breaking changes. The breaking changes in lodash 4.18.0 affect `_.unset`, `_.omit`, and `_.template` methods, none of which are used in this codebase. The `form-data` package is listed as a dependency in `yarn.lock` (as a transitive dependency), but the `setBoundary()` method is not called anywhere in the codebase. All breaking changes by upgrading lodash from version 4.17.21 to 4.18.1 ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/releases/tag/4.18.0)) | Version | Description | | --- | --- | | 
4.18.0
| `_.unset` / `_.omit` now block `constructor` and `prototype` as non-terminal path keys unconditionally. Calls that previously returned `true` and deleted the property now return `false` and leave the target untouched. | | 
4.18.0
| `_.template` now throws `"Invalid imports option passed into _.template"` when `imports` keys contain forbidden identifier characters, which were previously allowed. | All breaking changes by upgrading form-data from version 3.0.1 to 3.0.4 ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/form-data/form-data/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)) | Version | Description | | --- | --- | | 
3.0.4
| `setBoundary()` method now validates boundary type, which may reject previously accepted non-string boundary values |
✅ 2 CVEs resolved by this upgrade
This PR will resolve the following CVEs: | Issue | Severity           | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | 
[CVE-2026-4800](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/8436246/detail?groupId=21538#CVE-2026-4800)
| 
HIGH
| [lodash] A vulnerability in _.template allows arbitrary code execution through untrusted key names in options.imports or prototype pollution, as validation was incomplete after a prior CVE fix. An attacker can inject malicious code that executes during template compilation. | | 
[CVE-2025-7783](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/13487100/detail?groupId=21538#CVE-2025-7783)
| 
HIGH
| [form-data] Use of Insufficiently Random Values vulnerability in form-data allows HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/form_data.Js.

This issue affects form-data: < 2.5.4, 3.0.0 - 3.0.3, 4.0.0 - 4.0.3. |
🤖 Remediation details Fix security vulnerabilities in lodash and form-data (and transitive dompurify, qs, webpack) ## Short summary This PR remediates CVEs in two directly declared vulnerable packages — **`lodash`** and **`form-data`** — plus three additional vulnerable transitive packages (**`dompurify`**, **`qs`**, **`webpack`**) identified during review. Changes touch the root `package.json` (direct dependency version bump, new `resolutions` block) and `yarn.lock` (lockfile entries refreshed to patched resolved versions). ### lodash `lodash` is declared directly in root `package.json` as `^4.17.21`; the spec was raised to `^4.18.1` so the lockfile resolves to the patched version. A second lockfile instance was held at the exact version `4.17.21` by exact-pin declarations from `@corva/ui` and `@corva/dc-platform-shared` — confirmed across all published versions of both parents, none of which ever widened their lodash pin. A `resolutions` entry (`"lodash": "^4.18.1"`) was added as a last resort to override those exact pins, collapsing all instances to `4.18.1`. ### form-data `form-data` is a transitive dependency pulled in by `jsdom` (spec `^3.0.0`) and `superagent` (spec `^3.0.0`). Both parent ranges already permitted `3.0.4`, so the lockfile entry `form-data@^3.0.0` was stale at `3.0.1`. A targeted `yarn upgrade 'form-data@^3.0.0'` refreshed the lockfile selector to resolve `3.0.4` without any manifest change. The `form-data` entry that `yarn upgrade` temporarily added to `package.json` as a direct dependency was removed, and the lockfile was re-verified as transitive-only. ### dompurify `dompurify` is a transitive dependency pinned at the exact version `3.2.4` by `@corva/ui@3.60.1`. Inspection of all published `@corva/ui` releases up to the latest (`3.63.0-0`) confirmed that every version continues to declare `dompurify` as the exact string `"3.2.4"`, making a parent bump impossible. A `resolutions` entry (`"dompurify": "^3.4.0"`) was added to the root `package.json` as the only viable path, resolving the lockfile to `3.4.8`. ### qs `qs` appeared in three lockfile instances. The instance at `6.15.2` (selectors `^6.14.0`, `^6.14.1`, `~6.15.1`) was already patched. The stale instance at `6.10.3` (selectors `^6.10.1`, `^6.9.4` from `auth0-js` and `superagent`) had parent ranges that already permitted `6.15.2`, so a lockfile refresh was sufficient for that entry. The third instance at `6.13.0` was an exact-pin from `body-parser@1.20.3` and `express@4.21.2`, which cannot be resolved by a parent bump. A `resolutions` entry (`"qs": "^6.15.2"`) was added, which simultaneously refreshed the stale range entry and overrode the exact pin, consolidating all instances to a single resolved version of `6.15.2`. ### webpack `webpack` is a transitive dependency pinned at the exact version `5.94.0` by `@corva/dc-platform-shared@0.62.0` — the only published version of that package, which always declares webpack as `"5.94.0"`. No parent bump path exists. A `resolutions` entry (`"webpack": "^5.104.1"`) was added to the root `package.json`, resolving the lockfile to `5.107.2`. ## Version changes | Package | From | To | Why updated | |---|---|---|---| | `lodash` | `^4.17.21` (declared); `4.17.21` / `4.17.20` (resolved) | `^4.18.1` (declared); `4.18.1` (resolved) | Direct CVE fix; manifest spec raised + `resolutions` override to break exact-pin from `@corva/ui` and `@corva/dc-platform-shared` | | `form-data` | `3.0.1` (lockfile) | `3.0.4` (lockfile) | Transitive CVE fix; lockfile selector `^3.0.0` refreshed via `yarn upgrade` | | `dompurify` | `3.2.4` (lockfile) | `3.4.8` (lockfile) | Transitive CVE fix; `resolutions` override required — `@corva/ui` exact-pins `3.2.4` across all published versions | | `qs` | `6.10.3` + `6.13.0` (lockfile) | `6.15.2` (lockfile, consolidated) | Transitive CVE fix; stale `^6.10.1`/`^6.9.4` entry refreshed + `resolutions` override for exact-pin `6.13.0` from `body-parser`/`express` | | `webpack` | `5.94.0` (lockfile) | `5.107.2` (lockfile) | Transitive CVE fix; `resolutions` override required — `@corva/dc-platform-shared` exact-pins `5.94.0` |

author: fourcolors
body:
## What & why

A fast `systemctl restart` of the chat-server can start the new process before the outgoing one releases its **DuckDB/SQLite WAL/SHM** handles → `SQLiteError: unable to open database file` (`SQLITE_CANTOPEN`) at boot. That was the 2026-06-08 stable-deploy incident; the fix for the deploy path (`scripts/luna-update-server`) landed in #91 as a clean **stop → settle → start**.

Two **other** restart paths still used the racy fast restart and open the same DBs. This PR applies the same fix to both siblings.

## Changes

**`scripts/restart-channel.sh`** (manual operator restart tool)
- Replaced the single `RESTART=(…)` array with per-channel `STOP=(…)` / `START=(…)` arrays, with a host-side settle between them (`LUNA_RESTART_SETTLE_SECS`, default `6`, `0` disables).
- The settle is **host-side** even on the dev (`incus exec`) channel — the DB files are bind-mounted, so elapsed wall-time is what matters and it avoids an extra `incus exec` round-trip.
- `"${STOP[@]}" || true` so a non-zero `stop` never aborts before `start` under `set -e` (`start` is idempotent → strictly more robust than the old atomic `restart`).
- Settle value is **validated**; an invalid/negative value **warns loudly and proceeds** instead of silently skipping the settle (mirrors the `cb43956` hardening of `luna-update-server`).
- Arrays stay non-empty → no `set -u` empty-array gotcha. The unrelated post-start `sleep 2` (start→health gap) is preserved.

**`install.sh`** — agent-cli auto-recovery defaults (only when `--enable-ssh-recovery`)
- `STABLE_START_COMMAND` (keeps its `--user` scope) and `DEV_START_COMMAND` (in-container unit via `incus exec`, host-side settle between the two execs) now default to `stop; sleep 6; start`.
- The bare `;`-sequence survives the `.env` round-trip (`parseDotEnv` strips only whole-value quotes) and runs as-is in both local-shell and ssh recovery. 6s fits comfortably under the 30s recovery `startTimeoutMs` default, so recovery won't SIGKILL mid-sequence.

## Tests
- New `test/restart-channel.test.ts` — 7 hermetic tests (stubs `systemctl`/`incus`/`curl`/`ss`/`journalctl`): `bash -n` smoke, stop-before-start for both channels, settle wiring, invalid-value-warns, and failing-stop-still-starts.
- New lock-in test in `test/deploy-scripts.test.ts` pinning the safe install.sh defaults.
- `bash -n` + `shellcheck` clean. All affected suites green: **86** root tests (restart-channel 7 + update-server 19 + deploy-scripts 60) and **42** agent-cli tests (recovery 7 + chat-config 35).

## Reviewer notes
- **Scope:** `scripts/luna-update-server` and `test/update-server.test.ts` are intentionally untouched — that fix is #91, and there is **zero file overlap** between the two changes.
- **Preserved deliberately:** the two stable paths use **different** systemd scopes — `restart-channel.sh` stable = *system* unit, recovery stable = `--user` unit. These were **not** harmonized.
- **Preventive for new/re-run installs only:** an existing `.env` (including the running box) keeps the old `restart` command until re-installed or hand-edited. Recovery is lower-risk than the deploy path (the old process is usually already gone when recovery fires).
- **Follow-up (not in this PR):** several docs still show the old fast `restart` for *manual* ops (`docs/jax-box-deploy.md`, `docs/luna-terminal-client.md`, `docs/container-runtime.md`); updating those also requires touching the `test/deploy-scripts.test.ts:1615` assertion.

author: baseballyama
body:
## What

Two byte-identical performance wins surfaced by an **adversarial perf review of #934** and confirmed on the same pprof transform profile (18 KB `a11y-role-supports-aria-props` fixture).

### 1. `clean_nodes` no longer clones the sibling slice when there's nothing to reorder
In legacy (non-runes) mode, `clean_nodes` ran `sort_const_tags(nodes.to_vec())` on **every** sibling group — deep-cloning the entire `TemplateNode` slice. But `sort_const_tags` is a no-op whenever there are ≤ 1 `{@const}` tags (the overwhelmingly common case), so that clone was pure waste.

`sort_const_tags` now borrows `&[TemplateNode]` and returns `Some(reordered)` **only** when it actually reorders (> 1 const tag); otherwise `None` lets the caller keep borrowing the original slice (like the runes branch already does).

Result on the profile: `clean_nodes` (~8.7% inclusive) and the `TemplateNode::clone` it drove (~5.4%) **both drop out of the transform hot frames entirely.**

### 2. `generate_id` hashes the `next_suffix` key once, not twice
The conflict path did `next_suffix.get(base)` before the loop and `next_suffix.get_mut(base)` after. Holding a single `get_mut` slot across the loop (which only touches the separate `conflicts` map) folds those into one lookup. ~5% on the conflict-path microbench.

## Correctness — byte-identical

- `sort_const_tags` returns the same order in all cases (the ≤1 path already returned nodes unchanged; the > 1 path clones each node exactly once, same total work as the previous move-based path, but only on the rare reorder branch).
- `generate_id` suffix sequence and `next_suffix` bookkeeping are untouched.
- **`compatibility_report`: 16/16** categories · **`svelte2tsx_fixtures`: 15/15** · `clippy --all-features -- -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt` (rustc 1.96.0) clean.

author: enthouan
body:
Closes #5.

Makes self-hosted HTTP deployment safe by default and documents the credential
and network exposure model. Exposing the server beyond the local machine is now
always an explicit, deliberate choice.

## Changes
- **Loopback by default** (**Breaking**): new `HOST` var, default `127.0.0.1` (was a hardcoded `0.0.0.0` bind). A fresh HTTP deployment is reachable only from the local machine.
- **Exposure guard**: `loadConfig` refuses to start an HTTP server bound to a non-loopback address with no `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, with a remediation message. `ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_EXPOSURE=true` is the documented opt-out for when exposure is contained at another layer.
- **Origin validation**: `POST /mcp` rejects disallowed `Origin` headers (403) as a DNS-rebinding / CSRF defense for loopback deployments. Loopback origins and `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` are allowed; non-browser MCP clients send no Origin and are unaffected. Done as Hono middleware since the SDK's built-in DNS-rebinding options are deprecated.
- **`src/security.ts`**: pure, unit-tested `isLoopbackHost` / `isAllowedOrigin` predicates kept apart from transport wiring.
- **Docker**: `docker-compose.yml` now publishes to the host loopback only (`127.0.0.1:3000:3000`), so the container is host-local by default; LAN exposure requires editing `ports` and setting a token.
- **Docs**: new `SECURITY.md` (credential risk model, network exposure model, vulnerability reporting), updated README config table + Security section, rewrote `.env.example`, CHANGELOG entry.
- **Logging audit**: confirmed no secret leakage (client logs only `{endpoint, status}`; error results never surface the API key or response body). Documented the guarantee.

## Test plan
- `pnpm typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `build` all pass.
- `pnpm test`: 48 pass (was 31; +17 across the config guard and the new security predicates).
- Manual runtime checks: guard refuses `HOST=0.0.0.0` without a token (exit 1); loopback start + `/health` OK; evil `Origin` → 403; localhost/absent `Origin` passes; `ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_EXPOSURE=true` override starts with a warning; existing `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` 401 gate still works, with Origin checked first.

<!-- If PR doesn't fully resolve the issue, replace 'Fixes' below with 'Related to'. -->
<!-- If there is no issue being resolved, open one before creating this pull request. -->
Fixes #5310 

<!-- Concisely describe what the pull request does. -->

Moves logic for determining which common data to return to its proper place within `get_common_data`, so it's consistently applied.

**Technical details**
<!-- Add any other information or technical details about the implementation; or delete the section entirely. -->

The underlying problem causing #5310 was that the 404 handler was calling `get_common_data` rather than `get_anonymous_common_data`. The design of the common data getters meant the caller had to know which to call. After this change, the getter dispatches based on whether the user is logged in or not. This solves the issue, and probably other random bugs that may have arisen from trying to get a common data blob for which some info was privileged.

NOTE TO REVIEWERS:

The issue #5310 only occurred in prod, or at least when `DEBUG=false`. So, verification that this fixes the problem needs to be done in those situations. However, when `DEBUG=false`, but you're running in the dev docker environment, the static files don't really work (unrelated to these changes), so the best way to test this is to build a prod image with

```
docker build -t mathesar/mathesar:latest .
```

and then run the app in prod mode with `docker compose up`.

Then, navigate to `http://localhost/aslkfjasflkj`

Note that after this fix, the back end returns 404, but the front end does not render anything because it _never_ renders `index.html`. I think this is a net improvement, and it does solve the linked issue, but we should consider figuring out what we want to actually render in cases where non-logged-in users navigate to a non-existent path and implement that (someday).

author: theheroayush
body:
### 💡 What
Reorganized the boolean logic in `app.js`'s `renderSkillsHub()` filter callback to use early returns. Inexpensive category matching is now evaluated first.

### 🎯 Why
In the original implementation, `.toLowerCase().includes()` was executed up to three times per skill per iteration (for `name`, `tagline`, and `desc`) *even if* the skill failed the `matchCat` category check. By short-circuiting the logic, we bypass these computationally expensive string allocations entirely when they aren't needed.

### 📊 Impact
In benchmark tests using 10,000 mocked skill objects over 100 iterations, the time taken dropped from ~390ms to ~54ms.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run the application and switch between categories in the Skills Hub; the rendering speed is visibly faster on lower-end devices or when handling large lists. Validated via local benchmarking script and `node build.js`.

author: gmoro
body:
🚨 **Severity**: MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability**: The daemon initialization logic in `proxydhcpd/cli.py` called `os.umask(0)`, which sets the file creation mask to 000. This causes any files created subsequently by the daemon process (e.g., logs, temporary files) to be created world-writable, allowing unprivileged users to modify them.
🎯 **Impact**: If the daemon creates files, they could be tampered with by any user on the system, potentially leading to denial of service, log tampering, or privilege escalation depending on how those files are used.
🔧 **Fix**: Changed `os.umask(0)` to `os.umask(0o022)` to ensure files are created with secure default permissions (e.g., rw-r--r--). Also logged learning in `.jules/sentinel.md`
✅ **Verification**: Run `PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/` to ensure no functionality is broken. Check `proxydhcpd/cli.py` to see the new umask.

Second module split under the Codacy Lizard complexity epic (STRK-168 / STRK-169). Drops `js/inventory-import.js` below the `Lizard_file-nloc` gate (1500) by moving the CSV-export cluster into a new sibling file.

### What moved
`exportNumistaCsv`, `buildCsvContent`, `exportCsv` → new `js/csv-export.js`. These are the inventory CSV/Numista export functions — a cohesive, self-contained concern.

### Pure code motion — zero behavior change
- Functions moved **byte-identical** to the committed original (verified via a `git show HEAD` diff; bodies preserved at their original 2-space indent).
- `inventory-import.js` is a strict-mode IIFE, so `csv-export.js` is wrapped in its **own `"use strict"` IIFE** and re-exposes the same window API: `window.exportCsv` / `exportInventoryCSV` / `exportNumistaCsv`. The three `window.*` export lines moved **with** the functions (leaving them behind would ReferenceError at IIFE load).
- The cluster reads only **external globals** (`inventory`, `Papa`, `formatCurrency`, `spotPrices`, valuation/format helpers from `utils.js`) — **no IIFE-private dependencies** — so the two files end up fully decoupled (neither references the other).
- New file loads immediately **after** `inventory-import.js` in both `index.html` and `sw.js` `CORE_ASSETS` (order-matched).

### Verification
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `inventory-import.js` NLOC | 1576 → **1353** (clears the 1500 gate, 147 margin) |
| `csv-export.js` NLOC | **226** |
| Core Playwright suite | **215/215 green** (incl. `import-export.spec.js` — drives the CSV export/import round-trip through the relocated functions) |
| ESLint / Prettier | clean |

### No version bump
Per the STRK-169 campaign policy, the 10 splits ship unbumped; a single `/release patch` closes the campaign. The `sw.js` `CACHE_NAME` auto-stamped so the cache still invalidates; `check-release-sync` stays green at 3.35.14.

### No test changes
Pure refactor — CSV export/import is covered by the existing `import-export.spec.js` core spec (green). No new/moved/deleted test files.

Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (6.4.2 → 8.0.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

author: sarahasad23
body: ### What changes were proposed in this PR? This PR introduces persistent Python Virtual Environments (PVEs) by moving them out of the Computing Unit (CU) lifecycle and storing them in the database. Previously, PVEs were managed through Computing Units and existed only within the CU they were created in. As a result, PVEs were lost when the corresponding CU was terminated. This PR adds a new `virtual_environments` table to persist PVE configurations and introduces a dedicated dashboard interface for managing them. Users can now create, view, update, and delete their own Python virtual environments through a new "Environments" page in the dashboard sidebar. PVE definitions are stored as user-owned resources in the database and can be managed independently of Computing Units. Note: This PR only introduces persistence for PVE metadata and configuration. Creating, updating, and deleting a PVE in this PR only affects the corresponding database records. The execution-time behavior of materializing and using these virtual environments inside a Computing Unit is not part of this change and will be introduced in a future PR. K8s configurations for this feature will be added in a future PR. ### Any related issues, documentation, discussions? Related discussions and issues: #5360, #5361. ### How was this PR tested? body:
### Motivation
- Implement ADR-024 requirement to expose service-scoped rehearsal workflow status and operational context in planning views and recommendation diagnostics without affecting deterministic recommendation selection.
- Provide actionable summaries (readiness, blockers, open issues, upcoming rehearsals, overrides) while preserving catalog truth and redaction rules for public/audience-partitioned diagnostics.

### Description
- Added domain types and DTOs for rehearsal workflow summaries and indicators: extended `RehearsalWorkflowModels` with audience/session/issue/summary types and implemented `RehearsalWorkflowSummaryService` to aggregate sessions, issue counts, action counts, overrides and redact sensitive fields by audience.
- Exposed workflow data in API contracts and models: updated `apps/api/src/main/openapi/components/schemas/service-plans.yaml` and `setlists.yaml` to include `WorkflowOperationalSummary`, `WorkflowIssueIndicator`, and `workflowIssues` on `ServicePlanBlock`; regenerated OpenAPI models (`target/generated-sources/openapi/...`).
- Wired summaries into server controllers and responses: added `WorkflowSummaryResponseMapper`, injected `RehearsalWorkflowSummaryService` into `ServicePlanController` and `SetlistService`, populated `ServicePlanResponse.workflowSummary`, per-block `workflowIssues`, and optional `SetlistProposalResponse.operationalWorkflowSummary` (diagnostics only) while ensuring these are clearly separated from deterministic recommendation facts.
- Implemented rendering isolation for overrides and audience redaction: `RehearsalWorkflowSummaryService` builds view-mode-aware `WorkflowSummary` and helpers map to generated DTOs; `SetlistService` attaches operational context only when a `serviceTeamContext` is provided and does not mutate selection/order logic.

### Testing
- Ran OpenAPI generation to verify contract and model synchronization with `mvn -pl apps/api -DskipTests generate-sources`, which completed successfully and produced updated generated model classes under `apps/api/target/generated-sources/openapi`.
- Added unit tests for summary aggregation and redaction: `apps/api/src/test/java/com/cadentia/rehearsal/RehearsalWorkflowSummaryServiceTest.java` verifies counts, sessions, overrides, open issues, and redaction behavior, and `apps/api/src/test/java/com/cadentia/reng/SetlistServiceTest.java` was updated to assert that attaching operational workflow diagnostics does not change recommendation status or audit messages; tests were added but not executed in this change (no full `mvn test` run in this rollout).

author: joshuamckenty
body:
Follow-up to #3. The comic action lines (and heartburst's under-glow) were still landing at screen centre while the centrepiece sat on the card.

**Root cause:** the panel-runner bound `uCenter` — the point the procedural parts radiate from — to the **canvas centre**, while the panel centrepiece (word/heart) is drawn at the **anchor**. Once the anchor stopped being the screen centre (the #3 card-targeting), they split.

**Fix:** bind `uCenter` to the anchor, y-flipped to `gl_FragCoord` space exactly as the pure-shader runner does for `uOrigin`. Now every part of a panel effect coheres on one point. This matches the Swift side, which already uses the anchor (`usesOrigin`).

Verified: 187 vitest tests pass; headless captures show comic's lines radiating from the burst and heartburst's glow under the heart, both on the card.

author: evgunter
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in `mngr_claude` that wrote cruft into the user's shared `~/.claude/` on every *local* agent provision.

### Bug 1: recursive self-referential symlinks
`_sync_user_resources` used plain `ln -sf` as an idempotent command. On the second and later provisions the destination was already a symlink-to-directory, so `ln` dereferenced it and nested a new link **inside the shared source** (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/skills -> ~/.claude/skills`, `~/.claude/commands/commands`, `~/.claude/plugins/cache/cache`, etc.). Each local provision re-triggered it.

Fix: all sync symlinks now use `ln -sfn` (`--no-dereference`) — directory, child, and individual-file links (including credentials and `keybindings.json`), so re-provisioning replaces the dest symlink instead of following it. `-n` is portable across GNU and BSD/macOS `ln`.

### Bug 2: skill-provisioned agents' primary skill leaked into every local agent
`_install_skill_locally` wrote the agent's primary skill (`code-guardian`, `fixme-fairy`) to global `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. `_sync_user_resources` then symlinked all of `~/.claude/skills/` into *every* local agent's config dir, so the skill showed up in the skill list of every agent.

Fix: the skill is now installed into the agent's **own per-agent config dir** (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), strictly agent-scoped — mirroring the already-agent-scoped remote install. To let a per-agent real skill file coexist with the user's other (symlinked) skills, `skills/` is now synced via **child-level symlinks** (the same pattern `plugins/` already uses) rather than one dir-level symlink; the install breaks any same-named child symlink before writing so it can't corrupt the shared source. The local install is now **silent** (no interactive prompt), matching the always-silent remote install.

## Tests
- New: `_sync_user_resources` is idempotent across two provisions with no self-referential loops (covers both the dir-level branch and the child-level branch).
- New: `_install_skill_locally` writes into the per-agent config dir, and breaks a child symlink into shared skills instead of following it.
- Updated the existing `_install_skill_locally` tests for the new per-agent-dir signature; removed the now-obsolete interactive-prompt test.
- Verified locally (other test slices run in CI; a foreign session held the global pytest lock during this run): `skill_agent_test.py` 33 passed, `plugin_test.py` 199 passed, `test_ratchets.py` 56 passed, `ty check` clean on all four files. Also confirmed empirically that `ln -sf` reproduces the loop and `ln -sfn` fixes it.

## Notes / tradeoffs
- This only prevents *new* loops; pre-existing loops on machines in the wild are not self-healed (deliberate, per design discussion). A safe cleanup one-liner exists if needed.
- Child-level `skills/` symlinks mean a skill the user adds to `~/.claude/skills/` after provisioning won't live-propagate into already-provisioned agents (same tradeoff `plugins/` already has); it re-syncs on the next provision.
- Remote install is unchanged (remote hosts are isolated machines, so no cross-agent leak there).

author: samcarey
body:
## Summary

Adds two cross-day long-press gestures to the multi-day time-window editor — in **both** the create-poll Time Windows card and the voter availability ballot — coordinated by a new `components/DayTimeWindowsList.tsx` that owns the multi-day selection state.

- **Bulk-edit windows** — long-press a time-slot pill → selection mode (blue ring + haptic). Tap pills to multi-select across any days, then **"Edit N"** opens one time-picker whose value is applied to every selected pill.
- **Copy a day's times to other days** — long-press a day → "Copy times to other days" menu. Tap target days (source greys out + is excluded), then **"Paste N"** copies the source day's slots onto each.
- **Autofix after the modal closes** — `fitWindowsToBounds` (`lib/timeUtils.ts`) clamps each window into the creator's allowed window it most overlaps (or snaps it, preserving duration, to the nearest one), then sorts + merges overlaps. Runs after every bulk-edit/paste so the result can never trip the "outside allowed times / overlap" submit-blocker; a transient "Adjusted slots to fit the allowed times" toast shows when anything moved.
- **Long-press no longer selects the slot text** — `select-none [-webkit-touch-callout:none]` on the pills + long-press day label (also suppresses the iOS callout).

## Implementation notes
- `DayTimeWindowsInput` gains an optional `selection` prop (pill/day long-press + tap wiring, blue-ring selection, copy-mode checkboxes); both call sites render through the new coordinator. Long-press uses a non-hook factory + shared ref (pills render in a loop, so a hook can't be used per-pill).
- `fitWindowsToBounds` is pure + unit-tested (`tests/__tests__/time-poll/fit-windows-to-bounds.test.ts`).
- `DayTimeWindowsInput` is intentionally not `React.memo`'d, so per-day selection objects are rebuilt each render (a handful of rows; memoizing yields no render savings without `memo` on the child).

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for `fitWindowsToBounds` (clamp, snap-preserving-duration, merge, no-op-same-ref, never-trips-blocker)
- [x] Verified live on a real browser via Playwright: windows-mode multi-select + "Edit N", copy→paste with source greyed, paste autofix clamped out-of-bounds slots (9–12 → 2–5 PM / 6–9 PM) with toast and **no** invalid banner, and `getComputedStyle(pill).user-select === "none"`

- Genetics data is educational scaffolding from published sources — not a substitute for hands-on herd verification
- D, E, and V loci are included but unplaced on OryCun2.0; UI notes this when those loci are selected
- Branch name keeps the existing `inital-config` typo (already on remote)

Three small, independently-verified build/test hygiene changes — no behavior change, no public-API change.

## Commits

**1. `test_helpers.rs` → `tests/common/mod.rs`** (`6ba9b67`)
A top-level `tests/test_helpers.rs` has ZERO `#[test]` fns yet Cargo auto-compiles it as its own integration-test binary. Moving it into the conventional `tests/common/` subdir (not a test target) drops that one redundant build+link unit. `make_draw_ctx!` is `#[macro_export]`, so the 4 consumers just swap `mod test_helpers;` → `mod common;` — no call-site changes, zero snapshot churn.

**2. `fs4 0.8 → 1.1` to dedupe `rustix`** (`971a2fc`)
`fs4 0.8` pulled `rustix 0.38` (+ `linux-raw-sys` + the `windows-sys 0.52` family) while crossterm/tempfile already pull `rustix 1.1` — two full `rustix` compiles. `fs4 1.1` drops that second tree: `cargo tree -d` now shows **zero `rustix` duplicates** (~8 transitive crates removed). API migration is `try_lock_exclusive()` → `try_lock()`, called via **UFCS** (`fs4::FileExt::try_lock`) on purpose — std stabilized an *inherent* `File::try_lock` in 1.89 that would otherwise shadow the trait and silently raise our MSRV above the declared 1.78. Lock-on-contention semantics are identical (`TryLockError::WouldBlock` stays an `Err`). fs4 1.1's own MSRV is 1.75.

**3. `cargo update` lockfile refresh** (`6cd5f0d`)
Lockfile-only. Every direct dep is already on its latest stable major (`notify 9` is an RC, so we stay on 8); this just picks up ~28 semver-compatible transitive bumps (ratatui 0.30.1, chrono 0.4.45, log, mio, socket2, …).

## Verification
- `just preflight` green (lint → clippy → hack → test), full suite **1108 tests**.
- `cargo tree -d`: rustix dedup'd; only an unavoidable transitive `hashbrown` skew remains.
- Lock-path tests (install 7 + config 59) green; semantics unchanged.

## Context
Came out of a measurement-driven compile/test-speed audit (clean build is already ~13.4s, deps already `default-features=false`-trimmed). These were the only clean wins; file-splits / dep-drops were measured as not worth it. Sibling test reorg was #191.

author: sunapi386
body:
## Context

`citadel vnc enable` on Linux previously required sudo even when the logged-in user's own X authority file was available. The `findXAuthFile()` function returned the auth file path but didn't distinguish between user-readable files (no sudo needed) and root-only display manager files (sudo required). This meant running x11vnc with unnecessary privilege escalation, and error messages when sudo was actually needed were unclear.

Ref: aceteam-ai/aceteam#3471

## Summary

**Sudo reduction for Start()** -- Replaced `findXAuthFile()` with `resolveXAuth()` that returns `(authFile, needsSudo)`. The resolution priority is:
1. `$XAUTHORITY` env var (user-readable, no sudo)
2. `~/.Xauthority` (user-readable, no sudo)
3. Display manager auth files -- lightdm, gdm, sddm (root-only, sudo required)
4. No auth file found -- uses `x11vnc -find` for auto-discovery (no sudo)

Previously, finding `~/.Xauthority` still triggered `needsSudo=true` because the old logic was `needsSudo := authFile != "" && os.Getuid() != 0`. Now only DM auth files set `needsSudo=true`.

**Auto-discovery fallback** -- When no auth file is found, x11vnc is started with `-find` instead of `-auth guess`. The `-find` flag probes `/tmp/.X*-lock`, `XAUTHORITY`, and running X sessions to auto-discover the display and auth cookie without needing sudo.

**Improved error messages** -- Added `ErrSudoRequired` sentinel error with actionable message: "VNC server installation requires sudo. Run: sudo citadel vnc enable". The `cmd/vnc.go` handler surfaces this directly to the user without wrapping.

**zypper support** -- Added openSUSE's zypper package manager to `Install()`.

**Sudo availability check** -- `Install()` now checks for the `sudo` binary before attempting package installation as non-root, returning the actionable error immediately.

## Bundling research

Explored three approaches for bundling a VNC server to avoid sudo for installation:

| Approach | Feasibility | Verdict |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| Static x11vnc binary | x11vnc depends on libX11, libXtst, libXdamage, OpenSSL -- too many shared-lib deps for static linking | Impractical |
| Go-native VNC server sharing existing X display | Would require X11 bindings (XGB) + XTest/XDamage extensions; large implementation effort | Impractical for this scope |
| Pre-built download from releases bucket | Viable but adds download infrastructure and trust concerns | Deferred |

The package-manager approach with clear sudo messaging is the right tradeoff for now.

## Deferred

- **TigerVNC fallback** -- Issue #3471 mentions falling back to TigerVNC if x11vnc is unavailable. Not implemented in this PR; can be a follow-up.

## Test plan

| Category | Tests | Coverage |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `buildX11VNCArgs` | 4 cases: explicit auth, DM auth, auto-discover, custom port | Arg construction, `-find` vs `-display` branching |
| `buildX11VNCArgs` ordering | 2 cases: `-find` first when no auth, `-display` first with auth | Argument position correctness |
| `ErrSudoRequired` | 2 assertions: contains "sudo", contains fix command | Error message content |
| Existing tests | All pass unchanged | Regression safety |
| Full suite | `go test ./...` passes | No breakage |

**VM testing**: Not performed in this session (SSH access to 192.168.2.43 was unavailable). Manual testing on a Linux desktop with an X display is recommended before merging:
```bash
GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o /tmp/citadel-linux ./cmd/citadel/
scp /tmp/citadel-linux jason@192.168.2.43:/tmp/citadel-test
# On the VM:
/tmp/citadel-test vnc status
/tmp/citadel-test vnc enable
```

Key runtime behaviors to verify manually:
- `x11vnc -find` starts successfully without sudo (replaces `-auth guess`)
- Package install with `sudo apt-get` works when run via `sudo citadel vnc enable`

author: lstein
body:
## Problem

When first-run setup runs on macOS, `uv tool install` can trigger an Xcode
**"install command-line developer tools"** dialog — an annoying interruption for
non-technical users the signed launcher is meant to serve.

### Root cause

uv's default `--python-preference` is `managed`, which *prefers* a managed
interpreter but **falls back to a system/framework CPython** if it finds a
matching version. On macOS that's the non-relocatable python.org build at
`/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/...`. Building the tool venv from it makes
uv rewrite the copied executable's Mach-O load paths with **`install_name_tool`**
(part of the Xcode CLT) — which pops the install dialog when the CLT aren't
present. uv's managed (python-build-standalone) builds are relocatable, so they
never invoke `install_name_tool`.

## Fix

Set `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed` in the launcher's `uvEnv()` — the single
place that configures every `uv` invocation, so `python install`, `tool install`,
and the GPU-reinstall path are all consistent. The launcher already pins **3.12**
and runs `uv python install 3.12` first; this just closes the gap where
`tool install` could still bind to the framework interpreter.

Also folded the same flags (`--python 3.12 --python-preference only-managed`)
into the documented PyPI/`uv` recipe across the docs and READMEs, since the
manual CLI path hit the same prompt.

## Tests

- New `TestUVEnvForcesManagedPython` asserts the env carries `only-managed`.
- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, `gofmt -l` all clean.

author: angaziz
body:
Closes #8.

## Problem (P0 — trust break)
The hub sent `ack(ok:true)` to the device **unconditionally** after every permission decision (`AppDelegate.swift:82-83`), even when `bridge.resolve` did nothing because the id was unknown or the prompt had already timed out (`finish` no-ops on done/missing). Combined with the device clearing its prompt the instant it **enqueued** the BLE decision (`buddy_hud.cpp:28`), a late Approve — tapped after the 25s cap already denied — showed the prompt vanish with a **success ack**, so the user believed they approved when CC had already proceeded as denied.

## Fix

### Step 1 — Mac/Swift (fix the lie first)
- `resolve`/`finish` now report `applied` / `late` / `unknown` (synchronous `queue.sync`, verified deadlock-safe for the BLE => @MainActor => bridge path).
- `AppDelegate` sends `ack(ok:true)` only when the decision actually applied, `ack(ok:false)` when late/superseded, `err(unknown_prompt_id)` otherwise (nil-bridge included). No unconditional `ok:true` path remains.
- Documented `ok:false` = "decision did not apply (late/superseded)" in `hub/CONTRACT.md` + `docs/tech.md`. No wire/schema change — `ok` was already a bool.

### Step 2 — Device/C++ (wire the real ack)
- Added device-local `buddy_prompt_t.decision_state` (not on wire).
- **Centralized** the decide path into `buddy_decide()` so **all 7 buddy views** (hud, calm, editorial, led, analog, blueprint, oscilloscope) stop clearing the prompt on local enqueue — they now enter `PROMPT_PENDING` and keep the prompt visible.
- Wired the real app-level ack: `on_frame` tries `hub_parse_ack` before status, routing to `hub_apply_ack` => `SENT_OK` (clear) on ok, `TOO_LATE` (keep visible) on `!ok`/`err`, ignore on id mismatch.
- Each view renders a distinct **PENDING** ("SENT - AWAITING") and **TOO_LATE** ("DIDN'T APPLY", negative color) state with a dismiss affordance. A too-late prompt never renders as success.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Late/unknown-id decisions produce `ack(ok:false)`/`err`, not `ok:true`.
- [x] Device shows a distinct "too late / didn't apply" state instead of a success beat.
- [x] Device no longer clears the prompt purely on local enqueue.

## Verification
- Swift: `swift test` => 11/11.
- Firmware native: `pio test -e native` => 83/83 (6 new: ok:false parse + 5 `hub_apply_ack` transitions).
- Device build: `pio run -e beacon` => SUCCESS (Flash 60.1%).
- Plan reviewed by codex (verdict: revise => both concerns folded in: ok:false doc + all-7-views centralization); implementation independently verified by a second agent (verdict: SHIP).
- [ ] On-device manual test pending (late-approve race).

body:
## What this PR does

Implements the edit-expense feature so that logged-in users can update any expense they previously recorded. This step replaces the `GET /expenses/<id>/edit` stub with a real form-based flow: a GET loads the expense pre-populated, a POST validates and persists the changes, and the user is redirected back to the profile page with a confirmation message. The profile page now also shows a filterable expense list table with an Edit link per row. Ownership is enforced at both the Python and database level — users can only edit their own expenses.

## Changes

- `app.py` — implemented `GET`/`POST /expenses/<int:id>/edit`; added `_validate_expense_form()` helper shared by both add and edit routes; updated `profile()` to fetch and pass the filtered expense list; added `?edited` success banner; added `AND user_id = ?` to the UPDATE WHERE clause; switched `debug=True` to env-var controlled
- `templates/edit_expense.html` — new pre-populated edit form mirroring the add-expense layout
- `templates/profile.html` — added "My Expenses" table with date-filter-aware expense list and per-row Edit links
- `tests/test_08-edit-expense.py` — 82 tests covering auth guards, ownership enforcement, form pre-population, all validation paths, sticky form values, DB side-effects, and profile expense list
- `.claude/specs/08-edit-expense.md` — feature spec

## Definition of done

- [x] `GET /expenses/<id>/edit` renders the edit form pre-populated with the expense's current values for a logged-in owner
- [x] `GET /expenses/<id>/edit` redirects to `/login` for an unauthenticated visitor
- [x] `GET /expenses/<id>/edit` returns 404 when the expense does not exist or belongs to another user
- [x] Submitting the edit form with valid data updates the row in the `expenses` table and redirects to `/profile?edited=1`
- [x] The profile page shows "Expense updated successfully." after the redirect
- [x] Submitting with a missing or zero/negative amount re-renders the form with an error and does not update the row
- [x] Submitting with an invalid category re-renders the form with an error
- [x] Submitting with a missing or invalid date re-renders the form with an error
- [x] Previously submitted form values are preserved on validation failure (sticky form)
- [x] The profile page expense list shows all expenses for the logged-in user (respecting the date filter) with an Edit link per row
- [x] App starts without errors after all changes

## How to test

1. Run `uv run python app.py`
2. Log in as any user
3. Visit `/profile` — you should see a "My Expenses" table with an Edit link on each row
4. Click Edit on any expense — the form should open pre-populated with that expense's values
5. Change any field and click "Save changes" — you should be redirected to `/profile?edited=1` with "Expense updated successfully."
6. Try submitting the edit form with a blank amount, invalid category, or bad date — the form should re-render with an error and your entered values preserved
7. Try navigating to `/expenses/9999/edit` — you should get a 404

## What does this PR do?

The Cosmos DB service cached several resources using keys that did not fully capture the request context. The `CosmosClient` cache key was built only from account name and auth method, and the `ListDatabases` / `ListContainers` keys were built only from account (and database) name.

This PR scopes all three cache keys to the full request context so cached entries are only reused for matching requests:

- `GetCosmosClientAsync` now includes `subscription` and `tenant` in the client cache key.
- `ListDatabases` now includes `subscription`, `tenant`, and `authMethod` in its cache key.
- `ListContainers` now includes `subscription`, `tenant`, and `authMethod` (alongside account and database) in its cache key.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (7.2.0 → 7.2.1) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion

Impact

PROXY protocol support for Puma was added in version 5.5.0.

When PROXY protocol v1 support is enabled, Puma reads incoming bytes into an internal buffer. It waits for "\r\n" to determine whether a PROXY v1 line is present. If an attacker opens a TCP connection and continuously sends bytes without CRLF, Puma keeps appending to this pre-parse buffer.

This can cause unbounded in-process memory growth and additional CPU cost from repeatedly scanning the growing buffer for CRLF. A single, unauthenticated TCP connection can drive significant memory growth and may cause process/container OOM or degraded availability.

Only Puma servers using the following non-default config are affected:

   set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

  • Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:
  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1
  • Restrict direct network access to Puma listeners using PROXY protocol:
    • Only allow trusted load balancers/reverse proxies to connect.
    • Block arbitrary client TCP access with firewall/security group rules.

Resources

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
  • CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation
  • Puma client PROXY protocol parsing code
  • Puma constants, including PROXY_PROTOCOL_V1_REGEX
Release Notes

7.2.1

  • Bugfixes
    • Limit and anchor PROXY protocol v1 parsing to prevent abuse via crafted inputs ([#3947])
    • Parse PROXY protocol only once per connection to prevent injection on keep-alive requests ([#3947])

Security advisories

  • CVE-2026-47736 / GHSA-qpgp-93vx-g8v8: Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion
  • CVE-2026-47737 / GHSA-2vqw-3mp8-cgmx: Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

New phase: emergent spiral pattern on the pulsating wavefront, separate from the sinc wave CA (to be integrated later). Previous sinc files preserved with `_sinc` suffix.

**Spiral mechanism** — no multiplication, no division, no lookup tables, no floats at runtime:

1. Each cell carries a direction vector `(spiral_x, spiral_y)` propagated during BFS
2. On z-transitions, a **Bresenham accumulator** (`spiral_acc`) decides whether to apply a **CORDIC micro-rotation**:
   ```
   // shift+add only — arctan(2^{-CORDIC_SHIFT}) per step
   new_sx = sx - (sy >> CORDIC_SHIFT);   // CCW going up
   new_sy = sy + (sx >> CORDIC_SHIFT);
   ```
3. `CORDIC_N ≈ π·2^k` rotations are distributed over `R_MAX` z-levels → total rotation ≈ π (half turn, pole to pole)
4. `CORDIC_SHIFT` auto-scales with `L` via compile-time `#if` cascade (not a table — single constant)
5. Per z-level, a **Bresenham line** from center to `(spiral_x, spiral_y)` marks `spin=1` — arm width is constant (`SPIRAL_W=2` cells) regardless of `L`

**Visualization** (3 panels + graph):
- Panel 1: wavefront z=MID slice (green gradient + yellow sweep ring)
- Panel 2: spin overlay at z=MID (cyan=spin, white=spin∧active)
- Panel 3: y=MID side view (xz plane, shows helix structure)
- Bottom graph: `spiral_y` and `spiral_x` vs z (unwrapped spiral)

```
nmake /f Makefile.nmake    → spiral.exe
```

author: deblasis
body:
## #170 bucket H — INPUT-side flattening fixes (from holistic code review)

A holistic post-merge **code review** (via `superpowers:requesting-code-review`) of bucket-H Passes 11–15 surfaced two INPUT-side gaps the per-PR reviews missed. Both are fixed here, TDD-first.

### C1 (Critical) — nested-struct input block left its inner struct undefined
`in VertexIn { Foo a; }` emitted `struct VertexIn { a: Foo }` but never declared `Foo`:
```
naga: no definition in scope for identifier: `Foo`
```
The Pass-14 corpus fixture **masked** this — a sibling plain input forced `Foo` to be emitted as a side effect. A minimal single-block shader rejects.

**Fix:** the OUTPUT side (Pass 15) already force-emitted inner structs; the INPUT side now does too. `emitOneStructForwardDecl(blockType)` emits the member structs (it early-returns on the block struct itself, which is pre-seeded into `emitted_structs` to suppress the generic emitter), then the block is emitted manually as a plain struct.

### I2 (Important) — input block array member → naga-invalid `@location`
`in Blk { float a[4]; }` → `@location(0) a: array<f32, 4>` (naga reject), because the input gate (`structHasStructMember`) only detected struct members.

**Fix:** the input gate is now the same `blockHasAggregateMember` (struct/array/matrix) the output side uses, and `emitFlattenedIoParams` / `buildIoReconExpr` were extended to flatten an array member per element and reassemble with an array constructor:
```wgsl
fn main(@location(0) b_a_0: f32, … @location(3) b_a_3: f32) -> … {
    let io_b: Blk = Blk(array<f32, 4>(b_a_0, b_a_1, b_a_2, b_a_3));
```
— symmetric to the array OUTPUT case (#228). A **matrix** member or an **array-of-aggregate** at a `@location` honest-errors (`error.UnsupportedOp`).

### Refactors
Shared `arrayTypeLen` helper (3 call sites) + `emitOneIoParam`; dead `structHasStructMember` and a duplicate `outputBlockNeedsDeepFlatten` removed.

### Result
- Both bugs fixed; **single-level plain input blocks byte-identical**; existing fixtures still naga-PASS.
- Conformance unchanged: **PASS 2087 / FAIL 0**. `zig build test-wgsl` 132/132.

### Tests (naga-gated)
Minimal nested-input inner-struct decl, array-member input flatten, matrix-member input honest-error.

### Review
The fix was re-reviewed by an adversarial subagent (deep nesting `Blk{Mid{Inner}}`, array-of-struct, vector-element array, comma/`first` handling, no double-emission, shared-struct dedup, honest-error reachability) — verdict **Ready to merge, no issues**; it also confirmed the OLD binary reproduces both bugs.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ puma (7.1.0 → 7.2.1) · [Repo](https://github.com/puma/puma) · [Changelog](https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/main/History.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

Impact

Puma is vulnerable to source IP spoofing when set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1 is enabled and persistent connections are used.

PROXY protocol v1 is a connection-level protocol. Support was added to Puma in v5.5.0. A proxy sends one PROXY header at the beginning of a TCP connection, before any HTTP data. Puma incorrectly re-parsed PROXY protocol headers after each keep-alive request on the same connection. An attacker able to send HTTP requests through a trusted proxy could therefore inject a second PROXY header between HTTP requests. Puma would treat the injected header as authoritative for the next request and overwrite REMOTE_ADDR.

This can mislead applications or middleware that use REMOTE_ADDR for security decisions, rate limiting, auditing, or allow/deny lists.

Only deployments that explicitly enable PROXY protocol v1 are affected, and will have set:

set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Puma's default configuration is not affected. Deployments that do not use persistent connections to Puma are also not expected to be affected by this issue.

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:

  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Users can also disable persistent connections to Puma, for example:

enable_keep_alives false

References

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CVE-2025-31135 / GHSA-c2c3-pqw5-5p7c: go-guerrilla repeated PROXY command source IP spoofing
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation

🚨 Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion

Impact

PROXY protocol support for Puma was added in version 5.5.0.

When PROXY protocol v1 support is enabled, Puma reads incoming bytes into an internal buffer. It waits for "\r\n" to determine whether a PROXY v1 line is present. If an attacker opens a TCP connection and continuously sends bytes without CRLF, Puma keeps appending to this pre-parse buffer.

This can cause unbounded in-process memory growth and additional CPU cost from repeatedly scanning the growing buffer for CRLF. A single, unauthenticated TCP connection can drive significant memory growth and may cause process/container OOM or degraded availability.

Only Puma servers using the following non-default config are affected:

   set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1

Patches

Users should upgrade to versions 7.2.1 or 8.0.2.

Workarounds

  • Disable PROXY protocol v1 parsing if it is not required:
  # remove/comment this:
  # set_remote_address proxy_protocol: :v1
  • Restrict direct network access to Puma listeners using PROXY protocol:
    • Only allow trusted load balancers/reverse proxies to connect.
    • Block arbitrary client TCP access with firewall/security group rules.

Resources

  • HAProxy PROXY protocol specification
  • CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
  • CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
  • Puma set_remote_address documentation
  • Puma client PROXY protocol parsing code
  • Puma constants, including PROXY_PROTOCOL_V1_REGEX
Release Notes

7.2.1

  • Bugfixes
    • Limit and anchor PROXY protocol v1 parsing to prevent abuse via crafted inputs ([#3947])
    • Parse PROXY protocol only once per connection to prevent injection on keep-alive requests ([#3947])

Security advisories

  • CVE-2026-47736 / GHSA-qpgp-93vx-g8v8: Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Parser Allows Remote Memory Exhaustion
  • CVE-2026-47737 / GHSA-2vqw-3mp8-cgmx: Puma PROXY Protocol v1 Accepts Repeated Protocol Headers on Persistent Connections

7.2.0

7.2.0 On The Corner

author: guilhermegor
body:
## Description
**What**: Pin the per-field decimal scale of every `Decimal` field in the CVM Monthly Profile (Perfil Mensal) models to the CVM XML standard [`PadrãoXMLPerfil739`](https://cvmweb.cvm.gov.br/SWB/Sistemas/SCW/PadroesXML/PadraoXMLPerfil739.asp), and fix three serializer fields that emitted the wrong number of decimals.
**Why**: Previously every monetary/percentage/quantity field was typed as a bare `Decimal` (or `PercentField`, which only bounded 0–100). The model enforced "is a decimal" but not *how many decimal places* the CVM spec mandates — so the model did not actually mirror `PadrãoXMLPerfil739`.
**How**: Annotated `Decimal` types with `Field(decimal_places=…)` (plus `max_digits=…` where the spec also bounds integer digits), and a `BeforeValidator` that truncates excess precision toward zero (`ROUND_DOWN`) so a reported value is never inflated.

---

## Changes Made
**Added**:
- `_truncate_to_scale(decimal_places)` before-validator factory (ROUND_DOWN) in `_models_monthly_report_cvm.py`.
- Scale-pinned annotated types: `OneDecimalField` (1dp), `TwoDecimalField` (2dp), `FiveDecimalField` (5dp), `VarPercentPlField` (≤14 digits, 4dp), `AvgTermField` (≤8 digits, 4dp); extended `PercentField` to 1dp/≤4 digits/≤100.
- 5 new unit tests covering truncation, `max_digits` rejection, the truncate-then-cap interaction, and the serializer's 2-decimal output.

**Updated**:
- Every decimal field now uses a scale-pinned type. Scales per spec: `VAR_PERC_PL` 4dp, `PRAZ_MED_CART_TIT` 4dp, `PR_*` 1dp, `TOTAL_RECURS_*`/`VAL_PERCENT`/`VAL_PERCENT_OUTROS`/`VAR_DIAR_*`/`VAR_PATRIM_FDO_N_PRECO_ACOES`/`VAL_COLATERAL` 2dp, `VALOR_PARTE`/`TOT_ATIVOS_*` 1dp, `VAL_COTA_FUNDO` 5dp.
- Version 3.1.1 → 3.1.2 (via `make bump_version`). That recipe also ran `poetry update`, which is the source of the large `poetry.lock` churn.

**Fixed**:
- Serializer emitted `VAR_DIAR_PERC_PATRIM_FDO_VAR_N_TAXA_ANUAL`/`_CAMBIO`, `VAR_PATRIM_FDO_N_PRECO_ACOES` and `VAL_PERCENT_OUTROS` with **4** decimals; the standard mandates **2** ("numérico com duas casas decimais").

---

## Testing
### Automated Testing
- **Unit Tests**: `tests/unit/test_monthly_report_cvm.py` — **45 passed**.
- Verification run: `make test_feat MODULE=monthly_report_cvm` (codespell + docstring/type consistency + ruff + pytest) and `make lint` ("All checks passed!").

### Manual Testing
**Not Applicable**: pure model/serializer change covered by unit tests.

---

## Documentation
- **Code**: Module docstring documents the ROUND_DOWN truncation policy; each annotated type carries the verbatim spec wording it implements.

---

## Additional Notes
**Reviewer Focus**:
- `MONTANTE_DISTRIB` is **absent** from `PadrãoXMLPerfil739`. It's pinned to 2dp (matching its monetary nature and the existing serializer default) but flagged inline — confirm the intended scale.
- `poetry.lock` churn (~17 transitive upgrades) comes from `make bump_version` running `poetry update`. If you'd rather keep this PR focused, the version-bump commit can be dropped/reworked to avoid the lock update.
- Truncation runs *before* the `≤100` cap on `PR_*` fields, so e.g. `100.05` rounds down to `100.0` and is accepted; only values still >100 after truncation are rejected.

author: ruzin
body:
Ten commits batched for the next release. Roughly grouped:

## Bedrock
**`8cec8a5` fix(bedrock): allow application inference profile ARNs in Converse URL**
- `urllib.parse.quote(target_id, safe=":.-")` percent-encoded the slash inside application inference profile ARNs (`arn:aws:bedrock:…:application-inference-profile/abc123`) to `%2F`, producing HTTP 400 *"model identifier invalid"*.
- Added `/` to the safe set; extracted URL construction into `bedrock_converse_url()` at module level so `_bedrock_chat` and `simple_recorder.test_cloud_api` can't drift on the rules again.
- 4 new tests in `tests/test_bedrock_converse_url.py` pin the three concrete shapes (application profile ARN, system profile id, bare model id).
- **Impact**: This is the standard auth shape for governed AWS environments (IAM policies that allow `bedrock:InvokeModel` on application profiles but not system profiles). Without the fix, Bedrock is unusable for those users.

## Calendar
**`be18686` fix(calendar): drop declined events at the IPC boundary**
- Moved the declined-event filter from `Home.tsx` into `normalizeCalendarEvent` so the IPC contract guarantees `events` is the "meetings the user is attending" list — no new UI surface can accidentally show one.

**`6558bc8` fix(home): restore 3-per-page pagination on upcoming events**
- Pagination was added in #139, accidentally removed by #144. Restored the `< > ↻` cluster + `UPCOMING_PAGE_SIZE = 3` slice from `09bc584`.

**`67427be` fix(home): render all-day events as full UpcomingCards when expanded**
- The "+ N all-day events today" toggle expanded into plain text buttons; now uses the same `UpcomingCard` component as the timed carousel. `UpcomingCard` short-circuits its time labelling for `is_all_day` events ("All day" + "Today" instead of fabricating "Started 108 mins ago" from a UTC-midnight start).

**`2ab81ba` + `508cc0d` + `7f5427e` + `37b1d11` fix(calendar): tighter freshness, kept what worked**
- 5 min poll → **2 min poll** (down from 5)
- `staleTime: 60 s` to throttle focus-refetch and request dedup
- `useCalendarEvents()` mounted at App level so polling survives route changes
- Tried route-change refetch; reverted after it didn't deliver in practice (was redundant against the 2 min poll + focus refetch)

**`6c4ddb5` fix(calendar): drop declined-by-organizer events + raise `maxResults` 7 → 50**
- Two related bugs from real-world Google Calendar testing:
  - `normalizeCalendarEvent`'s organizer short-circuit (`self.organizer ? 'organizer' : …`) overrode the actual `responseStatus` when the user owned the event. If you organised a meeting and then declined it, the previous code labelled it `'organizer'` and the declined-filter let it through. Now a real `declined` raw status wins.
  - `fetchCalendarEvents` (Google) + `fetchOutlookCalendarEvents` (Outlook) were both capped at `maxResults=7`. One all-day block + a couple morning meetings burned through the cap before noon; everything past lunch silently disappeared. Bumped to 50.

## Cleanup
**`b6c84a2` chore: drop stale dev cruft (prompt_tests, setup.py, build-constraints)**
- `prompt_tests/` — standalone summarisation-prompt comparison harness, not in CI, dormant. Resurrectable from git history.
- `setup.py` — broken; `entry_points` pointed to `main:cli` which doesn't exist. Version still `0.1.0`. Misleading for anyone trying `pip install -e .`.
- `build-constraints.txt` + matching `PIP_CONSTRAINT` env line in `build-release.yml` — was specifically for source-built pywhispercpp wheels on the Intel runner. v0.4.0 dropped Intel.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m unittest discover tests` — 75 tests pass (71 existing + 4 new Bedrock URL)
- [x] `npm run typecheck:renderer` clean
- [x] **Manual:** Application inference profile ARN in Settings → Bedrock → Test connection → succeeded against real AWS account (was: HTTP 400)
- [x] **Manual:** Declined Google Calendar event → no longer appears in carousel (was: still visible, including for organizer-then-declined events)
- [x] **Manual:** 4+ meetings today → `<` `>` chevrons in Upcoming header, page through 3-at-a-time
- [x] **Manual:** Expand all-day events → render as full cards with "All day" / "Today" labels
- [x] **Manual:** Add an event externally → appears in the carousel within ~2 min (or sooner on window focus)
