author: sunapi386
body:
## Summary

Users want to deploy common developer tools on their Citadel nodes. This PR adds a modular app catalog that uses Docker containers under the hood, giving users one-command access to:

- **code-server** -- VS Code in the browser (linuxserver/code-server)
- **jupyter** -- Jupyter Notebook for Python development (jupyter/minimal-notebook)  
- **filebrowser** -- web-based file manager (filebrowser/filebrowser)
- **ollama-webui** -- Open WebUI for local LLM chat (ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui)

### New CLI commands

```
citadel app list                    # Show available apps with status
citadel app install <name>          # Deploy an app
citadel app status                  # Show running apps and their ports
citadel app start <name>            # Start a previously stopped app
citadel app stop <name>             # Stop a running app
citadel app uninstall <name>        # Remove app, container, and data
citadel app uninstall <name> --keep-data  # Remove app but preserve data
```

### Architecture

- **`internal/apps/catalog.go`** -- `AppManifest` struct and built-in catalog (4 apps with image, ports, volumes, env, health check)
- **`internal/apps/state.go`** -- `State` struct persisted to `~/.citadel/apps/state.json` tracking installed apps, container IDs, and port assignments
- **`internal/apps/docker.go`** -- Docker integration via `CommandRunner` interface (abstracts `docker run/stop/start/rm/inspect` for testability)
- **`cmd/app.go`** -- Cobra command tree (`app list|install|status|start|stop|uninstall`)
- **`internal/status/types.go`** -- New `AppInfo` type and `Apps` field on `NodeStatus` for heartbeat reporting
- **`internal/status/collector.go`** -- `collectAppStatus()` queries installed apps' Docker container status

### Key design decisions

- **`docker run` over Docker Compose** -- simpler, no compose file management; each app is a single container
- **Port auto-allocation (8100-8199)** -- avoids conflicts between apps; ports are tracked in state.json
- **`CommandRunner` interface** -- all Docker CLI calls go through an interface so tests use a mock runner (no Docker required in CI)
- **Heartbeat integration** -- installed apps automatically appear in the `apps` field of the NodeStatus payload so the platform can show them on the Fabric page

## Test plan

| Area | Tests | Coverage |
|------|-------|----------|
| Catalog lookup | 5 apps (4 found + 1 not-found), field validation, sorted list | `catalog_test.go` |
| State management | Round-trip save/load, remove, installed names, port allocation, exhaustion | `state_test.go` |
| Docker commands | Install, stop, start, uninstall, container status, error cases, mock runner | `docker_test.go` |
| Full suite | `go test ./...` passes (all existing + new tests) | All packages |
| Build verification | `go build -o /tmp/citadel ./cmd/citadel/` compiles cleanly | Binary |
| Manual verification needed | `citadel app list` and `citadel app install code-server` on a machine with Docker | User |

> **Note:** The `jupyter/minimal-notebook` image boots with a login token. Users need to check `docker logs citadel-app-jupyter` to get the token URL. This is standard Jupyter behavior and not something we should suppress.

## Related

- Closes #3473

author: krishnanprash
body:
## Overview

Drives the Mistral parser-parity row on the M2 dashboard to zero unclassified divergences. Mistral tool calls are `[TOOL_CALLS][ ...json... ][/TOOL_CALLS]`, where the closing marker is optional. Three divergences are real Dynamo bugs fixed here in code (Mistral-only, no other family touched); the rest are cases where Dynamo is already correct and a peer engine differs, now recorded with a `reason:`. Each case below shows the raw model output and the per-engine result.

## Code fixes

### streaming close-marker leak

`stream.1.b` - complete call streamed, `[/TOOL_CALLS]` in its own chunk
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="[/TOOL_CALLS]"
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text=""
vllm:          calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="[/TOOL_CALLS]"
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""
```

`stream.2` - multi-call streamed character-by-character
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}, {"name": "get_time", "arguments": {"timezone": "EST"}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=NYC), get_time(timezone=EST)]  text="[/TOOL_CALLS]"
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=NYC), get_time(timezone=EST)]  text=""
vllm:          calls=[]  text="[TOOL_CAL"
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""
```

`stream.3` - single call streamed character-by-character
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="[/TOOL_CALLS]"
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text=""
vllm:          calls=[]  text="[TOOL_CALL"
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""
```

### keep the boundary space before the marker

`batch.2.c`
```
model output: Both: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}, {"name": "get_time", "arguments": {"timezone": "EST"}}][/TOOL_CALLS] Done.
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=NYC), get_time(timezone=EST)]  text="Both:"
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=NYC), get_time(timezone=EST)]  text="Both: "
vllm:          calls=[get_weather(location=NYC), get_time(timezone=EST)]  text="Both: "
sglang:        calls=[]  text="Both:"
```

`batch.8.a` (and `8.c`, sandwich)
```
model output: I will check the weather. [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="I will check the weather."
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="I will check the weather. "
vllm:          calls=[get_weather(location=NYC)]  text="I will check the weather. "
sglang:        calls=[]  text="I will check the weather."
```

`batch.8.d` - two back-to-back envelopes
```
model output: I will check the weather. [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}][/TOOL_CALLS] Then check LA weather. [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "LA"}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[]  text="I will check the weather."
after dynamo:  calls=[]  text="I will check the weather. "
vllm:          error: ValueError: Only one BOT token should have been outputted
sglang:        calls=[]  text="I will check the weather."
```

### incomplete or unterminated call suppression

Consistent handling of an unterminated `[TOOL_CALLS]` (opener present, no `[/TOOL_CALLS]` close) whose JSON did not parse cleanly: recover only the complete leading calls (no brace-balancing fabrication) and suppress the truncated tail rather than leaking raw markup. Matches hermes incomplete-call handling.

`batch.5.e` - multi-call, trailing call truncated mid-value
```
model output: I'll start by fetching the weather for both Boston and New York at the same time![TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Boston"}}, {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "New York
before dynamo: calls=[get_weather(location=Boston), get_weather(location=New York)]  text="I'll start ... at the same time!"
after dynamo:  calls=[get_weather(location=Boston)]  text="I'll start ... at the same time!"
vllm:          calls=[]  text="[{...Boston...}, {...New York"  reason=vLLM leaves the raw truncated body; Dynamo keeps the complete leading call and drops the truncated tail without fabricating it
sglang:        calls=[]  text="I'll start ... at the same time!"  reason=SGLang emits no call and keeps narration; Dynamo keeps the complete leading call
```

`batch.5.c` - single call truncated mid-arguments (no close marker)
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"loc
before dynamo: calls=[]  text='[TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"loc'
after dynamo:  calls=[]  text=''
vllm:          calls=[]  text='[{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"loc'  reason=vLLM leaves the truncated body in content; Dynamo suppresses the unterminated call
sglang:        calls=[]  text=''
```

`stream.4.b` - stream ends mid-arguments (finish_reason=stop)
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"loc
before dynamo: calls=[]  text='[TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"loc'
after dynamo:  calls=[]  text=''
vllm:          calls=[get_weather(arguments='{"loc')]  text=""  reason=vLLM emits a malformed partial call; Dynamo suppresses the unterminated call
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""
```

## Documented divergences (no Dynamo change)

SGLang format mismatch - `batch.2.a, 2.d, 4.d, 6.a, 6.b, 7.a-7.e, 8.b, 30.b, 30.c, 31.b` (representative `7.a`)
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "book_flight", "arguments": {"destination": "Paris", "passengers": 2, "first_class": true}}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[book_flight(destination=Paris, passengers=2, first_class=true)]  text=""
after dynamo:  calls=[book_flight(destination=Paris, passengers=2, first_class=true)]  text=""
vllm:          calls=[book_flight(destination=Paris, passengers=2, first_class=true)]  text=""
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""  reason=SGLang accepts only the spaced "[TOOL_CALLS] [...]" form, not the bracket-close form Dynamo emits
```

`batch.6.c` - no `arguments` key
```
model output: [TOOL_CALLS][{"name": "get_time"}][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[]  text=""
after dynamo:  calls=[]  text=""
vllm:          calls=[get_time({})]  text=""  reason=vLLM fabricates empty args; Dynamo and SGLang drop the call
sglang:        calls=[]  text=""
```

`stream.4.c` - bare body, no opener, repeated closers (finish_reason=length)
```
model output: [{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "NYC"}}][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS]
before dynamo: calls=[]  text='[{...}][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS]'
after dynamo:  calls=[]  text='[{...}][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS]'
vllm:          calls=[]  text='[{...}][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS][/TOOL_CALLS]'
sglang:        calls=[]  text='[{...}[/TOOL_CALLS[/TOOL_CALLS[/TOOL_CALLS'  reason=SGLang strips the trailing ] from each orphan close marker
```

body:
## Summary
- **New** \`internal/requestid\` middleware: respects an inbound \`X-Request-ID\` or mints a clean 32-char hex via \`id.New()\`, seeds request context, and sets the \`X-Request-ID\` response header. Replaces chi's \`middleware.RequestID\` (which only seeded context, so the id was invisible to clients).
- \`httpresp.Response\` and \`httpresp.ErrorResponse\` gain a \`request_id\` field (omitempty), populated by every helper via \`w.Header().Get()\` — **zero churn** at the ~45 \`httpresp.*\` call sites.
- \`running/handler.go\` threads \`request_id\` through every \`importSession\` outcome log.
- The \`storage_failed\` branch additionally logs the wrapped archiver error (\`err=%v\`) — the original motivating fix.

## Why
A real TCX upload returned \`{"code":"storage_failed"}\` against \`v0.38.2\`, but the matching CloudWatch line read only \`outcome=storage_failed\` — \`AccessDenied\`, \`NoSuchBucket\`, \`PermanentRedirect\`, and network errors all looked identical.

Once this ships, every error response carries a \`request_id\` in the JSON body and on the \`X-Request-ID\` header. An end user (or a frontend toast) can copy the id straight into:

\`\`\`
fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /request_id=<id>/
| sort @timestamp desc
\`\`\`

…against the \`/prog-strength/api\` log group and land on the single matching line — including the wrapped S3 error.

## Test plan
- [x] \`go test ./internal/requestid/ -v\` (3 tests cover header generation, inbound-id propagation, empty-context default)
- [x] \`go test ./internal/httpresp/ -v\` (6 tests cover request_id surfaces in OK, Error, ErrorWithCode, ErrorWithCodeData, omits when absent, ServerError stays generic)
- [x] \`go vet ./...\`, \`go build ./...\`, full \`go test ./...\` green
- [ ] Post-deploy: upload a TCX that fails, copy \`request_id\` from the response, paste into CloudWatch Insights to confirm reverse-search lands on the import line with the wrapped S3 error.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- \`httpresp.ServerError\` still logs only \`op + err\` — extending its format to include \`request_id\` from the ctx it already takes is a small follow-up.
- Frontend can render the id discreetly (small footer / "Show details" / copy button) on error toasts — separate repo PR.

author: romeromarcov
body:
## Síntoma

En el `.exe` (Electron), tras un login exitoso (login/me/empresas/sucursales todos 200) la app rebotaba al login. DevTools mostraba **`GET /api/auth/profile/ → 401`**.

## Causa

`isAuthEndpoint` en `frontend/src/services/api.ts` matcheaba **todo** `/auth/`, y para esos endpoints el cliente **no adjunta** `Authorization: Bearer` (y no dispara refresh+retry). Pero `/auth/profile/`, `/auth/profile/update/` y `/auth/change-password/` son `@permission_classes([IsAuthenticated])` y **necesitan** el Bearer. Sin él → 401 → `hydrateSession` falla → `signalLogout` → recarga → bucle de login.

`/core/usuarios/me/` (que usa el login) funciona porque no es `/auth/` → sí lleva Bearer.

## Fix

Acota `isAuthEndpoint` a los endpoints de intercambio de credenciales:
```ts
return /\/auth\/(login|logout|token)\b/.test(endpoint);
```
Así `profile`/`change-password`/`profile-update` vuelven a llevar Bearer. `api.test.ts` actualizado (nuevo caso: `/auth/profile/` DEBE llevar Bearer).

## Nota

Solo cambia frontend. El `.exe` debe recompilarse para tomar el fix. Afecta también a web en recarga (hydrate vía `/auth/profile/`).

author: keerthiprasad10
body:
## Bug

The "Top opportunities this week" board showed the **same category repeated** — Coffee appeared 3× (France/All-markets/Poland) with identical WHY, IMPACT, and origin breakdown.

## Cause

Opportunities are built one-per-trigger, and triggers are per `(category, market)`. But the supply-side payload (origins, focus partner, competitors, and thus WHY/IMPACT) is **category-level**, so multiple markets of one category render as near-duplicate cards. The committed snapshot has **14 triggers across only 8 categories** (Coffee ×4, Footwear ×3, Tea ×2), and the Overview's `slice(0, 3)` therefore grabbed three Coffee cards.

## Fix

In `buildModel`, collapse opportunities to the **top-scoring market per category** (the list is already sorted by score). The board now shows distinct categories; the "Active opportunities" tile and "All N" link reflect the de-duped count (8) — consistent with the "across tracked categories" label.

## Verification
- typecheck ✅ · build ✅
- Rendered locally: top opportunities are now **Coffee, Drinkware & Tumblers, Knitwear & Apparel** — no repeats.

## Note
This is a view-model fix, so it de-dupes both the committed-fallback render and the live Supabase render. A deeper future option is making the supply-side payload market-specific in the pipeline (so per-market cards would be genuinely distinct), but that's a correlation-layer change; this resolves the visible duplication now.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1697 — the orchestration C++ codegen emitted a tensor's SSA-versioned `const Tensor&` alias at the deep `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) { ... }` indent. A task placed **after** a `pl.manual_scope` that read that tensor referenced the now-out-of-scope alias, so the generated `.cpp` failed to C++-compile:

```
error: '<name>__ssa_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

`compile_for_test` / `--smoke` generate the `.cpp` but do **not** C++-compile it, so this only surfaced on a real orchestration build.

A `pl.manual_scope` is a **scheduling** region, not a storage/value scope: a tensor it touches flows transparently to tasks placed after the block. The fix follows from that principle, and a follow-up commit generalizes the mechanism to remove an inconsistency it exposed.

## Commit 1 — `fix(codegen)`: resolve `manual_scope` cross-scope tensors

Two mechanisms keep every after-scope-readable name in the enclosing scope, both gated on one enclosing-scope-validity predicate:

- **Output remap** — a caller-allocated kernel/submit output that aliases an enclosing-scope source is no longer given its own `const Tensor&` decl; its emit name is remapped to the source (the strategy `tensor.assemble` already used), so every reference resolves to the enclosing name directly. The output is the same physical tensor as its source (in-place write), so a shared name is exact. Phi/loop-carry reassignments are excluded.
- **Allocation hoisting** — a buffer *created inside* the block (`alloc_tensors`) has no scheduling dependency, so its declaration is hoisted to the enclosing scope. This covers a `pl.create_tensor` placed inside the scope.

A tensor created **before or inside** the scope and read after it now resolves to a single enclosing-scope `const Tensor& buf = ...;`, with the after-scope task doing `add_input(buf)` — no per-SSA-version alias.

## Commit 2 — `refactor(codegen)`: unify output aliasing on emit-name remap

Since a kernel/submit output is the same physical tensor as the `Out`/`InOut` arg it writes in place, the `const Tensor& <result> = <source>;` rename is pure redundancy. The remap above now applies to **every** caller-allocated output (not just inside manual scopes), dropping the redundant alias decls everywhere and removing the inside/outside-manual-scope inconsistency.

```cpp
// before                              // after
const Tensor& o1 = ext_ta;            (gone)
const Tensor& o2 = ext_tb;            (gone)
...                                    ...
params_t1.add_input(o1);             params_t1.add_input(ext_ta);
params_t1.add_input(o2);             params_t1.add_input(ext_tb);
```

Exclusions unchanged: phi/loop-carry reassignments keep their `<name> = <src>;` form; runtime-allocated `task_<n>_outs.get_ref(...)` outputs keep their real binding.

## Test plan

- New regression tests (`tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py`): a tensor written inside a `manual_scope` and read after it, with the `pl.create_tensor` placed both **before** and **inside** the scope, each verified with a generated-code C++ scope checker (`_out_of_scope_tensor_refs`) that catches the "was not declared in this scope" class without invoking a real compiler.
- The 3 existing tests that asserted the eliminated alias decls now assert the consumer reads the correct source; the name-hint-collision test gives its two calls distinct `Out` args so element→call attachment stays observable under remap.
- Local (worktree build): `tests/ut/codegen/` and `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` — **1985 passed**; `tests/ut/ir/` + `tests/ut/language/` — **3101 passed / 2 skipped**. clang-tidy clean on the diff.

## Docs

Updated `docs/en/dev/codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md` and the `zh-cn` mirror: rewrote *Alias Generation* → *Output Aliasing (emit-name remap)* and added a *Cross-scope tensors and `manual_scope`* section.

author: naka-gawa
body:
## Summary

`iq -I` without a file argument returned `--interactive requires a file argument`, making `cat config.ini | iq -I` impossible. This PR wires up pipe-via-stdin support for interactive mode and adds the `WithInput` option needed to decouple keyboard input from data input.

**Review target (4 files, +98 / -5 lines):**

| File | Reason |
|---|---|
| `internal/tui/model.go` *(start here)* | Adds `Option` / `WithInput` functional-options pattern; `Run` now accepts `...Option` |
| `cmd/root.go` | Interactive dispatch: stdin-pipe detection, `/dev/tty` redirect, early-error for no-file/no-pipe |
| `internal/tui/model_test.go` | Unit tests for `WithInput` option construction and `Run` wiring |
| `internal/e2e/e2e_test.go` | `iqWithStdin` helper; E2E tests for no-file/no-pipe and pipe+no-tty error paths |

## Why

When INI content arrives via stdin, `os.Stdin` is occupied by data. bubbletea defaults to reading keyboard events from `os.Stdin` too, so the two consumers collide and the TUI never renders. The fix is to open `/dev/tty` for keyboard input and pass it to bubbletea via `tea.WithInput`.

## How

Three distinct cases are now handled in `dispatch()`:

| Invocation | Stdin state | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `iq -I file.ini` | anything | reads file; bubbletea uses default stdin |
| `cat f.ini \| iq -I` | pipe | reads INI from stdin; opens `/dev/tty` for keyboard |
| `iq -I` (no file, no pipe) | char device / TTY | returns clear error with usage hint |

If `/dev/tty` is unavailable (Docker without TTY allocation, some CI environments), a descriptive error is returned rather than hanging.

## Reviewer notes

- **`TestE2E_Interactive_PipedStdin_NoTTY_ReturnsError` skips on TTY-capable machines.** The test self-skips when `/dev/tty` opens successfully to avoid launching and hanging a real TUI session. It is intended to run in CI where `/dev/tty` is absent.
- **`WithInput` nil-guards.** When no option is passed, `progOpts` stays empty and `tea.NewProgram` falls back to its default input — behaviour is identical to before this PR.

## Tests

```
go test -race -count=1 ./...   # 214 passed
```

Closes #65
Closes #66
Closes #67

## Summary

Fixes #4988 — Session file path overflow on Windows caused by duplicated user_id/session_id in filenames, and inter-agent tool calls (`list_agents`, `chat_with_agent`) failing with connection errors in Desktop mode.

## Root Cause

### Issue 1: Session filename duplication
- `build_agent_chat_request()` did not include `user_id` in the cross-agent payload
- `agentscope_runtime` fallback logic set `user_id = session_id` when user_id was missing
- `session.py` then produced filenames like `{session_id}_{session_id}.json`, exceeding Windows MAX_PATH (260 chars)

### Issue 2: Desktop inter-agent connection failure
- Desktop mode uses a random port (`port=0`), persisted via `write_last_api()` to config.json
- Tools resolve the API URL via `read_last_api()` which reads config.json from disk
- If the persisted value is stale or overwritten by migrations/file-lock races, tools fall back to hardcoded port 8088, which doesn't match the actual running port

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py` | Add `"user_id": caller_agent_id` to cross-agent request payload |
| `src/qwenpaw/app/runner/session.py` | Add uid==sid dedup guard + null session_id validation in `_get_save_path()` |
| `src/qwenpaw/config/utils.py` | Add in-process `_runtime_last_api` cache with thread-safety docs and debug logging |


## Testing

- All 34 unit tests pass ✅
- Pre-commit hooks (black/flake8/pylint/mypy) all pass ✅
- Verified in Desktop installer build (v1.1.10):

## Make the Scope editor feel like the old UI

The previous Phase-3 Scope editor was a raw `attr/key/value` row builder — unusable next to the per-source options form (labeled fields + live value picker). This makes the topology Scope **inherit that exact interaction**.

## How

- **core**: `PluginConfigProperty.scope?: { kind: 'include'|'exclude'; key: string }` marks an options field as a topology scope dimension. A marked `array` field is surfaced in the topology Scope editor; each value maps to a `MembershipCriterion {attr:'metadata', key, value}` of that kind.
- **zabbix**: mark `hostGroups` (include) and `groupExclude` (exclude), both keyed to `metadata.hostGroups` (the node carries it since #422). `groupExclude` gains the host-group `optionsSource` so it autocompletes too.
- **web**: the topology Scope renders the scope-marked fields via the **same shared `SchemaForm` + `optionsSource` picker** — so it reads/edits exactly like a source's options ("Host groups" multi-select with live candidates) — and maps the form values to/from the topology scope criteria. The raw row editor is removed.

No per-plugin UI branching — the field list is schema-driven (collected from each topology source's scope-marked schema).

On test6 the topology Scope shows "Host groups" / "Exclude groups" with live autocomplete (like the old per-source form), and selecting groups scopes the whole topology via the criteria the resolver enforces post-merge.

author: givewgun
body:
## Summary

Consolidates GunVest client resilience patterns by extracting retry and concurrency limiting logic into shared `util/resilient.js` helpers (already used by the Ollama provider), and adds request deduplication for the macro snapshot endpoint to reduce load during scheduler sweeps.

## Key Changes

- **Extract resilience helpers**: Moved `createLimiter` and `retryAsync` to `src/util/resilient.js` and switched `retryAsync` to use the `p-retry` library for battle-tested backoff math. Added `maxDelayMs` parameter to cap exponential backoff growth.

- **Add macro snapshot caching**: Implemented `getMacro()` with TTL-based deduplication so concurrent callers within the cache window share a single in-flight request. Failed fetches are evicted immediately to allow retries rather than caching failures. Configurable via `macroTtlMs` (default 60s; ≤0 disables).

- **Increase default timeout**: Raised `DefaultTimeoutMs` from 8s to 15s to accommodate slower upstream news providers during single-threaded scheduler sweeps, with detailed comments explaining the rationale.

- **Centralize config**: Added `createGunvestFromConfig()` helper so all resilience knobs (timeout, retries, concurrency, macro TTL) are tuned via environment variables in one place rather than hardcoded at call sites.

- **Config integration**: Extended `loadConfig()` to expose `gunvest` section with environment overrides (`GUNVEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `GUNVEST_RETRIES`, `GUNVEST_MAX_CONCURRENT`, `GUNVEST_MACRO_TTL_MS`).

- **Update all entrypoints**: Switched agent runners and backtest/reliability/risk scripts to use `createGunvestFromConfig()` for consistent resilience tuning.

## Implementation Details

- `retryAsync` now wraps `p-retry` with a stable signature matching our domain-specific error classification (transient vs. fatal).
- Macro cache uses a simple `{ at, promise }` entry that's evicted on rejection, allowing the next caller to retry.
- Error classification in `attemptFetch` uses `Object.assign` to attach `transient` flag for `retryAsync` to inspect.
- Tests verify deduplication, TTL expiry, failure eviction, and backoff capping.

author: brilliantwasp
body:
## Summary
Cycle-10 pass on main/joybus (51KB, biggest absolute unmatched in B4).

**MakeJoyData** CRC loop: 85.81% -> 86.76% (unit 89.37347% -> 89.38127%).

### What worked
The CRC accumulation loop computed `(crc << 8)` and `(crc >> 8)` on an `unsigned int` masked only at the end. mwcc emitted plain `srwi`/`slwi`. The target uses `extrwi`/`clrlslwi` (16-bit extract/clear-shift) — the `unsigned short` byte idiom. Adding explicit `(uVar5 & 0xFFFF) << 8` and `(uVar5 >> 8) & 0xFF` masks reproduced the target's `clrlslwi`/`extrwi` opcodes exactly. (A literal `unsigned short crc` retype regressed to 79%; the explicit-mask form on the `unsigned int` is what matches.)

### Blockers (confirmed walls, per campaign notes)
- **RestartThread / CreateInit**: `...rodata.0` base-CSE vs target's named `s_dvd_gba_dir@ha/@l` anchor. R3 def-reordering not viable for static-const strings. Plus deep register-window shift (target saves r26-r31, we save r23-r31 / r24-r31).
- **GBARecvSend**: mwcc fuses the `op==0x1c||0x1d||0x1e||0x1f` dispatch into a range check (`subi;cmplwi;ble`) where the target emits 4 separate `cmpwi;beq`; this drives a whole register-window shift (one extra saved reg). OR-reordering does not defeat the fusion. Permuter found 0 candidate mutations.

author: thiagomendonca-eu
body:
## What

Fixes the hardcoded POSIX `/tmp/` path used for the shared-state file, which silently breaks the tool on Windows.

Closes #22

## Problem

```ts
// packages/server/src/services/shared-state-service.ts
static SHARED_STATE_PATH = '/tmp/mcp-pointer-shared-state.json';
```

On Windows, Node resolves `/tmp/...` to `C:\tmp\...` (root of the current drive), which usually doesn't exist. As a result:

1. The extension sends the element and the server receives it (`📨 Received message from browser`).
2. `saveState()` → `fs.writeFile('/tmp/...')` fails with `ENOENT`.
3. The error is swallowed by the `try/catch` (only `logger.error`), so nothing is visible in the production build.
4. `getPointedElement()` → `readState()` → `ENOENT` → returns `null`.

Net effect: the extension reports `✓ Element sent successfully`, but `get-pointed-element` **always** returns `"No element is currently pointed"` on Windows.

## Fix

```ts
import os from 'os';
import path from 'path';

static SHARED_STATE_PATH = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'mcp-pointer-shared-state.json');
```

Cross-platform, and it preserves the cross-instance shared-state behavior — all server instances for the same user resolve to the same temp dir on every OS.

## Testing

- Windows 11, Node 24, Chrome 145, extension/server `0.6.0`, Claude Code.
- **Before:** no state file written; `get-pointed-element` always empty.
- **Confirmed root cause:** manually creating `C:\tmp` works around it (state file appears, tool returns the element).
- **After (this fix):** state file is written to `os.tmpdir()` and `get-pointed-element` returns the pointed element.
- **No change on macOS/Linux:** `os.tmpdir()` resolves to the existing system temp dir (`/tmp` on Linux, `/var/folders/...` on macOS).

Single-file change, no API or behavior change beyond the path resolution.

author: mnot
body:
Fixes #169: in `conditional-etag-precedence`, both `If-None-Match` (matches the stored ETag) and `If-Modified-Since` (≈now, after the stored `Last-Modified`) independently evaluated to 304, so any evaluation order passed `expected_status: 304` and a cache that gave `If-Modified-Since` precedence was not caught.

This moves `If-Modified-Since` to before `Last-Modified` (`-10000` vs the response's `-5000`), so it alone would yield 200 while `If-None-Match` still yields 304. Only a cache that correctly gives `If-None-Match` precedence (RFC 9110 §13.2.2) returns the expected 304.

Closes #169

## What does this PR do?

Adds Gemini TTS performance-control features requested in #41832:

- Adds `tts.gemini.persona_prompt_file`, allowing a local Markdown/text persona or director-notes file to be prepended to Gemini TTS requests without showing that context in chat replies.
- Adds `tts.gemini.audio_tags`, an explicit opt-in for Gemini 3.1 TTS hidden audio-tag insertion.
- Adds an `auxiliary.tts_audio_tags` task so the hidden tag rewrite defaults to the main chat model but can be routed to a cheaper/faster model.
- Gates hidden tag insertion to Gemini 3.1 TTS-shaped model IDs and falls back to untagged TTS if the rewrite fails.
- Sends Telegram auto-TTS output as Ogg/Opus so replies arrive as native Telegram voice notes instead of MP3 audio attachments.
- Documents the new config keys and updates the example config.

Fixes #41832

- `hermes_cli/config.py`: adds defaults for `tts.gemini.persona_prompt_file`, `tts.gemini.audio_tags`, and `auxiliary.tts_audio_tags`.

author: zardus
body:
Adds a new **Endian Escapades** module to Computing 101, teaching little-endian byte order through reverse engineering. Inserted before Assembly Assortment; **no changes to any other module**.

### Structure
Two lectures — *Little-Endian* and *Bytes, Words, and Friends* — then seven RE levels. Each ships a SUID `/challenge/reverse-me` that randomizes a password at container start and bakes it into the code as the little-endian immediates of width-specific compares. The learner disassembles it, endian-corrects the immediates, and runs it to get the flag.

| Level | Teaches |
|-------|---------|
| `endian-qword` | a single qword (introduces `movabs`) |
| `endian-qwords` | two qwords |
| `endian-dword` | four dwords |
| `endian-word` | eight words |
| `endian-byte` | sixteen bytes — the no-reversal contrast |
| `endian-struct` | a mixed-width struct (read width/offset/value per field) |
| `endian-struct-scrambled` | the same struct checked **out of memory order**, so you must track each field's offset, not just read top-to-bottom |

### Mechanism
Shared: each level's `.init` sets a width list and includes `common/reverse-me`; one offset-aware private solver recovers the password from the disassembly regardless of chunk widths or check order.

### Testing
All seven levels pass `pwnshop test` under `nix develop`.

## Summary

  `OpenAIAdapter.stream_chat` and `AnthropicAdapter.stream_chat` only wrapped
  errors from *opening* the stream; an error raised *during* iteration escaped
  uncaught. A provider can open the stream 200 and then inject an SSE error event,
  which the SDK re-raises as a bare `APIError` mid-iteration. That exception
  propagated past `_try_open_stream_native` — which only catches `AdapterError` —
  bypassing the router's failover and surfacing as a 500 instead of a clean
  502/failover. This wraps the iteration loop in both adapters so those errors are
  classified and the router can fail over.

    so it's the failover-critical one). Existing happy-path stream tests unchanged.

author: yimincong
body:
## Problem

On github.com (web and the iOS app) many formulas in the guides rendered as a red error box **"The following macros are not allowed: operatorname"** showing raw LaTeX instead of the formula.

**Cause:** GitHub renders math with KaTeX in a *restricted* mode that **disallows the `\operatorname` macro**. Every formula using `\operatorname{Re}`, `\operatorname{Im}`, `\operatorname{tr}`, `\operatorname{Res}`, `\operatorname{Cov}`, etc. failed. (The files were otherwise well-formed; `$`/`$$` balanced, Chinese already spaced.)

## Fix

Replaced all **1708** occurrences of `\operatorname{...}` (and `\operatorname*{...}`) with the GitHub-allowed `\mathrm{...}` across all **48** guide files (24 guides × English + 简体中文). `\mathrm` renders the same upright-roman operator name and is on GitHub's allowed list, so the formulas now display on github.com web **and** the GitHub iOS app (both use the same KaTeX renderer).

## Verification

- `\operatorname` remaining repo-wide: **0**.
- All 39 EN/ZH guide pairs still match on anchors / `$$` / heading counts; `$$` balance unchanged (pure macro rename inside math).
- No other GitHub-blocked macros (`\def`, `\newcommand`, `\href`, `\includegraphics`, …) are present.

author: abakymuk
body:
## P3 — Observability (DRA-23)

Closes the observability part of DRA-23 (parent DRA-19). Turns the Day-1 silent failure modes into signals that would have caught the incident in minutes. **Gmail Push/Pub-Sub is intentionally NOT in this PR** (needs GCP infra — separate follow-up).

### What
- **`sync_runs` table** — one row per delta `historySync` run: `running → succeeded | held`, with `seen / persisted / failed / capped / cursor_advanced / start+target historyId`. A crash leaves a detectable `running` row. Append-only (one finalize update). Applied via **`pnpm db:push`** (this project's convention — the migrations snapshot is push-managed, so `drizzle-kit generate` is not used).
- **`sync-runs.ts`** — `startSyncRun` / `finishSyncRun`, **best-effort**: journaling never breaks or holds the real sync (all errors swallowed, including the table not existing before `db:push`).
- **`gmail-sync.ts`** — opens the run after reading the cursor, closes it after the cursor decision (records `held` vs advanced + counts).
- **`integrity.ts`** — `runIntegrityChecks()` (the §7 health queries: orphan threads, analyzed-without-event, event-without-message, duplicate `(mailbox,gmail_msg_id)`, `fetched` backlog >3h, stale `running` runs >1h, held/failed runs in 24h, unhealthy batches) + pure `summarizeHealth()`.
- **integrity cron** (`0 */6 * * *`) — **throws on unhealthy** so Inngest records a failed run and fires its failure alert, with the exact problems in the message. No extra alerting service.

### Tests
- `tests/integrity.test.ts` — `summarizeHealth` unit tests (all-zero healthy; any nonzero named; held-cursor signal).
- `pnpm build` + **112 unit tests** green.

### Deploy note
Run **`doppler run --config prd -- pnpm db:push`** to create `sync_runs` before/with deploying this PR. Journaling is best-effort so it won't break sync if the table is missing, but the integrity cron will report a (false) failure until the table exists.

### Out of scope (separate follow-up)
- Gmail Push/Pub-Sub (`users.watch` + Pub/Sub topic + webhook) — removes idle polling; needs GCP IAM/topic setup.

author: keneliteedganalytics
body:
## Summary

Manual Ingest (PR #33, `ManualIngestModal`) successfully created the card server-side and returned the green success toast, but the dashboard never refetched — so the new card never appeared without a manual page reload. The card *was* persisted correctly (confirmed: `GET /api/cards` and `GET /api/cards/4` return it with full tiered race data). This was purely a client-side React Query cache-invalidation bug.

Root cause: `queryClient` is configured with `staleTime: Infinity`. `invalidateQueries`'s default `refetchType: "active"` did not reliably refetch the dashboard's card-list queries under that config, leaving the UI showing stale data.

## Fix

In `ManualIngestModal`'s `onSuccess`:
- Force `refetchType: "all"` on every card/race-list key the dashboard reads — `/api/cards/drafts` (DraftCardsSection), `/api/cards/latest` (active card), `/api/cards`, and `/api/cards/archived`.
- `await Promise.all([...])` so invalidation is fully triggered before the modal flow proceeds (modal close / "Enter Results" navigation).
- Mirrors the existing invalidation convention used by `PullCardModal`, `DraftCardsSection`, and `useLiveEvents`.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run client/src/components/ManualIngestModal.test.tsx` — 2 passed
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] After successful manual ingest, the new draft card appears immediately on the dashboard with no page reload (renders via DraftCardsSection from the now-refetched `/api/cards/drafts`).
- [x] Tight diff, no layout/look changes.

body:
PR Summary by Qodo

Implement RAG upload + chat API with Supabase vectors, Cohere embeddings, and Groq ✨ Enhancement ⚙️ Configuration changes 📝 Documentation 🕐 40+ Minutes

Walkthroughs

User Description
…ckend integration for PDF and text processing
AI Description 
• Add /api/upload to parse PDFs/text, chunk content, embed via Cohere, and index Supabase.
• Add /api/chat RAG endpoint: embed query, retrieve context via Supabase RPC, answer with Groq.
• Route frontend calls through internal APIs and refresh landing/upload UI styling.
Diagram
```mermaid graph TD UUI(["Upload UI"]) --> AUP[["/api/upload"]] --> DP["PDF/text processing"] --> COH{{"Cohere Embed"}} --> SB[("Supabase pgvector")] CUI(["Chat UI"]) --> ACH[["/api/chat"]] --> COH --> SB ACH --> GRQ{{"Groq Chat"}} subgraph Legend direction LR _ui(["UI Page"]) ~~~ _api[["API Route"]] ~~~ _proc["Processor"] ~~~ _ext{{"External API"}} ~~~ _db[("Database")] end ```
High-Level Assessment
The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Use Supabase Edge Functions for upload/chat APIs - ➕ Keeps server-side logic closer to Supabase and can simplify secret management - ➕ Potentially lower latency to Supabase for vector retrieval - ➖ PDF parsing via pdf-parse may be difficult or impossible on Edge runtimes - ➖ Operational complexity if mixing Edge + Node runtimes across endpoints
2. Keep n8n webhooks as the sole backend (as in existing prompt doc) - ➕ Reduces custom backend code in the Next.js app - ➕ Centralizes orchestration and retries in n8n - ➖ Extra network hop and more moving parts for core UX flows - ➖ Harder to version and test alongside the frontend compared to in-repo routes
3. Use Supabase client with RLS + per-user auth instead of service role - ➕ Improves security posture by avoiding service role access in application code - ➕ Enables per-user document isolation with database-enforced policies - ➖ Requires auth flows and schema/policy work (more product scope) - ➖ May complicate server-side ingestion if embeddings storage must bypass RLS
**Recommendation:** The current Node.js route approach is a pragmatic fit given PDF parsing requirements and the need to keep secrets server-side. However, reviewers should explicitly validate (1) service-role usage is only on the server and never exposed to clients, (2) Node runtime requirements (pdf-parse and Supabase packages indicate Node >=20.16+) match deployment, and (3) documentation alignment—doqify-prompt.md currently states “no backend routes needed,” which conflicts with this implementation.

author: aieradev
body:
Replaced the Contents API with the low-level Git Data API for audio file uploads. This bypasses the Contents API's practical ~1MB limit and supports files up to GitHub's 100MB hard limit.

Changes:
- Added uploadLargeFile() function using the 6-step blob upload flow:
  1. Get current branch HEAD SHA
  2. Get tree SHA from commit
  3. Create blob with base64 content
  4. Create new tree including the blob
  5. Create commit pointing to new tree
  6. Update branch ref to new commit

- Updated publishAudio() to use uploadLargeFile() for audio files
- Updated size validation from 1MB to 100MB
- Kept putFile() for small files (JSON metadata, thumbnails)

This allows publishing audio samples and clips up to 100MB, which is sufficient for typical studio use cases. For files larger than 100MB, Git LFS would be required (not implemented).

Technical notes:
- Base64 encoding inflates file size by ~33%
- Git blob API is the correct path for programmatic binary uploads
- JSON files continue using simpler Contents API

author: eric-song-nop
body:
## Summary

- Detect when a local Markdown file changed externally before workspace saves write back to disk.
- Use the same source-file conflict path for ordinary editor saves and owner-hosted shared saves.
- Handle Dropbox/local write-conflict errors by pausing autosave and showing one two-choice conflict dialog: reload the file or keep the pending edits.
- Move Markdown hashing into a shared local-md-workspace helper and add focused conflict helper tests.

## Why

The workspace previously had separate conflict behavior for normal local edits and shared owner materialization. Shared conflicts could create `*.shared-conflict-*.md` copies, while ordinary local conflicts used the simpler reload-or-overwrite flow. Both cases are the same three-value problem: the last materialized file hash, the current source file, and the pending editor/shared text.

## Impact

When the selected source file has diverged, autosave stays in an error/conflict state until the user chooses whether to reload the current source file or overwrite it with pending edits. In shared mode, reload also resets the CRDT document to the source file and use-shared writes through the owner backend before sending the saved-to-host ack. This intentionally does not create `*.local-conflict-*` or `*.shared-conflict-*` copies.

## Validation

- `vp install`
- `vp check --fix` from `apps/local-md-workspace`
- `vp check`
- `vp test src/lib/workspace-file-conflict.test.ts src/lib/collaboration/markdown-document.test.ts` from `apps/local-md-workspace`
- `node --check apps/local-md-workspace/smoke/ui-smoke.mjs`
- `vp run @codemirror-treesitter/opendal-wasm-browser#build:wasm`
- `vp run local-md-workspace#build`
- `git diff --check`

## Known Existing Failures

- Full `vp test` still fails outside this change in `share-storage.test.ts` because localStorage is unavailable, `apps/collab-editor/src/share.test.ts` on rotated-link lifetime behavior, and `packages/language-data/tests/language-data.test.ts` on Markdown strikethrough delimiter ancestry.
- `local-md-workspace#smoke:ui` previously reached the mock Dropbox empty-folder flow, then failed because the current UI says `0 markdown files` while the smoke test waits for `No markdown files` or related text.

- `staff_performance` — por mesero: ventas, mesas, propinas, ticket
- `staffing_estimate` — meseros sugeridos por franja según volumen
- `kitchen_bottlenecks` — prep real vs target por estación/hora (% sobre target)

- `top_searches` — términos más buscados + % sin resultados

author: nagajyothi-tammisetti
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #1401

## Summary

This pull request resolves an issue where the Search page generated redundant API requests when filters were repeatedly cleared and reapplied. The existing implementation allowed multiple identical requests to be triggered for the same filter state, resulting in unnecessary network traffic, increased backend load, and a less efficient user experience.

The fix improves the search request lifecycle by ensuring that API calls are only triggered when a meaningful filter state change occurs. Additional safeguards have been implemented to prevent duplicate requests, reduce unnecessary re-renders, and improve overall search performance.

## Changes Made

### Eliminated Duplicate Requests

Added logic to prevent multiple API calls from being triggered for identical filter states. The application now compares filter values before initiating a new request.

### Optimized Effect Dependencies

Reviewed and refined search-related effect dependencies to ensure requests are triggered only when required. This prevents redundant executions caused by unnecessary state updates.

### Improved Request Management

Added protection against rapid filter changes by introducing request control mechanisms such as debouncing and cleanup handling where appropriate.

### Added Cleanup Logic

Implemented cleanup behavior for pending requests to prevent outdated responses from affecting the current search results.

### Preserved Existing Search Functionality

The search experience remains unchanged from a user perspective. Filters, sorting, and result updates continue to function normally while avoiding redundant network activity.

## Testing

* Applied multiple search filters.
* Cleared filters repeatedly.
* Reapplied filters several times.
* Monitored browser Network tab activity.
* Verified only one request is sent per valid filter state change.
* Confirmed search results update correctly.
* Tested rapid interactions to ensure duplicate requests do not occur.
* Verified no regressions in existing filter functionality.
* Confirmed application builds and runs successfully.

## Result

The Search page now performs API requests more efficiently by eliminating duplicate calls for identical filter states. This reduces unnecessary backend load, improves responsiveness, and provides a smoother search experience while maintaining existing functionality.

body: ## Pull Request Description This PR introduces an isolated structural rendering fix for a Sticky Table Header Border Collapse Disappearance Bug placed strictly inside the submissions/examples/sticky-table-fix/ sandbox directory. It addresses a long-standing browser rendering layout defect in Chromium (Blink) and Firefox (Gecko) engines where applying sticky constraints to elements inside a collapsed table grid causes bottom row boundaries to separate, vanish, or fail to follow the header cell during vertical scroll movements. author: kaisermoon
body:
## 动机

1. **rpy2 桥接物理不可行**：conda R 4.4.3 环境下 `R_getVar` 符号缺失（pip rpy2 链接了已删除的 R framework 库路径），无法通过重装解决。系统 R 4.2.3 同样缺失。
2. **PI 决策 B**：SoupX 放弃 rpy2，改走 subprocess Rscript 模式，与 DESeq2/Monocle3/hdWGCNA 等重型 R 工具统一——工艺隔离更稳，R 脚本可独立调试。
3. **ADR-0009 合规**：stage2 笔记本中大量英文代码注释改为中文并讲 why（QC 阈值为什么这么设、scrublet/SoupX 各干什么）。

## 改动

- **新增 `scripts/soupx_run.R`**：独立 SoupX R 脚本。支持 autoEstCont 三级渐进式回退（默认参数→降低 tfidfMin/soupQuantile→forceAccept），在极端稀疏数据上优雅降级而非崩溃。
- **重写 `stage2_qcd.ipynb` SoupX cell**：从 rpy2 `%%R` in-notebook 改为 subprocess Rscript 模式。工作流：Python 侧导出过滤后矩阵（10x mtx）→ subprocess 调 Rscript → 读回校正矩阵。三重守卫（raw_path 存在→Rscript 可用→SoupX R 包可加载）保持优雅跳过行为。
- **新增 RSCRIPT_BIN PARAMS**：在 stage2 PARAMS cell 声明 Rscript 绝对路径，作为全项目 R 工具路径约定的样板。
- **stage2 注释中文化**：全部 22 个 cell 的代码注释改为中文，面向非 CS 学生，解释每个步骤的 why（QC 阈值含义、scrublet 跳过逻辑、SoupX 工作原理、内存纪律等）。
- **ADR-0007 修订**：SoupX 从 rpy2 改判为 subprocess Rscript，2026-06-09 修订历史标注。rpy2 路径完全废弃（仅 `read_with_manifest` 读 RDS 格式保留内部 rpy2 调用）。
- **SPEC.md 同步**：R Bridge 章节改为统一 subprocess 策略，SoupX 示例改为 subprocess 模式，stage2 cell 序列规格同步更新，stage7 描述修正。

## 测试

- **SoupX R 脚本独立测试**：用 Nancang 夹具真实样本（GSM7966226，207 cells）验证端到端流程——矩阵读入、barcode 匹配、快速聚类、autoEstCont 三级回退、输出写入。autoEstCont 在 207 细胞极稀疏子集上触发优雅降级（预期行为），流程完整输出 corrected_counts.mtx。
- **Notebook JSON 有效性**：nbformat 验证通过，22 个 cell 结构完整，PARAMS→加载→QC→SoupX→过滤→可视化→记录→写入→释放的 cell 序列正确。
- **Pre-commit hooks**：全部通过（large files / merge conflicts / EOF / trailing whitespace / secret scan / protected branch）。
- **未完成**：因无 stage1 中间产物且项目规则禁止单 turn 跑端到端 pipeline，完整 `nbconvert --execute` 留待 PI 在 jupyter 手动验证或 CI 执行。

## 风险

- **BREAKING-CHANGE: stage2 notebook 不再依赖 rpy2**，改用 subprocess + RSCRIPT_BIN。已安装 `scrna-integration-r` conda 环境的用户无需额外操作；未安装 R 环境的用户需 `conda env create -f environment-r.yml`（SoupX cell 会优雅跳过）。
- SoupX subprocess 流程在数据极稀疏时 autoEstCont 可能降级为不校正（返回原始计数），`ambient_correction_applied` 仍正确标记为 True/False。下游分析读取此列即可。
- SPEC.md 中 rpy2 相关描述已清理，`read_with_manifest` 的 RDS 读取仍保留内部 rpy2 调用（不受影响）。
- 无新增 Python/R 依赖，无付费服务调用。

author: somnerd
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
Hardcoded weak default passwords (`searchboost_pass`) were defined in several configuration files (`configs/redis.json`, `configs/db.json`, `configs/warden.ini`, `configs/service_settings.json`), and used as fallback defaults in Pydantic models and Docker Compose files.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
Any unauthorized entity with read access to the repository or config files would be able to discover the default credentials, which could lead to unauthorized database or Redis access, compromising system security and data integrity.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
- Removed hardcoded default passwords from all `.json` and `.ini` config files.
- Updated Pydantic defaults in `searchboost_service/searchboost_src/configurator.py` to be `Optional[str] = Field(default=None)` instead of hardcoded strings.
- Refactored `docker-compose.yml` to rely entirely on environment variables (e.g. `${REDIS_PASSWORD}`) without providing fallback strings.
- Added conditionals in the `docker-compose.yml` `redis` entrypoint to only use `--requirepass` if a password variable is supplied, preventing startup failures when a password is not needed in dev, while forcing Postgres configuration to explicitly fail when variables are omitted.
- Updated `warden.ini` environment variable mapping in `docker-compose.yml` to inject the Redis password.

author: colekelley777-del
body:
## Summary

Two real fixes plus performance polish on top of #2 (the motion-enhancements PR that landed just before this one):

- **HTML comment was broken** — the head comment block contained `<!-- SECTION: NAME -->` inside an outer HTML comment, which is illegal per spec. Chromium parsed the inner `-->` as the close, all of the head turned into text, the body collapsed to 50px tall, no IntersectionObserver ever fired, and the new stats counters were stuck at 0. Caught by driving the page with Playwright. Rephrased the comment to avoid `--` sequences.
- **Hero video is 5.5MB** — now injected by JS only when the connection is healthy and the user is on desktop. Phones, slow-2g/2g/3g, and Save-Data visitors get a layered radial vignette + pattern fallback that still feels deliberate (the breathing gold glow + the mark + the chevron carry it).
- **Render-blocking Google Fonts** — switched to `rel="preload" as="style"` + `onload` swap pattern with a `<noscript>` fallback.
- **LCP nudges** — `<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">` on `mark.png`, explicit `width`/`height` to prevent reflow, shortened the `markIn` entrance from 1.1s -> 700ms so the LCP image hits full opacity inside Lighthouse's measurement window.

### Numbers (mobile = simulated slow 4G + 4x CPU slowdown — pessimistic vs real iOS)

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile performance | 69 | 75 |
| Desktop performance | 98 (unchanged) | 98 |
| Mobile total bytes | 6,382 KiB | 735 KiB |
| Mobile TBT | 280 ms | 0 ms |
| Mobile Speed Index | 8.7 s | 3.1 s |
| CLS | 0.005 | 0.005 |
| Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO | 96 / 100 / 100 | 94 / 100 / 100 |

The mobile LCP (5.6s simulated) is now network-bound on the slowest realistic profile — the page is genuinely light, but Lighthouse mobile penalizes any image-LCP hero on 1.6Mbit. Getting to 90+ mobile would mean replacing `mark.png` with inline SVG and we'd lose the custom brand mark. Recommend leaving the brand intact.

## Test plan

- [x] Counters animate to real DB values (4,496 / 8,810 / 784 / 17,127) — verified via Playwright `textContent` assertion
- [x] Reduced-motion path: counters jump straight to final, no parallax, no errors
- [x] No JS console errors at any viewport size
- [x] Mobile hero fallback (no video) looks deliberate, not empty
- [x] Desktop video still autoplays and parallax still tracks scroll
- [x] CLS 0.005 (no layout shift from video swap-in)
- [ ] Cole eyeballs it in Safari (iOS + macOS) before merge — that's the bar I can't simulate

## Notes for Cole

author: olemarkus
body:
## What

Collapses `deviceActionProjection.ts`'s two stepped-load checks onto a single profile-only predicate `hasSteppedLoadProfile`, and removes the lone `controlModel`-AND form.

## Why

`isSteppedLoad` gated the EV and temperature boost resolvers on `controlModel === 'stepped_load' && steppedLoadProfile?.model === 'stepped_load'`, while **every other site** keys on the profile alone — the planner (`planSteppedLoad`, `planCurrentState`, `planTypes`), the observer (`observedState`), and even the sibling `isSteppedLoadDeviceShape` in the same file. `controlModel` is a producer-only setting, not part of the discriminant.

The two forms are equivalent **only** because the producer (`decorateSnapshotWithDeviceControl`) sets `controlModel: 'stepped_load'` and `steppedLoadProfile` atomically. That coupling is a latent drift seam: a future producer path attaching a profile without the controlModel would make the boost resolvers and the planner disagree on "is this stepped?". Flagged during release review of `v2.11.4..main` (P2).

## Scope

No behavior change for producer-decorated devices — proven: the producer sets the two atomically, so `controlModel==='stepped_load' ⟺ valid steppedLoadProfile`.

## Validation

- New regression test: a device with a valid `steppedLoadProfile` but no resolved `controlModel` is still treated as stepped. **Verified it fails under the old AND form and passes with the fix.**
- `planEvBoost`, `planTemperatureBoost`, `deviceActionProjectionShedIntent` unit suites + `planActionMaterialization`, `planDevices`, `planShedding` integration suites all green.
- `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean; runtime `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: lupinesse
body:
Closes — two targeted fixes for the 'No meetings today' regression.

## Fix A — `?debug=1` diagnostic endpoint

`/api/calendar?debug=1` now returns a JSON object with both the meetings array and a `_debug` field:

```json
{
  "meetings": [...],
  "_debug": {
    "storeCount": 2,
    "storesSkipped": 0,
    "folderCount": 2,
    "pass1Count": 0,
    "pass2Count": 0
  }
}
```

Visit that URL in the browser while the server is running to see exactly how many stores and calendar folders Outlook reported, and how many meetings each pass found. Zero `folderCount` means the calendar folder walk failed; non-zero `folderCount` with zero pass counts means the date filter matched nothing.

The normal API response (no `?debug=1`) is unchanged — still a plain JSON array — so the JS client requires no update.

## Fix B — `Add-ComRef` double-release guard

`Add-ComRef` now checks `List.Contains()` before tracking a COM object. If Outlook returns the same RCW pointer for consecutive `FindNext()` calls (possible when the COM cache coalesces references), the previous code would track and `ReleaseComObject()` it twice — decrementing the COM ref count below zero and invalidating the object while the loop is still using it. The exception would be silently swallowed by the surrounding `catch {}`, producing an empty result with no error surfaced to the client.

body:
Bundles three changes that landed in one focused session.

## 1. Critical ATS scoring trust fix
Users were seeing different scores when re-uploading the same resume + JD.
Root cause: OpenAI calls used default temperature=1.0 (non-deterministic),
AND the "projected score after tailoring" was fabricated by the rewrite
prompt instead of computed by the actual scoring function.

Backend changes:
- All 5 OpenAI calls now use temperature=0 (deterministic)
- /analyze-jd: fixed missing return statement (was returning None)
- /generate-tailored-resume rewritten as chained pipeline:
  1. Score the original first → get critical gaps + recruiter concerns
  2. Pass those gaps into tailoring prompt for targeted improvement
  3. Re-score the tailored result with the SAME scoring function
  4. Safety net: if tailored < original, return original with explanation
  
Result: same resume + same JD = same score, every time. Tailored score 
is REAL, not LLM marketing.

## 2. Skill confirmation modal
New /detect-missing-skills endpoint lists JD tools missing from the resume.
After clicking Tailor, user sees a modal asking "have you used these?" 
with Yes/No for each. Only confirmed skills get added to the tailored 
resume. This raises scores legitimately by surfacing real skills the 
candidate forgot to list, while never inventing experience.

## 3. Settings page + Manage subscription
New /app/settings page with Stripe Customer Portal integration. Users
can update payment method, view invoices, cancel anytime. Sidebar updated
to surface Settings as a top-level nav item.

## Testing
- Backend: /detect-missing-skills verified working via curl
- Frontend: end-to-end flow tested locally (upload → analyze → tailor 
  → modal → confirm → tailored result)

author: pannpers
body:
## Summary

Collapses the 6-state onboarding step machine into a single `isOnboarding` boolean and fixes #444 at the root. Implements OpenSpec change `simplify-onboarding-to-single-flag`.

### Why
The ordered step machine (`LP→DISCOVERY→DASHBOARD→MY_ARTISTS→CONSENT→COMPLETED`) only enforced forced navigation ordering the product no longer needs. Repurposing a hype change as the `MY_ARTISTS→CONSENT` trigger caused **#444** (the 2nd hype tap reverts), and pure guests got stranded at `CONSENT` so onboarding never completed.

### What changed
- **Single-flag state**: `OnboardingService` is now one `@observable onboardingComplete` with `isOnboarding`/`isCompleted` getters and a one-way idempotent `finish()`. Step enum, `STEP_ORDER`, route map, `readyForDashboard`, and the discovery-count mirror are deleted.
- **#444 fix**: `onHypeInput` no longer branches on onboarding or reverts — every tap applies and persists.
- **Soft gate**: `AuthHook` drops onboarding ordinal gating (auth-only now); the dashboard is always reachable, with an empty-state CTA for zero-follow guests instead of a redirect.
- **CoachMarkService**: coach mark extracted from `OnboardingService` into a dedicated, non-blocking service triggered by live follow/concert counts.
- **Completion latch (B1∧B2)**: `finish()` fires on the first *meaningful* dashboard arrival (region set + data loaded + `followedCount >= 1`, independent of whether the celebration renders) and on sign-up. Legacy `onboardingStep` localStorage is migrated once.

### Out of scope
The analytics consent screen is **not** shown — only the `CONSENT` onboarding step is removed. Consent application logic (fail-closed PostHog default, settings opt-out) is untouched; independent of the in-flight `introduce-analytics-tool` change.

### Testing
`make check` green — 1247 tests pass (incl. #444 regression, migration, latch timing/engagement-gate, reactivity, soft-gate guard, coach-mark trigger). New rendered UI (empty-state CTA + non-blocking coach mark) means **visual baselines will regenerate**.

Closes #444

body:
## Summary

oras-go v2.6.0 had a bug where `credentials.ServerAddressFromRegistry("registry-1.docker.io")` returned `"registry-1.docker.io"` instead of the canonical `"https://index.docker.io/v1/"`.


## Root cause

oras-go v2.6.0 had a bug where `credentials.ServerAddressFromRegistry("registry-1.docker.io")` returned `"registry-1.docker.io"` instead of the canonical `"https://index.docker.io/v1/"`. To work around this, `pkg/registry/client.Login()` added a second normalization call: `key = credentials.ServerAddressFromHostname(key)`. oras-go v2.6.1 (PR #966) fixed `ServerAddressFromRegistry` to return the correct key for all Docker Hub host variants, making the Helm workaround redundant.

Separately, the test expected values for the provenance layer digest and size were stale (695 bytes / old digest). The actual test data file `signtest-0.1.0.tgz.prov` is 715 bytes. This mismatch was hidden by a different oras-go v2.6.0 regression (CopyError on FetchReference) that is also fixed in v2.6.1.


## What changed

author: carlolucibello
body:
Closes #218.

cuDNN exposes two average-pooling modes (`cudnnPoolingMode_t`): one that includes padding zeros in the averaging denominator (`CUDNN_POOLING_AVERAGE_COUNT_INCLUDE_PADDING`) and one that excludes them (`..._EXCLUDE_PADDING`). NNlib's `meanpool` only implemented the include-padding mode.

This PR adds a `count_include_pad` keyword to `meanpool`:

- **`true` (default)** — padding elements are counted, dividing each output by the full window size `prod(k)`. This is the existing behavior, so the change is **non-breaking**.
- **`false`** — only the in-bounds (non-padding) elements are counted, matching cuDNN's exclude-padding mode and PyTorch's `count_include_pad=false`. Has no effect when `pad == 0`.

### Implementation
- **CPU** ([`meanpool_direct!`](src/impl/pooling_direct.jl) and `∇meanpool_direct!`): handled per-window in the padded regions only. The central region (windows that never touch padding) is unchanged, so the hot path has no overhead. An empty-window guard returns `0` rather than `NaN`.
- **CUDA** ([NNlibCUDACUDNNExt](ext/NNlibCUDACUDNNExt/pooling.jl)): selects the cuDNN pooling mode from the keyword (including the 1D→2D reshape path).
- Only `meanpool` is affected — `maxpool` already ignores padding and `lpnormpool` has no averaging denominator (matches cuDNN/PyTorch).

### Testing
- **CPU**: forward checked against a hand-computed example and a brute-force reference across spatial ranks 1–3 / `Float32`+`Float64`; gradients checked via `gradtest`. Full `pooling.jl` suite passes (1087 pass, 4 pre-existing broken).
- **GPU**: CPU-vs-cuDNN agreement for both modes (forward + backward), run on a local TITAN RTX — `ext_cuda/pooling.jl` 36 pass. CPU and cuDNN match to ~1e-16 and the two modes genuinely differ.

body: Implements #1822 (Phase 1): a "go deeper" pointer from each StaffML question back into the textbook, tied to the question's **topic** (not its answer), derived once per topic and inherited by all ~10.7k questions. Builds on the draft `topic_chapter_map.yaml` + design analysis from ed68fda. ## What changed **vault-cli (build join + link-checker)** - New `BookRefResolver` joins `topic → chapter` via `schema/topic_chapter_map.yaml`, reads each chapter's display title from its `.qmd` H1, and **link-checks every mapped chapter at build time** — a mapped chapter with no `.qmd` source fails the build. This turns the original "defer until mlsysbook.ai URLs stabilize" blocker into "URLs are enforced valid." - `book_refs` is emitted as a top-level field so it rides into the summary bundle and renders **synchronously** (no worker fetch). - Regenerated `corpus-summary.json`: **all 9,525 published questions now carry `book_refs`** (100% of the 87 topics mapped, 0 orphaned). **staffml (UI)** - New `BookRefCard` renders a "Learn more in the textbook" card **after the attempt** — primary chapter with a Volume badge + an authored *why* line, plus 0–2 "also see" chapters. - Supersedes the older area-level `ChapterLinks`; retires `chapter-map.json` / `chapters.ts`. ## Fixes a live 404 bug `ChapterLinks` was already shipping per-question links (keyed on `competency_area`), but its URLs **404'd**: | URL | Result | |---|---| | `…/contents/vol1/nn_architectures/` (old `ChapterLinks`) | **404** | | `…/vol1/contents/vol1/nn_architectures/nn_architectures.html` (new `book_refs`) | **200** | The new links are topic-granular (87 vs 13), carry a *why* line, and are build-link-checked against the verified-200 pattern. ## Pedagogy The card is a recommended-reading pointer tied to the topic, **not an answer key** — it renders after the solution is revealed, so it's a consolidation/go-deeper step rather than a shortcut around the reasoning. ## Tests - `test_book_refs.py` — resolver resolution, primary/also_see ordering, `.qmd` title extraction, **link-check fails on missing chapter**, standalone slug fallback, and `book_refs` survives into the summary bundle. - Full suites green: vault-cli `96 passed` (1 pre-existing `codegen --check` baseline failure, unrelated — confirmed failing on a clean tree); staffml `tsc --noEmit` clean + vitest `93 passed`. ## Follow-ups (Phase 2/3, not in this PR) Prerequisite-on-wrong-answer remediation; per-question `details.resources` overrides + `kind` enum; bidirectional chapter→practice links; section-level deep links once anchors are stabilized.

Porta al generador **Firewall Básico** (`firewall.js`) las mismas mejoras que se aplicaron al Anti-Blacklist, alineadas con la documentación de MikroTik. Todas son opcionales (checkboxes/selector), así que se puede seguir generando un firewall mínimo.

All three previously-flagged P1 issues from prior review rounds are addressed in this version: the fail-safe `entry.newSha` CAS guard in `restoreBackfill`, the `updateMany`-on-`updatedAt` TOCTOU fix, and the `updatedAt: Date` addition to `DbClient.landingPage.findUnique`. - **Template + targeting**: 176-line Kajabi-faithful HTML artifact (`.su-mc`-scoped, token-driven, coach-photo as `` not `background-image`); targeting computes a per-workshop re-render of the backed-up old template and compares SHAs — correct approach for interpolated snapshots. - **Safety guards**: `--expect-count` gate, sanitizer-strip block on apply, CTA/price/coach-photo/new-value preflights per target row, prod guard (`ASSESSMENT_PROD_EXPECTED_HOST` + `--i-know-this-is-prod`), backup-before-write, and CAS `updateMany` on every write path. - **Test coverage**: 48 guard tests across 7 suites covering both scripts, every preflight variant, corrupt-backup handling, TOCTOU scenarios, and artifact-sanitize assertions.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the migration tooling is operator-run, not on the live request path, and carries multiple layers of production guards that prevent accidental or destructive writes. All three previously-flagged issues in restoreBackfill (fail-open CAS guard, TOCTOU between read and write, missing updatedAt in the DB interface) are fully resolved. The apply and restore paths now match in safety: updateMany with where: { id, updatedAt } on every write, fail-safe newSha guard before any restore write, and an explicit updatedAt == null defense-in-depth check. Preflights (CTA, price, coach photo, new-value validity, sanitizer strips) give operators clear signals before any page is touched. The only finding is a minor efficiency nit — two extra buildWorkshopVariables calls per workshop that can't be found, which does not affect correctness. No files require special attention.

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary
Generated images now deliver natively on every gateway platform (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, …) without depending on the model restating the file path.

`image_generate` returns its artifact as a JSON payload (`{"success": true, "image": "/abs/path.png"}`) with no `MEDIA:` tag. The gateway's auto-append path only recognized literal `MEDIA:` tags from `text_to_speech`, so image delivery silently relied on the model echoing the path into its reply. When it didn't, the image was dropped.

## Changes
- `gateway/run.py`: add `image_generate` to `_AUTO_APPEND_MEDIA_TOOL_NAMES`; the auto-append scanner now extracts the local-file path from the tool's JSON result (`host_image` → `image` → `agent_visible_image`, first deliverable wins) and synthesizes a `MEDIA:` tag. Reuses the existing extension-anchored `_TOOL_MEDIA_RE` and history-dedupe set, so remote URLs, unknown extensions, failed generations, and already-delivered paths are all rejected.
- `tests/gateway/test_media_extraction.py`: 4 new tests — JSON path delivery, host-path preference, failure/URL rejection, history dedupe.

## Validation
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `image_generate` JSON → `MEDIA:/path` | delivered |
| host vs sandbox path | host path wins |
| `success: false` / remote URL / unknown ext | not delivered |
| path already in history | not re-sent (no dupes) |
| existing `text_to_speech` MEDIA: path | unchanged |

`tests/gateway/test_media_extraction.py test_platform_base.py test_stream_consumer.py test_tts_media_routing.py` → 262 passed.

Closes the one path from #19105 not already covered by the WhatsApp native-media work on `main`. The other four paths in that issue (WhatsApp `send_message` MEDIA:, native image/video/audio bridge sends, inbound video paths, history dedupe) were independently implemented since the issue was filed; PR #19106 (@hedirman) was closed in favor of that work with credit.

author: arnavnagzirkar
body:
## Summary

`auto_functionalized` and `triton_kernel_wrapper_functional` are both higher-order operators that act as functional wrappers around mutable operations. Their CompositeExplicitAutograd (dense) implementations share the same core pattern: 1.


## Root cause

`auto_functionalized` and `triton_kernel_wrapper_functional` are both higher-order
operators that act as functional wrappers around mutable operations. Their
CompositeExplicitAutograd (dense) implementations share the same core pattern:

1. Clone selected tensor kwargs using `clone_preserve_strides`
2. Run the underlying mutable operation
3. Return the cloned (now-mutated) tensors

The cloning logic was duplicated across both functions with slightly different
coding style: `triton_kernel_wrapper_functional_dense` used an inline dict
comprehension, while `auto_functionalized_dense` used an explicit for-loop with
conditional handling of `None` and list values. Additionally, `auto_functionalized_dense`
did not handle `None` elements inside list-typed mutable args, which was a
latent bug.


## What changed

**Added** `torch._higher_order_ops.auto_functionalize._clone_tensors` - a shared
helper function that clones specified entries in a kwargs dict using
`clone_preserve_strides`. It handles three cases uniformly:
- `None` values (left as `None`)
- `list` values (each non-`None` element cloned)
- Tensor values (cloned directly)

**Refactored** `torch._higher_order_ops.auto_functionalize.auto_functionalized_dense`
to use `_clone_tensors`, replacing the inline loop. This also fixes a latent issue
where `None` elements inside list-typed mutable args would have caused a crash.

**Imported** `_clone_tensors` in `torch._higher_order_ops.triton_kernel_wrap` and
**refactored** `torch._higher_order_ops.triton_kernel_wrap.triton_kernel_wrapper_functional_dense`
to use it, replacing the inline dict comprehension.

Both functions now share the same cloning implementation, with behavior preserved
for all existing uses.


## Issue

Fixes #133443

Issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/133443


## Diffstat

```
torch/_higher_order_ops/auto_functionalize.py | 50 ++++++++++++++++-----------
 torch/_higher_order_ops/triton_kernel_wrap.py | 6 ++--
 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 24 deletions(-)
```


## Testing


- Ran the relevant tests and linter for the changed files while developing.

- Kept the change minimal and focused on this one issue.


## AI assistance


I used GitHub Copilot to help write parts of this change. I've reviewed and tested it myself, I understand what it does, and I'll follow up on any review feedback.

author: swaibat
body:
## Summary
This PR overhauls the game request dialog UI to match the Godot GameRequestDialog design, adds comprehensive connection state handling during live matches, and includes several gameplay and stability improvements.

## Key Changes

### Game Request Dialog Redesign
- Completely restyled the incoming/outgoing challenge modal with a radial gradient backdrop, opponent vs. YOU avatar layout, countdown ring timer, and centered VS/stake display
- Added avatar support to game requests, displaying both players' avatars in the dialog
- Implemented `dlg_avatar()` and `dlg_timer()` helper functions for circular avatar discs and animated countdown rings
- Updated dialog positioning and styling to match the Godot reference design with proper color scheme (red VS text, cyan titles, gold accents)

### Connection State Management
- Added comprehensive websocket connection monitoring with zombie-connection detection (no inbound traffic for 13+ seconds triggers forced reconnect)
- Implemented `conn_overlay` UI system to display connection status during live matches with grace-period countdown
- Added handlers for `ws_player_dc` (opponent disconnect), `ws_player_rc` (opponent reconnect), `ws_net_down/up` (own socket drop/recovery), and `ws_net_failed` (reconnect failure)
- Connection overlays show appropriate titles ("OPPONENT DISCONNECTED", "CONNECTION LOST", "DISCONNECTED") with grace-period timers where applicable

### Replay/Rematch System
- Implemented replay request timeout (12 seconds) — if opponent doesn't accept/decline a rematch request, player is returned to lobby instead of waiting indefinitely
- Added `ws_replay_declined` message handling to bounce players back to lobby when rematch is declined
- Clears connection overlays before showing game-over modal to prevent UI layering issues

### Online State Synchronization
- Enhanced deck/hand reconciliation in `finalize_state_sync()` to detect server-side reshuffles and animate the discard pile back into the deck instead of spawning fresh cards
- Detects reshuffle by checking if deck jumped significantly while played cards pile was reset, then triggers proper riffle animation

### Gameplay Rules
- Added heads-up rule: an 8 (skip) cannot be played on another 8, preventing infinite skip chains in 1v1 matches

### Stability & Configuration
- Added `ZOMBIE_TIMEOUT` config (13 seconds) for detecting dead-but-open socket connections
- Improved websocket keep-alive with pre-send zombie check to avoid false positives
- Updated message routing in controller to use pub/sub tokens for connection events instead of direct forwarding
- Added `_seq` sequence tracking to prevent stale timer callbacks from affecting new game instances

## Implementation Details
- Avatar IDs are now passed through game request lifecycle and stored in dialog state
- Connection overlay uses socket.gettime() for accurate grace-period countdown
- Reshuffle detection prevents visual glitches when server reshuffles deck mid-game
- All connection state changes properly notify the HUD layer for UI updates

author: corycharlton
body:
## Problem

The library declared its Avalonia dependency as `12.0.4`, which NuGet emits into the nuspec as `[12.0.4, )` — a *minimum*. Consumers pinned to an earlier 12.0 patch (e.g. 12.0.3) fail to restore because their Avalonia version doesn't satisfy the floor.

## Fix

Apply a `VersionOverride` to the library's own `PackageReference` so the packed dependency becomes `[12.0.0, 13.0.0)`:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Avalonia" VersionOverride="[12.0.0, 13.0.0)" />
```

- Only the **library package's** declared dependency is widened — any 12.0.x (incl. 12.0.3) now satisfies it.
- The CPM pin in `Directory.Packages.props` stays at `12.0.4`, so the Demo (and future test) projects keep building/testing against 12.0.4.
- The `< 13.0.0` upper bound matches the convention of the package major version tracking the supported Avalonia major.

This mirrors the same pattern already used in `ccswe-avalonia-viewlocator`.

## Verification

`dotnet pack` succeeds and the emitted nuspec confirms the loosened range:

```
<dependency id="Avalonia" version="[12.0.0, 13.0.0)" exclude="Build,Analyzers" />
```

## Note

The control templates were forked/authored against Simple 12.0.4. Patch-level drift between 12.0.3 and 12.0.4 is normally trivial, but a runtime smoke test of a consuming app on 12.0.3 is worthwhile for full confidence.
