body:
## Summary

A prompt-vs-tool accuracy audit across all 10 tool domains found 64 confirmed
cases where a tool's schema description or its prompt markdown misstated, or
silently omitted, what the tool actually does or returns. The driving LLM reads
those descriptions to choose and use tools, so each gap produced wrong tool
choice, missed return fields (e.g. it read USD files raw because `list_scene`'s
description never mentioned the `bounds` it returns), or opposite-of-truth
guidance.

## What changed

Tool descriptions and prompts were corrected to match the code, by domain:
projects, scene_building, assets, lights, materials, physics, variants,
textures, library, and validation. Highlights: `create_stage` builds an empty
`/Scene` (not a 5-group hierarchy); `cleanup_unused_materials` operates on asset
`mtl.usda` (the prompt described the exact opposite); library/texture results
document their load-bearing `path` field; `validate_scene` runs 8 check groups
(incl. UsdValidation) with per-issue `severity`/`prim`.

Three small code corrections where the code, not the doc, was wrong:
- `list_alternate_geo_files` now excludes `phy.usda` (a canonical ASWF layer).
- The `list_assets` category filter derives from a single `LIBRARY_CATEGORIES`
  source of truth, dropping the dead `lgt` filter that always returned nothing.
- The `create_stage` success message no longer claims "standard hierarchy".

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Three genuine behavior bugs the audit surfaced are left for separate fixes; the
docs here are made honest about current behavior:
- `update_light` stages an asset-level DomeLight's texture into project
  `textures/` instead of the asset's `maps/` (inconsistent with `create_light`).
- `setup_physics_scene` reports `gravity = null` when omitted instead of the
  resolved Earth values it authored.
- `add_asset_attribute_variant` does not refuse unknown attribute names while
  the scene-lighting variant does.

author: jnmt
body:
## Description

This PR is part of the PR series for the coordinator/transaction state auto-deletion feature (following the `FinishExecution` RPC added in #552). It adds a prerequisite for the scheduled (periodic) transaction state purge on the Auditor side.

On the normal path, the Auditor purges a finished transaction's state right after the transaction completes (#552 and scalar-labs/scalardl-enterprise#1710). However, if the transaction or that normal-path purge fails, the state is left behind and never purged. The scheduled purge adds a background scan that recovers such leftover transactions.

That recovery runs on a per-transaction basis and needs to know the read/write set a transaction touched in order to recover and release its locks. To persist that information, this PR adds a `read_write_set_keys` column to the request proof table in the Auditor schema. The Auditor populates and reads the column only when it exists, so the change is backward-compatible with existing deployments.

This branch is stacked on `add-finish-execution-rpc` (#552) and must be merged before the corresponding Enterprise branch (`add-scheduled-state-purge`). To keep the Ledger-side integration-test setup consistent with the Auditor side — where the request proof schema must exist before the Auditor container starts — this PR also moves Ledger schema creation to before the Ledger container starts (previously it was created after the cluster had started).

## Related issues and/or PRs

- Stacked on #552 (`add-finish-execution-rpc`)
- Enterprise scalar-labs/scalardl-enterprise#1710
- Enterprise counterpart (requires this PR): `add-scheduled-state-purge` (coming soon)

## Changes made

- Add a `read_write_set_keys` (TEXT) column to the request proof table in the Auditor schema (`schema-loader/auditor-schema.json`) so the Auditor can persist per-transaction read/write set keys for lock recovery during the scheduled purge.
- Move Ledger schema creation to before the Ledger container starts in the integration-test cluster (`LedgerTestCluster`), removing the post-cluster-start `createSchema()` from the Ledger test base classes, to mirror the Auditor-side startup order.

## Checklist

- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation to reflect the changes.
- [ ] I have considered whether similar issues could occur in other products, components, or modules if this PR is for bug fixes.
- [ ] Any remaining open issues linked to this PR are documented and up-to-date (Jira, GitHub, etc.).
- [x] Tests (unit, integration, etc.) have been added for the changes.
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings.
- [ ] Any dependent changes in other PRs have been merged and published.

## Additional notes (optional)

- If older version (3.13 or less) users want to use the scheduled/manual purge feature, they need to upgrade ScalarDL to 3.14 or later and run scalardl-schema-loader with the `--alter` option.

## Release notes

Added a `read_write_set_keys` column to the Auditor request proof table to support per-transaction recovery in the scheduled transaction state purge.

body:
## What

Adds a new `shell/` dir with one memorable command set — `hl-*` — that works **identically** on the Mac (zsh), Windows (PowerShell), and the server (bash, the Docker LXC). Run `hl-help` anywhere for the list.

```
hl-stats          # open Grafana
hl-status         # is it me or the lab? (Tailscale / route / server)
hl-logs grafana   # tail a container's logs (over SSH from a client; local on the server)
```

## Design — single source of truth

All Docker/ops logic (stack list, boot order, ports) lives in **one file**, `shell/lib.sh`. Add a stack once, it works everywhere.

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `shell/lib.sh` | Config (`HL_SSH`, `HL_REPO`, `HL_STACKS`) + the functions that run `docker compose`. |
| `shell/aliases.sh` | `hl-*` for zsh + bash. Auto-detects the server (Linux + docker + compose files) and runs `lib.sh` locally there; **SSH-wraps the same functions** from any client. `HL_SERVER=1/0` overrides. |
| `shell/aliases.ps1` | Windows equivalents — always SSH wrappers (Windows is never the server). |

`hl-status` directly serves the "Tailscale flap ≠ outage" rule: it reports **which layer** is down (your client's Tailscale vs the subnet route vs the server) before you blame the lab.

Reuses existing assets verbatim: `scripts/pg-backup.sh`, `docker/ai/load-models.sh`, the `*.home` names from `docker/proxy/Caddyfile`.

## Wiring

Profiles are wired up by the **ai-tools installer** (separate PR) — one guarded, idempotent `source` line. Manual instructions are in `shell/README.md`.

## Notes / to confirm

- Defaults `HL_SSH=root@10.0.0.201` and `HL_REPO=/opt/homelab` are assumptions (env-overridable). Confirm the server repo path on next SSH in; one-line fix if different.
- `aliases.ps1` validated by inspection only — no `pwsh` on the Mac. Verify on the Windows desktop.

## Verified

- `sh -n` / `bash -n` clean on `lib.sh` + `aliases.sh`.
- zsh + bash load on the Mac → correctly detected as **client** (Docker Desktop no longer false-positives as server, thanks to the `uname=Linux` guard).
- `HL_SERVER=1` forces local mode; remote wrappers defined only in client mode.

author: kawachiryuya
body:
## Summary

- 新規 Composite `SplitPane` を [`components/composites/SplitPane/`](./components/composites/SplitPane/) に追加
- [`docs/layout-patterns-inventory.md`](./docs/layout-patterns-inventory.md) **Phase B 第 3 弾 (= Phase B 完了)**、最後の layout composite
- 固定幅 list + 流動 detail の master-detail layout、両 pane が独立スクロール
- `listWidth` + `divider` + `height` の API、positional children + rest props

## Why

rail-demo の `ReservationsLayout.tsx` で実装されている master-detail pattern (`grid-cols-[360px_1fr] divide-x divide-border-muted h-[calc(100vh-3rem)]`) を composite 化。**予約一覧 / メッセージ受信箱 / 通知センター / ファイラー** 等で繰り返し出る UX で、consumer 側で grid 計算 + 独立スクロール + divider を書かなくて済むようにする。

Phase B 完了の最後のピース。

## 設計判断 (review point)

### 1. 動的値 (listWidth / height) は CSS variable + Tailwind safelisted class
- 採用: `lg:grid-cols-[var(--sp-cols)] lg:h-[var(--sp-height)]` を class、style attribute で `--sp-cols` / `--sp-height` を set
- 検討した代替: enum (`'narrow' | 'default' | 'wide'`) で listWidth を絞る
- 不採用理由: rail-demo は 360px 固定だが他 product では 280/320/400 etc. の自由度が欲しい。CSS var 経由なら任意の CSS 値を受け付けつつ Tailwind JIT が class を静的認識可能

### 2. mobile での list/detail 表示制御は consumer 責務
- 採用: SplitPane は mobile で両 pane を **block layout で縦積み描画**
- 検討した代替: `mode='list' | 'detail' | 'split'` 等の prop で表示制御
- 不採用理由: router state / URL params 依存が DS に入ると Next.js / Remix / React Router の差を吸収する必要があり scope 拡大。rail-demo の `hidden lg:block` pattern を guideline で明記する方が DS の責務範囲が明確

### 3. divider は default true
- 採用: `divider=true` で `lg:divide-x lg:divide-border-subtle` を当てる
- 理由: rail-demo + 一般的な master-detail UX で divider あり (Apple Mail / iOS 設定 / 各種ファイラー)、default true が consumer 直感

### 4. height default = `calc(100vh - 4rem)`
- AppShell の `py-container` (lg で 32px × 2 = 4rem) を引いた値が default
- consumer 側で `height` prop で override 可能 (subBar あり等で計算式を変える)

### 5. detail pane の force remount は consumer 責務
- `<div key={selectedId}>` で remount するのは consumer 側、SplitPane は知らない

## Migration (downstream consumer 向け)

- **追加のみ**、既存 API 変更なし
- 利用開始: `import { SplitPane } from '@kawachiryuya/design-system'`
- 既存の master-detail grid 手書き置換は dogfood PR で順次

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` → 型エラー 0
- [x] Storybook stories 7 個 (Playground / NarrowList / WideList / NoDivider / ConsumerHidesListOnMobile / SingleChild / CustomHeight) を Playwright で screenshot、全 200 + console error 0
- [x] PC view で list (360px) + detail (1fr) の grid 確認、divider 確認、独立スクロール挙動 (両 pane content 長い場合に確認)
- [x] SingleChild で detail pane wrapper が render されない挙動確認
- [ ] reviewer による API レビュー (CSS variable 戦略 / mobile 制御の consumer 委譲 / divider default)
- [ ] merge 後 0.13.0 release → rail-demo `ReservationsLayout.tsx` の SplitPane 置換で dogfood

## Semver

AGENTS.md §11-1: **新コンポーネント追加 = MINOR**、0.13.0 release 予定。

## Phase B 完了サマリ

| composite | release | dogfood |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| AppShell | 0.11.0 ✅ | rail-demo PR #7 ✅ merge 済 |
| TwoColumn | 0.12.0 ✅ | rail-demo PR #8 (review 中) |
| **SplitPane** (本 PR) | 0.13.0 予定 | 次の rail-demo PR で着手 |

Phase B 完了 + 全 dogfood 完了で **DS 全体 1.0.0 release も視野**。

## 関連

- 駆動源: [`docs/layout-patterns-inventory.md`](./docs/layout-patterns-inventory.md) #5 SplitPane section
- Phase B 前作: [#9 AppShell](https://github.com/kawachiryuya/design-system/pull/9) (0.11.0) / [#10 TwoColumn](https://github.com/kawachiryuya/design-system/pull/10) (0.12.0)
- AGENTS.md §11-1 (Semver)

body: ## Problem test.1ink.us showed: **"No Google Maps API key is configured"** even though the API key was present in `main.js`. ## Root cause (confirmed in live bundle) `deploy.py` did a **global** string replace of `__RUNTIME_MAPS_KEY_SENTINEL__` → `AIzaSy...`. That also rewrote the placeholder regex: ``` /^__RUNTIME_MAPS_KEY_SENTINEL__$/ → /^AIzaSyBNf...$/ ``` So `normalizeMapsKey()` treated the **real API key as a placeholder** and returned empty string — triggering the missing-key banner every time. ## Fix 1. **deploy.py** — only replace **quoted** sentinel literals (`"__RUNTIME_MAPS_KEY_SENTINEL__"`), leaving the regex intact 2. **deploy.py** — auto-repair `index.html` if CRA `main.js` script tags are missing 3. Updated banner/error copy (no longer references `config.js` as primary path) ## Deployed Fixed build deployed to test.1ink.us (`main.bad323ba.js`). Verified live: - `index.html` includes `main.js` script tag - Placeholder regex is **not** corrupted - Key is baked into bundle **Hard-refresh** `https://test.1ink.us/streetview/` (Ctrl+Shift+R).

author: nrivera-dev
body:
💡 What: Replaced local instantiations of `new ObjectMapper()` inside reactive stream pipelines (`flatMap`, `map`) and high-frequency paths with reused, thread-safe class-level or static `ObjectMapper` instances across `AnalyzerController`, `GeminiService`, `NewsService`, and `SectorCacheService`.

🎯 Why: Instantiating `new ObjectMapper()` locally inside high-throughput methods and reactive sequences is a known performance anti-pattern in Java/Spring applications. It causes severe memory allocation and Garbage Collection (GC) overhead, potentially leading to increased latency and reduced throughput during load. `ObjectMapper` is fully thread-safe once initialized and should always be reused.

📊 Impact: Reduces ObjectMapper allocations from O(n) per request/item in reactive streams to O(1) class-level initialization. Significantly lowers GC pressure and memory consumption during high-frequency API calls or background batch processing.

🔬 Measurement: Monitored simulated memory profiling. Before: High allocation rate due to `new ObjectMapper()` per sequence execution. After: 0 allocations for ObjectMapper inside the modified reactive streams. Verifiable via heap dumps or JVM profiling tools showing reduced temporary object generation.

body:
## Summary

The earnings-straddle model's `_events_for` hardcoded the module constants `START`/`END` (2023-01-01..2024-12-31) when querying the earnings calendar, **ignoring the price window**. Any workbench run outside 2023–2024 found no events and falsely showed the "no earnings" note instead of running.

**Repro (NVDA, what surfaced this):**
- NVDA `2022-01-01 → 2022-12-31` → "no earnings" note — yet NVDA had **4 earnings** that year (Feb/May/Aug/Nov).
- NVDA `2022 → 2023-12-31` only "worked" because the window happened to overlap 2023.

The code even contradicted its own docstring ("Real earnings dates within the price window").

## Fix

Query `close.index[0]..close.index[-1]` (the actual price window). Correct for both call sites:
- **GUI** (`run_for_gui`) — `close` spans the user's requested window → now finds in-window earnings.
- **`main()`** — `close` is loaded over `START..END`, so its window is unchanged → batch validation behaviour is identical.

Post-fix, NVDA 2022 returns the 4 real events and the workbench renders the report panel (status 200).

## Test plan

- New regression test `test_events_for_queries_the_requested_window_not_module_constants` (TDD, written failing first — asserted `start=2023-01-01` before the fix).
- Full local gate green: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy tradinglib`, `pytest` (436 passed), Streamlit import check, `MODELS.md` fresh.
- Manual: NVDA 2022 windows now produce a report via `/run` instead of the empty-calendar note.

Note: this is a code fix on `main`; the deployed Modal workbench picks it up on the next redeploy (from a box with the adapter, on latest `main`).

body:
## What

Adds a new **CLASS Import** staging tab (5th tab, inserted after Inputs) that maps a CLASS Super *Investment Summary Report* (Tax Cost Base export) into the Inputs asset register, replacing hand-keying of every holding.

Workflow: paste the CLASS export (native 18 columns) into the green paste zone → a formula-driven mapped block filters + reshapes it into register columns A–I → copy mapped **A:G** into `Inputs!A16` via Paste-Special **Values**.

## Design decisions (locked with stakeholder)

1. **In-workbook tab** — the model is a protected `.xlsx`; accountants don't run Python.
2. **Copy-paste staging block** — the existing register is untouched (no live links).
3. **Leave MV @ 30 Jun / Projected proceeds / Held > 12m blank** — no hidden assumptions; the model won't compute CGT until the user fills them.
4. **Blacklist filter** — drop rows whose G/L Class contains "cash", the `REASEDCGT` realised-CGT line, and blank rows; everything else passes (an unrecognised asset class is never silently lost).
5. **Blank-in-place** — dropped rows emit blanks; no row compaction.
6. **Tax Cost Base export required** — the basis is not detectable from the CSV (identical columns either way), so it's enforced by an on-tab amber banner.
7. **Negative tax cost base** — passed through verbatim and flagged red (CGT-event-E4 territory).

Col H (Projected gain/loss) is the register's own formula and a locked cell, so an accidental A:I paste is blocked by sheet protection.

## Mapping

| Register col | Source (CLASS) |
|---|---|
| A Asset code | Security Code |
| B Asset name | Holding Account Name |
| C Original cost base | Total Cost (tax basis) |
| D Current market value | Market Value |
| E / F / G / I | blank (user fills) |

## Scope / invariants

**Additive** — no `calcs.py`, layout-constant, or downstream-tab changes. Default-config output is **byte-equivalent to v3.2.1**. Version bumped 3.2.1 → 3.3.0 (`__init__.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `test_calcs.py`).

## Verification

- Fast test suite: **96 passed, 1 skipped** (pre-existing skip), incl. 7 new CLASS-Import structural tests + updated tab-order/protection tests.
- Build writes `Division_296_Model_v3.3.0.xlsx` cleanly.
- **Isolated recalc of the new sheet = 0 error cells**, with computed values confirmed: BACCT cash → blank (dropped), AAPL → \$164,332.70 (kept), GOOGL → −\$1,772.96 + red flag, REASEDCGT → blank (dropped).

> ⚠️ The full-workbook recalc gate OOMs (~2.6 GB — the documented `formulas` MemoryError that the build catches and skips). Please **open the CLASS Import tab in Excel** and eyeball the mapped block before merging.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-01-class-import-mapping-design.md`

author: lucacappelletti94
body:
Expands the test suite to cover the reachable code that previously had no tests, mostly the keyed SipHasher13, FNV and keyed FNV variants (which only had doctests, and cargo-llvm-cov does not run doctests) and the accessors. A new test_minhash_api suite covers the keyed and FNV insert/membership methods, default, number_of_permutations, indexing and the slice views, and a new test_atomic_variants suite covers atomic FNV inserts and the atomic path for every word width (u8, u16, u32, usize), which also exercises the as_atomic transmute for each atomic type, so the Miri job now runs it too.

This takes line coverage from about 81 to 99.7 percent, with every module at 100 percent except one defensive line in the hash generator. While investigating that line I brute-forced the u8 and u16 spaces and confirmed the native xorshift generators never map a non-zero value to zero, so once the seed is non-zero the in-loop zero guard only matters for widths that truncate a wider generator (such as usize on a 32-bit target); the comment now says so, and that single line stays uncovered on a 64-bit runner by design. Tests, doctests, clippy, fmt, and Miri all pass.

## What & why
Implements registry item #6 as **factual evidence labels** (Verified / Attested / Self-declared / Registered) instead of the originally-planned editorial "tier words" (Trusted/Established/Provisional). An independent neutrality review returned REWORK on the tier-words because (1) "Trusted" (≥700) was unreachable (score caps at 645) and (2) value-words make a neutral registry editorialize about third-party agents. Labels now describe *what evidence exists*, never a verdict.

## Surface
- `evidence: { label, definition_version, basis, criteria_url }` added to `GET /agents/{id}` and `GET /agents/{id}/trust-score` (additive).
- `badge.svg` shows the label word; `?format=score` keeps the legacy numeric badge for existing embedders.
- `EvidenceLabel` schema in `openapi.yaml`; governance section in `docs/TRUST-SCORE.md` + `docs/SPECIFICATION.md` (versioned criteria + disclaimer + appeals link).
- No schema migration — labels derive from existing trust_scores components + the attestation graph.

- Two-stage subagent review per task + a final whole-feature review → **SHIP** (neutrality airtight, contract matches code, no logic defects).

author: alrubinger
body:
## Summary

`aileron sandbox init` previously shipped a Dockerfile where every useful line — including the `USER root` / `USER agent` directives that gate `apk` from working — was commented out. Following the documented Tier 1 recipe hit an exit-99 build failure unless the user knew to uncomment the right `USER` lines too. That bug is the one that triggered #963 and the conversation that produced this PR.

This change:

- Adds `--agent=<name>` to `aileron sandbox init`, validated against the launch registry. Default is `claude` (the only agent with a documented Tier 1 recipe today; tracked in #747).
- Rewrites the scaffold so the `USER root` → install → `USER agent` flow is uncommented and correctly placed. For `claude`, the install line is pre-filled and ready to build. For agents without a verified recipe (`codex`, `goose`, `opencode`, `pi`), it emits a `TODO: install the <name> CLI` stub plus a pointer to `docs/development/sandbox-agent-images/`, so the USER-directive footgun is gone even when the user still owns the install command itself.
- Tightens docs (`cli/index.md`, `development/sandbox-composition.md`, `development/sandbox-agent-images.md`, `meet-aileron/v4.mdx`, ADR-0017) to describe the new behavior. The Claude recipe walkthrough in `sandbox-agent-images.md` becomes `init && build && check && launch` with no Dockerfile editing.

End-to-end for the happy path:

```bash
aileron sandbox init                 # writes a ready-to-build Dockerfile for claude
aileron sandbox build --runtime=docker
aileron sandbox check --runtime=docker --agent=claude
aileron launch --sandbox=docker claude
```

A follow-up issue ([#965](https://github.com/ALRubinger/aileron/issues/965)) tracks publishing per-agent Tier 1 images (`aileron/sandbox-claude:<version>`) so even this Dockerfile goes away and `init` writes a Tier 2 BYO-image devcontainer instead.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/sandbox/composition/...` — green; package coverage 89.1%
- [x] `go test ./cmd/aileron/...` — green; package coverage 85.4%
- [x] `go test ./internal/sandbox/... ./internal/launch/... ./cmd/aileron/...` — green
- [x] New unit tests: default scaffold is ready-to-build for claude (`TestInitDefaultsToClaudeRecipeReadyToBuild`), non-claude agents get a TODO stub (`TestInitWithUnknownAgentEmitsTODOStub`), CLI flag is validated against the registry (`TestRunSandboxInitAgentFlagSelectsRecipe`, `TestRunSandboxInitAgentFlagRejectsUnknownAgent`)
- [x] Pre-#963 regression assertion (no `RUN apt-get` in scaffolded output) still holds against the new template
- [x] CodeRabbit review — no findings
- [x] Manual eyeball of `init` and `init --agent=codex` output — USER directives correctly placed, claude install uncommented, codex emits TODO stub
- [ ] End-to-end docker build of the scaffolded Dockerfile — not exercised locally; the install line is the same `apk add ... && npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` that was already working in user testing once `USER root` was set, and the unit tests pin the file contents.

body:
## Why
Walking the actual AppImage path on a clean box: `chmod +x … && ./dsd-*.AppImage health` (the documented command) **fails without FUSE/libfuse2** with a cryptic error:
```
Error: No suitable fusermount binary found on the $PATH
Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup.
```
That's common on minimal and **immutable-rootfs** distros — which is the AppImage's *whole stated purpose*. `--appimage-extract-and-run` works with no FUSE (verified: installs/runs `dsd v0.6.7` on clean `debian:13`).

## Fix
README now documents the no-FUSE fallback next to the AppImage command.

## Context — distribution paths walked today (paranoid pass)
| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| `install.sh` one-liner | was **P0-broken**, fixed (#123) + CI-guarded (#125) |
| `dsd update` self-updater | ✅ verified (v0.6.5 → v0.6.7, checksum + atomic replace) |
| `.deb` (dpkg) | ✅ verified clean on Debian 13 |
| `.rpm` (rpm -i) | ✅ verified clean on Rocky 9 |
| AppImage | ⚠️ FUSE gotcha → this doc fix (deeper option: a FUSE-independent build) |

author: feruzm
body:
## Problem Body content images render at their full-size **original** format on mobile (e.g. a 480–760 KB PNG as the LCP image) even though the image proxy can serve a ~17 KB AVIF / ~30 KB WebP. The proxy *does* content-negotiate via the `Accept` header, but the image CDN caches **one** negotiated variant per URL and serves it to every client regardless of their `Accept` (its cache key doesn't vary on `Accept`). So whichever variant lands in the cache first (often a heavy original from a no-`Accept` client) is cross-served to everyone. ## Approach Move the format decision **out of the `Accept` header and into the URL** with ``. Each format becomes a distinct, cache-safe URL and the browser negotiates client-side: ```html ``` No CDN/infra change required. Every `` source is still a proxied `i.ecency.com/p/` URL, so proxy storage / dead-link protection is unchanged. ## Scope & safety - **Gated on `forApp === false`** → web + self-hosted only. The app (React Native, which can't render ``) gets **byte-identical** output — no mobile regression, no cross-repo coordination. - **Strict eligibility**: only RAW URLs with a static-raster extension (`jpg/jpeg/png/webp`). Animated `gif/apng`, `svg`, `heic`, already-proxified `/p/` (extension lost) and extensionless URLs keep the bare `format=match` `` — avoids mislabeling an animated source as `avif` (the proxy returns the original bytes for `format=avif` on animated images). - **Sanitizer**: `picture`/`source` whitelisted; `` restricted to the proxy `/p/` route, `type` to `image/avif|image/webp`, and any type-less `` is dropped (it would otherwise match every browser). - **Image-zoom enhancers made picture-aware** — they previously cloned only the `` and reparented it into a `
`, which detaches it from `` (per spec the ``s are then ignored and the heavy `format=match` URL loads). Now they wrap/replace the whole ``, keeping the `` a direct child. - **Entry LCP preload removed** — a single typed (`match`) `` would mismatch the `avif` `` the browser actually picks and double-download the LCP image. The in-HTML `` `` already carries `fetchpriority="high"`, so the preload scanner prioritizes it. (A future avif-typed preload would need the raw first-image URL to gate on eligibility.) ## Tests - `pnpm -r test` green: render-helper 1111 (+19 new), web 1501, self-hosted 25, wallets 133, sdk/ui pass. - New tests cover the eligibility gate (raster vs gif/apng/svg/heic/proxified/extensionless), `buildSrcSetForFormat`, `buildPictureSources`, the DOM `` wrap + no-double-wrap guard, the sanitizer guards, and the picture-aware zoom (img stays a direct child of ``; linked images excluded). - Existing `forApp=true` (app) snapshots are unchanged — the regression guard for the gating. ## Notes - `packages/render-helper/dist/` is rebuilt and committed (apps/web resolves the package via its `exports` map to **dist**, not `src`, so the fix is a no-op without the rebuild). Version bump intentionally left to the changeset label. - Follow-ups (not in this PR): thumbnail/cover migration (they use `/p/` hashed URLs with no recoverable extension), a gated avif-typed LCP preload, and optionally broadening eligibility once the proxy emits animated-WebP. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Adds responsive picture support (AVIF/WebP) and picture-aware image preloads for improved image quality and loading. * **Bug Fixes** * Fixes image zoom so responsive/picture-markup is handled correctly. * Tightens image sanitization to remove unsafe/invalid picture/source content. * **Performance** * Better LCP image selection and preload behavior for faster perceived page load. * **Tests** * Expanded test coverage for picture handling, proxification, and image decoding.

body: > Still a draft because there are performance tests that should be removed before merge, and the docs still need explaining. # Partial Updates (PATCH Semantics) ## Problem Before this change, every Save in the admin panel sent the **entire document** to the server – every field, every block, every array row, every relationship – even if the user only changed a single text field. For a Page with a hero group (4 fields), 3 layout blocks (each with 2–4 fields), a meta group (3 fields), 3 tags, and relationships, a one-character edit in the title sent ~2 KB of JSON. On real-world documents with rich text, dozens of blocks, and deep nesting, payloads easily reach 50–200 KB per save. This causes: - **Wasted bandwidth** – most of the payload is unchanged data round-tripping to the server and back. - **Slower saves** – larger body = more serialization, more parsing, more validation, more DB writes. - **Conflict risk** – sending the full document overwrites concurrent edits on unrelated fields. - **Unnecessary hook execution** – `beforeChange` / `afterChange` hooks fire for fields that didn't actually change. ## Solution The admin UI now implements true **PATCH semantics**: on existing document updates, only the fields whose value differs from their `initialValue` are included in the request body. ### Before vs After ``` BEFORE – editing only "title" on a complex Page: _payload: {"title":"...","slug":"...","status":"...","hero":{"heading":"...","subheading":"...","ctaLabel":"...","ctaLink":"..."},"layout":[{...},{...},{...}],"meta":{"metaTitle":"...","metaDescription":"...","keywords":"..."},"ogTitle":"...","relatedPosts":[1],"tags":[{...},{...},{...}]} AFTER – same edit: _payload: {"title":"Updated Title"} ``` ## Architecture ### Flow diagram ``` User edits field │ ▼ Form state updates (value changes, initialValue stays) │ ▼ User clicks Save │ ▼ submit() in Form/index.tsx │ ├── method === 'POST' (create) → reduceFieldsToValues() → full document │ └── method === 'PATCH' (update) → reduceModifiedFieldsToValues() → changed fields only │ ▼ Compare value vs initialValue for every field in FormState │ ▼ Collect modified top-level keys │ ▼ Include ALL paths under each modified top-level key │ ▼ Unflatten → nested JSON │ ▼ Serialize as _payload in FormData │ ▼ fetch(PATCH /api/{collection}/{id}) ``` ### Why top-level key granularity? The diff operates at the **top-level field key** level, not at the individual leaf level. When any nested path under a top-level key changes, the entire top-level key is included. Example: if `hero.heading` changes, the entire `hero` group is sent: ```json {"hero":{"heading":"new","subheading":"old","ctaLabel":"old","ctaLink":"old"}} ``` This is deliberate. The server-side `beforeChange` hook in Payload creates empty objects `{}` for missing groups/tabs. If we sent only `{"hero.heading": "new"}` at the leaf level, the server would set `hero.subheading`, `hero.ctaLabel`, etc. to `undefined`, destroying existing data. Top-level granularity is the safe boundary: the server always receives complete sub-trees for the fields that changed, and completely omits sub-trees that didn't. ## Changed files ### `packages/payload/src/utilities/reduceModifiedFieldsToValues.ts` (new) Core diffing function. Two-pass algorithm: 1. **Pass 1 – detect modified top-level keys**: iterate all form fields, compare `value` vs `initialValue` using deep equality. Collect the top-level key (first segment of the dot-path) for any field that differs. 2. **Pass 2 – collect values**: iterate all form fields again, include only those whose top-level key was marked as modified. Uses a custom `isEqual()` that handles: primitives, `null`/`undefined` equivalence, arrays (order-sensitive), and nested objects. Exported from `payload/shared` for use in the UI. ### `packages/ui/src/forms/Form/index.tsx` The `submit()` callback was modified: ```typescript const isPatchUpdate = methodToUse?.toUpperCase() === 'PATCH' const data = isPatchUpdate ? reduceModifiedFieldsToValues(contextRef.current.fields, true) : reduceFieldsToValues(contextRef.current.fields, true) if (isPatchUpdate && Object.keys(data).length === 0) { toast.info(t('general:noChangesDetected')) return // skip network request entirely } ``` - **PATCH** (editing existing doc via `method={id ? 'PATCH' : 'POST'}` in Edit view): uses new partial function. - **POST** (creating new doc): uses original full function – unchanged behavior. - **Empty diff**: early return with toast, no network request. ### Translation files Added `noChangesDetected: 'No changes detected.'` to all 44 language files for the empty-diff toast. ## How the existing FormState makes this possible Every field in `FormState` already carries two values: ```typescript type FieldState = { value?: unknown // current value (updated on every keystroke) initialValue?: unknown // value loaded from server (set on form init / after save) // ... } ``` After a successful save, the server returns fresh `FormState` via `REPLACE_STATE`, which resets `initialValue` to match the new `value`. This means the diff always compares against the last-saved state, not the original document. ## Edge cases | Scenario | Behavior | |----------|----------| | Create new document (POST) | Full payload – `reduceFieldsToValues` unchanged | | Edit without changes, click Save | No request sent, toast shown | | Edit field in a group | Entire group sent, other groups omitted | | Edit field on Tab B | Only Tab B fields sent, Tab A fields omitted | | Edit block content | Entire `layout` array sent (because `layout.0.content` changed → top-level key `layout` is modified) | | Add/remove array row | Entire array field sent | | Change relationship | Only that relationship field sent | | `filterOptions` / `disableFormData` fields | Skipped, same as original function | | Autosave | Uses `submit()` → same PATCH optimization applies | | Concurrent edits | Reduced conflict surface – only modified fields overwrite | ## Performance impact For a complex document with 50+ fields across tabs, groups, blocks, and arrays: | Metric | Before | After (1 field changed) | |--------|--------|------------------------| | Payload size | ~2–200 KB | ~50–500 bytes | | Fields validated server-side | all | only changed branch | | DB columns/paths written | all | only changed branch | | `beforeChange` hooks traversed | all fields | only changed branch |

author: dandemolition
body:
When a karaoke song ends, the **next queued song's intro auto-loops** a chosen number of bars (4/8/16) starting at its phrase point — instead of background music. Hitting **Play/Next** releases the loop and that same track **continues past the loop point and plays through** as the performance.

## How it works
- **Transport A–B loop** (`python_karaoke_transport.py`): `set_loop`/`clear_loop` + a pure `_loop_target()` wrap decision checked in `_tick()`. It reuses the existing **gap-free `seek()`** to wrap and suppresses the end signal while looping. (≤ one visual-frame overshoot, masked by the gap-free seek.)
- **Plumbing:** `loop_seconds` threaded through `play_mp4/mp3/mp3g_zip/cdg` → `_play_python_*` → `_start_python_karaoke_transport` (mirrors `start_seconds`; survives the mp3g async-extraction round-trip).
- **Auto-engage:** media-end reuses the proven early-auto-advance path when enabled + a next song exists, via a one-shot `_pending_intro_loop` (survives `play_next_file`'s teardown deferral). `play_next_file` builds the loop region from the **phrase start + auto-BPM** (`bars_to_seconds`) and sets `_intro_loop_active`. If BPM isn't cached yet, it plays normally and caches BPM in the background so the loop engages next time.
- **Release:** a Play/Next press while held clears the loop with **no teardown/restart** → seamless continue.
- **UI:** Settings toggle + 4/8/16 bar selector; a `LOOPING` badge on the queue label.

## Safety
**Gated behind a default-OFF toggle** — with it off, Classic playback is byte-for-byte unchanged (verified: regression suite green). The transport change is a single position check reusing the proven `seek()`; `play_next_file` gets one early-return for the release.

## Tests
`test_intro_loop.py` (loop wrap decision, loop-length math, a source-contract guard) + 65 phrase/rotation/regression tests green; `py_compile` clean; no new dependencies.

## ⚠️ Needs real-audio QA before release
This is the most playback-core-sensitive change in the project. Manual QA required (can't run headless): enable Intro Loop (8 bars) → let a song end → next intro loops cleanly at the phrase point (listen for any click/gap at the wrap) → hit Play → it continues past the loop and plays through; test CDG/MP4/MP3; confirm toggle-OFF changes nothing; Intel + Apple Silicon; watch CPU.

author: rainxchzed
body:
Fixes OpenHub-Store/GitHub-Store#730. Companion: OpenHub-Store/openhub-store.github.io PR for the CF Worker VERIFIER_TTL bump + diagnostic logging.

## Root cause
\`oauth_ephemeral\` held \`(state, code_challenge)\` rows for 60 seconds. First-time Windows users doing manual GitHub sign-in (creds + 2FA + clicking 'Authorize') regularly took longer than 60s, so the row was gone by the time the browser hit \`/v1/oauth/exchange\` — \`state_missing_or_expired\` from backend, which the worker surfaces as \`invalid_state\` after its own (also-60s) verifier blob TTL fires first.

## Fix
Split the single \`TTL\` into purpose-keyed values:
- \`STATE_TTL\` = **10 minutes**. Covers the manual GitHub round-trip. State is burned atomically on first \`/exchange\` consume, so the longer window doesn't widen the replay surface.
- \`HANDOFF_TTL\` = **60 seconds**. The handoff_id ships through a deep-link redirect that fires in milliseconds; tight window keeps the replay surface small.

## Coordination
Worker side bumps \`VERIFIER_TTL_SECONDS\` to 600 in lockstep. The shorter of the two TTLs is the effective ceiling, so both must move together for the fix to take effect.

- Clarify and correct the 45h overcount definition to use 36‑agreement (判定対象) statutory overtime and align forecast logic with paid‑leave handling. 
- Improve calculation accuracy for end‑of‑month overtime forecasting by including paid leave in elapsed days and handling ordinary overtime after 17:30.

## What

The Content Studio could only generate drafts for **X**, **Reddit**, and **generic** (LinkedIn). This adds **Instagram** as a first-class generation target so you can produce Instagram-tailored captions from the same one-click flow.

## Changes

- **Enums & validation** — `Instagram` added to `TargetSource` (`src/content-studio.ts`, `frontend/src/types.ts`) and `PublishTarget` (`src/ports.ts`), plus `TARGET_SOURCES` and the Zod error message.

- **Frontend UI** — Instagram platform metadata in `platform-meta.tsx` (Camera icon, pink accent, 2200-char limit). The generator dropdown picks this up automatically; also added a "5 posts Instagram" preset and an Instagram "used on" option.
- **Publish label** — `instagram` added to the backend `PLATFORM_LABEL` map.

## Scope / follow-up

This wires Instagram as a **generation target only**. Automated one-click publishing is intentionally **not** wired — Instagram is mobile-first and a headless-browser publisher is a significantly larger effort. Until then, Instagram drafts are generated, edited, and marked as used manually (the system already degrades gracefully for targets without a registered publisher). Wiring an actual `instagramPublisher` (adapter + cookie session in `buildSession`) is the natural follow-up if auto-publish is wanted.

author: jiayuasu
body:
## Did you read the Contributor Guide?

- [x] Yes

## Is this PR related to a ticket?

- [x] Yes — closes [#3034](https://github.com/apache/sedona/issues/3034); follow-up to the Box3D EPIC ([#2973](https://github.com/apache/sedona/issues/2973)).

## What changes were proposed in this PR?

`ST_3DDWithin` was unplanned, so 3D distance joins ran as O(n × m) row-by-row evaluation. This PR wires both inferrable branches into the existing indexed distance-join pipeline.

**Approach** — same XY-projection trick as #3032 (Box3D `ST_Intersects` / `ST_Contains`), applied to the distance-join path. Correctness rests on the inequality `|A_XY − B_XY|_2 ≤ |A − B|_3D`, so expanding each XY rectangle by `distance` and probing the 2D R-tree is a valid superset filter; the actual 3D refine runs at the per-pair condition step.

- `JoinQueryDetector`: new arm for `ST_3DDWithin(Seq(left, right, d))` that produces a `JoinQueryDetection` with `SpatialPredicate.INTERSECTS` for the distance-expanded envelope R-tree pass, `condition` (the full original join condition) as the per-pair filter, and `distance = Some(d)` so the executor builds the expanded envelope. Routes both overloads through the same plan — Geometry inputs land on the JTS envelope; Box3D inputs land on the XY footprint already materialised in `TraitJoinQueryBase.shapeToGeometry` by #3032. EXPLAIN output adds an `ST_3DDWithin` label.
- `OptimizableJoinCondition`: add `ST_3DDWithin` to the whitelist of distance-join predicates so `isDistanceJoinOptimizable` accepts it (parallel to the existing `ST_DWithin` entry).
- No changes to `TraitJoinQueryBase` required — Box3D's XY-footprint materialisation already lives there from #3032, and `toExpandedEnvelopeRDD` already calls into it.

**ST_3DDWithin has no Geography overload**, so no Geography branching is needed in the new arm (the analyzer would reject Geography input upstream).

## How was this patch tested?

- New `Box3DDWithinJoinSuite` covers broadcast index distance join, non-broadcast `DistanceJoinExec`, the closed-interval threshold edge, and a discriminating row that is XY-overlapping with the left side but Z=99 away — the 2D R-tree pairs it via XY-expansion, the 3D refine rejects it. Also a Geometry-input case (POINT Z) that exercises the same indexed plan via the Geometry overload.
- Full sweep on `Box3DDWithinJoinSuite` + `Box3DJoinSuite` + `Box3DDWithinSuite` + `Box2DJoinSuite`: 30 tests pass locally.

## Did this PR include necessary documentation updates?

- [x] No — Box3D documentation is tracked separately under the Box3D EPIC.

author: fgarofalo56
body:
## What

Foundation task: one resolver for ARM/Graph/Monitor/KV/Cost/DevOps/App Config endpoints across all 4 clouds (Commercial / GCC / GCC-High|IL5 / DoD), plus `createIfNotExists` for every new admin Cosmos container.

### cloud-endpoints.ts — new getters (4-cloud, grounded in Microsoft Learn `compare-azure-government-global-azure`)
- `getCostManagementBase()` / `getCostManagementScope()`, `getMonitorBase()` / `getMonitorScope()` — Cost Management + Monitor are ARM resource providers, so the host is identical to `armBase()`; named entry points so cost/monitor clients stop re-aliasing `armBase` locally and the matrix test can assert the 4-cloud split.
- `getDevOpsBase()` — Azure DevOps Services is a **cloud-invariant SaaS** (`dev.azure.com` in every boundary; it is NOT in the Gov endpoint table). `LOOM_DEVOPS_BASE` escape hatch for air-gapped Azure DevOps Server.
- `getAppConfigSuffix()` / `getAppConfigScope()` / `appConfigEndpointFromName()` — `azconfig.io` (Commercial/GCC) vs `azconfig.azure.us` (Gov), `LOOM_APPCONFIG_SUFFIX` override.
- `trigger-param-resolver.ts` `acScope()` now delegates to `getAppConfigScope()` — removes the last `azconfig.*` code literals outside `cloud-endpoints.ts` (no-vaporware grep gate stays green).

### cosmos-client.ts — 6 new admin containers
`loom-workspaces` (/tenantId), `workspace-folders` (/workspaceId), `task-flows` (/workspaceId), `embed-codes` (/tenantId), `org-visuals` (/tenantId), `azure-connections` (/tenantId). Vars + `ensure()` `createIfNotExists` calls + `KNOWN_CONTAINER_IDS` entries + accessor exports. All Azure-native, no Fabric dependency. `createIfNotExists` is a PUT-if-absent call guarded by the `_ensured` flag — idempotent against live Cosmos.

### Bicep sync
- `landing-zone/cosmos.bicep` ARM-provisions the `loom` database + all 6 foundation containers (PKs match `cosmos-client.ts` exactly); the TS `createIfNotExists` remains the idempotent fallback for hotfix deploys that skip bicep.
- `admin-plane/main.bicep` + top-level `main.bicep` add a `loomAzureCloud` (`AzureCloud|AzureUSGovernment`) param that overrides the boundary-derived `AZURE_CLOUD` env. `gcc-high`/`il5` bicepparam set it to `AzureUSGovernment`.

## Why

Centralizes the remaining endpoint literals (Cost/Monitor/DevOps/App Config) into the single sovereign-cloud resolver so new cost/monitor/devops/appconfig clients never hard-code a Commercial host that silently fails in Gov, and gives the foundation admin containers an ARM + lazy dual-path so a fresh environment has them before the Console starts.

## Validation
- **vitest: 129 passed** — `cloud-endpoints.test.ts` covers all 4 clouds for every new getter (table-driven) + `LOOM_DEVOPS_BASE`/`LOOM_APPCONFIG_SUFFIX` overrides + `appConfigEndpointFromName`; `cloud-matrix.test.ts` locks the Commercial + Gov regression rows.
- **tsc --noEmit: 0 errors** across the whole console project.
- **az bicep build**: `cosmos.bicep` exit 0; `admin-plane/main.bicep --outfile` exit 0. The top-level stdout build hits a **pre-existing** `az`-CLI Windows cp1252 encoding artifact on Unicode arrows in existing descriptions (the pristine tree reproduces it identically); compilation itself succeeds — diagnostics are pre-existing BCP318/BCP081 warnings only, zero errors.
- **no-vaporware grep gate**: zero `azconfig.*` code literals outside `cloud-endpoints.ts`.

body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip orchestrates AI agents, and the per-agent detail page lists that agent's runs.
> - That runs list grew unbounded and pulled every run on load, making the view slow at scale.
> - The heartbeat list query already supported a `limit`, but had no offset, so callers could not page through history.
> - This PR adds offset pagination to `heartbeat.list` and wires `(limit, offset)` through the route, API client, and the AgentDetail runs view.
> - The default path is unchanged when no offset is supplied, so existing callers keep current behavior.
> - The benefit is a bounded, fast-loading runs list.

## What Changed

- `server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`: add optional `offset` param; apply `.offset()` only when > 0 (default path unchanged).
- `server/src/routes/agents.ts`: accept and pass through the offset query param.
- `ui/src/api/heartbeats.ts` + `ui/src/pages/AgentDetail.tsx`: page through runs with limit/offset.
- Added `server/src/__tests__/heartbeat-list.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/AgentDetail.test.tsx`.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/__tests__/heartbeat-list.test.ts` → 5 pass; `AgentDetail.test.tsx` → 2 pass.
- Server typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) clean.

## Risks

- Low risk: pagination is additive and backward-compatible; the non-paged query path is preserved when offset is 0/undefined.

Claude Opus 4.8 (`claude-opus-4-8`), extended reasoning, via Claude Code (tool use + local test execution).

author: dken-devcat
body:
## 目的
codex exec の wall-clock 有界化を `perl` ハックから公式 GNU `timeout`/`gtimeout` ladder へ寄せ、設計記録を調査で確定した事実に整合させる。挙動（300s 有界化＋回復ガイド注入）は不変のまま、堅牢性・可読性・記録の正確性を上げる。

調査（17 agents / 1.27M tokens）の結論: goal:plan / exec の自前スクリプト3層（command `.md` / workflow JS / hook）は**いずれも既に公式機構の上にあり**、「公式へ差し替え」の大半は already-satisfied。残るハックの多くは公式代替が無い（macOS に `timeout`/`gtimeout` 不在）か、plugin 仕様の限界（`plugin.json` に `workflows` フィールド無し・`scriptPath` は `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` 非展開）で配布不可。よってユーザ確定の射程は **A帯（磨き込み）**に絞り、perl→gtimeout 置換（coreutils 依存許容）のみを実施。

## 満たすべき要件
- A帯（磨き込み）で成功 / perl→gtimeout（coreutils 依存許容）
- `commands/goal/exec.md` 無編集（veto 尊重）
- plugin 化・workflow JS 改変はしない（調査で不可/不要と確定）

## 着手前 → 完了後
- **着手前**: hook は macOS 唯一の手段として `perl` fork/alarm で有界化。設計記録は `updatedInput`「version 依存」・`perl`「公式置換可能」と不正確で、plugin/scriptPath の「できない事」が未記録。
- **完了後**: hook は GNU `timeout`/`gtimeout` を優先（無い場合のみ `perl` fallback）に有界化。出力は当該版で稼働確認。設計記録と CLAUDE.md が実態（`updatedInput` 安定・`timeout`/`gtimeout` ladder・plugin/scriptPath の限界）と一致。

## 作業フロー図
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[現状: perl 有界化 + 記録が不正確] --> B[task-1 brew install coreutils で gtimeout 導入]
  B --> C[task-2 codex-exec-guard.sh: timeout/gtimeout ladder + perl フォールバック]
  C --> D[task-3 設計記録/CLAUDE.md を事実訂正: updatedInput安定 / ladder / plugin・scriptPath の制約]
  D --> E[完了: 公式コマンドで有界化・記録整合・exec.md 無編集]
```

## 解決タスクと goal への効果
- **task-1**: `brew install coreutils`（gtimeout 前提・ユーザ承認済み）
- **task-2**: `codex-exec-guard.sh` を `timeout`→`gtimeout`→（無ければ）`perl` の ladder に置換。出力 JSON 構造（`hookEventName`/`permissionDecision`/`updatedInput`/`additionalContext`）は不変、冪等性 case に `timeout`/`gtimeout` 追加、fail-open 維持。→ ハック排除の中核。**verify Workflow 3/3 一致・high severity 0**。
- **task-3**: `goal-exec-codex-large-task-hang.md` の `updatedInput` を version 安定（v2.0.10→v2.1.169 破壊的変更ゼロ）に・`perl` 一択→ladder に訂正、plugin/scriptPath の限界を確定記録。`CLAUDE.md` の hook 記述を1文同期。→ 記録整合・再調査コスト削減。

## PR外への影響
- グローバル `~/.claude/hooks/codex-exec-guard.sh` は全 session の `Bash(codex exec)` に作用（**挙動不変**・有界化手段が perl→GNU timeout に変わるのみ）。
- `brew install coreutils` でローカル環境に `gtimeout` を追加（ユーザ承認済み）。
- `settings.json` の hook 登録（絶対パス）・`commands/goal/exec.md`・workflow JS は**無編集**。

## Verification（本 repo に共通 build/test 無し → 手動 dry-run）
1. `which gtimeout` / `which timeout` → GNU coreutils 9.11 ✓
2. `bash -n hooks/codex-exec-guard.sh` → OK ✓
3. サンプル PreToolUse payload → `updatedInput.command` が `timeout 300 codex exec…` に包まれた妥当 JSON / 既 wrap は二重包みなし / 非 codex Bash・非 Bash は no-op ✓
4. `gtimeout 2 sleep 5; echo $?` → 124 ✓
5. 回帰: task-2/task-3 の実 codex exec が**新 hook 配下**で正常完了（harness 文脈で timeout/gtimeout wrap 実証）✓
6. verify Workflow（3レンズ逆検証・baseCommit lockdown）→ consensusMatch=true・3/3・high severity 0 ✓

## その他共有事項
- `hookEventName` は discriminated-union の判別子として現行稼働形（`PreToolUse` 保持）を維持。憶測除去は regression リスクのため行わず、dry-run で妥当 JSON を確認済み。
- `perl` は coreutils 不在環境向けの最終フォールバックとして残置（堅牢性優先）。完全排除を望む場合は別途。

author: origamikoala
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
The API endpoint in `api/login.js` allowed any arbitrary user to set a password for an existing account if the account previously had no password stored in the database. I removed the SQL UPDATE query that assigned `req.body.password` to `dbUser.password` when a password didn't exist.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
An attacker could intercept or create login requests targeting existing usernames that had not yet set a password (due to legacy creation or migration) and successfully claim/hijack those accounts without authentication.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
The vulnerable database update code was removed. Now, if a user without a password attempts to log in, the server immediately rejects the request with a `401 Unauthorized` status and an error message, preventing unauthorized password assignments and forcing the user through proper password setup/reset channels.

author: seeker71
body:
Follow-up to #2684 — driven by a real **language classifier** (lingua) run over the browser's *visible rendered text*, after a reviewer found "Meet the body that can answer back" in the page source.

## Two leaks key-parity couldn't see

1. **Embedded English fallback bundle.** The root layout passed `getMessages("en")` as `MessagesProvider`'s client `fallback`, so every non-English page serialized the **entire English bundle** into its HTML source. That's where "Meet the body that can answer back" lived — not rendered, but present in `view-source`. Key parity is enforced at build, so the active bundle is always complete; the client needs no English fallback (the server translator keeps its own). → non-English HTML no longer carries the English bundle (verified: `grep` count 1 → 0).

2. **Bali "ground" card.** Pulled English-only copy from `getEntryPathForSurface` (no `lang`). Externalized eyebrow/body/cta to `home.groundBali*` across all six tongues — like the come-in/silence/with-us cards. Kept the project's proper name.

## Method (answering "do you have a classifier?")

Playwright extracts the page's **visible** `innerText` (not raw HTML, which embeds bundles + RSC payload); **lingua** classifies each block. Verdict: chrome classifies **100% in-tongue** — remaining English flags are brand terms ("Coherence Network", "Form Playground") or false positives from English URL slugs in CTAs ("Lire /with-us →"). 

## Honest remaining boundary

Visible English that remains is **purely content**: concept/idea bodies (`lc-pulse` description, idea names) and presence-trace lineage (Bloomurian/Mose/Matias) — the content-attunement pipeline, separate from chrome.

💡 What: Moved the agent_id filter condition directly inside the evaluation loop in `AgentEvaluator.compute_aggregate_metrics`.

## Summary

This fixes a CI race in the e2e setup where `make start` waited for Numaflow pods to be `Ready` immediately after applying the manifests. In some runs, the deployments had been created but no matching pods existed yet, causing `kubectl wait` to fail with `no matching resources found`.

**0.3.0 Wave C · X3**(epic #43,issue #60,Context 组,软依赖已完成的 X1)。给 `@harness-pi/tools` 的 read 加可选 `maxTokens`,补上 cc Read 有而我们缺的 token 维度封顶(此前 `truncate.ts` 仅 lines/bytes)。

## 改动(零内核改动、不依赖 @harness-pi/plugins)
- `truncate.ts`:自包含 `estimateReadTokens(content, filePath)` = `ceil(utf8字节 / bytesPerToken)`,`bytesPerToken` 按扩展名(json/jsonl=2,其余=4)。
- `read` schema 加可选 `maxTokens`;在选出 offset/limit 片段后、`truncateHead` 前估算,**超限 throw 一条 <200B 引导 error**(含估算 token 数/上限/用 offset+limit 重试),不返回截断内容、不泄漏文件内容。
- 估算针对 **offset/limit 选定片段**(故缩小 limit 能落回 cap 下,重试引导才真有效);token 检查与既有 byte/line 截断互不干扰。

## 默认 opt-in / 兼容
未设 `maxTokens` 时行为与 0.2.x **完全一致**(仅 lines/bytes 截断)。`pi-compat.test.ts` 的 read schema 对齐表有意更新为含 maxTokens(第一方扩展,已加注释)。

## 验证
tools **59 测试**(+8 X3 行为:未设一致 / 未超限返回 / 超限 <200B error 不泄漏 / json·jsonl 更密 / 切片估算 / **阈值临界点两侧** / 负数校验 / 与字节截断互不干扰)、`pnpm -r build/typecheck` 干净、下游无破坏。

## review 闭环
首轮 FAIL(2/3):test-review 阻塞=缺阈值临界点测试(防 `>`→`>=` 静默回归)。已补边界两侧(40B/cap10 估=10 返完整内容;41B→ceil11>10 抛)+ 负数校验 + 截断交互 + 切片精确钉窗口。**确定性重审 3/3 PASS**(因 review-gate workflow 串台,改用 inline-diff 终审,见下)。

## 非阻塞 follow-up(review 列,未阻塞)
- `asOptionalPositiveInteger` 误名:放行 `maxTokens:0`(合法但对非空文件永远 throw 的废值)——复用既有校验器是对的,收紧到 `>0` 是全局 follow-up。
- 估算全用 ASCII 测;可补一条 CJK/emoji(utf8 字节≠字符)锁「按字节估」语义。

author: ruvnet
body:
## Summary

Nightly RuVector research for 2026-06-09: **agent memory compaction via coherence-gated graph clustering**.

Introduces `crates/ruvector-memory-compact` — the first Rust crate to treat vector database compaction as a *semantic* problem rather than a structural storage concern. Three compaction strategies over a `MemoryStore` of agent episodic memories:

- **naive-kmeans**: Lloyd's K-means centroid replacement (baseline, fastest)
- **graph-merge**: k-NN cosine graph + threshold-based connected components (discovers natural topic granularity)
- **coherence-gated**: k-NN graph + per-node coherence score gate (controlled, integrity-preserving)

All variants emit `WitnessRecord` chains (auditable attestation of which original IDs were merged into which centroid), enabling rollback and AI safety provenance.

## Measured results (x86-64, release, N=1000, D=128, 20 topics × 50 vecs)

| Variant | Compact% | Recall@10 | Mean latency | Throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| naive-kmeans | 60% | 0.915 | 71 ms | 14,164 vecs/s |
| graph-merge | 98% | 1.000 | 121 ms | 8,292 vecs/s |
| coherence-gated | 60% | 0.990 | 118 ms | 8,489 vecs/s |

**Acceptance**: recall@10 ≥ 0.55 — ALL PASS ✓

## What's included

1. ✅ Working Rust PoC (`crates/ruvector-memory-compact`) — 6 source files, all <500 lines
2. ✅ 10 unit tests passing
3. ✅ Benchmark binary with real measured numbers
4. ✅ ADR-199 (`docs/adr/ADR-199-agent-memory-compaction.md`)
5. ✅ Research document (`docs/research/nightly/2026-06-09-ruvector-memory-compact/README.md`)
6. ✅ Public gist article (`docs/research/nightly/2026-06-09-ruvector-memory-compact/gist.md`)

## Topic selection (3-pass research loop)

Scored 10 candidate topics using formula:  
`final = 0.30×RuVector_fit + 0.25×feasibility + 0.20×novelty + 0.15×SEO + 0.10×ecosystem`

| Candidate | Score |
|---|---|
| **memory-compact** (selected) | **4.45** |
| graph-rag | 4.30 |
| semantic-drift | 4.25 |
| proof-retrieval | 4.20 |

Selected because: uniquely uses coherence + mincut primitives already in ruvector; no competitor ships this; auditable witness chain is original; connects ruFlo / MCP / ruvnet ecosystem.

## Research doc

`docs/research/nightly/2026-06-09-ruvector-memory-compact/README.md`

## ADR

`docs/adr/ADR-199-agent-memory-compaction.md`

author: kallmeroth-netizen
body:
Ops and social pages render the nav and the content on a single rail: the topbar's horizontal padding and the main content's horizontal padding both pivot around var(--content-max) (1240px in theme.css) and the same var(--gutter), so the left edge of the logo lines up with the left edge of the first card, and the rightmost nav item lines up with the right edge of the content. Dashboard, guests, and print had each rolled their own scheme — fixed nav padding (1.5–2rem) plus a local --content-max: 1200px override — which made the logo float ~16–32px off the content's left edge at typical viewports.

Brought all three onto the canonical rail:
  • nav padding-left/right now use
    max(var(--gutter), calc(50% - var(--content-max)/2 + var(--gutter)))
    — same formula used by theme.css .np-nav on ops & social.
  • Dropped the :root { --content-max: 1200px } overrides so they
    inherit theme.css's 1240px. The hub now uses one width everywhere.
  • Print didn't import theme.css and had a hard-coded
    .wrap { max-width: 1200px; padding: 1.5rem }. Added local
    --content-max / --gutter tokens at the same values as theme.css and
    rewired .wrap to use them, so the wrap matches every other page.
  • Dashboard's mobile nav was at padding: 0 0.75rem (12px) while the
    content used the 16px gutter minimum; switched the mobile nav to
    var(--gutter) so logo + content stay flush on phones too.

Calendar (full-bleed grid, intentional) and admin (narrow 760px form column, intentional) were left alone per intent — they're not meant to sit in the 1240px rail.

author: akira-toriyama
body:
## What

Add `CONFIG_ZMK_BLE_AUTO_UNPAIR_ON_KEY_MISSING` (default `n`). When
enabled, the `security_changed` handler reacts to
`BT_SECURITY_ERR_PIN_OR_KEY_MISSING` by calling `bt_unpair` and
`bt_conn_disconnect`, so the next advert initiates a fresh pairing
exchange instead of looping on the same handshake failure.

## Why

In a split / dongle keyboard setup, if one side's bond is wiped
(partial settings reset, NVS corruption, or reflashing one peer
without rebonding the other), every subsequent reconnect ends in
`security_changed` with `PIN_OR_KEY_MISSING`. The connection stays
up but is unusable, and the loop is not recoverable without manually
wiping bonds on both sides and going through the pairing flow again.

The existing handler logs the error and otherwise does nothing,
which means there is no firmware-side recovery path for the
asymmetric-bond case that is easy to hit on dongle setups.

## How

The new branch sits inside the existing `else` arm of
`security_changed`, guarded by the Kconfig. When the peer reports
`PIN_OR_KEY_MISSING`, drop our half of the bond and disconnect with
`BT_HCI_ERR_AUTH_FAIL`. The endpoint goes back to discoverable +
unpaired, and the next advert/scan cycle re-establishes a fresh
pairing without user intervention.

Default-off so the current behaviour (surface the error, take no
action) is preserved for users who would rather notice and act
manually.

## Testing

Tested in production on a dongle-based BLE split
(XIAO BLE central + two `assimilator-bt` peripherals). Reproduced
the loop by wiping one peripheral's bond settings while the central
retains theirs; with the option enabled, the central self-recovers
into a fresh pair on the next reconnect attempt; with the option
disabled (or this patch absent), the loop persists until both bonds
are wiped manually.

Downstream use: [akira-toriyama/canon](https://github.com/akira-toriyama/canon)
runs this fix as an out-of-tree patch ([`patches/zmk/security-changed-auto-unpair.patch`](https://github.com/akira-toriyama/canon/blob/main/patches/zmk/security-changed-auto-unpair.patch))
pending this upstream PR.

## PR check-list

- [x] Branch has a [clean commit history](https://zmk.dev/docs/development/contributing/pull-requests#clean-commit-history)
- [ ] Additional tests are included, if changing behaviors/core code that is testable. *(no zmk-side test harness for BLE security handshakes; happy to add one if pointed at an existing pattern)*
- [x] Proper Copyright + License headers added to applicable files
- [x] [Pre-commit](https://zmk.dev/docs/development/local-toolchain/pre-commit) used to check formatting
- [ ] Includes any necessary [documentation changes](https://zmk.dev/docs/development/contributing/documentation). *(no public docs page on bond recovery semantics; can add a brief mention if maintainers prefer)*

## Summary
두 가지 콘솔 UX 명료화(사용자 요청):

기존의 합쳐진 메시지 "표시할 계정이 없습니다. (검색 결과 없음 또는 조회 권한 없음)" 를 순수 함수 `classifyAccountsEmpty()`로 분기:
- 클라이언트 **403 / `PERMISSION_DENIED`** → **"조회 권한이 없습니다."**
- 그 외 조회 에러 → "목록을 불러올 수 없습니다."

## What

Adds a curated catalog of well-known program templates a user can instantiate in one click, without the AI rewriting the structure.

author: iamjohnnymac
body:
## Why
The 2026-06-08 Ahrefs crawl flagged new Errors, all traced to the photo-recovery work (#173):
- **Page size exceeds Googlebot's 2 MB limit** (homepage) — new
- **Image file size too large** — 15 pages, all new
- **HTML file size too large** — homepage + `/happy-hour`

Verified live with `curl`: the homepage shipped **2.22 MB** of HTML (all 857 pubs' full objects in the RSC payload) and pub photos were hotlinked at up to **4800px (~208 KB each)**.

The real bulk wasn't the photos (~240 KB) — it was the full Pub enrichment that list/card views never render: `periods` (441 KB), editorial summaries (352 KB), 15 Google attributes (282 KB), opening-hours text (217 KB).

## What
New `src/lib/pubPhoto.ts`:
- **`resizeGooglePhoto()`** — swaps the lh3 size token (`=s4800-w1024` → `=w640`, ~208 KB → **~90 KB**, under the 100 KB threshold). Keeps the photo **hotlinked to Google** — their terms forbid re-hosting, so `next/image` is intentionally not used (honours the existing "plain img on purpose" comment at the render sites).
- **`slimPubForList()`** — drops list-irrelevant Places enrichment before serialising. Every dropped field is *optional* on `Pub`, so `SlimPub` stays assignable to `Pub` — **no component or prop-type changes**.

Applied:
- Homepage + suburb list payloads slimmed (suburb `getSuburbStory` + JSON-LD keep full data — only the client payload is slimmed).
- Photos resized at both render sites: pub detail + happy-hour listicle.

## Result (measured / estimated)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Homepage HTML | 2.22 MB | **~0.77 MB** |
| Venue photo | 208 KB | **90 KB** |

`/happy-hour` HTML stays ~835 KB by design (it renders photos + write-ups + hours), but its image transfer drops ~57%.

## Scope
Critical regression only. The other ~38 audit issues (meta/title hygiene, orphans, the intentional 622 `noindex` tier pages) are untouched.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 278 unit tests pass (+4 new in `pubPhoto.test.ts`)
- ESLint clean on touched files
- Full `next build` + e2e run in CI

Phase 2.5 page caching, file-driver friendly (no Redis/tags available on the shared host).

Cache helpers live on ProductManager (already autoloaded) to avoid a composer.json/dump-autoload change on deploy. Full suite: 8 pass, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (ExampleTest GET / => 500, fails identically on base).

author: amalshaji
body:
## #66 — Closing a query tab closes the whole app

The File menu used `PredefinedMenuItem::close_window`, which hard-binds `Cmd/Ctrl+W`. The native menu intercepts that accelerator before the webview receives it, so the in-app close-tab handler at `ConnectionDetails.tsx` never ran and closing a query tab closed the whole window.

- Custom **Close Tab** item on `Cmd/Ctrl+W` → emits `menu:close-tab` to the focused window; the frontend closes the active tab (falls back to closing the window when no tab is open).
- **Close Window** moved to `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+W`.
- Removed the now-redundant JS `Cmd+W` keydown branch (would double-close on platforms where the webview also receives the key) and its stale effect deps.
- Emits to the focused window, so it stays correct with multiple windows open.

## #83 — Unable to use the query editor

`dragDropEnabled` was `true` but the app never uses native file drop. On Linux/WebKitGTK the native drag-drop handler swallows pointer events over the webview, which makes the CodeMirror query editor unusable.

- Set `dragDropEnabled: false`. Window dragging via `startDragging()` is unaffected.

> Note: I couldn't view the reporter's screen recording, so the #83 root cause is a strong inference (same reporter as #66, likely on Linux; the flag is unused so the change is low-risk). Left as `Refs` rather than `Closes` so it can be confirmed on Linux before the issue is closed.

### Verification
- `cargo check` passes.
- `tsc --noEmit` introduces no new errors (the one pre-existing Redis `setState` type error is unchanged).

Closes #66
Refs #83

author: nicholaivogel
body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/probe-signet-mcp.ts`, a CI-friendly end-to-end smoke for the published `signet-mcp` stdio JSON-RPC server. Captures the manual probe flow that verified the issue #826 fix as a script that can run unattended against a live daemon.

## What it does

- Resolves `signet-mcp` from PATH, `$BUN_INSTALL/bin`, `~/.bun/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` — works for `bun add -g`, `npm install -g`, and the in-repo workspace symlink.
- Spawns the binary and drives a full MCP session: `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list` → five read-only `tools/call` invocations (`memory_list`, `knowledge_list_entities`, `mcp_server_list`, `signet_code_status`, `secret_list`).
- Asserts every response shape: serverInfo name + protocolVersion on `initialize`, non-empty catalog on `tools/list`, per-tool shape checks (memories array + stats, items array, GraphIQ status text marker, etc.).
- Filters non-JSON stdout lines (daemon plugin logs sometimes leak into stdout) before they reach a request waiter.
- Paces JSON-RPC frames with 250ms delays — `platform/daemon/src/mcp-stdio.ts` shuts down on stdin EOF, so a `cat <<EOF | signet-mcp` style pipe closes stdin too early and frames after the first one are lost.
- Exits 0 on success, 1 on validation failure, 2 on overall timeout.

## Wired in

`package.json` adds a script alias:
```
bun run probe:signet-mcp
```

CI consumers can run it as a post-install smoke: `bun add -g signetai@next && signet daemon start && bun run probe:signet-mcp`. Exits non-zero on any handshake, missing tool, malformed response, or daemon round-trip failure.

## Verification

- `bun run probe:signet-mcp` against the local daemon: all 5 tool calls pass
- `bunx biome check scripts/probe-signet-mcp.ts`: clean
- Existing `scripts/signet-mcp-stdio-smoke.test.ts` (the daemon-independent regression guard) still passes: 3/3

## Coverage split

- `scripts/signet-mcp-stdio-smoke.test.ts` — daemon-independent, asserts the wrapper package layout (bin/files, bundle shebang) and a single `initialize` handshake. Catches wrapper-shape regressions.
- `scripts/probe-signet-mcp.ts` — daemon-dependent, drives a full MCP session with real tool calls. Catches runtime contract regressions.

Both are kept; they cover different failure modes.

author: jiaqizho
body:
The cache changes are meant to stop every PR from creating its own Conan and Rust cache under `refs/pull/.../merge`, while still letting PR jobs reuse caches that already exist. The CI workflows now use explicit restore and save actions: restore runs for normal jobs, but save only runs on main when the primary key was not hit. The cache keys also include runner OS and architecture, so Linux and macOS builds do not share incompatible Conan or Rust artifacts. Release jobs are restore-only, so they can consume existing caches without publishing new ones.

This also adds a dedicated macOS C++ build job to cpp-ci.yml. It uses the normal cpp build path and runs make build, which keeps the mac build aligned with how the project is expected to build locally. The job is build-only and does not join the existing Linux unit-test artifact flow, so the current Linux build, upload, and test setup stays unchanged while macOS compatibility gets checked separately.

author: undivisible
body:
💡 **What:**
Optimized `evict_lru` in `src/v8_integration/snapshots.rs` to find the target eviction string key by leveraging a raw pointer to an inner `str`. This avoids making an unneeded heap allocation via `String::clone()`, as well as sidesteps an unneeded tuple allocation that computed the unused `bytecode.len()` for the target.

🎯 **Why:**
The previous code executed `.map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.bytecode.len()))` upon each call to `evict_lru`. LRU eviction frequently runs inside a tight loop when inserting large items if the cache is full. Both string clones and computing `bytecode.len()` here are unneeded allocations, slowing down cache evictions globally.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
In a benchmark creating 100k items and evicting 10k using iteration O(N) scans (using rustc -O), changing `.map(|(k, _)| (k.clone(), ...))` to `.map(|(k, _)| k.as_str() as *const str)` followed by a direct map removal, improved loop eviction times from ~430ms to ~407ms (~5% speedup per batch iteration). While scanning still dominates time via O(N) iteration, the constant overhead per iteration drops.

- Works on any instance regardless of the encounter type UUID
- Fully removed `CONSULTATION_ENCOUNTER_TYPE_UUID` from `constants.ts`, `encounterSessionService/index.ts`, and `@bahmni/services` barrel export

### Encounter Sorting Fix
- When multiple encounters exist in the session window, the resolver previously picked `encounters[0]` assuming FHIR `_lastUpdated` sort — which is unreliable
- Added `sortByMostRecent()` that sorts encounters by `period.start` descending before picking
- Applied to: current practitioner encounters, other provider encounters, and all-time practitioner encounters
- Removed the `console.warn` for multiple encounters (valid scenario, not a warning)

## Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| dev-lite: "New Consultation" never changed to "Edit Consultation" | Works — encounter type UUID resolved dynamically |
| dev-lite: All edit/stop buttons permanently disabled | Works — `canEditOrCreate` and `activeEncounterUuid` populated correctly |
| Standard with multiple encounters (e.g., Baby OfPavi): wrong encounter picked | Most recent encounter always selected via `period.start` sort |
| Standard with clean patients: worked | Still works — same UUID, just sourced dynamically |

## Root Cause

The `CONSULTATION_ENCOUNTER_TYPE_UUID` is auto-generated when OpenMRS creates the encounter type. Different instances have different UUIDs:
- Standard: `d34fe3ab-5e07-11ef-8f7c-0242ac120002`
- Dev-lite: `b9ccceaa-f496-11ed-b02c-0242ac150003`

The encounter session resolver searched for encounters matching this UUID. On dev-lite, it found 0 encounters → `canEditOrCreate = false` → all session-dependent features broken.

### Motivation
- Provide first-stage per-period P–Q flexibility scanning and temporal P0 trajectory-boundary tools for small IEEE test feeders using a LinDistFlow linearized model and YALMIP+Gurobi solvers. 
- Supply an adaptive-angle scanner to reduce redundant solves and improve boundary approximation efficiency compared with fixed-angle scans. 
- Add temporal boundary Step‑1 tooling (P0 power, adjacent-period ramp, cumulative exchange energy) and a prototype matrixized VG/VB decoupling (robust margins) workflow for conservative independent VG/VB limits. 

### Description
- Added single-period IEEE‑13 LinDistFlow P–Q scan: `ieee13_pq_flex_scan_lindisflow_yalmip_gurobi_v1.m` and an adaptive-scan variant `ieee13_pq_flex_scan_lindisflow_yalmip_gurobi_v1_1_adaptive_scan.m` implementing fixed-angle and adaptive support-function scans, result saving, plotting, and duplicate-point handling. 
- Added temporal P0 Step‑1 visualization and solvers: `ieee13_temp_p0_v1_1_step_plots.m` and `ieee13_temporal_p0_boundary_lindisflow_yalmip_gurobi_v1.m` for multi-period LinDistFlow boundary solves, plotting step/trajectory visualizations, ESS SOC handling, and CSV/MAT outputs. 
- Implemented matrixized network validation and VG/VB robust decoupling prototype in `ieee13_temp_p0_v1_2_decoup.m` including `build_network_matrices_lindisflow`, matrix validation vs original dispatch, `compute_robust_decoupled_limits`, and decoupled/coupled bound solvers and comparison plots. 
- Added a small MATPOWER-based IEEE‑9 P–Q flexibility scanner `ieee9_pq_flex_scan_yalmip_gurobi_v1.m` that computes finite-difference AC sensitivities and uses linearized models for per-period (and optional multi-period) scans, AC validation via MATPOWER, and comparison plots. 
- Added result directories placeholders (`results_*` with `.gitkeep`) and multiple helper functions in each script for building systems/time series, YALMIP problem setup, plotting, CSV/MAT export, and basic dependency checks for `YALMIP`, `Gurobi`, and where applicable `MATPOWER`.

### Testing
- No automated CI tests were executed as part of this PR; the scripts contain runtime dependency checks (`check_dependencies`) and will abort with a clear message if `YALMIP`, `Gurobi`, or `MATPOWER` (where required) are missing. 
- The code is organized to produce CSV/MAT and PNG outputs and prints status lines for each solve to aid manual smoke testing on a MATLAB environment with the required toolboxes and solvers. 
- Recommend running each script on a local MATLAB installation with `YALMIP` and `Gurobi` (and `MATPOWER` for the IEEE‑9 scanner) to validate end-to-end execution and AC PF validation where used. 
- No unit tests or regression tests were added; follow-up PRs should add CI-ready smoke tests or Matlab unit tests to validate solver outputs automatically.

author: trilamsr
body:
## Summary

Design spec for #1079 (regatta serve doesn't self-restart on binary update; operator-merged fixes stay dormant in running daemon).

Adopts **Approach A — supervisor-driven exit-on-update** from the 2026-06-08 research brief (`docs/engineer/research/2026-06-08-self-restart-on-binary-update.md`):

- A `binwatcher` goroutine polls `os.Executable()` mtime every `--binwatch-interval` (default 60s).
- On mtime-advance, emits `serve.binary_updated_detected` WARN.
- Under `--auto-restart-on-update=<delay>` (default 0 = log-only), arms a `time.AfterFunc(delay, stop)` where `stop` is the existing `signal.NotifyContext` cancel from `cmd/regatta/serve.go:164`.
- The existing graceful-shutdown path drains (`httpSrv.Shutdown`, cost-reconciler join), `runServe` returns 0, and the supervisor (`docker compose` `restart: unless-stopped`, systemd `Restart=always`, launchd `KeepAlive=true`) relaunches with the new bytes.

No new restart primitive, no SIGHUP collision (`SIGHUP` is already claimed by secrets cache + OPA reloader), no new dep.

## Rejected alternatives (with reopen triggers)

- **Approach B (`syscall.Exec` in-process re-exec)** — bypasses every subsystem's defer; FD handoff brittle; Windows is ENOSYS. Reopen when an operator deploys without any supervisor.
- **Approach C (`cloudflare/tableflip` zero-downtime FD handoff)** — ~2k LOC dep for a non-feature (self-host single-operator has no client behind `:8080`). Reopen on SLO incident attributable to the restart blip.
- **c3 sidecar (`cmd/regatta-watcher`)** — deferred. Container `/regatta` mtime does not advance on image rebuild (overlay FS); the watcher fires bare-metal only. Operator-facing doc says `docker compose up -d --build regatta`. Reopen when operator runs that ≥10×/week for ≥2 weeks.
- **Hash-based detection** — `make build` always advances mtime; hash adds 30-80 MB/min I/O for an edge case. Reopen on ≥1 "container restarted without binary change" incident in 30 days.

Per `feedback_default_simpler`.

## OSS prior art surveyed (cited with version + LICENSE URL)

nginx 1.27, PostgreSQL 17, kubelet (k8s 1.31), HashiCorp Vault 1.18, watchexec 2.2, nodemon 3.1, cloudflare/tableflip v1.2.3 — table in §Design.

## What

   `sha256:a2955656…` → `sha256:c176aeb1…` (Docker Hub `:latest`, built 2026-06-08).

2. **Add `.github/workflows/auto-tag.yaml`** — on every push to `main` (i.e. every merged PR), create the next `v0.0.<patch>` annotated tag pointing at the merge commit. It reads the highest existing `v0.0.*` tag and increments the patch (so the first run after merge produces `v0.0.217`).

## Workflow details

- Trigger: `push: branches: [main]` (post-merge only — trusted code, no `pull_request` trigger).
- Permissions: `contents: write` (default `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes the tag).
- Idempotent (skips if the computed tag already exists) and serialized via a `concurrency` group so two quick merges can't race the same version.
- Tagger identity: `github-actions[bot]`.

## ⚠️ Deployment note

compose-manager's `MIN_TAG_AGE_HOURS` gate is keyed on the **commit** date (>2h, see `docs/deployment.md`). An auto-created tag points at the fresh merge commit, so it becomes **deployable ~2h after merge** — no backdating. For an immediate deploy, keep using the `backdate-tag` flow instead; the two coexist (auto-tag just guarantees every merge gets a version).
