author: noe-charmet
body: Introduces the single source of step-advance logic for the per-step runner protocol (T2), operating directly on the existing `steps` table with no HTTP, token, or Temporal coupling: - `nextStepForJob(jobId)` — returns the lowest-position non-terminal step and marks it `running`. Idempotent: a retried pull returns the already-`running` step rather than skipping ahead. - `recordStepResult({jobId, stepId, status, error})` — guarded never-downgrade report; on `failed` it cancels the remaining steps, and it signals `{jobFinished, status}` once every step is terminal. ## Why The runner protocol is moving from job-atomic (ship a whole job, run all steps locally, report once via `/complete`) to per-step pull/report, so steps transition `pending → running → terminal` one at a time for live status and so some steps can be decided at run time. T2 is the pure domain core of that flip. ## Notes for review - **Atomicity / crash-safety:** a `failed` report is two writes (mark step failed, then cancel siblings). Both `nextStepForJob` and `recordStepResult` wrap their work in one `db().transaction()` and open with a `SELECT … ORDER BY position FOR UPDATE` locked read (shared lock order). This makes the failed path atomic — a crashed-then-retried report can never strand the remaining steps `pending` — and prevents concurrent double-dispatch. The one-runner-per-leased-job invariant is the primary serialization; `FOR UPDATE` is defense-in-depth (covered by a concurrent-pull race test). - **Protocol guard:** `recordStepResult` rejects a result for a never-dispatched (`pending`) step (`StepNotRunningError`) and for unknown/cross-job step ids (`StepNotFoundError`); a duplicate/retried report on a terminal step is an idempotent no-op. - **DRY:** `cancelRemainingSteps` delegates to the existing guarded sweep `bulkUpdateStepStatuses` (now `tx`-aware). The new DB primitives are intentionally **not** exported from the `db` barrel — callers go through the core service. - **Dormant:** nothing wires these into a runtime path yet (routes/auth → T3, Temporal cutover → T6), so this is safe and reversible. Changeset is `patch` (internal, no consumer impact yet). Refs ENG-396 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a per-step progression domain service to `@shipfox/api-workflows` for the T2 runner protocol. It provides idempotent step pull/report with atomic failure handling and stays dormant until wired; supports ENG-396. - **New Features** - `nextStepForJob(jobId)` returns the in-flight or next pending step and marks it running; serialized with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. Unknown job → `JobNotFoundError`. - `recordStepResult({jobId, stepId, status, error})` applies results, cancels remaining steps on failure, never downgrades, and returns `{jobFinished:false}` or `{jobFinished:true, status}`. - Completion: all steps succeeded → `succeeded`; any failure or all-cancelled → `failed` (no vacuous success). - Infra/exports: `withTransaction`; tx-only DB primitives (`getStepsByJobIdForUpdate`, `markStepRunning`, `applyStepResult`, `cancelRemainingSteps`); `bulkUpdateStepStatuses` is tx-aware; export `nextStepForJob`, `recordStepResult`, and types; add `JobNotFoundError`, `StepNotFoundError`, `StepNotRunningError`. Tests cover idempotency and concurrent pulls. Written for commit 0b925ad59dbb7c0c1436768f7bb1c98a1b67780e. Summary will update on new commits.

## What

Azure-native parity with the Fabric / Power BI Admin portal's **Embed codes** (F22) and **Organizational visuals** (F23) surfaces — with **no Microsoft Fabric or Power BI workspace dependency**.

### F22 — Embed codes
An embed code is a read-only **Blob Storage user-delegation SAS URL** (signed with the Console UAMI's Microsoft Entra credentials via `getUserDelegationKey` — never the account key) over a real Loom embed-manifest blob in the DLZ `org-visuals` container.
- **Create** → uploads a manifest blob + mints a loadable signed URL (shown in a copyable field).
- **Revoke** → deletes the backing blob (URL 404s immediately) + flips Cosmos status to `revoked`.
- **GET** lazily re-mints SAS for codes within 24h of expiry (Azure user-delegation max is 7 days).
- List with status badge, created-by, expiry, copy/open/revoke actions.

### F23 — Organizational visuals
- **Upload** a real `.pbiviz` bundle (stored as a Blob) with name + version.
- List with version, size, uploaded-by; **enable/disable tenant-wide** via Switch; **delete** (removes blob + metadata).

## Why
Completes Fabric-parity for the two tenant-admin reporting surfaces using Azure Blob Storage + Cosmos only — honoring `no-fabric-dependency.md` (Azure-native default), `no-vaporware.md` (real backends, honest gate), and `ui-parity.md` (LoomDataTable + Fluent v9, full functionality).

## Changes
- `lib/azure/adls-client.ts`: `uploadBlob` (block-blob) + `generateReadSasUrl` (user-delegation SAS, sovereign-cloud correct).
- `lib/azure/cosmos-client.ts`: `embed-codes` + `org-visuals` containers (PK `/tenantId`) + accessors + `KNOWN_CONTAINER_IDS`.

body:
This fixes async Redis Cluster node connection handling so acquired connections are returned to the per-node free queue even when write-side setup fails. `ClusterNode.execute_command()` and `ClusterNode.execute_pipeline()` now place lazy disconnect and `send_packed_command()` inside the release-guarded `try` block.

The cleanup path also now releases the connection even if the final `disconnect_if_needed()` raises. This prevents a failed disconnect during cleanup from stranding the connection in `_connections` and eventually exhausting `max_connections`.

Regression tests cover both direct command execution and node pipeline execution with `max_connections=1`. The tests simulate write failures and disconnect failures, then verify the same connection is returned to `_free` and can be reused instead of leaking.

Fixes #4110

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes connection lifecycle on error paths in async cluster command/pipeline execution; incorrect cleanup could still leak or double-release connections, but scope is limited to ClusterNode pool handling and is covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **async Redis Cluster** per-node connection pooling so acquired connections are always returned to `_free`, even when work fails before a response is read.
> 
> `ClusterNode.execute_command()` and `execute_pipeline()` now wrap lazy disconnect, `send_packed_command`, and response handling in a **`try`/`finally`** cleanup path. **`release(connection)`** runs in a nested `finally` so it still executes if **`disconnect_if_needed()`** raises during teardown—avoiding stranded connections and **`MaxConnectionsError`** under **`max_connections=1`** (fixes #4110).

author: grover-c13
body:
## What changed

The verdict cache keyed only request fields (`unwind`, `ua`, `solver`,
`externalSatPath`, `msl`, `timeout`). Any flag hard-coded in `Jbmc.args()`
(or driven by a `-Dbmc.*` property) was absent from the key, so it could
change a verdict yet be served from a stale cache entry — the recent
`--slice-formula` / `--drop-unused-functions` flags bypassed the key
entirely and relied only on the coarse runtime-identity bump.

- Factor the verdict-relevant flag set into one builder
  (`Jbmc.appendVerdictRelevantFlags`) used both to assemble the real jbmc
  command and to derive a canonical flag signature
  (`Jbmc.verdictRelevantFlags`). `VerdictCache.computeKey` hashes that
  signature, so the key is built from the same place as the command and
  cannot drift from the flags actually passed — a future hard-coded or
  `-Dbmc.*`-driven flag is captured automatically.
- The signature **includes** every verdict-changing flag: `--unwind`,
  `--unwinding-assertions`, `--max-nondet-string-length`, and the full
  solver selection (`--external-sat-solver` / `--smt2`+`--external-smt2-solver`
  / `--z3` / `--boolector` / `--cvc4` / `--cvc5` / `--sat-solver`).
- The signature **excludes** the machine/shard-volatile and non-verdict
  parts: the executable path, the `--classpath` value (its content is keyed
  via the reachable-cone digest; the path varies per shard), the
  `--function`/entry (keyed separately), and the pure output/UI flags
  (`--json-ui` / `--trace` / `--verbosity`). The non-flag inputs the
  signature can't carry — the string-refinement mode and the per-proof
  timeout — stay explicit per-field updates. The existing per-field updates
  are kept as belt-and-suspenders.
- Clean the stray NUL byte that made `VerdictCache.kt` a "binary" file: the
  cone memo-key separator was a literal NUL; it is now a space (no runtime
  behavior change).
- Tests: add flag-signature coverage to `VerdictCacheTest` — the signature
  includes the verdict flags and excludes the classpath/entry/UI parts, a
  verdict-relevant flag change perturbs both the signature and the key, and
  a volatile-only change (a different classpath PATH, same flags) does not.

`./gradlew -p core :bmc-runtime:test --tests org.bmc4j.engine.VerdictCacheTest`
and `./gradlew -p core :bmc-models-conformance:test` both pass locally.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
## Summary

Optimize `src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py` so per-bar regime scoring can be re-enabled on the live VM without re-triggering the 2026-06-09 CPU wedge (BL-20260609-001 / MB-20260609-001).

**Tier-2** (live-path file `src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py`). **Do not merge until operator OK.**

## Context

On 2026-06-09 the live trader's 2-core OCI VM wedged ~30-40 min at 95-100% CPU. The operator-approved A/B (`REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=1`, #3075) confirmed per-bar regime scoring was the driver: with it OFF, CPU dropped to 0-10% across 18 min (#3076-#3078). The kill-switch is currently ON on the live VM, which pauses the strong regime heads' per-bar track-record accrual and blocks the yz-1h shadow→advisory promotion (MB-20260527-004).

## Root cause

`emit_regime_bar_predictions` did the expensive work **PER predictor PER 60s tick**:
- `connector_for_symbol()` rebuilt an exchange client per call
- `fetch_candles()` made a network REST call per call (Bybit / IBKR)
- `feature_row_for_predictor()` recomputed 4 range-vol estimators per call

For N shadow regime heads sharing M unique `(symbol, timeframe)` pairs (typical N=8, M=3-5), the work ran N times per tick instead of M times per bar close. A 1h-cadence head paid the fetch cost 60×/hour when 1× suffices. Same cost class as the sim/engine.py O(n²) fix from MB-20260531-001, but on the live path.

## Fix

Three changes in `src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py` (the live-path file). Per-bar evidence still accrues identically — same dedup key, same `shadow_predictions.jsonl` writes, same `feature_row_for_predictor` shape per head — but bounded per-tick cost:

1. **Group predictors by `(symbol, timeframe)`** so multiple heads on the same market share ONE fetch + ONE shared `closes` view per tick. The per-head `feature_row_for_predictor` still runs (each head has its own frozen `edges`/`labels`/`vol_feature_column`) but over already-fetched data.
2. **Wall-clock fetch gate** (`_BAR_SECONDS - _FETCH_GATE_BUFFER_S`, 30s buffer). A 1h head is fetched ~1×/hour instead of 60×; a 5m head ~1×/5min instead of 5×. **A failed fetch does NOT arm the gate**, so a transient exchange blip never silences a head for a full bar duration.
3. **Cache the exchange client per call** in `_live_fetch_fn` so BTCUSDT 5m and 15m share one Bybit client (the IB path's connect-probe + circuit-breaker is real cost too).

## Backward compatibility

- Same module-level dedup (`_REGIME_BAR_SEEN`) and same predictor cache.
- New module-level wall cache (`_REGIME_FETCH_WALL`) with a `wall_cache` injection parameter mirroring `seen`'s test-injection shape, plus a `now` callable for clock control in tests.
- `REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED` kill-switch unchanged.
- Observe-only contract preserved: only `ShadowPredictor.predict`, never the order path; never raises.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/runtime/test_regime_bar_scoring.py` — 28 pass (was 14)
- [x] `ruff check src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py tests/runtime/test_regime_bar_scoring.py` — clean
- [x] New `TestFetchGate` (6 cases): default-true, unknown-tf permissive, within-gate-false, past-gate-true, 1h gate longevity, no-arm-on-failure
- [x] New `TestPredictorGrouping` (2 cases): two heads same (sym,tf) → one fetch; different (sym,tf) → independent fetches
- [x] Existing `TestEmit` tests updated to pass `wall_cache={}` for hermeticity; the one test that calls emit twice with different bar timestamps (`test_new_bar_scores_again`) now advances a simulated clock past the gate
- [ ] **Operator gate**: review + approve this Tier-2 change
- [ ] Merge + `pull-and-deploy` to the live VM (ict-trader-live.service)
- [ ] `set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0` (operator-gated) to re-enable
- [ ] Re-run the CPU A/B: `status-check` + poll `/api/diag/status::vm_health.cpu` for ~20 min across several bar closes (5m, 15m, 1h) — PASS = CPU stays bounded (load << 2.0), heartbeat keeps ticking, the strong heads resume emitting per-bar shadow records
- [ ] Resolve MB-20260609-001 with the before/after CPU evidence; update BL-20260609-001
- [ ] Unblocks MB-20260529-001 / MB-20260527-004 (yz-1h soak)

## Out of scope (separate concerns, intentionally not bundled)

- **cgroup `CPUWeight` / `Nice` on `ict-trader-live.service`** for defense-in-depth — keep the optimisation PR focused; can land as a separate small deploy-side PR if the operator wants the extra isolation.
- Per-head cadence coarsening (e.g. "only score the 1h head when its own 1h bar closes") — the wall-clock gate already collapses 1h-head fetches to ~1×/hour, so this would be a marginal additional win on top, not required for the CPU fix.

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Bakes AI risk review into the **synchronous** elevation request flow as a first-class, audited gate. Previously `ztna-api`'s `createRequest` trusted a client-supplied `risk_level` and never called the model; now every request is scored server-side (Bonsai-8B via `aiclient`), the verdict + rationale + inputs are persisted for audit, and the request transitions `requested → ai_reviewed` before routing. The gate is **fail-OPEN for advisory scoring** (model down → deterministic `medium` / `needs_review`, never auto-approve) and **fail-CLOSED where it gates authorization** (high-risk approval requires step-up MFA).

### Backend

- **New FSM state `ai_reviewed`** (`state_machine.go`): `requested → ai_reviewed → approved/denied → provisioning → provisioned → active → expired`. Direct `requested → approved/denied/cancelled` edges retained so the JML lane, async workflow engine, and pre-WS5 rows keep working. Illegal transitions still rejected by `allowedTransitions`.
- **`RiskReviewService`** (`risk_review_service.go`): calls the agent, strictly schema-validates/normalizes model output, persists an immutable `AccessRiskVerdict`, and writes the audited `requested → ai_reviewed` transition. The client can no longer self-assert risk — `RiskLevel`/`RiskFactors` are dropped from the create path:
  ```go
  review, err := riskReview.ReviewRequest(ctx, RiskReviewInput{...})
  // unreachable agent → verdict{score: medium, recommendation: needs_review, degraded: true}
  // a "sensitive" resource tag always forces high_risk
  ```
- **Step-up gate** in `approveRequest`: a high-risk verdict requires `MFASatisfied` read from the **verified token claims** (never the request body) — returns `403` otherwise.
- **Anomaly hooks**: approved/auto-approved elevations are fed to the anomaly-detection skill **out of band** — `runAnomalyHook` launches a detached, timeout-bounded goroutine (`context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30s)`, mirroring the `internal/gateway/*` pattern) so the advisory round trip never adds latency to the approve/create response. Observations persist as advisory `AccessRequestAnomalyFlag` rows (fail-open, never change FSM state) and surface on the request.
- Every new table/row is **workspace-scoped**; verdict + anomaly tables are append-only. New migration `0012` (auto-embedded). AI client wired in `main.go` (`NewAIClientFromEnv`; unconfigured → fail-open fallback).
- **Self-service contract fix**: aligned the handler binding with the long-standing service contract — `role` is required, `target_user_id` is optional and defaults to the authenticated requester (it was inconsistently the reverse).

### Python agent

`access_risk_assessment` emits a schema-validated `recommendation` (`auto_approve_eligible` / `needs_review` / `high_risk`). It mirrors the Go `lifecycle.recommendationFor` **exactly**: only the canonical `sensitive_resource` factor forces `high_risk`; an `elevated_resource:*` tag (prod/pii/…) only bumps the score band — so a prod read-only request is `needs_review`, matching Go. The skill emits the canonical `sensitive_resource` factor for the `sensitive` tag so both sides share one vocabulary (Go de-dupes). The Go control plane re-derives the authoritative recommendation, so this field never drives an authorization decision.

### UI (`ui/`)

- **Create flow**: collects optional `resource_tags` / `duration_hours`; on submit shows the AI risk panel **inline** (score, factors, recommendation, rationale) — never silently auto-approves.
- **Approver view**: risk rationale + anomaly flags, with the **approve button gated** behind step-up MFA for a high-risk verdict (the control plane enforces `403` regardless; the UI pre-empts it).
- Risk/recommendation/anomaly **badges** (ok/warn/danger) throughout; `riskScoreTone` shared via `lib/format`. SN360 tokens, all **12 locales**, code-split lazy routes (`RiskPanel` is its own chunk).

### Tests (all green locally)

`go build/vet/test ./...` (incl. `-race`), `golangci-lint` (0 issues on changed dirs), `tsc -b`, `eslint . --max-warnings 0`, `vite build`, and the Python `pytest` suite (90) + `ruff` + `mypy`. Coverage: verdict persisted, fail-open fallback to needs-review, malformed-output normalization, FSM incl. illegal-transition rejection, high-risk requires human + step-up, self-service target default, role-required, cross-tenant isolation, and Python↔Go recommendation alignment (prod read-only → needs_review). The `aiclient` transport is mocked in tests (documented test-only escape hatch).

body:
PR Summary by Qodo

feat: add active development time engine and ROI ranking ✨ Enhancement 🕐 40+ Minutes

Walkthroughs

User Description
工具叫「Agent-ROI」卻只算成本、沒有 ROI。人們用 AI 開發時最在意的價值其實是**時間**——「這個東西花了我 2 小時 + \$40，值得嗎」。這個 PR 把**實際開發時間**變成一級維度，並讓成本與時間對照。 ## 核心：active-time 引擎（`core/active_time.py`） 天真的首尾相減無用——session 常開著過夜，把時間灌水約 **48 倍**（真實資料 1,667h vs 實際約 35h）。改成**加總回合之間的間隔、排除閒置區段**。 閒置閾值**由資料導出，不寫死「5 分鐘」**（每個人工作節奏不同）。在每位使用者**自己的** gap 分布上，結合兩個純數學、零依賴的估計量取較大者： - **Otsu 自然分界**（在 log-gap 上找「工作群」與「離開群」之間的谷底） - **第 90 百分位數** 實測落在約 6.7 分鐘——正好是「agent 連續工作」主峰（中位間隔約 8 秒）與「人離開」長尾（數小時）之間的谷底。動手前我在真實資料上**實測比較過三種候選**才定案：raw Otsu 會貼主峰砍掉正常思考間隔，p90 兜底救回。 ## 串接整個 stack - `SessionSummary` 新增 `active_seconds` + 計算欄位 `active_minutes` / `usd_per_hour`；新 `TopicROI` 聚合每主題的成本 vs 時間。 - `Service.roi_by_topic` + `db.active_time_by_session`（閾值每個時間窗只導出一次，確保所有 session 同基準）。 - **CLI**：新增 `agent-roi roi`（標出最高 \$/hr）；`sessions` 加 Active 與 \$/hr 欄。 - **API**：新增 `GET /api/roi`；sessions/detail 帶上 active time。 - **Web**：新 ROI 頁（成本 vs 時間、燒錢最兇者標紅）、session modal 顯示時間、11 語系 i18n（8 個真譯）。 ## 順手補上 - 上個 PR 漏記的 `min_topic_sessions` 寫進 `configuration.md` / `.zh.md`。 - 兩份 README 更新。 ## 實測（真實資料） | topic | 成本 | 活躍時間 | \$/hr | |---|---|---|---| | token pypi github | \$219 | 114.7m | **\$115** 🔥 | | reports analyst pdf | \$128 | 106.4m | \$72 | | gemini kiro session | \$42 | 71.8m | \$35 | ## 驗證 - `ruff` ✅ / `mypy` ✅ (29 files) / `pytest` ✅ (86，含 active-time 引擎 8 + service 整合 2) - `web tsc` ✅ / `npm run build` ✅ - `/api/roi` smoke test 回 200、資料正確 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
AI Description 
• Adds core/active_time.py: estimates active dev time from inter-turn gaps, excluding idle spans
  via a data-derived threshold.
• Threads active time through models/DB/service, exposing active_minutes and $/hr for sessions
  and topics.
• Adds ROI surfaces across CLI (agent-roi roi), API (GET /api/roi), and web (new ROI page +
  session modal).
• Updates i18n (11 locales) and documents min_topic_sessions plus README usage examples.
Diagram
```mermaid graph TD CLI["CLI: agent-roi roi"] --> SVC["Service.roi_by_topic"] --> DB["db.active_time_by_session"] --> AT["core/active_time\nOtsu+p90"] API["API: /api/roi"] --> SVC --> MOD["Models\nSessionSummary/TopicROI"] WEB["Web: ROIPage"] --> API subgraph Legend direction LR _ui["UI/CLI"] ~~~ _svc["Service"] ~~~ _core["Core algo"] end ```
High-Level Assessment
The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Persist active_seconds in the database - ➕ Avoids recomputing gap distributions on every sessions/roi request - ➕ Can support historical analysis without full rescans - ➖ Requires schema migration/backfill - ➖ Stored values can become stale as more data changes the derived threshold - ➖ Adds complexity to ingest/update flows
2. Use a fixed idle threshold (e.g., 5–10 minutes) - ➕ Simpler implementation and easier to reason about - ➕ No distribution fitting edge cases - ➖ Non-robust across users with different interaction rhythms - ➖ Over/under-counts work when sessions are left open or when users pause to think
**Recommendation:** Keeping the threshold data-driven (Otsu on log-gaps with a p90 floor) is a strong strategic choice that matches the product goal (ROI grounded in real time). The only meaningful architectural alternative is persisting active time for performance; given the project’s offline/single-user nature and the desire for consistent, window-derived thresholds, recomputing on demand is a reasonable default for now.

File Changes

Enhancement (13)
app.py Expose ROI ranking via 'GET /api/roi' +6/-0
>Expose ROI ranking via 'GET /api/roi' > >
>• Adds an '/api/roi' endpoint that windows by since/until and returns 'svc.roi_by_topic()' results.
>
> >src/agent_roi/api/app.py
main.py Add 'roi' command and show Active + $/hr in session list +61/-2
>Add 'roi' command and show Active + $/hr in session list > >
>• Replaces the sessions table’s token column with Active time and $/hr. Adds a new 'agent-roi roi' command that ranks topics and highlights the steepest $/hr burn rate.
>
> >src/agent_roi/cli/main.py
active_time.py Implement adaptive active-time estimation (Otsu + p90) +148/-0
>Implement adaptive active-time estimation (Otsu + p90) > >
>• Introduces a dependency-free engine to compute active seconds by summing inter-turn gaps under an adaptive idle threshold. Derives the threshold from the user’s gap distribution as 'max(otsu(log-gaps), p90)' with a small-sample fallback.
>
> >src/agent_roi/core/active_time.py
models.py Add TopicROI model; add active time + $/hr computed fields +49/-0
>Add TopicROI model; add active time + $/hr computed fields > >
>• Adds 'TopicROI' for per-topic ROI rows. Extends 'SessionSummary' with 'active_seconds' plus computed 'active_minutes' and 'usd_per_hour' fields.
>
> >src/agent_roi/core/models.py
service.py Compute active time for sessions and aggregate ROI by topic +61/-3
>Compute active time for sessions and aggregate ROI by topic > >
>• Enriches session summaries with 'active_seconds' from 'db.active_time_by_session' (threshold derived once per window). Adds 'roi_by_topic' aggregation and includes active time in session detail responses.
>
> >src/agent_roi/core/service.py
db.py Add 'active_time_by_session' window pass over interaction timestamps +39/-0
>Add 'active_time_by_session' window pass over interaction timestamps > >
>• Fetches '(session_id, timestamp)' rows, builds per-session timestamp lists, derives a single window threshold, then returns per-session active seconds plus the threshold used.

author: luongdev
body:
This is the **relaypoint half** of desk's `m1-observability-foundation` change (O.4), adopting the shared logging + trace-correlation contract (ADR-0011). It completes the **cross-module golden vector** and the **NATS subscribe-side traceparent** propagation.

## What's here
- **`internal/obs`** — a conforming twin of desk's FIXED obs. `obs.go`, `trace.go`, and `testdata/golden.json` are **byte-identical** to desk's `origin/change/m1-observability-foundation`:
  - slog JSON handler, canonical schema `ts,level,msg,service,env,trace_id,span_id,request_id,tenant_id,user`; `ts` = RFC3339Nano UTC; **lowercase levels** via `ReplaceAttr`; `service`/`env` (`OBS_ENV`, default `dev`) base fields.
  - `TraceContext` + W3C traceparent parse/validate (version 00, non-zero 32-hex trace / 16-hex span, 2-hex flags, length-bound) / format; `crypto/rand` ids that can never be all-zero; `FromInbound` reuses a valid trace id + mints a child span.
  - context helpers: `WithTrace/TraceFromContext`, `WithLogger/Logger` (base fallback, never nil/panic), `WithRequestID/RequestID`, `WithCorrelation`, `InjectTraceparent`, `ContextFromTraceparent`, idempotent `StartSpan`.
- **No HTTP server** in relaypoint (the router is NATS), so `http.go` and the **chi dependency are omitted** — only the NATS + logger + trace pieces are ported. `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged (obs is stdlib-only).

## Wiring
- `cmd/router/main.go`: `slog.SetDefault(obs.New("relaypoint-router"))`; each received NATS message seeds its context from the publisher's `traceparent` header via `obs.ContextFromTraceparent` and derives a correlated logger via `obs.WithCorrelation` — the **subscribe side** of `// @spec:obs.nats-traceparent-propagated`. A missing/malformed header mints a fresh trace (never a drop).
- `internal/signaling`: `HandleCommand` emits one correlated boundary log via `obs.Logger(ctx)`, carrying the publisher's `trace_id`.
- `scripts/check-logging.sh` (`// @spec:obs.no-adhoc-logging`, copied from desk; scope adapted to relaypoint's `internal/ cmd/` layout) wired into a new `go-ci` workflow that runs build/vet/gofmt/test -race + the gate.

## `// @spec` ids covered
- `obs.cross-module-golden-vector`
- `obs.nats-traceparent-propagated` (subscribe side + missing-header fresh trace)
- `obs.log-is-json-schema`, `obs.label-cardinality-split`, `obs.traceparent-malformed-treated-as-absent`, `obs.logger-fallback`, `obs.span-end-idempotent`
- `obs.no-adhoc-logging` (gate script + CI)

## Verification (relaypoint module, `GOWORK=off`)
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `gofmt -l .` — clean (empty)
- `go test ./... -race` — all packages ok

author: hayee-bhatti
body:
The framework already produces a consolidated report for a local sequential
run. This brings the same idea to the parallel CI workflow: after a run, the
aggregate job now produces one consolidated report covering every matrix
target (PG x family x arch), instead of only per-target reports you'd open
one by one.

The report shows per-(target, component, container) results with run-wide
totals and a header describing what the run actually covered (PG versions,
families, arches, components, repo, mode). It links back to each target's
existing detailed report, so nothing about the per-target or local reports
changes.

A couple of things it makes explicit:
* A green matrix target means the workflow completed, not that every test
  passed. The report shows the real pass/fail/skip per row and flags
  report issues (missing, unparseable, or empty reports).
* A target that resolved no containers is shown as "no containers selected"
  and kept out of the real test totals, rather than looking like skipped
  tests.

author: zrbecker
body:
Capstone for milestone #7's north star (ONE binary). After #896/#898 there were **two** binaries both named `boule`; this collapses them into a single user-facing binary and adds the CI lane that finally covers it.

## Before → After

**Before**
- `boule-cli` `[[bin]] name="boule"` — `init/start/key/config/snapshot/reconfig/rotation/endpoint` (+ reth-gated `genesis/faucet/rpc-proxy`); reth-SDK-free, CI-covered.
- `boule-bundle` `[[bin]] name="boule"` — `node` (reth in-process); CI-EXCLUDED, verified only by a local `smoke.sh`.

**After**
- `boule-cli` becomes a **library**: the reth-free `cli::Command` tree (the single source of truth) + the `testnet` driver bin. There is **no `boule` bin here anymore**.
- `boule-bundle` `[[bin]] name="boule"` is the **ONE** binary. Its `main.rs` flattens `boule-cli`'s `cli::Command` (built with the `reth` feature) alongside `node` via clap `#[command(flatten)]`, so the single binary hosts **every** subcommand. The reth-free subcommands are reused verbatim — not duplicated.

The root workspace still **never compiles the reth SDK** in its normal `build`/`clippy`/`test`/`deny`; `boule-cli`-as-lib stays reth-free. Only the new bundle lane (and local bundle builds) link reth.

## Unified `boule` subcommand surface
```
node init start key config snapshot reconfig rotation endpoint genesis faucet rpc-proxy
```
(`boule --help` lists all 12.)

## CI
- **New `bundle` lane** in `ci.yml` — *"Unified boule binary (reth in-process)"* — the **only** lane that builds reth. It builds the unified binary, asserts the full subcommand surface, runs the relocated CLI integration tests against `CARGO_BIN_EXE_boule`, and runs the single-process `boule node` smoke (`--ignored`). Path-gated via the `Detect changes` job's new `bundle` output to the `bundle/reth-node/reth/cli/consensus/node/core/transport-libp2p` crates (+ the workflow). Reuses the `install-solc` action, Swatinem cache (`prefix-key: bundle`), and the clang/bindgen libclang workaround.
- `smoke.yml` now builds the bundle workspace (the `smoke_sweep` sweep moved there).

## Tests + scripts (north star: zero loose `.sh`)
- Relocated `crates/boule-cli/tests/*` → `crates/boule-bundle/tests/`; the bundle gains a `testnet` bin so `CARGO_BIN_EXE_testnet` resolves.
- Folded `crates/boule-bundle/smoke.sh` into a Rust integration test (`tests/bundle_smoke.rs`) that provisions entirely through the unified binary's own subcommands — `boule genesis dev` + `boule init` + `boule genesis bls-pop` (replacing the deleted `gen-genesis`/`gen-bls-genesis` bins) — then runs `boule node` and asserts blocks commit. **Deleted `smoke.sh`.**
- **Deleted `crates/boule-reth/run-reth.sh`** (superseded by `boule node`); updated `node-demo.md` / `join-testnet.md` / `README.md` to use the unified `boule node`.

## Summary
- Make `neo` the default theme (`DEFAULT_THEME`), so new visitors land on the redesigned look.
- One-time migration: existing users with a saved `theme` cookie are forced to `neo` once, tracked by a `theme_neo_default` flag cookie. After the migration their later theme choice is respected and never overridden again.

## Details
- `registry.ts` — `DEFAULT_THEME` flipped to `neo`; added `THEME_MIGRATION_COOKIE_NAME` (`theme_neo_default`).
- `init.ts` — pre-hydration init script now checks the migration flag. If unset, it forces `neo`, writes the `theme` cookie, and sets the flag (once per user). If already migrated, it reads the saved theme as before.

The migration runs synchronously before hydration, so there's no flash of the old theme.

body:
## What changed

- Build a local `quickpizza-mobile-local:ci` Docker image before the Android telemetry runtime starts.
- Point Docker Compose at that local image instead of `ghcr.io/grafana/quickpizza-mobile-local:latest`.
- Emit the native iOS simulator `.app` path as an absolute path, matching the Flutter and React Native iOS app outputs.

## Why

The manually approved scheduled run `27192828350` failed after all mobile builds completed:

- Android failed immediately in `Start QuickPizza backend (Docker Compose)`.
- iOS failed immediately in `Install iOS apps and run e2e tests`.

The Android workflow currently pulls `ghcr.io/grafana/quickpizza-mobile-local:latest`, but anonymous GHCR access for that package is denied. Building the image locally avoids package visibility/token drift and avoids mutable `latest` behavior.

The iOS native app build step ran from `Mobiles/ios` and wrote `app_path` as a relative `DerivedData/...` path. The later install step runs from the repository root, so that relative path points at the wrong directory. Writing an absolute path fixes the handoff.

## Verification

- Parsed `.github/workflows/mobile_demo_telemetry.yaml` with the Ruby YAML parser.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Could not fetch raw GitHub job logs/artifacts because the API requires repo admin/auth for this repository, but job step metadata and timings were available via the API.

body:
## Summary

A 3-agent audit (content.js security, Data Loader correctness, React state/bridge) surfaced several issues. Verified each against the real code and fixed the genuine ones:

| Severity | Area | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CRITICAL** | Data Loader | Unbounded live-log memory (1.10.7 regression) → tab crash on large imports (O(n²) spread + ~1GB retained) | Lightweight `fullLog` ref + bounded 2000-row state buffer |
| **HIGH** | content.js | CRLF/changeset injection via upsert key value in multipart `$batch` | Strip control chars; PK values reduced to GUID chars |
| **HIGH** | Data Loader | Final Import Log fabricated from success counts (synthetic rows) | Built from real per-row log; Download Log exports full set with columns |

author: flora-li-builder
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the `competitor-profiling` skill to better support environments where Firecrawl is available but DataForSEO is not.

The main goal is to avoid treating these runs as simple “quick scans” when Firecrawl can still provide high-quality official website content. Instead, the skill now distinguishes between:

- Firecrawl-powered content scans
- Missing traditional SEO/backlink metrics due to DataForSEO being unavailable
- Optional AI SEO / citation readiness analysis when relevant

## Changes

- Added a Firecrawl-enabled workflow for competitor profiling
  - Uses Firecrawl to map competitor sites
  - Scrapes high-value official pages such as homepage, pricing, features, docs, use cases, customers, case studies, integrations, blog, changelog, security, and enterprise pages
  - Saves raw Firecrawl outputs under `raw/firecrawl/{competitor-slug}/{date}/`

- Clarified behavior when DataForSEO is unavailable
  - Marks traditional SEO metrics as unavailable
  - Avoids inventing keyword, backlink, traffic, authority, or ranking metrics
  - Writes a clear note to `raw/seo/not-available.json`
  - Uses “Firecrawl content scan without SEO/backlink data” instead of calling the whole run a quick scan

- Added optional AI SEO handoff
  - When the `ai-seo` skill is available and the user asks for AI visibility, GEO, AEO, LLMO, ChatGPT visibility, Perplexity visibility, Google AI Overviews, or citation opportunities, the profile can include an AI SEO / Citation Readiness section
  - Clarifies that AI SEO can assess content structure and citation readiness, but does not replace DataForSEO for traditional SEO metrics

## Why

This makes `competitor-profiling` more accurate and useful in partial-tool environments.

With Firecrawl available, the skill can still produce strong competitor profiles based on official website content, even without DataForSEO. Missing SEO/backlink data should be clearly marked as unavailable rather than causing the whole profile to be labeled as a quick scan.

## Testing

Manually reviewed the updated `SKILL.md` structure and confirmed the new sections were added before the output format section so they can guide source collection and synthesis before final profile generation.

author: toyo54
body:
This PR introduces the semantic analysis phase to the `tnt` transpiler pipeline. It acts as the bridge between the Lark AST parser and the future code generation phase. This iteration focuses on establishing symbol scoping and foundational type validation, though it intentionally defers several complex semantic checks to future phases via explicit `pass` handlers.

**Key Features & Additions:**

* **AST Visitor Pipeline (`semantic.py`):** * Implemented a comprehensive `SemanticAnalyzer` that traverses the AST generated by `ast_tree.py`. 
  * Achieved 100% node coverage for all dataclasses defined in `ast_nodes.py`, entirely eliminating previous `NotImplementedError` parsing crashes.
* **Scope & Symbol Management (`SymbolTable`):**
  * Built a stack-based `SymbolTable` to accurately track variable declarations and lifetimes across nested blocks (e.g., inside `if` statements, `for` loops, and `fn` bodies).
  * Actively prevents "Undefined Identifier" and "Duplicate Declaration" bugs.
* **Base Type Checking:**
  * Added type evaluation for core expressions and literals.
  * Implemented the `expect_type` utility to enforce type matching on variable assignments, initializations (`let`), and function returns. *(Note: This enforces type matching, not memory lifetimes).*
* **Rich Error Reporting (`TntSemanticError`):**
  * Replaced default Python stack traces with a custom, compiler-style error engine.
  * Errors are intercepted and printed to the terminal with ANSI colors, clear titles, contextual details, and actionable developer hints.
* **Pipeline Integration (`transpiler.py`):**
  * Wired the `SemanticAnalyzer` into the main `transpiler.py` loop to run immediately after AST generation.

**Bug Fixes:**
* Addressed static analysis (Ruff/Mypy) complaints by explicitly typing AST nodes and adding the `NoReturn` hint to the error termination sequence.
* Fixed type resolution for `StringLit` to correctly evaluate as a `RefType(PlainType("char"))`.

**Known Limitations & Explicit `pass` Behavior (Technical Debt):**

To maintain development velocity, several AST nodes currently evaluate to `pass` and bypass strict semantic verification. These will need to be addressed in future iterations:

* **Struct Field Resolution:** `StructDecl` parsing and deep field access validation (e.g., ensuring the `.x` field actually exists on a `Point` struct) currently `pass` through the analyzer unverified.
* **Loop Control Context:** `BreakStmt` and `ContinueStmt` currently `pass` without context verification. A developer could erroneously place these outside of a loop block, which will bypass the analyzer and cause a downstream C compilation error.
* **Import Processing:** `import` statements currently `pass` the semantic analyzer; their resolution is strictly deferred to the code generation phase.
* **Inline Assembly:** `TntString` and `TntInt` arguments are passed straight through to the architecture without semantic policing, assuming the developer knows what the target OS requires.
* **Function Call Signatures:** While the analyzer verifies that a called function exists in the symbol table, strict matching of argument types against parameter definitions is pending.

author: teoslayer
body:
## Summary

The save-duration histogram render in /metrics was double-cumulating bucket counts. Production scrape:

\`\`\`
pilot_save_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"10\"}   5
pilot_save_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"30\"}   32   ← should be ≤27
pilot_save_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"60\"}   59   ← should be ≤27
pilot_save_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"+Inf\"} 27
\`\`\`

## Cause

\`Histogram.Observe\` already stores cumulative counts: \`counts[i] = samples <= buckets[i]\`. The WriteTo loop was treating \`counts[]\` as per-bucket increments and running a sum on top, so each output was the prefix-sum of an already-cumulative array.

Histogram percentile derivation in the dashboard (\`computeDerived\`'s save-duration p99 walk) was working from the wrong buckets — explains why I was surprised by the values.

## Fix

Emit \`counts[i]\` directly, drop the leftover \`cum\` accumulator. No state change.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go build ./...\` + \`go test ./metrics/...\` green
- [ ] Deploy, confirm \`le=\"60\"\` ≤ \`le=\"+Inf\"\` count

author: werdnum
body:
## Summary

A self-contained **TestFlight / App Review sandbox** deployment of Family Assistant — isolated from
production, gated to a single demo account via a bundled [Dex](https://dexidp.io/) OIDC provider, and
running the **entire agentic feature set on one cheap model through OpenRouter** so a reviewer can
exercise the app without exposing real data or a production LLM key.

Lives entirely under `deploy/testflight-sandbox/` plus a few small, general core improvements (below).

## How it runs on OpenRouter

- **Chat + embeddings both go through OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API** — i.e. the app's `openai`
  provider pointed at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` via `OPENAI_BASE_URL` (and `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`).
  One quota-capped OpenRouter key powers everything.
  - Chat: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` — cheapest output among reputable tool-calling models, with
    the best agentic-tool-use benchmarks in its tier (reliable function calling is what the demo needs).
  - Embeddings: `openai/text-embedding-3-small` (1536-dim), via the OpenAI-compatible embedding
    provider from #909.
- `config.yaml` pins **every** service profile (default + research / complex_tasks / automation /
  camera / etc.) to that one model with `provider: openai`, so nothing falls back to a
  Gemini/Claude/GPT model that would need another key. (OpenRouter rejects the `openrouter/` model
  prefix, so `provider: openai` + a base-URL override is the correct path.)

## What's in `deploy/testflight-sandbox/`

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `render.yaml` | Render Blueprint: Postgres + app + Dex, wired together. |
| `docker-compose.yaml` | Self-hosted (VPS) variant behind a reverse proxy. |
| `.env.example` | Template for the compose variant. |
| `config.yaml` | Pins all profiles to the cheap model; caps `max_iterations`; disables untrusted channels. |
| `mcp-empty.json` | Empty MCP config (disables the bundled MCP servers in the sandbox). |
| `dex/` | Minimal Dex image + config (one static demo account, gomplate-templated). |
| `README.md` | Security model, prerequisites, Render + self-hosted instructions. |

## Small core changes (general improvements, needed to deploy)

- **`embeddings.py`: lazy-import sentence-transformers.** It was imported at module load whenever
  installed, pulling in **torch (~600 MB resident)** for every process — even when a cloud embedding
  provider is used and the local model is never instantiated. Detected via `find_spec` and deferred
  to actual use. This also cuts prod RAM substantially (prod uses Gemini embeddings).
- **`__main__.py`: `CONFIG_FILE` env** to point at a config overlay without mounting `./config.yaml`
  (Render ships it in the image under a subdir).
- **`storage/base.py`: normalize `postgresql://` → `postgresql+asyncpg://`** so the async engine
  accepts standard libpq / Render connection strings.
- **`dex/config.yaml`: gomplate templating + `hashFromEnv`.** The official Dex image renders config
  with gomplate (`{{ getenv "X" }}`), not shell `${X}`; the bcrypt hash uses `hashFromEnv` so its
  `$` aren't mangled.

## Dependency

Builds on **#909** (OpenAI-compatible embedding provider), now merged to `main`.

## Status

Deployed and verified live on Render: OIDC login (demo account), an LLM chat round-trip through
OpenRouter (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), and embeddings all confirmed working end-to-end.

author: vedant-moxie
body:
Production hardening for **concurrent allocation by multiple ops users** (4–5 people). Two parts.

## 1. Configurable, atomic email reference series

**Found & fixed a real concurrency bug:** the old counter did read → +1 → write inside a READ COMMITTED transaction, so two simultaneous sends could both read `100` and both write `101` → **duplicate `MB-26/27-101`, skipped `102`.**

- New first-class **`Counter`** table (`key` / `prefix` / `value`). `nextEmailRef()` issues via a single `UPDATE … value = value + 1 RETURNING` (Prisma atomic increment) — concurrent allocators serialize on the row and each gets a **distinct** number.
- Seeds from the legacy counter so the live series doesn't reset.
- **Settings → "Allocation email reference series"**: edit the **prefix** and set the **next number**, with a live subject preview. The email subject uses the editable prefix (not the env constant).

**Verified:** 25 concurrent `nextEmailRef()` → 25 distinct, contiguous numbers, zero duplicates.

## 2. Multi-user allocation lock (no double-allocating a PO)

- `PurchaseOrder` gains `claimedById` / `claimedByLabel` / `claimedAt`.
- **Atomic claim** (`po-claim.ts`): a conditional `updateMany` (claim only if unclaimed, already mine, or stale) — two users racing to claim **can't both win**. 20-minute TTL auto-releases abandoned claims.
- **Hard guarantee:** `allocateAndEmailPo` re-asserts the claim **inside the allocation transaction**; if someone else holds it, the txn rolls back with `PoClaimedError` — the email + status flip can never happen twice.
- **UX:** opening a PO claims it (released on navigate-away / TTL); the allocator goes **read-only** with a "being allocated by *name*" banner if someone else holds it. The allocation list shows a **🔒 chip** and disables select/Open for locked rows; bulk select skips them, and the server skips any claimed by others.
- New `POST`/`DELETE /api/pos/[id]/claim`; `/api/settings/email-series` GET/PUT.

**Verified:** Alice claims → Bob's claim returns `ok:false` (by Alice) → Bob's allocate throws `PoClaimedError`, no email, rolled back; releasing clears it. `tsc` + eslint clean. Migration applied.

## Notes
- Per-user locking is meaningful once **Clerk identity** is enabled in production (each person a distinct account). In demo (one shared login) the atomic counter + transaction guards still hold; the lock just can't distinguish people.
- Default claim TTL = 20 min; claimed-PO behaviour = **show-as-locked** (greyed + 🔒), not hidden.

author: timsehn
body:
Completes the alter* family triage (after #1289 gated alter3/alter4). All failures are intentional DDL/schema divergences, never wrong data — each assertion individually reproduced and confirmed:

**altercol** (11)
- `11.1` — `sqlite_schema` row order (doltlite returns catalog order; multiset-equal).
- `13.2.*`, `14.1`, `14.2` — tests 13.1.4–13.1.8 deliberately corrupt the schema with `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON; DELETE FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='x1i'`. doltlite's index lives in its **structural catalog**, not the sqlite_master text, so the raw DELETE orphans the catalog index; every later schema op in the same db (no `reset_db` until line 674) reports `malformed database schema (x1i) - orphan index`, where stock simply dropped it. The accepted `writable_schema`-corruption boundary.

**altercons** (3)
- `3.7.2`/`3.8.2` — trailing space in rewritten `CREATE TABLE` after DROP COLUMN. `6.4.1` — DDL normalizes `CHECK (` → `CHECK(`.

**altercons2** (3)
- `1.*.3` — `writable_schema` raw `UPDATE sqlite_schema SET sql=...` ignored; doltlite regenerates DDL from the structural catalog (same class as `alterdropcol-8.2`).

Harness: `OK: altercol (258 tests, 11 known divergences)`, `OK: altercons (179, 3)`, `OK: altercons2 (69, 3)`, no unused entries.

Note for follow-up: the orphan-index-after-writable_schema-DELETE leaves doltlite stuck reporting malformed schema. It's the accepted writable_schema boundary, but if we ever want to tighten it, the fix would be to either fully reject `writable_schema` index-row deletes or reconcile the structural catalog. Not doing that here.

body:
### Motivation

- Convert the simple Questions listing into a dedicated, split question-and-answer management workspace to improve Q&A workflows and visibility. 
- Preserve backward compatibility with existing question data and reader integrations while hardening repair/load logic to avoid null-pointer or empty-answer issues.

### Description

- Replace the two vertical question sections with a horizontal `JSplitPane` workspace where the left side is a typed, scrollable `JList<StudyQuestion>` question library and the right side is a selected-question detail panel with an independently scrollable answers list. 
- Add filters and search controls for status (`All`/`Unanswered`/`Answered`), book, chapter, reference, question text, and answer text, plus a results counter and dynamic book/chapter population. 
- Implement answer management in the detail panel with `Add`, `Edit`, `Delete` (with confirmation), `Duplicate`, and `Copy` actions, per-answer created/updated timestamps, and empty-answer guards so blank answers are not saved.

body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

`ProjectionExprs::project_statistics` panics with an out-of-bounds index when a projection references a `Column` whose index is ≥ `stats.column_statistics.len()`. Triggered by Spice metadata columns (`_location`, `_last_modified`, `_size`) — or any column appended to `TableSchema` past the file-level statistics — being projected through `FileScanConfig::partition_statistics`.

spiceai-52 worked around it externally: `partition_statistics` post-processed the output and inserted `ColumnStatistics::new_unknown()` at metadata-column positions. The DF53 reconcile (`d599c7272`) folded metadata columns into `TableSchema` and dropped the post-processing, feeding metadata indices straight into the unguarded `column_statistics[col.index()]`.

## Fix
Bounds-guard the `Column` arm in `ProjectionExprs::project_statistics` (`datafusion/physical-expr/src/projection.rs`): if `col.index()` is beyond the input stats width, fall back to `ColumnStatistics::new_unknown()` instead of indexing.

- New regression test `test_project_statistics_column_index_beyond_input_stats` — projects `_location` at index 3 over file stats of width 3, asserts trailing column comes back as unknown.
- All `project_statistics` tests pass (8/8).
- All `datafusion-datasource` metadata tests pass (10/10).
- `test_partition_statistics_projection` (the call-site path) passes.

author: indyjonesnl
body:
Continues (real-operator readiness via cert-manager). Two typed-client-compat fixes found by driving cert-manager's controllers. **Includes #1020's protobuf commit until that merges** — review the top two commits here; the diff collapses to just those once #1020 lands.

## Bugs fixed
1. **Watch bookmark kind** — `resource_type_to_kind_and_version` produced `Apiservice` / `Cert-manager_io_certificate` (CamelCase fallback) instead of `APIService` / `Certificate`, so client-go failed to decode watch bookmarks and dropped the watch. Fix: add `apiservices ⇒ APIService`; thread the CRD's real Kind + `group/version` into CR watch bookmarks.
2. **CR list kind** — CR LIST returned `kind: List`, `apiVersion: v1` instead of the typed `CertificateList` / `cert-manager.io/v1`. Typed informers decode a LIST against their scheme, where `List`/`v1` isn't registered, so **every cert-manager.io informer failed** (`no kind "List" is registered for version "v1"`) and the controllers never reconciled. Fix: `crd.spec.names.listKind` (fallback `<Kind>List`) + `group/version`.

## Verified end-to-end (with #1020)
`no kind "List"` errors → **0**; all cert-manager.io watch/list errors clear; cainjector injects the `caBundle`; **the SelfSigned Issuer reconciles to `Ready=True`**. Unit tests added (APIService kind + built-in regression).

## Remaining
Issuer reaches Ready but the controller **hot-loops** re-setting the condition — CR **status-subresource** updates don't propagate to watchers, blocking final Certificate issuance. Deeper, tracked separately.

author: histrio
body:
PR #2148 mapped ID=almalinux to EcosystemAlmaLinux using the full os-release VERSION_ID as the suffix. On a real host VERSION_ID is a point release (e.g. "9.8"), producing the ecosystem "AlmaLinux:9.8".

OSV.dev keys AlmaLinux (ALSA) advisories by major version only ("AlmaLinux:9"), so the point-release suffix matches zero advisories.

Empirical check against the OSV.dev API for an AlmaLinux 9.8 host with 416 installed packages:
  AlmaLinux:9    -> 38 packages with vulns, 532 vuln refs
  AlmaLinux:9.8  -> 0 packages, 0 vulns
e.g. NetworkManager 1.54.3-2.el9: AlmaLinux:9 => 3 vulns, 9.8 => 0.

Trim VERSION_ID to the part before the first "." so "9.8" -> "9". A bare major such as "9" is returned unchanged by strings.Cut.

author: next-nf
body:
Two CI test-reliability/performance changes.

## 1. Deterministic peer-node startup for the multi-node suites

The flakiness in `udr_hss_dist_SUITE` (intermittent on fresh runners) was the `?CT_PEER` node-init pattern — **not** distribution being unavailable. Root cause, traced through OTP 29 `peer.erl` / `test_server.erl`:

- **Code path pushed post-boot.** Peers booted with empty args, then the real path was added with `erpc:call(Node, code, add_paths, ...)`. Now baked into the boot args instead — `args => ["-pa" | code:get_path()]` — the documented `peer` idiom.
- **`wait_boot` default is 15s** (`peer.erl:308`). A slow peer boot on a cold/loaded runner does `erlang:exit(timeout)` (`peer.erl:943`), which **crashes `init_per_suite` and trips rebar3's exit code** rather than skipping. Set `wait_boot => 20000`.
- **Distribution is no longer started inside the suite.** Per `verify_args` (`peer.erl:861-863`), `?CT_PEER` requires `erlang:is_alive()`. The suites now require the CT node to already be distributed and **skip cleanly** otherwise (no more ad-hoc `net_kernel:start`). CI runs `rebar3 ct --sname test`.

Applied to both `udr_hss_dist_SUITE` and `udr_cluster_dist_SUITE`. Pattern follows the working `smf_dist_test_lib` reference.

## 2. Preload running apps' modules during CT (`udr_preload_cth`)

Erlang loads each `.beam` lazily on first call; off a cold CI disk that first-call latency surfaces inside tests as sporadic slowness / timetrap flakiness. A global CT hook walks `application:which_applications/0` after each suite starts its apps and `code:ensure_loaded/1`s every module they own (≈227 modules / 9 apps once `udr_hss` is up). Load-only and error-swallowing — it never changes a suite's result.

## Verification

- `rebar3 ct --sname test` → **all 109 pass**; both dist suites genuinely run (not skip).
- Each dist suite distributed → runs + passes, exit 0.
- Undistributed → **clean skip, exit 0** (the original crash-on-init symptom is gone).
- `rebar3 dialyzer` → clean.

author: niksedk
body:
## Summary

Fixes the custom continuation style not reaching the fix/merge engine, and makes the custom continuation style **per rule profile** instead of a single global setting.

### The core bug
The libse fix/merge engine reads the custom continuation style from `Configuration.Settings.General` (14 fields + `ContinuationPause`). The SE5 settings bridge only copied the `ContinuationStyle` **enum** there and never the custom fields — so selecting the **Custom** style silently fell back to libse defaults in **Fix Common Errors** and **Merge**. Presets were unaffected (only the enum matters for them).

### Per-profile storage + refactor (#2/#3)
- New `CustomContinuationStyle` value object (`src/libse/Common/CustomContinuationStyle.cs`) collapses the 14 flat fields into one object, used by `RulesProfile`, `ProfileDisplay`, and `SeGeneral`.
- The flat-field mapping the engine reads is centralized on the value object (`ApplyToGeneralSettings` / `FromGeneralSettings`).
- The active profile is mirrored onto `SeGeneral` and bridged to libse via a single `Se.ApplyContinuationStyleToLibSe()`, called from both bridge sites (`MainViewModel.SetLibSeSettings` and `FixCommonErrorsViewModel.InitStep1`).
- Adding a future field now touches the value object + libse `GeneralSettings`/engine + the one mapping, instead of ~12 hand-copied sites. Net **−119 lines** in `SettingsViewModel`.

### Additional fixes
- "Edit custom style" button not appearing when the settings page was reopened with a Custom-style profile.
- Continuation settings not reset by **Reset Rules**.
- `ColorDurationTooLong` not reset by **Reset Syntax Coloring** (self-assignment no-op).

### Notes
- **No migration** is performed for the old *global* custom style (this is pre-release; an upgrading tester's global custom values reset to defaults). Deliberate, per discussion.
- The legacy `RulesProfile.Serialize/Deserialize` (used by old SE, not SE5) does not carry the per-profile custom style — SE5 persists it via System.Text.Json.
- Null-safety hardened on the engine path (null-tolerant copy-ctor, bridge coalesce, `Se.SetDefaultValues` guards mirror + profiles).

## Tests
- **libse**: `CustomContinuationStyle` (defaults match legacy, deep copy, null-tolerant copy, `ApplyTo`/`From` round-trip), `RulesProfile` (copy/serialize).
- **UI**: `Se.ApplyContinuationStyleToLibSe()` bridges into libse `Configuration`; per-profile custom style survives a real `SaveSettings`→`LoadSettings` round-trip.
- Full suites pass: **libse 383**, **UI 333**. Solution builds clean.

author: focused-asshu
body:
### Motivation

- Fix critical correctness and security issues in the MVP risk engine so very large transactions, structuring/smurfing patterns, and dangerous CSV payloads are handled correctly and explainably. 
- Ensure validation prevents negative/zero/invalid data and spreadsheet-formula/HTML injection at upload time. 
- Improve explainability by exposing contribution-level breakdowns for every scored transaction. 
- Maintain demo-friendly, deterministic scoring while making the rules easier to audit and test.

### Description

- Replaced fixed amount thresholds with progressive amount scoring ranges from `$10k` through `$1B+`, exposed as `AMOUNT_SCORING_RANGES`, and included category-level `riskBreakdown` and a capped final score. 
- Added structuring/smurfing detection that flags groups of 3+ sub-$10k transactions from the same wallet to the same counterparty within any 7-day window when combined value > $10k and attaches an explainable risk factor to each affected transaction. 
- Hardened CSV parsing and upload: strict date validation (YYYY-MM-DD + real calendar check), `direction` normalization, rejection of negative/zero/non-numeric amounts, configurable row/file-size limits, detection/rejection of spreadsheet formula prefixes (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) and script/HTML-like tags, and surfaced clear row-level errors. 
- Sanitized CSV exports to mitigate CSV formula injection by prefixing unsafe cells, added contribution columns (`amountContribution`, `jurisdictionContribution`, `structuringContribution`, `directionContribution`, `watchlistContribution`, `otherContribution`, `riskCalculation`) to exported CSVs, and updated the dashboard to show inline breakdowns and prioritized alerts; README updated with the new scoring ranges and validation behavior.

- Ran `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` with no errors.

## Problem
A USB disk attached behind a `usb-hub` hung during enumeration on OHCI. Traced (via a temporary COM2/COM3 serial debug channel across usbd and usb_storage) to an **intermittently lost WDH completion interrupt**: under the extra scheduling load of an attached hub — `usb_hub` is a second driver process polling the hub's port status continuously — the DDEKit cooperative scheduler occasionally fails to deliver a Writeback-Done-Head interrupt to the waiting device thread, so a control-transfer stage never completes and enumeration stalls. The child device never reaches CONNECTED, so usb_storage is never handed the device.

## Fix
A **completion poll-backstop**: a low-priority thread polls the in-flight TD's condition code every ~2 ms and, if the HC has retired it while its completion is still pending, delivers the completion the ISR missed. This works precisely in the stall condition — when a transfer is genuinely stuck, the device thread is blocked, so the dispatcher runs on each clock tick and wakes the backstop from `msleep`, letting it read the TD status directly and bypass the missed interrupt. An `ohci_xfer_pending` flag (set on TD submission, test-and-cleared by whichever of the ISR or backstop fires first) guarantees exactly-once delivery.

## Validation (QEMU, amd64)
- **Disk behind `usb-hub` on OHCI**: enumerates reliably (4/4 runs) and reads byte-correct — 64 KB multi-sector reads at LBA 500 cksum-match the host exactly.
- **Regression-clean**: direct single- and two-disk OHCI and single-disk xHCI still byte-correct.

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)
- devmand assigns `usb_hub` a block major (65) even though it isn't a block device, so the disk behind it lands at the next major (66). Cosmetic; works at 66.
- EHCI/xHCI hub support additionally needs per-device topology (EHCI split transactions for FS/LS behind a HS hub; xHCI route string). OHCI needs none of that (native full/low speed), which is why it works with the completion fix alone.

author: j-mentiora
body:
## What & Why

The observational per-request **`network_entries` ≥64KB offload-or-inline** logic was
copy-pasted in two places in `loom-host`:

- `navigate_execute` (`host_function_table/host_impl.rs`)
- `WasmHost::network_log` — the `loom.web.network_log` tool (`wasm_host/wasm_host.rs`)

Both had their own `const … = 65_536`, their own serialize → `content_store.put` →
warn+degrade branch. This PR extracts that into a single helper
`offload_or_inline_network_entries` in a new `loom-host/src/network_offload.rs` module, so
the 64KB threshold and the fail-open graceful-degrade policy live in one place and can't
drift. (Addresses the one remaining item in the repo's cleanup backlog,
`id:7e1a4c9b2f60`.)

## Decisions

- **Scope = the 2 network_entries sites only.** `evaluate_execute` has the same shape but
  is intentionally **not** folded in: it compares with `>` (a *tested* boundary —
  `integration_evaluate_result.rs`) and is **fail-closed** (propagates put errors), vs
  network_entries' `>=` + **fail-open** (drop + `truncated=true`; "must never fail a
  navigate"). Merging it would risk an off-by-one on a tested boundary or a worse
  abstraction.
- **Neutral return enum** `NetworkEntriesPayload { Inline(Vec<u8>), Offloaded(ContentRef),
  Dropped }` + effective `truncated`. Each caller adapts: `host_impl` → WIT ref via
  `core_ref_to_wit` / raw JSON bytes; `wasm_host` → bare `sha256` / `Vec<serde_json::Value>`.
- **Two strictly-better unifications** in practically-unreachable error paths: `network_log`
  now warns + flags `truncated` on a whole-list serialize failure (was a silent
  `unwrap_or_default`); warn message text unified.
- New module placement: a single-file `pub mod network_offload;` (matches the existing
  `mocks.rs` convention; can't be file-local since two files share it).

## Schema changes
None.

## Security
No new secrets, endpoints, auth surface, or data-scoping. The helper's `warn!` logs only
`session_id` + `entry_count` + `error` (no URLs / PII) — same privacy posture as the code it
replaces.

## Determinism (NFR-DET-01)
Unaffected. Both sites are the **observational side-channel**, never folded into the
manifest `ReceiptPayload` / replay hash chain (confirmed in `navigate_outcome.rs` +
`capture_policy.rs`). Refactor is replay-equal.

## Tests
- New `loom-host/src/network_offload.rs` `mod tests` — **5 tests** via a `FailingContentStore`
  double (none existed before): inline / offload-success / **put-error → dropped+truncated**
  (the degrade branch was previously **untested**) / exact `>=` 65_535↔65_536 boundary /
  incoming-truncated passthrough.
- `cargo test -p loom-host -- --test-threads=1`: 5 new GREEN, full suite green, 0
  regressions, 2 real-browser e2e ignored (unchanged).
- RED→GREEN: tests first referenced the not-yet-implemented helper (panic) → all pass after
  implementation.

## Plan fidelity
100% — all plan items implemented, no deviations. `evaluate` fold explicitly out of scope.

## Policy compliance
`cargo build` ✓ · `cargo clippy -p loom-host --all-targets` ✓ (no warnings) · `cargo fmt` ✓.
No generated-artifact regeneration needed (no action-registry / WASM-surface change).

## Files
**New**
- `loom-host/src/network_offload.rs` — helper + `NetworkEntriesPayload` + 5 unit tests

**Edited**
- `loom-host/src/lib.rs` — register `pub mod network_offload;`
- `loom-host/src/host_function_table/host_impl.rs` — navigate site calls helper (−45 net)
- `loom-host/src/wasm_host/wasm_host.rs` — `network_log` site calls helper (−37 net)

## Cost summary
$0 — Size S; council skipped per size gate, no OpenRouter calls this run.

body:
💡 **What:** Migrated the audio preprocessing and chunking logic from disk-based temporary files to a full in-memory pipeline using FFmpeg pipes and NumPy array slicing.

🎯 **Why:** Disk I/O and redundant FFmpeg calls for chunking created unnecessary latency and complex cleanup logic. In-memory processing is significantly more efficient for the hardware target (Ryzen 3 3300U).

📊 **Impact:** 
- Preprocessing and chunking phase is ~11.5x faster for 10-minute (600s) audio files (reduced from ~2.1s to ~0.18s).
- Chunking overhead itself is reduced from ~0.26s to virtually instantaneous (0.00s).
- Overall pre-transcription latency reduced by ~50% for standard 60s files.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verified using a custom benchmarking script that compared the old `preprocess_to_wav` + `chunk_audio` logic against the new `preprocess_to_memory` + NumPy slicing. Correctness verified with `py_compile`.

author: missingroberto
body:
## Summary

Implements **Prep P0.8** (grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1174), part of grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1166.

Per-repo stats data is kind-agnostic, but the presentation wasn't: `RepositoryListItem.tsx` routed per kind with a hardcoded `if` chain and showed the raw GVR string, and `RepositoryOverview.tsx`'s only action was a hardcoded "View Folder" link that assumed folder-containment.

This drives label/icon/route from a descriptor keyed on `group`+`resource`, with graceful fallback for unknown kinds, so a **new provisioned kind renders correctly with no edits to these files**.

## Changes

### New — `utils/resourceKinds.ts`
A small registry keyed on `group`+`resource`. Each entry carries `group`, `resource`, `icon`, a localized `getLabel()`, and a `getListUrl(ctx)`. Helpers:
- `resolveResourceKind(group, resource)` — `resource` is the discriminator (the API group is not unique); falls back to a group-only match; returns `undefined` for unknown kinds.
- `getResourceLabel` / `getResourceIcon` / `getResourceListUrl` — all degrade gracefully (raw resource string / generic icon / folder-or-dashboards route).
- Registered today: `folders`, `dashboards`, `playlists`. Adding a kind is one entry.

### `RepositoryListItem.tsx`
Replaces the hardcoded `getListURL` if-chain and the raw resource string with descriptor-driven routing + friendly labels.

### `RepositoryOverview.tsx`
- Resource table cell shows a friendly icon + label instead of the raw `resource`.
- The hardcoded "View Folder" action becomes descriptor-driven view links built from the repo's stats (deduped by destination). Folder-synced repos still collapse to a "View Folder" button; the no-stats case preserves the prior fallback button.

## Testing

- New `utils/resourceKinds.test.ts` (13 cases: lookups, routing, label/icon fallbacks).
- Existing Repository suites pass (31 tests total).
- `yarn typecheck`, ESLint and Prettier clean on changed files.
- `make i18n-extract` added `provisioning.resource-kind.{dashboards,folders,playlists}`.

## Notes

- Frontend-only. Behavior is preserved for current kinds (dashboards/folders).
- Playlists is wired into the registry but only surfaces once the backend reports it in repository stats.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] No breaking changes
- [ ] Documentation updated (registry is self-documenting; broader docs land with P0.7)

author: zyie
body:
### Overview

From chrome 150+, the experimental HTML-in-Canvas API ([WICG/html-in-canvas#128](https://github.com/WICG/html-in-canvas/pull/128/changes)) changed the method signatures for uploading DOM elements to textures, addressing community-group feedback. This adapts both the WebGL and WebGPU `HTMLSource` uploaders to the new signatures via runtime arity detection (`.length`), so the texture uploads keep working on chrome 150+ while still supporting older Chrome builds that ship the previous signatures.

#### Fix

- `HTMLSource` / `ElementImageSource` now support the chrome 150+ HTML-in-Canvas upload signatures, with automatic fallback to the pre-150 signatures for backwards compatibility.
  - WebGL `texElementImage2D` collapsed to `(target, internalFormat, source)` ([KhronosGroup/WebGL#3752](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/WebGL/pull/3752)).
  - WebGPU `copyElementImageToTexture` collapsed to `(sourceDict, destDict)` ([gpuweb/gpuweb#6250](https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/pull/6250)).

##### Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [ ] Documentation is changed or added

LightChain's own explorer shows a **"Jailed"** badge and nothing more. We read the underlying on-chain state and explain it: **why** a worker can't take jobs, **how close** it is to suspension, and **how much** stake is exposed right now.

New **"Suspension & slashing"** action (`/api/operator-preview` + Worker ops panel), composed entirely from existing SDK reads (no new SDK surface):

- **Standing verdict** derived from chain truth: *active / below-floor / suspended (jailed) / no-models / unregistered*. `suspended` = registered + above the stake floor but `WorkerRegistry.isEligible()` is false for every served model (the authoritative jailed signal), with the AIConfig cooldown to clear it.
- **Per-model on-chain eligibility** badges.
- **Suspension countdown**: lifetime timeouts vs the AIConfig suspension threshold, with a meter and *"N more timeouts triggers a <cooldown> suspension"*, flagging jobs stuck right now that would count.
- **Live slash exposure**: total LCAI + bps at risk from currently-stuck jobs (capped at maxBps), broken down per job (ack vs completion, bps, time past deadline) - from `getWorkerLiveness`.
- The full **slash schedule** from AIConfig (ack / completion / dispute / max bps).

This is the first build of the broader 'expose what their tools don't' initiative (ROI calculator, deep worker explorer, contracts verifier to follow). tsc clean, build green, 420 unit tests.

## Summary

Use python3 for tar.gz extraction instead of BSD tar, which fails
when the archive contains a `.` root directory entry.

## Problem

BSD tar on macOS exits with code 1 when extracting an archive that
contains a `.` entry:

```
.: Can't replace existing directory with non-directory: Invalid argument
tar: Error exit delayed from previous errors.
```

The files ARE extracted correctly, but the non-zero exit code
triggers `set -e` and aborts the script.

## Fix

- Prefer python3 for extraction (filters out the `.` entry)
- Fall back to BSD tar with `|| true` if python3 is unavailable
  (files still extract despite the warning)

## Verification

- [x] `bash -n` syntax check passed
- [x] `shellcheck` clean
- [x] Tested: python3 extracts cleanly, binary installs correctly

author: leihb
body:
Four robustness fixes from the memory-feature review (items 1–3 + the scoping edge).

## 1. Truncation is no longer silent
`MEMORY.md` is injected truncated to 200 lines / 25 KB. Previously, exceeding that just dropped the tail (often the newest entries) with no signal. `truncateForInjection` now reports whether it cut anything, and `RenderInjection` appends an explicit warning **inside the injected block** so the model knows entries past the cut aren't loaded.

## 2. Parse / budget failures are visible
New `memory.Lint(dir)` flags the two silent degraders:
- the index is over budget (entries past the cut aren't loaded);
- a bullet under `## 触发提醒` has no parseable `(触发: …)` clause — it still *looks* present in the file but **can never be recalled** (the most insidious failure).

`octo memory` now prints these warnings (`⚠ …`) for the project and inherited dirs.

## 3. Worktree scoping (the edge from the review)
`ProjectRoot` derived the scope from the per-worktree `--show-toplevel`, so every worktree of a repo got its **own, empty** memory. It now derives the root from the git **common** dir (`<root>/.git`, shared by the main checkout and all linked worktrees), so a worktree shares the main repo's memory. The result is symlink-resolved so one repo always maps to one slug — and the main-checkout result is unchanged from the old (also-resolved) `--show-toplevel`, so **existing memory dirs keep their slug** (no migration).

## 4. Stale flag help
`--no-memory` claimed it disables "the remember tool" — there is no remember tool. Fixed to "MEMORY.md injection + the writable memory directory".

## Tests / docs
- `TestProjectRoot_WorktreeSharesRoot` (real git: worktree root == main root, ≠ worktree dir), truncation flag, injected warning, `Lint` (clean / no-trigger rule / over-budget).
- `go test -race ./internal/memory/ ./cmd/octo/` + `go vet` clean.
- `dev-docs/memory-design.md` updated for the worktree scoping and truncation warning.

Not done (from the review, by design / out of scope): semantic recall, confidence/recency/conflict-resolution, code-driven consolidation — left to the "dumb storage + smart model" philosophy unless recall misses prove painful.

author: renecannao
body:
## Merge order: **2 of 3** — depends on #1

Second of three PRs forming the initial implementation.

| # | PR | Branch | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #1 — charts + scaffolding | `pr1/charts` | **merge before this one** |
| 2 | this one — **operator + CI + e2e** | `pr2/operator` | merge after #1 |
| 3 | #3 — docs + examples + final README | `pr3/docs-examples` | merge after this one |

**Conflicts with #1** on `README.md`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — this PR's versions supersede #1's, so rebase-resolve in favor of this PR after #1 merges.

In CI, this PR self-validates without #1's charts present (only `proxysql-operator` is in `charts/` here, and it's excluded from `ct install` by `.github/ct.yaml`). The expanded CI pipeline runs in full and will exercise the operator from this PR alone.

## What this PR adds

**Kubebuilder operator** (`operator/`, module `github.com/ProxySQL/kubernetes/operator`) with two CRDs under `proxysql.com/v1alpha1`:

| Kind | Short | What it owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ProxySQLCluster` | `pxc` | `StatefulSet`, headless + ClusterIP Services, `Secret` (admin/radmin/monitor passwords, minted by the operator), `ConfigMap` (bootstrap proxysql.cnf), `PodDisruptionBudget`, optional `ServiceMonitor` |
| `ProxySQLConfig` | `pxcfg` | Nothing — runs SQL writes against each replica's admin port |

Package layout:

- `operator/api/v1alpha1/` — CRD types (deep-copy generated)
- `operator/internal/controller/` — the two reconcilers, with watches on `Pod` and `ProxySQLCluster` so a Ready pod gets config pushed without waiting for the 30s safety requeue
- `operator/internal/controller/builders/` — **pure** desired-state builders (Secret, ConfigMap with bootstrap cnf, Services + Headless, StatefulSet, PDB, unstructured ServiceMonitor). No I/O, no client calls; trivially unit-testable.
- `operator/internal/proxysqlclient/` — thin MySQL-wire client for ProxySQL's admin port + `Sync()` that DELETE/INSERT/LOAD/SAVEs every admin table. Takes an `Executor` interface so tests use a recording fake.
- `cmd/main.go` — standard controller-runtime wiring + leader election + ldflag-injected version/commit

**Test coverage (`make test` is fully green):**

- `internal/proxysqlclient` — **6 unit tests** for the SQL builder via an `Executor` fake (no real ProxySQL needed)
- `internal/controller/builders` — **13 unit tests** for spec defaulting, naming, bootstrap-cnf rendering, container ports, persistence on/off, headless service shape, PDB logic, labels, RandomPassword length, ServiceMonitor gating
- `internal/controller` — **11 envtest integration specs** (real apiserver via `setup-envtest`) asserting the cluster reconciler creates Secret/ConfigMap/Services/StatefulSet/PDB with correct shape, owner refs on every owned object, idempotency, scale-up propagates, BYO secret is honored, single-replica PDB omission

**`charts/proxysql-operator/`** — operator install chart: CRDs (bundled under `crds/`), ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding, leader-election Role, ServiceAccount, manager Deployment, metrics Service.

**`test/e2e/proxysql-cluster.sh`** — self-contained kind e2e: build operator image → kind-load → helm install → apply a 1-replica `ProxySQLCluster` + a `ProxySQLConfig` → wait for `syncedReplicas=1` → assert `runtime_mysql_servers` contains the row we declared via a one-shot `mysql:8` client pod.

**Expanded `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`** — from #1's 2 jobs to **7 parallel jobs**:

| Job | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `charts-lint` | `make lint` + kubeconform (unchanged from #1) |
| `chart-testing` | `ct lint` + `ct install` on kind (unchanged from #1) |
| `operator-test` | `make test` — Go unit + envtest integration |
| `golangci` | `make -C operator lint` — golangci-lint v2.11.4 (operator's pinned config) |
| `shellcheck` | `test/` shell scripts |
| `operator-image` | buildx build + Trivy CRITICAL/HIGH gate; exports image as artifact |
| `e2e` | kind up → import image → run `test/e2e/proxysql-cluster.sh` |

**`.github/workflows/release.yaml`** — fires on `v*` tag or manual dispatch:
- `charts` — `chart-releaser-action` publishes to `gh-pages` so users can `helm repo add proxysql https://proxysql.github.io/proxysql-on-k8s`
- `image` — `docker/build-push-action` publishes `ghcr.io/<owner>/proxysql-operator` multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) with provenance + SBOM attestations, GHA buildx cache

**`CLAUDE.md`** — documents the critical conventions a fresh Claude Code session needs to know: keep CRDs in sync between `operator/config/crd/bases/` and the chart copies, use `*bool` for `Enabled` fields that default to true (and why), builders are pure, `proxysqlclient.Sync` takes `Executor`, write-to-all is intentional (not cluster-sync-only), PSA `restricted` everywhere.

## Validate locally

```bash
# Unit + envtest (auto-downloads kube-apiserver/etcd binaries)
cd operator && make test

# Build the image and run the full kind e2e
cd ..
make operator-image
make e2e
```

## File count

| Status | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Added  | 91 |
| Modified | 1 (`README.md`) |
| **Total** | **92** |

Of these, the `.coderabbit.yml` from #1 excludes generated files from review (`zz_generated*.go`, `operator/config/**`, `operator/hack/boilerplate.go.txt`, `charts/proxysql-operator/crds/**`, `operator/go.sum`), trimming roughly 30 files of generated/scaffolded noise.

## Real bugs to flag explicitly

`PersistenceSpec.Enabled`, `MetricsSpec.Enabled`, and `PodDisruptionBudget.Enabled` are `*bool` (not `bool`). The `bool + omitempty` combo dropped `enabled: false` on marshal, and the CRD's `+kubebuilder:default=true` re-defaulted it — meaning users **literally could not disable** persistence/metrics/PDB. `*bool` restores the standard K8s tri-state idiom. `ServiceMonitor.Enabled` is intentionally still plain `bool` because its default is `false`.

## NOT in this PR

- **Standalone charts** (`charts/proxysql`, `charts/proxysql-cluster`) → in #1
- **Backend cookbook examples** → in #3
- **Architecture and migration docs** → in #3
