author: pkarw
body:
Fixes #2116

## Problem
`requireCustomerEntity`, `requireTimelineParentEntity`, and `requireDealInScope` in `packages/core/src/modules/customers/commands/shared.ts` looked records up by `id` (and `deletedAt`) **only**, with no `tenantId`/`organizationId` filter. They relied on a separate post-fetch `ensureSameScope(entity, …)` to reject cross-tenant rows.

- Several undo/redo paths skipped the follow-up `ensureSameScope`, so those code paths could return another tenant's row.
- The 404-vs-403 differential leaked whether a UUID existed in another tenant (cross-tenant existence oracle; subsumes audit finding C-05).
- Timing-attack surface.

## Root Cause
Scope was validated *after* the lookup instead of being part of the `where` clause, so the query itself could match cross-tenant rows.

## What Changed
- `requireCustomerEntity` and `requireTimelineParentEntity` now take a required `scope: { tenantId, organizationId }` argument applied directly in the `em.findOne` `where` clause.
- `requireDealInScope` already received `tenantId`/`organizationId`; those are now applied in the `where` clause too (no signature change).
- All call sites updated to thread scope from the available context (`parsed`, snapshot `before`/`after`, the owning entity, or — for the no-scope `recompute_next` command — `ctx.auth`).
- The post-fetch `ensureSameScope` checks are kept as belt-and-braces.
- A cross-tenant id now returns the same not-found response as a non-existent id (404 for the entity helpers, "Deal not found" 400 for the deal helper), removing the existence oracle.

## Tests
- `packages/core/src/modules/customers/commands/__tests__/shared.test.ts`: made the `findOne` mock scope-aware, threaded scope through existing cases, and added per-helper cross-tenant regression tests asserting 404/not-found (not 403) for all three helpers.
- `yarn workspace @open-mercato/core test src/modules/customers` → 798 passed.
- `yarn build:packages`, `yarn generate`, `yarn typecheck` → green.

## Backward Compatibility
- `requireCustomerEntity` / `requireTimelineParentEntity` are module-internal command helpers (no importers outside the customers module) — adding a required `scope` arg is not a public contract-surface change. `requireDealInScope`'s signature is unchanged.

## Qué

`loadTargets` ahora excluye los portátiles **refurbished** del enriquecimiento.

## Por qué

Medido durante el backfill: **461 de 462** de los 404 de una tanda eran slugs `-refurbished` (productos agotados cuya ficha ya no existe en PcComponentes). Como no quedan marcados, **cada tanda los re-procesaba**, hundiendo el rendimiento — la tanda 2 rindió la mitad que la 1 (328 vs 665 con datos).

Excluirlos (`laptops.refurbished = false`) hace que las tandas restantes sean casi todo producto vivo: ~2.199 normales sin enriquecer en vez de vadear ~994 refurbished que casi siempre dan 404.

Los ~994 refurbished quedan con las 6 specs en null. No se pueden enriquecer desde su propia ficha (404); cubrirlos sería **copiar del modelo "normal" equivalente** por slug — otra tarea, fuera de alcance.

body:
## Summary

This PR connects the frontend dashboard to the FastAPI analysis workflow through RabbitMQ and Celery.

The frontend now creates a research run, polls its processing status, retrieves the completed synthesis result, and maps that response into the dashboard UI.

## Changes

### Backend

- Added configurable CORS origins for frontend requests.
- Added `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/result`.
- Added a typed response schema for completed analysis results.
- Included signal count, source count, spam exclusion rate, and cost metrics in the synthesis output.
- Added a programmatic Alembic migration runner.
- Configured Docker Compose to run migrations before starting FastAPI.

### Frontend

- Standardized the API base URL through `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
- Connected the dashboard to the asynchronous workflow:
  1. `POST /api/v1/runs`
  2. Poll `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}`
  3. Fetch `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/result`
- Added a three-minute polling timeout.
- Removed the silent mock-data fallback.
- Added user-visible API error states.
- Mapped backend synthesis data into dashboard narratives and metrics.
- Allowed the configured backend origin through the Next.js Content Security Policy.

### Configuration

- Added `CORS_ORIGINS`.
- Made `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` configurable in Docker Compose.
- Updated README environment and migration instructions.

## API Flow

```text
Frontend
  |
  | POST /api/v1/runs
  v
FastAPI -> RabbitMQ -> Celery Worker
                         |
                         v
                  PostgreSQL/Supabase
  ^
  | GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}
  | GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/result
  |
Frontend Dashboard
```

## Validation

- Backend tests: `14 passed`
- Next.js production build: passed
- TypeScript check: passed
- ESLint: `0 errors`

## Problem

Migration `0030` was never applied in any environment because `0031` was already present when `0030` was merged. `isMigrated()` only compared the highest migration version against the DB version — any gaps were silently ignored.

This caused `column v.top_risk_tier does not exist` errors in production.

author: fmcuni
body:
## Problem

With realtime collab **ON** (prod: `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_ENABLED=true`), rejecting a tracked change in the **Review changes** panel didn't reflect in the **Edit** panel. Worse, the next keystroke silently re-introduced the rejected change.

**Root cause (not version history):** in collab mode the TipTap editor binds to the **Yjs CRDT as its source of truth** and ignores its `value` prop. Every external "working body" write only updated React `setHtml(...)` and never the Yjs doc, so the Edit surface (and the next `onUpdate`) kept the stale body. Reject was the reported symptom; the same gap affected AI apply-edits, comment/review-span edits, and snapshot restore.

## Fix

- **`replaceCollabDoc(ydoc, html)`** (`web/lib/run-editor/collab-html.ts`) — headless-editor whole-document replace into the shared Yjs doc, mirroring the existing `seedCollabDocIfEmpty`/`flattenCollabDoc` primitives.
- **`useWorkingBody({collabActive, ydoc, html, setHtml})`** (`web/lib/run-editor/useWorkingBody.ts`) → `applyWorking(updater)`:
  - collab **off** → identical to today's `setHtml` (updater passed straight through).
  - collab **on** → **dual-write**: `setHtml(next)` (Review diff reads React html; live editor is unmounted in Review so no `onUpdate` fires) **and** `replaceCollabDoc(ydoc, next)`, skipping the CRDT write when the body is unchanged (cheap `next !== prev` compare, so **accept** emits no spurious delta).
- Routed all **5 external write sites** in `/hitl2` and `/edit` through `applyWorking`. Left render-load + first-load snapshot hydration as raw `setHtml` (seed paths owned by `useSeedCollabDoc`); `committed` baseline stays React-only.

## Concurrency caveat

Whole-doc replace can merge unexpectedly against a concurrent peer's in-flight edit (rare at the HITL_2 review gate). Accepted for now; documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s collab section.

## Tests

- `useWorkingBody` unit: collab-off passthrough, dual-write, no-op skip (state vector unchanged), no stale ref.
- `collab-roundtrip`: `replaceCollabDoc` reflects in a live editor bound to the same doc.
- New collab **e2e** scenario: reject a tracked change → switch to Edit → asserts the rejected text is gone. `collab-e2e.yml` now also triggers on PRs into `main` (still skip-gated on `E2E_COLLAB_BASE_URL`, never runs against prod).
- **394 web Vitest green**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean.

## Scope

Frontend-only — no backend / Durable Object / migration changes. Reviewed by typescript-reviewer (no CRITICAL/HIGH correctness issues after refinements).

## Test plan
- [ ] CI: collab-e2e gate runs green on this PR
- [ ] Authenticated prod browser eyeball after deploy: reject in Review → Edit reflects; AI apply-edits + snapshot restore also reflect under collab

author: martinhbramwell

Closes #684. Fixes the #673 guardrail tool that taught me the wrong frame this session.

I called four umbrellas 'stale' on behind-count alone, having assessed none of their content. The risk-relevant measure is the reverse — commits a branch has that main LACKS.

- `ahead_count()` added; reported per branch: **0 unique ⇒ content already on main, safe to retire**; **>0 ⇒ unmerged work, ASSESS before retiring**.
- `classify()` level still behind-driven (base-currency, unchanged); the unmerged-work note is always appended so distance is never read as obsolescence.
- Language neutralized ('rebase before use' → 'rebase before branching off it'); sync_check §19 drops 'stale'.
- 7 colocated tests incl. the two cases that enforce the lesson.

Live: `257 behind … ; 0 unique commits — safe to retire` vs `344 behind …; 1 unmerged commit(s) — ASSESS before retiring`. Sibling of #683.

author: jerrinot
body:
Fixes a rare store-and-forward sender race that could silently drop a batch during high-throughput ingestion when a segment rotated while the sender was catching up.

**implementation details for reviewers**
Avoid skipping a frame published after trySendOne observes the old segment tip but before it observes that the producer rotated to a new active segment. Re-read the current segment's published offset before advancing so the I/O loop sends any newly published tail frame instead of moving to the next segment.

author: vjpixel
body:
## Contexto (#1952)
O editor reclama de uma **área cinza atrás do conteúdo** — faixas nas laterais, fora da coluna de 600px. Diagnóstico do issue: o HTML já é branco desde #1945, então o cinza vem do **canvas do e-mail** (a "tela" que o Beehiiv/preview desenha ao redor do corpo).

## Investigação
- **Worker draft** (`workers/draft/src/index.ts` `handleGet`): serve o HTML **raw**, sem shell — o preview reflete o e-mail exatamente. O cinza **não** vem de um wrapper do Worker.
- **Render** (`render-newsletter-html.ts`): `PAGE_BG = PAPER = #FFFFFF` (#1943/#1945). `<body>`, wrapper externo e container 600px são **todos brancos**; só os painéis de contraste (`SURFACE #EBE5D0`) seguem bege. Não há laterais cinza no nosso código.
- **Gap real:** o **fragmento** (forma sem `fullDocument` — é o que o Worker hospeda e o que é colado no Beehiiv) não tem `<body>` próprio. O preview dependia do default do browser e o **Beehiiv pinta o canvas cinza** por config global.

## Mudança
Adiciona `background:#FFFFFF` à regra `body{}` do `<style>` compartilhado (`DS_STYLE_BLOCK`):
- fixa o preview do Worker explicitamente (não depende do default do browser);
- se o Beehiiv honrar o `<style>` do snippet, sobrepõe o canvas cinza.

## Residual = ação do editor
Se o Beehiiv ignorar o `<style>` do snippet, o cinza remanescente é a **config global de background do e-mail no Beehiiv**: Settings → Publication → Email → Background color = **#FFFFFF** (1x, análogo ao rodapé branco do #1944). Documentado no comentário do issue.

## Teste
`test/email-design-white-1943-1946.test.ts`: trava `body{background:#FFFFFF}` no fragmento. Suite completa: 6113/6113 ✓. `tsc --noEmit` ✓.

⚠️ **Revisão visual do editor** (design cluster — não auto-mergear redesign): confirmar no test email + preview que as laterais ficam brancas.

author: zigrivers
body:
## Summary

Fixes Tracker injection-site rotation guidance so it is computed for the selected calendar day instead of reusing static protocol-level metadata.

## Root Cause

The Tracker page fetched `siteSuggestions` once per active protocol at page render and reused that object across every selected calendar date. The site age metadata also used `loggedAt`, which made backfilled prior-day doses appear as `Today` when viewed from the next scheduled day.

## Changes

- Derive Tracker `SiteData` per calendar event from `localLogs`, scoped to the protocol owner and compound.
- Use `scheduledDate` for site-age calculations when available, keeping `loggedAt` as the tie-breaker for ordering.
- Exclude future logs relative to the selected day and exclude the current log while editing.
- Update site age labels to show `Yesterday` for one-day-old use.
- Make rotation alert copy name the conflicting site, compound, and relative day.
- Include managed users' recent dose logs in the Tracker feed through an explicit allowed-userId predicate.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/acceptance/TRK-tracker.test.ts 'app/(dashboard)/tracker/_components/TrackerCalendar.test.tsx' 'app/(dashboard)/tracker/protocols/[id]/_components/DoseLogActions.test.tsx'`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint` (passes with existing warnings)
- `DATABASE_URL='postgresql://dev:dev@localhost:5432/peptides_dev?schema=public' pnpm check` (118 test files passed, 1143 tests passed, 22 todo, Prisma schema valid)

## Notes

The first full local test run without `DATABASE_URL` failed only because PostgreSQL-gated tests refused to run. A local Postgres container was already running, migrations were current, and the full check passed with `DATABASE_URL` set.

author: yarik01337
body:
## TASK-020 — Alerts cursor (keyset) pagination (Epic D)

Замена offset/limit-пагинации `GET /alerts` на стабильный keyset по `(first_seen DESC, id DESC)`. Scorer/delivery не трогаем — только читаем `alerts`.

### Backend
- **keyset** `service.py`: предикат `tuple_(first_seen, id) < tuple_(literal(fs), literal(id))` (row-value, bind-params), `ORDER BY first_seen DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1` (fetch+1 → next_cursor). Tiebreaker `id` обязателен (first_seen не уникален) — нет дублей/пропусков на границе и при вставке между страницами.
- **opaque cursor** base64url `[first_seen_iso, id]` (`_encode/_decode_cursor`); декодер валидирует тип И диапазон (отклоняет `bool`-как-int, ограничивает int8) → битый/crafted cursor = **422**, не 500 (DB-overflow). Cursor несёт только позицию; `user.id` из auth-сессии, tenant-scope (`Alert.user_id` И `Cluster.user_id`) + history-window (`PLAN_LIMITS`) безусловны и ДО keyset → обхода нет.
- **контракт** `AlertListResponse{items, next_cursor: str|None, history_unavailable}` (убраны total/limit/offset); `router.py` параметр `cursor` (offset убран).
- **индекс** `ix_alerts_user_first_seen(user_id, first_seen)` (модель + миграция **0006**, chain 0005→0006, up create / down drop).

### Frontend
- `useAlerts` infinite-query по `next_cursor` (стоп на null); вынесены `alertsNextPageParam`/`ALERTS_INITIAL_PAGE_PARAM` (unit проверяет реальные хелперы). `api.ts ListAlertsParams{cursor?, limit?}`. `list.tsx` не тронут (абстракция). gen.types/openapi.json регенерены офлайн.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1** ✅ cursor-листание без дублей/пропусков, tiebreaker (на ненулевых микросекундах), insert-between-pages стабилен, next_cursor=None на конце — integration.
- **AC2** ✅ миграция 0006 реально применяется (`alembic upgrade head`, `\di` подтверждает индекс), down дропает, единственная голова 0006.
- **AC3** ✅ контракт {items,next_cursor}; limit clamp (named const); битый + out-of-range cursor → 422; cursor opaque/bind-params.
- **AC4** ✅ tenant-scope + Free→empty+history_unavailable + Pro/Team окно сохранены.
- **AC5** ✅ фронт infinite по cursor; типы из gen.types; tsc/build зелёные.
- **AC6** ✅ G2 за nginx: 0006 применилась в стеке, GET /api/alerts auth-guard 401, Playwright alerts.spec.ts 4/4.

## Test plan
- [x] backend integration `test_alerts_api.py` — 15 passed (вкл. out-of-range cursor)
- [x] `test_migrations.py` + реальный upgrade/downgrade 0006
- [x] `make ci-fast` — ruff/mypy strict/244 unit зелёные
- [x] frontend lint/tsc/build + 128 unit зелёные
- [x] Playwright alerts.spec.ts 4/4 за nginx (`make build`+`make up`, чистый том)

## Review / Security
- Review (opus): 0 CRITICAL/HIGH; keyset-корректность и tenant/history-инварианты выдержаны. 2 MEDIUM + LOW исправлены (round-trip микросекунды, unit импортирует реальные хелперы, dict-типизация).
- Security (opus): 0 блокеров; SQL параметризован, обход tenant-scope через cursor невозможен, DoS-лимиты на месте, 422 без утечек. 2 LOW исправлены (валидация диапазона/типа id в декодере).

## Заметка
- Pre-existing flaky `watchlists.spec.ts:36` (create-watchlist таймаут) — вне scope TASK-020; alerts e2e изолированно 4/4.

author: a-canary
body:
## Symptom
Observed in task 000056-hygiene-cli-proxy-trash-retired-files: the factory dispatched a cli-proxy project into an `arc-agents-` worktree (the wrong physical repo). The branch name was correct (`worker/<id>`) but the worktree path was `~/worktrees/arc-agents-<id>/` instead of `~/worktrees/cli-proxy-<id>/`. Same routing bug as the grllm-58 journal entry's 'Cross-project quirk' section.

## Root cause
`bin/worker-shell.sh project_repo_path()` had a hardcoded case table (starlight → expert-horde, starlight-slm → starlight-slm) with a fallthrough to ${REPO:-} (the dispatcher's repo, arc-agents). For project=cli-proxy, the fallthrough kicks in and the worker ends up in the wrong physical repo.

## Fix
1. **Add the case entry** — `cli-proxy) echo "/home/aaron/repos/cli-proxy" ;;` in the project_repo_path() case table.
2. **Port the supporting plumbing** the worktree was missing — the function definition itself, WT_PARENT variable, CLAIM_PROJECT extraction from the claim JSON, the worktree-add sanity check, and the WT_PARENT-based worktree path. The worktree was forked from a main HEAD that did not have the function (the function only lived as uncommitted state in /home/aaron/repos/arc-agents at the time of dispatch), so this is the minimum-change path.
3. **Factory fails loud** — the `if [[ ! -d "$WT_PARENT" ]]; then ... exit 2; fi` guard aborts BEFORE the worktree-add attempt. A future typo'd or missing mapping surfaces as a clear stderr JSON line + exit 2, not as a silently-wrong-repo worker.
4. **Verify** via the new `bin/worker-shell-project-repo.test.ts` — 10 test cases, all pass.

## Test surface (10 cases)
- the new cli-proxy mapping (regression guard: must NOT be $REPO)
- the two pre-existing mappings (sibling regression guards)
- the back-compat fallthrough for unknown/empty projects (arc-agents, arc-webui, etc. still go to $REPO)
- the ARC_PROJECT_REPO_<project> env override contract:
  - dashes normalized to underscores in the env name
  - empty override does NOT silently route back to $REPO
- the non-existent-dir case stays in the function (pure); the missing-dir guard lives at the call site

## Behavior delta
- Before: project=cli-proxy → worker spawns in empty arc-agents worktree (wrong repo).
- After: project=cli-proxy → worker spawns in /home/aaron/repos/cli-proxy worktree.
- No change for arc-agents, arc-webui, arc-skills, or any other project that lives inside arc-agents: they still fall through to $REPO via the unchanged default case.

## Diff
```
bin/worker-shell-project-repo.test.ts | 165 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
bin/worker-shell.sh                   |  85 ++++++++++++++++--
2 files changed, 244 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
```

## Diff review
Logged as event seq (see ledger) with consequences, surprises_vs_brief, gaps_vs_brief, adr_conflicts. Self-review (no Agent tool in this worker environment; reduced independence flag noted in evidence_md at merge time).

author: villavicencio
body:
## The bug

The drive-path interactive-CAPTCHA auto-solver (PR #6) **never fired on real reCAPTCHA/Turnstile/hCaptcha widgets** — confirmed live: the solver is correctly wired and the provider has balance, but a solve was never attempted (no provider task, no error log, page left challenged).

**Root cause — a render race.** `navigate()` resolves at `waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"`, then `#settle` runs `#trySolveCaptcha` immediately. But the widget's response field (`g-recaptcha-response` etc.) is injected by the widget's **async** script, which runs *after* `domcontentloaded`. So the one-shot detect saw the container (`.g-recaptcha[data-sitekey]`) with **no response field yet** → `tokLen` = `-1` → the old boolean `responseEmpty` was `false` → `liveCaptchaToChallenge` returned `null` → `#trySolveCaptcha` bailed at `if (!challenge) return false`. The only other detect pass is the next action, which for a form submit re-navigates and re-races — so an async-rendered widget was **never** solvable.

The solver shipped validated only against already-rendered widgets (the spike tested `solve()` in isolation), so the full `navigate → settle → detect` timing was never exercised end-to-end on the HTTP/drive path. This is its first real E2E run.

## The fix

- **`DETECT_LIVE_CAPTCHA_JS`** now reports the response field as a tri-state **`respLen`** (`-1` absent / `0` empty / `>0` filled) instead of collapsing "absent" and "filled" into one "not solvable" boolean — the conflation that hid the render-in-progress state.
- **New pure `awaitSolvableCaptcha(detect, urlOf, wait, opts)`** polls out the race: returns a challenge as soon as the field renders **empty** (solvable), stops **immediately** when there's no widget or it's **already filled** (no speculative solve), and gives up after a **2s render budget** if a container never draws its field. The I/O is injected, so the decision logic is **pure and unit-tested without a browser**.
- **`#trySolveCaptcha`** wires page I/O (`page.evaluate` / `page.url` / `page.waitForTimeout`) to the helper; behavior is otherwise unchanged (re-verify, main-world inject, replay guard all intact).

## Tests

New regression coverage in `test/captcha-live.test.mjs` for the exact failure (container present, response field rendered late → solve **is** attempted), plus no-widget, already-solved, and never-renders cases. Existing pure-gate tests updated to the `respLen` tri-state.

**165 tests pass; typecheck clean.** No behavior change when no solver is configured (still no-ops). The in-browser solve is verified out-of-band against a live reCAPTCHA demo after deploy.

body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

This PR addresses two critical bugs related to account-switching and session lifecycle on Android TV devices:

1. HomeScreen State Retention (Stale ViewModel): When switching from the primary account to another profile (e.g. Arlie's), the home page loaded blank/stale data. This happened because GoRouter/Flutter reuses the existing `_HomeShellState` during fast transitions (`/home` -> `/startup?bootstrap=1` -> `/home`). It held a reference to the old user's `HomeViewModel` even though singletons were reset.
2. Silently Caught 401 Expirations: If a profile's token was expired/revoked (e.g. Hux's), the initial `getCurrentUser` check in `_postLoginSync` would catch a `401 Unauthorized` exception silently, failing to load any libraries or plugin stats, leaving the user stuck on a broken home page without feedback.

## What this adds

A maintainer-triggered, **advisory** review that posts a short, descriptive summary of what a submission actually does — viewed through the three bars (general-purpose, open system, novel contribution). **It makes no decision** (no approve/reject); a human still decides.

### How it works
- Add the **`arc-review`** label to a submission PR → workflow runs on a GitHub-hosted runner.
- Runs **Claude Code (Opus 4.8)** headless; reads the PR **and the linked code repo** via `gh` (the key lesson: the truth is in the repo, not the PR text).
- Posts/updates a **single** marked comment (no spam).
- **Never executes submission code** — `pull_request_target` with base checkout, reads file contents via the GitHub API only. PR/repo content is treated as untrusted data.

### Files
- `.github/skills/community-pr-review/SKILL.md` — agent-agnostic, descriptive-only review instructions
- `.github/scripts/generate_review.sh` — runs Claude Code, emits the comment body (marker-trimmed)
- `.github/scripts/upsert_comment.sh` — single-comment upsert
- `.github/workflows/community-review.yml` — label-gated workflow
- `.gitignore` — exclude `.env*`, `.claude/`, `review-comment.md`

### Validated locally
Real Opus 4.8 runs on PRs #10, #13 (hardcoded/replay patterns) and #17 (a genuinely general harness) produced accurate, descriptive summaries. Comment posting runs for real once merged + labeled.

### Before it works (post-merge)
1. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` repo secret — ✅ added

author: ppeble
body:
## Summary

Ports the four-event taxonomy from `platform-operations/claude-notify` into this shell tool. Each Claude Code hook is now wired with an event-key argument so it gets its own message and macOS system sound, instead of the three coarse hook-name events we had before. Keeps `SubagentStop` as an extra (the reference tool does not have it).

| Hook / matcher | Key | Message | Sound |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Notification` / `permission_prompt` | `permission` | 🔐 Permission needed to continue | Funk |
| `Notification` / `elicitation_dialog` | `elicitation` | ✏️ Waiting for your input | Funk |
| `PreToolUse` / `AskUserQuestion` | `question` | ❓ Claude has a question for you | Funk |
| `Stop` | `stop` | ✅ Task completed successfully | Glass |
| `SubagentStop` | `subagent` | Subagent finished | Glass |

## Changes

- **`notify.sh`**: dispatch by argv event key; distinct copy per event, Glass on "done" and Funk on "needs you". Title now carries session context (`Claude Code · project · session-id`) so concurrent sessions are tellable apart. Falls back to deriving the key from the stdin `hook_event_name` when called with no argument, so legacy wiring keeps working.
- **`install.sh`**: wires five matchers (splitting `Notification` into `permission_prompt` / `elicitation_dialog` and adding `PreToolUse` / `AskUserQuestion`). Re-running migrates an older install in place. `--no-stop` / `--no-subagent` preserved.
- **`uninstall.sh`**: also matches keyed commands.
- **macOS sounds**: `osascript` and `terminal-notifier` play the per-event system sound; `CLAUDE_NOTIFIER_SOUND` still overrides with a file on any platform.
- **`CLAUDE_NOTIFIER_EVENTS`**: accepts the new event keys and the legacy hook names.
- **Docs / versioning**: README events table, config, and manual setup updated. `VERSION` bumped `0.2.0` -> `0.3.0` with a matching `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

## Test plan

- `bash -n` clean on all scripts; ShellCheck clean.
- Install: an older bare-command install migrates to the five keyed matchers, idempotent on re-run, and an unrelated foreign hook is preserved.
- Dispatch (logger backend): each key emits the right message; legacy stdin fallback works; event gating works by both key and legacy hook name; `--test [key]` works.
- `--no-stop --no-subagent` correctly omits those two matchers.
- Uninstall removes all keyed hooks, prunes empty arrays, and keeps foreign hooks.

author: h-tacayama
body:
Closes #58

## Summary

Adds `ROWS` / `RANGE` window frames, enabling moving and cumulative window calculations and laying the groundwork for `LAST_VALUE` / `NTH_VALUE`. Scope matches the window-frame coverage of "SQLポケットリファレンス (改訂第5版)".

## API

Frames attach to an ordered window (a frame requires `ORDER BY`, enforced by the type system):

```csharp
Sum(u.Amount).Over(OrderBy(u.Date).Rows(UnboundedPreceding))                          // ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
Avg(u.Price).Over(OrderBy(u.Date).Rows(Preceding(4)))                                 // ROWS 4 PRECEDING (moving avg)
Sum(u.Amount).Over(PartitionBy(u.Dept).OrderBy(u.Date).RowsBetween(UnboundedPreceding, CurrentRow))
                                                                                      // ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
Sum(u.Amount).Over(OrderBy(u.Age).RangeBetween(Preceding(10), Following(10)))         // RANGE BETWEEN 10 PRECEDING AND 10 FOLLOWING
```

- Methods: `Rows` / `RowsBetween` / `Range` / `RangeBetween` (names mirror the SQL phrases, like `OrderBy`, `GroupBy`, `NullsFirst`). Each maps 1:1 to a distinct SQL frame form.
- Bounds: `UnboundedPreceding`, `CurrentRow`, `UnboundedFollowing` (properties); `Preceding(n)`, `Following(n)` (methods). Offsets are emitted as integer literals (SQL Server requires constant frame offsets).
- No global `Between` helper — `BETWEEN` is expressed by the `RowsBetween` / `RangeBetween` method names, avoiding any collision with the `col.Between(...)` condition.
- The extent is emitted verbatim; SqlArtisan does not validate bound combinations, consistent with the faithful-generation philosophy.
- `OverClause` is simplified to a single content part.

## Out of scope

- `GROUPS` frame unit and `EXCLUDE ...` (not in the reference; deferred).

## Dialect note

`ROWS` / `RANGE` frames require PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL 8.0+, SQLite 3.25+, or SQL Server 2012+.

## Testing

- Added `WindowFrameTests` (single bound, `ROWS BETWEEN`, `RANGE BETWEEN`, with `PARTITION BY`), Arrange-Act-Assert style.
- Full suite: 314 tests passing; Release build clean (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- README and CHANGELOG updated.

author: mahdighandi1989
body:
User's DevTools response headers on the failing chunk:
  server: cloudflare
  cf-ray: a0915aa10a4f1d87-DXB
  status: 403
  content-type: text/html
  content-length (req): 28040  ← only 27KB, well under 32KB cap

So this whole time it was NOT Render's edge cap rejecting the body. The backend is fronted by Cloudflare (Render's Dubai PoP) and CF's rate-limiter / bot-detector is the one returning 403:
  - first chunk POST → 200 OK
  - second identical-shape POST 41ms later → 403 (no body, HTML page)
  - no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on the 403 → browser surfaces it as the «Failed to fetch» / CORS-style error we kept chasing

The smaller-chunk fix was harmless but addressed the wrong layer. What actually trips the CF rule is the rapid-fire identical POSTs to the same path. Pacing them stops the rate-limiter from firing.

Both chunked uploaders (idea-text path in generatePrompt + the task-save chunk loop in savePromptAsTask) now:
  1. wait 350ms between successive chunk POSTs (only between, not before the first one) — this alone clears the rule in testing
  2. if a chunk still comes back 403, sleep 1500ms and retry once. One CF rate-limit window is plenty; a second 403 is treated as a real failure and surfaces to the user.

For a 200KB payload at 32KB/chunk that's 6 inter-chunk gaps × 350ms ≈ 2.1s extra latency. Compared to the user waiting 10+ minutes for the multi-pass prompt and then seeing the save silently fail, this is invisible.

Updated test_tasks_from_draft_chunked.py search window (6000→10000 chars) so the small-payload-direct-POST pin still finds the else branch after the new retry logic pushed it down.

Backend tests: 10/10 pinned tests pass. Frontend tsc: clean.

author: ellistarn
body:
## Summary

- Filter terminating instances from the Kind and RGD controller's forEach collections using `watchInstances.filter(i, !has(i.metadata.deletionTimestamp))`
- Fix compiler bug: deferred CEL validation now types watch nodes as `list(dyn)` (was `any`, which broke comprehension macros)
- Add e2e test proving the create/delete churn loop exists without the fix

## Problem

When a Kind instance is held in Terminating (e.g., by an external finalizer), the Kind controller's forEach re-creates the per-instance Graph on every reconcile. The new Graph immediately detects `ownerDeleting` and self-deletes, producing an unbounded create/delete loop (4+ wasted API calls per cycle).

## Fix

The forEach collection in `kind.yaml` and `rgd.yaml` now explicitly filters out instances with a `deletionTimestamp`. This is a template-level business logic decision: each controller declares it only iterates live instances.

The compiler's deferred expression validator had a latent bug that prevented this: `ChildScope` didn't distinguish watch nodes from other nodes, so all child IDs were typed as `any` instead of `list(dyn)`. CEL comprehension macros (`.filter()`, `.map()`) require `list` typing. Fixed by tracking `WatchNodeIDs` separately and registering them via `WithListVariables`.

## Testing

`TestKindForEachSkipsTerminatingInstances` — holds an instance in Terminating via a test finalizer, waits for the per-instance Graph to self-delete, then asserts the Graph stays absent for 5 seconds. Without the fix, the Graph is re-created within ~200ms.

author: rynaro
body:
## Problem

NeoVim only ever rendered the **dark** theme regardless of the active Potions variant. Switching to `white`/`sepia` (`potions theme set|cycle`) updated the terminal, Zellij, and shell — but nvim stayed dark.

**Root cause:** the nvim adapter emitted `colorscheme alchemists-orchid-light` / `-sepia`, but [`alchemists-orchid.nvim`](https://github.com/Rynaro/alchemists-orchid.nvim) (now **v2.0**) ships a **single** colorscheme whose palette is chosen at runtime via `require('alchemists-orchid').setup({ mode = 'dark'|'light'|'sepia' })`. Those per-variant colorscheme names never existed, so white/sepia silently fell back to plain `colorscheme alchemists-orchid` → `setup()` with no args → **always dark.**

## What changed

**Core — nvim now follows the rotation** (`.potions/lib/theme/adapters.sh`)
- Maps variant → plugin mode (`dark→dark`, `white→light`, `sepia→light`) and drives the real `setup({ mode, overrides })` API, with a graceful fallback to the bundled colorscheme if the plugin is missing/pre-2.0.
- Pins `bg`/`fg` to `COLOR_SURFACE`/`COLOR_ON_SURFACE` so the editor body byte-matches the terminal/Zellij surface.
- **Sepia rides the plugin's _light_ mode with parchment overrides** — the plugin's own `sepia` mode is a dark warm-brown (`#2E2A24`) that would clash with Potions' light-parchment sepia everywhere else.

**Chrome — light barbar shipped** (`white.tokens.json` + `sepia.tokens.json`)
- Adds variant-aware `component.nvim.*` blocks (tab active/visible/inactive, fg.bright/dim, muted, visual) so the barbar tabline, Visual selection, and cheat float are legible on light surfaces instead of inheriting the base Nord-dark shades.
- Cheat-float fg moves `COLOR_SECONDARY` → `COLOR_ON_SURFACE` (SECONDARY stays inherited, so the base-inheritance witness test holds).

**Plumbing**
- Recompiled `white.theme`/`sepia.theme` + regenerated `docs/color-palette.md`.
- Reload nvim matrix now points at `:source ~/.potions/nvim/generated/palette.vim` (re-sourcing applies the new variant live).
- Bumped `.version` → **2.15.1** + regenerated `.checksums`.

## Mode mapping

| Variant | Plugin mode | Editor surface |
|---|---|---|
| dark  | `dark`  | `#2e3440` (unchanged) |
| white | `light` | `#fafbfc` |
| sepia | `light` + overrides | `#f5f0e6` parchment |

## Testing

- **268/268 tests pass** (`./test.sh`), including compiler-drift, VG-DOCS, VG-PAIR, base-inheritance gates, and new `dark→dark, sepia→light parchment` mapping assertions.
- Verified generated `palette.vim` for all three variants: dark unchanged; white/sepia produce dark-on-light foregrounds across Normal, BufferCurrent, Visual, and the cheat float.

## Notes / deferred

- Non-truecolor **cterm** fallback for barbar still uses hardcoded named colors (`DarkGrey`/`Black`); the truecolor path is fully correct. Minor residual light-cterm quirk, deferred.

The split lens (from #530) already handled googletest's super-project subpackage target (it finds the artifact by glob, not `//:gtest`). The remaining deltas were all toolchain/codegen noise, now classified benign:

### 1. Weak-symbol emission variance
A **weak** (`nm W`/`V`) symbol present in only one artifact is benign: weak/vague-linkage items (inline funcs, implicit template instantiations) are emitted per-TU on demand and deduped at link, so the optimizer's emit-vs-elide choice — driven by codegen flags the cc **toolchain** owns (`-fPIC`/`-fstack-protector`/frame-pointer defaults Bazel adds, cmake doesn't), not the converter — never affects a consumer (it re-emits its own copy). Captured via `nm --defined-only -g`; classified `weak-symbol-only-in-{cmake,bazel}`. (gtest's pthread `Mutex`/`ThreadLocal`/`FilePath` weak ctors.)

### 2. libc/libstdc++ runtime undefined refs
Extend `isLibcRuntimeHelper` with the **stdio builtins** the compiler folds printf-family calls into (`puts`/`putchar`/`fputs`/`fputc`/`putc`/`fwrite`) and the **nested-std vtable/typeinfo/VTT** prefixes (`_ZTVNSt`/`_ZTINSt`/`_ZTTSt`/`_ZTTNSt` — e.g. `std::ostringstream`), alongside the existing direct-std `_ZTVSt`/`_ZTISt`.

`googletest.symfidelity` pins `-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=17` on the cmake side to match the `-std=c++17` the converter pins from gtest's declared standard (cmake's default-compiler configure omits it), trimming standard-version emission noise.

## Correctness story

- googletest symbol-fidelity **ok** end-to-end (888 / 29 benign / 0 impactful).
- `go build/vet/test ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `make staticcheck` clean.
- Guards: `TestClassifyExportedDeltas_WeakSymbolBenign` (weak-only benign, strong-only impactful), `TestIsLibcRuntimeHelper` (stdio + nested-std vtable/VTT recognized; project-own symbols not).

(Both classifier rules are general — they reduce false impactful deltas across the whole corpus, not just googletest.)

author: fukusaka
body:
## Motivation

This closes the five-task A2.5 audit follow-up that started after PR #736 (the seam knob 4-pack). The audit flagged the `readEnabled` flip ↔ multishot recv rearm sequencing as a high-priority gap — there was no deterministic seam coverage of what happens when an `IoUringIoTransport` cycles `readEnabled` while a multishot recv is still armed, and loopback integration tests rarely backpressure fast enough to exercise the race. Writing the seam test surfaced a latent double-arm bug — the same shape as `IoUringOwnedSource`'s `-ENOBUFS` double-arm fixed in PR #737.

## 動機

PR #736 (seam knob 4-pack) 直後の A2.5 audit follow-up 5 件を closeする最後の PR。 audit が `readEnabled` flip ↔ multishot recv rearm sequencing を high-priority gap と指摘していた — `IoUringIoTransport` が multishot recv armed 状態で `readEnabled` を cycle するとき何が起こるか deterministic seam coverage 無し、 loopback integration では backpressure が race を露呈するほど速く起きない。 seam test を書いた途端、 PR #737 で fix した `IoUringOwnedSource` の `-ENOBUFS` double-arm と同じ shape の latent bug が露呈。

## Modification

### Design decisions

- **Bug**: `IoUringIoTransport.readEnabled.setter` called `armRecv()` unconditionally on every `false → true` flip, even when `multishotSlot >= 0`. A backpressure cycle on a busy connection (`true → false → true`) submitted a second multishot recv SQE, orphaned the slot of the first multishot recv in `callbackSlots[]`, and the kernel double-delivered the same `bufId` CQEs into the shared `wrappers[]`. The same shape as PR #737, just on a different state-machine.
- **Fix shape**: gate `armRecv()` on `multishotSlot < 0 && !recvStarved`. The first half avoids re-arming over a live SQE. The second half avoids racing the `rearmRecvAfterStarvation` callback that the previous `-ENOBUFS` already registered with the provided-buffer ring — that callback re-checks `readEnabled` at fire time and arms there, so a setter-side arm at the same moment would again produce two SQEs sharing `wrappers[]`.
- **`armPollAddForFin` KDoc is aspirational**. While writing the tests, observed that the `armPollAddForFin` KDoc says "the multishot recv path only delivers `res = 0` CQE on FIN while it is armed — i.e. while `readEnabled = true`. When a user holds `readEnabled = false` ... no recv SQE is queued." That is the design intent, but the actual implementation does NOT cancel the multishot recv SQE on `readEnabled = false` (only `cancelIdleTimeout()` runs). The `POLL_ADD` for FIN is still needed regardless, because peer FIN detection through the recv path only works when buffers are flowing — but the rationale recorded in the KDoc overstates what the setter does today. The second test (`readEnabled true to false does not cancel ...`) pins the current behaviour; a future change that brings impl in line with the KDoc surfaces here.
- **Three seam tests in `IoUringTransportReadEnabledSeamTest`**: arm sanity, no-cancel-on-flip-down, no-double-arm-on-flip-up. Tests run on the test thread via the existing seam pattern (`assertInEventLoop` no-ops pre-`start`).
- **Red-Green verified**: the pre-fix setter produces `Expected <1>, actual <2>` on the double-arm test (second `getSqe` call from the duplicate `armRecv()`). Applying the gate flips it to `<1>`. No regression in the 45 pre-existing io_uring seam tests.

## 変更内容

### 設計判断

- **bug 本体**: `IoUringIoTransport.readEnabled.setter` が `false → true` flip のたびに無条件 `armRecv()` を呼ぶ。 `multishotSlot >= 0` (live な multishot recv が in-flight) でも armRecv が走り、 第 2 の multishot recv SQE が submit、 第 1 の slot は `callbackSlots[]` に orphan で残り、 kernel が同じ `bufId` の CQE を両方の slot 経由で配送して shared `wrappers[]` に二重書き込み。 PR #737 の `IoUringOwnedSource` double-arm と同型、 違う state-machine。
- **fix shape**: `multishotSlot < 0 && !recvStarved` で armRecv を gate。 前半で live SQE 上書きを防止、 後半で「先行 `-ENOBUFS` が provided-buffer ring に登録した `rearmRecvAfterStarvation` callback」 との race を防止 (callback は fire 時に `readEnabled` を再確認して arm する、 setter 側が同時に armRecv するとまた wrappers[] を共有する 2 SQE になる)。
- **`armPollAddForFin` KDoc は aspirational**。 test を書く過程で気付いたが、 `armPollAddForFin` の KDoc は「`readEnabled = false` の間 multishot recv SQE は queue されない」 と書いてあるが、 実装は `cancelIdleTimeout()` だけで multishot recv SQE は cancel しない。 POLL_ADD for FIN 自体は依然必要 (peer FIN 検出は recv path 経由だと buffer が流れているときしか効かないため) だが、 KDoc は setter の挙動を実装より強く表現している。 第 2 の test (`readEnabled true to false does not cancel ...`) は現実装を pin、 将来 KDoc に impl を合わせる change が表面化する。
- **`IoUringTransportReadEnabledSeamTest` に 3 seam test**: arm sanity / flip-down で cancel しない / flip-up で double-arm しない。 test thread 上で seam pattern を駆動 (`assertInEventLoop` は pre-`start` で no-op)。
- **Red-Green verify 済**: pre-fix setter で double-arm test が `Expected <1>, actual <2>` で fail。 gate を当てると `<1>`。 既存 45 件 io_uring seam test 無回帰。

## Test plan

- `./gradlew -Ptls -Pbenchmark :keel-engine-io-uring:linuxX64Test` on a Linux host — 3 new tests in `IoUringTransportReadEnabledSeamTest` all green; pre-existing io_uring seam tests green.
- Red-Green verified locally against the pre-fix setter.
- No production-path bench A/B needed — the fix removes a duplicate kernel submission on a degenerate backpressure path; the integration accept / echo tests cover the happy data path.
- detekt clean on touched files.

author: tempovote
body:
## Bugs fixed

### 1. Key mismatch: CIP-129 vs CIP-105 bech32

Koios `/drep_info` returns `drep_id` in **CIP-129** format (e.g. `drep1ygr9...`) while we generate **CIP-105** IDs (e.g. `drep1qe2...`). All `batchInfo[cip105Id]` lookups returned `null` → `liveVotingPower` fell back to Ogmios value, `delegatorCount` was always 0.

Fix: key the result map by `hex` (28-byte credential hash) which is format-stable.

### 2. `delegator_count` not in `/drep_info` response

The endpoint simply doesn't return this field. Fix: add `fetchDelegatorCount()` which calls `/drep_delegators?limit=0` with `Prefer: count=exact` — reads the count from the `Content-Range` header without transferring any rows.

## New leaderboard strategy

| Step | Calls | What |
|------|-------|------|
| Batch `drep_info` | 2 | `liveVotingPower` for all 200 candidates |
| Narrow by `liveVotingPower` | — | Take top `limit × 2` (≤40 DReps) |
| `drep_delegators` individual | ≤40 | `delegatorCount` for narrowed pool |
| Final sort + take | — | Sort by `delegatorCount`, take top `limit` |

Total: ~42 calls vs. previous ≤600 concurrent. Well under Koios burst limit.

author: achimdehnert
body:
## Problem

Self-hosted Runner teilen einen persistenten `setup-python`-Tool-Cache (`site-packages`). Parallele Jobs können sich während Uninstall/Reinstall-Fenstern gegenseitig sehen — `--force-reinstall` war Hotfix, eliminiert aber nicht den Shared-Mutable-Zustand (AD-2/AD-3).

## Fix

Neuer erster Schritt in der Composite Action: job-lokale venv in `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Jeder Job bekommt eine frische `site-packages`; Pip Wheel/Download-Cache bleibt geteilt. `GITHUB_PATH`-Eintrag aktiviert die venv für alle nachfolgenden Steps im Caller-Workflow.

`pip check` von advisory auf hard gate hochgestuft (saubere venv = keine vorbestehenden Konflikte). `--force-reinstall` bleibt vorerst (Sunset mit Messung nach Verifikation, REC-17).

## Canary / Rollback

Alle Repos nutzen `@main` → Merge rollt sofort für alle aus. Rollback: `git revert` + Push.

Fixes: achimdehnert/platform#357

author: albanm
body:
Add opt-in, consent-gated server-side storage of conversation traces, with admin review tooling, replacing the old in-browser session recorder and trace upload/handoff.

**What changed:**
- New `trace-requests` collection storing each physical gateway request/response; written fire-and-forget only when the org enables `storeTraces` *and* the user consents (`x-trace-consent`). Auto-expires after 30 days via a TTL index.
- Gateway tags and records turn / sub-agent / compaction / moderation requests; the trace is reconstructed into a reviewable session on the client.
- Admin API under `/api/traces`: paginated conversation list, fetch-by-conversation, delete-conversation, and GDPR per-user erasure (`DELETE /:type/:id?userId=`).
- New read-only **activity page** (config + usage + paginated traces) and **per-trace review page**; two-tab chat debug dialog with an admin review link and a consent sheet/toggle.
- Removed the in-browser session recorder, trace upload, and the old trace-review page/handoff.
- Merges `main`: adopts the `usage/enforce.ts` quota refactor (#16) and the parallel-tool-call streaming fix (#17), keeping trace capture in the same stream loop.

**Why:** give admins a way to review real conversations for debugging/quality, while keeping it strictly opt-in per org and per user, with bounded retention.

**Regression risks (reviewer focus):**
- `settings` PUT now omits `models` when the form sends none (documented form-diff fix); with `replaceOne` this clears a stored empty `models`. Confirm no consumer reads `settings.models`/`settings.quotas` without optional chaining — both are now optional in the schema.
- Streaming path now interleaves the parallel-tool-call indexing (from main) with trace tool-call accumulation — covered by the parallel-tool-calls API test.
- New TTL index means stored traces self-delete after 30 days; five new indexes are created on the `trace-requests` collection at startup.
- `GET /traces/conversation/:id` looks up across owners before authorizing (returns 403 with no data to non-admins of the owner).

author: fw-bot
body:
**Description of the issue/feature this PR addresses:**

When generating a SEPA QR code for a vendor bill payment, the embedded 
amount could occasionally contain excess decimal places instead of 
respecting the currency's expected precision.

This occurs because the `amount` variable in `_get_qr_vals` was being 
converted directly using `str(amount)`. Due to Python's floating-point 
arithmetic, the float value in memory can contain decimal drift.
Directly casting it to a string exposes this drift in the payload.

This commit resolves the issue by replacing `str(amount)` with 
`float_repr(amount, currency.decimal_places)`. This safely bypasses 
the float representation issue, ensuring the string strictly respects 
the currency's configured decimal precision before being injected 
into the QR code.

opw-5504258

**Steps to reproduce:**

- Select company “My Belgian Company”
- Create a 23% purchase tax
- Create vendor bill
   - Select Vendor “BE Company CoA”
   - Choose any single product, change price to 37.18 and choose the 23% tax. The Untaxed Amount should be 37.18, VAT tax should be 8.55, and Total should be 45.73
   - Confirm > Register Payment > scan QR code. EUR45.730000000000004 should show

**Current behavior before PR:**

- When generating a SEPA QR code for a payment, the embedded amount can contain excess decimal places due to floating-point drift.

**Desired behavior after PR is merged:**

- The SEPA QR code is generated with the correct number of decimal places.

author: bjcoombs
body:
## Summary

Doc-staleness flagged a doc by how long since the doc file itself last changed (the decaying-map churn ratio). For a **generated** doc - a Jira note dump, an API reference, codegen output - that is the wrong measure:

- A generated doc is fresh when it matches the data it was derived from, stale when its **source** has moved on - regardless of the file's wall-clock age.
- A freshly regenerated dump of ~1,200 notes shares one recent mtime (looks fresh) even when its source changed afterwards.
- An old-but-accurate generated doc reads as a `lying_map` under the age model when it is not.

The meaningful signal: a generated doc is stale **iff its source is newer than the doc**.

## Changes Made

- **`lib/doc_provenance.py`** (new) - resolves a doc's provenance and computes `source_newer`:
  - Frontmatter `source:` (string / inline list / block list) + optional `generated_by:`, parsed with a minimal stdlib parser (no YAML dependency). Resolved relative to the repo root, then the doc's directory.
  - `.assess/config.toml` `[[generated]]` array-of-tables mapping a folder to its source(s), for bulk-generated trees that can't each carry frontmatter. Frontmatter wins when both name a source.
  - `source_newer` compares last-change times on one axis (git commit time, falling back to mtime).
- **`lib/git_churn.py`** - extracted `file_last_commit_epoch` (raw commit timestamp) and reimplemented `file_last_commit_days` on top of it.
- **`lib/assess_config.py`** - `load_generated_sources` reads the `[[generated]]` map (degrades silently like the other loaders).
- **`lib/doc_staleness.py`** - resolves provenance per doc, carries the verdict in the `provenance` block of each doc dict, and forces `ratio = 0.0` when the source has not moved (so a fresh generated doc is never a decaying/lying map for any downstream consumer, including `stale_hubs`).
- **`lib/doc_complexity_join.py`** - `_signed_freshness` signs freshness from `source_newer` (+1 fresh / -1 stale) instead of the churn ratio when a provenance verdict exists; the verdict is treated as high-confidence and bypasses the repo-baseline / degenerate-churn confidence guards that exist only to discount the ratio.

The `lying_map` contract key is unchanged - only *when* it fires for generated docs changes.

## Testing

- `tests/test_doc_provenance.py` (new) - frontmatter parsing (scalar/list/block, quotes, comments, malformed), resolution precedence, config prefix-on-segment matching, and `source_is_newer` True/False/None.
- `tests/test_doc_staleness.py` - generated doc with source newer (flagged) vs not-newer (fresh, ratio 0); config-mapping path; ordinary doc carries no provenance block.
- `tests/test_doc_complexity_join.py` - source-not-moved is never a `lying_map` (the issue's hard requirement); source-moved-on is a `lying_map` even on a low-confidence repo-baseline doc; indeterminate verdict falls back to the ratio.
- Full `skills/assess` suite (599 passed), `scripts/` build suite (105), plugin contract (183), ruff + mypy all green.

## Risk Assessment

Low. Provenance is opt-in and additive: a doc with no `source:` declared and no `[[generated]]` mapping behaves exactly as before (no `provenance` block emitted, churn ratio drives freshness). The golden baseline is unchanged.

## Deployment Notes

Plugin version bumped to 1.39.0.

Closes #178

author: ranjitjhala
body:
(This is a redone version of #1644)

## Why?

Rustc often inserts intermediate basic blocks that serve only as merge points with no meaningful statements. When Flux treats these as join points, it emits unnecessary KVars that lose precision. By detecting these dummy blocks and skipping past them during checking, we preserve the type information flowing through the real control-flow edges. For example, consider the test `dummy_join00.rs`, which is

```rust
#[flux::spec(fn (x: i32) -> i32{v: 1 <= v && v <= 4})]
pub fn test(x: i32) -> i32 {
    if x == 0 {
        1
    } else if x == 1 {
        2
    } else if x == 2 {
        3
    } else if x == 3 {
        4
    } else {
        test(x - 1)
    }
}
```

In `main` we get the constraint (cargo x run tests/tests/pos/surface/dummy_join00.rs -- -Fdump-constraint) If you look at `dummy_join00.test.simp.fluxc` on `main`

```
∀ .
  ∀ a0: int.
    (a0 ≠ 0) =>
      (a0 ≠ 1) =>
        (a0 ≠ 2) =>
          (a0 ≠ 3) =>
            ∀ a1: int.
              (1 ≤ a1 ∧ a1 ≤ 4) => $k0(a1)[a0] ~ Goto(bb10) at 9:12: 13:6
          ¬(a0 ≠ 3) => $k0(4)[a0] ~ Goto(bb10) at 10:9: 10:10
          ∀ a1: int.
            $k0(a1)[a0] => $k1(a1)[a0] ~ Goto(bb11) at 7:12: 13:6
        ¬(a0 ≠ 2) => $k1(3)[a0] ~ Goto(bb11) at 8:9: 8:10
        ∀ a1: int.
          $k1(a1)[a0] => $k2(a1)[a0] ~ Goto(bb12) at 5:12: 13:6
      ¬(a0 ≠ 1) => $k2(2)[a0] ~ Goto(bb12) at 6:9: 6:10
      ∀ a1: int.
        $k2(a1)[a0] => (1 ≤ a1 ∧ a1 ≤ 4) ~ Ret at 3:5: 13:6
```

vs with this optimization, we get the constraint

```
true
```

Similarly, when you _do_ need an actual join, e.g. 

```rust
pub fn test2(x: i32) -> i32 {
    let res = if x == 0 {
        1
    } else if x == 1 {
        2
    } else if x == 2 {
        3
    } else {
        4
    };
    res + 1
}
```

where we can't just directly check the output type in each branch, you get a more compact constraint with a single kvar

```
∀ .  
  ∀ a0: int.  
    (a0 ≠ 0) =>  
      (a0 ≠ 1) =>  
        (a0 ≠ 2) => $k0(4)[a0] ~ Goto(bb9) at 25:9: 25:10
        ¬(a0 ≠ 2) => $k0(3)[a0] ~ Goto(bb9) at 23:9: 23:10
      ¬(a0 ≠ 1) => $k0(2)[a0] ~ Goto(bb9) at 21:9: 21:10
    ¬(a0 ≠ 0) => $k0(1)[a0] ~ Goto(bb9) at 19:9: 19:10
    ∀ a1: int.  
      $k0(a1)[a0] => (2 ≤ a1 + 1 ∧ a1 + 1 ≤ 5) ~ Ret at 27:5: 27:12
```

## What

  - Identify "dummy" basic blocks in the MIR — blocks with multiple incoming edges, only nop statements, and a single Goto terminator — and precompute their "real" (transitively reachable non-dummy) successor
  - In check_goto and fold_unfold's goto, skip dummy blocks by resolving directly to the real successor before the is_join_point check, avoiding spurious KVar emission at these artificial join points
  - Make BasicBlockData::terminator private and access it through Body::terminator_for to enforce consistent usage
  - Use BasicBlockData::new constructor in lowering instead of struct literal

## Key changes

  - crates/flux-rustc-bridge/src/mir.rs: Added DummyBlockTarget enum, mk_dummy_basic_blocks / get_transitive_dummy_target for precomputation, Body::resolve_dummy for lookup, and Body::terminator_for accessor
  - crates/flux-refineck/src/checker.rs: check_goto skips dummy blocks before the is_join_point check; check_basic_block and is_exit_block use terminator_for
  - crates/flux-refineck/src/ghost_statements/fold_unfold.rs: Same skip-dummy-block logic in goto; basic_block uses terminator_for
  - crates/flux-rustc-bridge/src/lowering.rs: Uses BasicBlockData::new constructor

author: copilot
body:
The `publish` GitHub Actions job was failing with a 404 when attempting to `npm publish` for `@harvard-lts/mirador-template-plugin`.

**Root cause:** The workflow was correctly configured for npm OIDC trusted publishing (`id-token: write`, Node ≥22, npm ≥11.5.1) but `npm publish` was missing `--provenance`. Without it, npm bypasses OIDC and falls back to `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, which `actions/setup-node` sets to the GitHub token — invalid for npmjs.org auth → 404.

**Fix:**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish-package.yml
- name: Publish to npm

body:
# Pull Request

Adds `.because(...)` support to architecture rules so users can attach a human-readable rationale to a rule.

When `assert_passes(...)` fails, the rationale is included in the failure message. This makes architecture test failures easier to understand and prepares the API for future generated architecture documentation.

Example:

```python
rule = (
    project_files("src/")
    .in_folder("**/controllers/**")
    .should_not()
    .depend_on_files()
    .in_folder("**/database/**")
    .because("controllers should stay thin and delegate persistence")
)

assert_passes(rule)

author: demircaliskan2009-pixel
body:
Adds a bounded deterministic bridge from BacktestAdmissionDecision plus explicit raw evidence objects into the existing backtest replay admission evaluator. No replay plan mirror, backtest engine, runtime/orchestrator wiring, persistence, connector/readiness, scheduler, live/private API, order-routing, execution, or BIST behavior changed.

## Summary
`build_backtest_replay_bridge(admission_decision, *, strategy_spec, leakage_bias_repaint_result, pit_parity_result, decision_ledger_records, replay_source_id, historical_data_source_id, replay_window, admission_policy, evidence_digest_by_stage=None, metadata=None, correlation_id)` is the **true bridge** (chosen over a parallel ReplayPlan mirror): it proves the supplied *raw* evidence is consistent with the high-level `BacktestAdmissionDecision`, then **delegates** to the existing `evaluate_backtest_replay_admission(...)`. It reuses `BacktestReplayAdmissionStatus` and embeds the existing `BacktestReplayAdmissionResult`; it does not re-implement window/source/policy/currentness validation.

New API: `BacktestReplayBridgeError`, `BacktestReplayBridgeResult`, `build_backtest_replay_bridge(...)`, `backtest_replay_bridge_result_to_dict(result)`.

## Bridge gate (then delegate)
- Wrong-typed `admission_decision` or empty `correlation_id` → `BacktestReplayBridgeError`.
- Pre-evaluator REJECTED (evaluator not reached): decision not ADMITTED/admitted, not paper_only, real flags set, malformed admission_digest, raw `strategy_spec_digest` ≠ `admission_decision.strategy_digest`.
- Pre-evaluator INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: fewer raw ledger records than `admission_decision.decision_record_count` (count-consistency proof — the decision carries only the count, not the per-record digests).
- Otherwise builds `BacktestReplayAdmissionInput` and returns the evaluator's verdict (window/source/policy/BIST/currentness all delegated), wrapped with the `admission_digest` for one-digest traceability.

## Fail-closed / determinism
- No fabrication: unresolvable raw spec or digest mismatch fails closed; no evidence is invented.
- Deterministic canonical SHA-256 `bridge_digest`; no wall-clock/random/IO; frozen dataclass; paper_only=True; no order/route/venue/scheduler/plan/runtime/persistence/store/engine field (asserted).

## Changed files (exactly 2; no __init__ edit)
- `src/crypto_core/validation/backtest_replay_bridge.py` (new)
- `tests/crypto_core/validation/test_backtest_replay_bridge.py` (new, 9 tests)

body:
## Summary

- **Runtime**: Add `RuntimeTestTimeSourceBox` (mutable nanosecond counter) and four `@_cdecl` functions: `kk_test_time_source_new`, `kk_test_time_source_plus_assign`, `kk_test_time_source_mark_now`, `kk_test_time_source_read`
- **Sema stubs**: Wire external link names for `TestTimeSource` constructor, `plusAssign`, `read`; add `markNow` override pointing to `kk_test_time_source_mark_now` so marks are based on the internal counter rather than the real monotonic clock
- **RuntimeABISpec + NonThrowingCallees**: Register all four new functions (required by ABI validation tests)
- **Tests**: Sema golden test (`test_time_source.kt/.golden`) and E2E codegen integration test verifying deterministic mark differences (5ms, 10ms, 15ms, 500ns) and `compareTo` ordering

## Key design note

`TestTimeSource.markNow()` must be overridden in the sema stubs — without the override it inherits `AbstractLongTimeSource.markNow()` which calls `kk_time_source_mark_now` (real monotonic clock), making all `TestTimeSource`-based mark comparisons non-deterministic. The new `kk_test_time_source_mark_now` creates a `RuntimeTimeMarkBox` from the stored nanosecond counter, so `mark2 - mark1` reflects exactly the advancement applied via `+=`.

### [`v4.99.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/HEAD/packages/wrangler/CHANGELOG.md#4990)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/compare/wrangler@4.98.0...wrangler@4.99.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​14169](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14169) [`0706fbf`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/0706fbf950548aaa8177a062a7c5d41822dfba0d) Thanks [@​edmundhung](https://redirect.github.com/edmundhung)! - Introduce `createTestHarness()` for integration testing Workers

  It runs Workers in a local preview environment using production build output and works with both Wrangler projects and Workers built by the Cloudflare Vite plugin.

  Use it from any Node.js test runner to send requests to individual Workers, trigger scheduled events, reset the server between tests, and mock outbound requests with libraries that intercept `globalThis.fetch()`, such as MSW.

  You can also capture structured logs from your Workers with `getLogs()`, or dump out a diagnostic timeline with `debug()` when tests fail:

  ```ts
  import { createTestHarness } from "wrangler";

  const server = createTestHarness({
    workers: [
      { configPath: "./dist/web_worker/wrangler.json" },
      { configPath: "./dist/api_worker/wrangler.json" },
    ],
  });

  await server.listen();
  await server.fetch("http://example.com");

  const apiWorker = server.getWorker("api-worker");
  await apiWorker.fetch("http://example.com/users/123");
  await apiWorker.scheduled({ cron: "0 0 * * *" });

  server.getLogs();

  if (testFailed) {
    server.debug();
  }

  await server.reset();
  await server.close();
  ```

- [#​14174](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14174) [`8cf8c61`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/8cf8c61efb9fd99892bcb250db12d7052b5fef08) Thanks [@​oliy](https://redirect.github.com/oliy)! - Surface pipeline status and failure reasons in `wrangler pipelines list` and `wrangler pipelines get`

  `wrangler pipelines list` now includes a `Status` column, and when any pipelines are in a `failed` state it prints a summary of each failing pipeline along with the reason reported by the API.

  `wrangler pipelines get` now shows the pipeline `Status` in the general details and, for failed pipelines, highlights the failure with the reason returned by the server so it is clear why a pipeline is not running.

- [#​14211](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14211) [`a61ac29`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/a61ac2936ae6b35146d637c18beb94567bb40bfa) Thanks [@​james-elicx](https://redirect.github.com/james-elicx)! - Add `--version-tag` support to `wrangler versions deploy` to deploy a version by its tag

  You can now roll out or roll back a version by the tag it was uploaded with (e.g. a commit SHA passed to `--tag` at upload time) instead of first looking up its Version ID:

  `wrangler versions deploy --version-tag <sha>@​100%`

  The tag is resolved to a Version ID against the worker's deployable versions, and the `<version-tag>@​<percentage>` shorthand works just like the existing `<version-id>@​<percentage>` notation, including splitting traffic across multiple `--version-tag` values. If a tag matches no deployable version, or matches more than one, the command errors and asks you to deploy by Version ID directly. Note that tags can only be resolved against recent (deployable) versions — older versions that have aged out of that window must still be deployed by Version ID.

Now this warning is always printed, and it remains non-blocking in non-interactive contexts.

author: oconnorv
body:
**Step 0 of the word-localization plan** — measurement scaffolding so every future word-box improvement is a measured before/after instead of a guess. No new dependencies; one new file (`tests/test_wordbox_eval.py`).

### What it does
- **Synthetic accuracy set** — lays sample lines with the bundled proportional font at known positions, giving *real* per-word ground truth with no labeling. Baseline today: **mean word IoU 0.859, 96.4% of words ≥0.5 IoU, 0 defects**. (Vertical extent is held at the line box, so IoU isolates *horizontal* word placement — the axis `split_line_into_words` controls.)
- **Optional real labeled set** — `tests/fixtures/wordbox_truth.json` (documented format) is scored when present; synthetic-only when absent. This is where cursive headroom will show.
- **Defect metrics** — degenerate / >50%-overlap / out-of-bounds counts, reusing the same classes the ALTO sanity-checker flags (so the "A0 sanitize" win has a number to drive to zero).
- **Pluggable strategy** — `synthesis_strategy` today; A1 (width-weighted split), A3 (ink-projection), B1 (ONNX detector) slot in as new strategies for apples-to-apples comparison.
- **Regression guard** — the pytest fails if mean IoU drops below 0.80 or the synthesis emits defects on clean input.

### Run it
```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_wordbox_eval.py      # 5 tests
python tests/test_wordbox_eval.py                # CLI report
```

Full suite stays green (197 passed). This unblocks the rest of the word-localization plan (A0 → A1 → A3, then B1 only if the harness shows A-tier is insufficient on cursive).

Added NHF routing capabilities, flowpath discretization, uplink routing, flow scaling, catchment-flow distribution updates, and support for routing through BMI interfaces. Expanded state-management capabilities through serialization messaging, time synchronization improvements, and coastal coupling integration. Improved routing accuracy and stability with numerous fixes to qlat handling, merged reaches, forcing generation, diagnostics, routing calculations, and result processing. Added extensive diagnostic, testing, and validation infrastructure, including CONUS-scale testing, routing diagnostics, flow animations, forcing-generation tools, and physics-validation workflows. Integrated the nwm-ewts logging framework, modernized logging and configuration management, and improved Docker, build, and dependency handling. Additional work included memory-management enhancements, batching of routing computations, NHF geopackage support, reservoir and channel-loss modeling improvements, coastal coupling support, and extensive code refactoring to improve performance, maintainability, and scalability.

## Additions
- Integrated EWTS logging support across affected components, including module-specific logging updates, optional logging behavior, Docker/build integration, and unit-test coverage where applicable.
- Added and expanded forcing workflow support, including updated configuration templates, forecast product handling, lagged-ensemble inputs, regional forcing behavior, and package-delivered forcing resources.

- Expanded verification and evaluation capabilities with additional metric calculation behavior, observation retrieval support, plotting updates, gage-source integration, and forecast-to-observation alignment.
- Added hydrologic model coupling capabilities, including SAC-SMA and Soil Moisture Profiles integration where present in the commit set.
- Implemented and expanded serialization support, including serialized size metadata, message constants, integer-based transfer structures, deserialization bounds handling, and state-transfer messaging.
- Added additional release updates covering additions for ql for flowveldepth multiindex, additions for devcontainer setup, debug diagnostics and add external n-samples control, additional offnetwork_upstreams fix in compute.py, and additions for uplink routing using offnetwork_upstreams.

## Removals
- Removed unused, duplicate, obsolete, and deprecated code paths, including stale helper functions, duplicated definitions, older EWTS references, and no-longer-needed implementation artifacts.
- Removed debug output, temporary testing code, unnecessary runtime messages, and related log noise from operational paths.
- Removed additional release updates covering removal of results merging from t-route model, fixes for bug that was leading to flow drops between run sets, removal of data dir references, patch: removed collect (), and removal of main start time.

## Changes
- Refactored BMI model interfaces and input-forcing behavior, including model-class selection, getter/setter behavior, bounds handling, and BMI calculation fixes.
- Refined configuration, realization, template, sample-config, and package-resource handling across supported workflows and deployment environments.
- Updated Docker, build, packaging, dependency, and installed-resource configuration.
- Updated geospatial metadata, regridding, CRS, mesh/geogrid, domain, gage, and crosswalk handling across forcing, verification, and realization workflows.
- Updated CI/CD, security scanning, downstream pipeline triggers, and customer-delivery workflow configuration.
- Improved validation, warning, exception, traceback, permission, and user-facing error-reporting behavior.
- Updated cache, dataset, temporary-file, scratch-directory, and data-access behavior, including lazy loading, explicit dataset closure, retry handling, and local/S3 access refinements.
- Refactored and cleaned up implementation details, including naming consistency, type hints, imports, property handling, and internal helper structure.
- Corrected unit conversions and size/type reporting across model calculations, serialized buffers, time-step handling, and BMI-facing data exchanges.
- Updated hydrologic model outputs and model-specific runtime behavior, including formulation outputs, GIUH/channel-inflow values, ponded-depth variables, and model-specific state/runtime handling.
- Reworked serialization behavior, message metadata, reported state types, size calculations, buffer validation, and transfer logic for state save and restore workflows.

author: timsehn
body:
Closes #1299. Running DDL from a UDF or row callback (`tkt3080`, `tkt-b72787b1`, `tkt-c694113d5`) aborted the still-running outer SELECT, where stock lets it finish. Three causes, all on the schema-changing autocommit path:

1. **Commit faulted every cursor.** `prollyBtreeCommitPhaseTwo` hard-faulted all cursors with `SQLITE_ABORT` before the catalog reload. Now saves this handle's cursors (re-seekable against the reloaded catalog) and faults only what can't be saved or whose table vanished in the reload; other handles' cursors fault as before.

2. **Hard statement expiry.** The same path called `sqlite3ExpirePreparedStatements(db, 0)`; hard expiry makes `OP_OpenRead` return `SQLITE_ABORT_ROLLBACK` for any running statement that re-opens a cursor — e.g. a `NOT EXISTS` subquery, once per outer row. Switched to advisory expiry (`iCode 1`), stock's schema-change semantics: running statements finish, then re-prepare.

3. **Pre-existing row loss, hidden on master.** `flushIfNeeded` dropped the *initiating* cursor to `CURSOR_INVALID`, so a SELECT resumed after a callback-issued `COMMIT` silently lost its remaining rows — on master today, `sqlite3_step` after a mid-scan COMMIT returns `SQLITE_DONE` with rows still in the table (masked because the blunt abort in (1) usually killed the statement first; capi3-11.4 exposed it once (1)/(2) stopped the aborts). Fixed by saving the initiating cursor before the flush, teaching `saveCursorPosition` to save map-sourced rows whose tree cursor is unpositioned, and resetting stale mutmap iterator state post-flush.

## Verification
- Minimal repro (CREATE INDEX in a row callback) returns all rows; `DROP TABLE` of a scanned table now correctly errors "database table is locked" (stock parity).
- **tkt3080 / tkt-b72787b1 / tkt-c694113d5 → 0 failures, gated.**
- **capi3 improves 10 → 9** known divergences: 11.4 *and* 11.5 now pass (entries removed; stale 11.13 reason corrected to `SQLITE_SCHEMA`). Mid-scan-COMMIT resume verified for table-created-in-txn, rows-pending-in-txn, and pre-existing-data shapes.
- No regressions: 38-suite sweep byte-identical to master (savepoint 48, trans 19/29, fkey2 7, trigger1 4, tkt3718 0, schema* 0, …); gate harness OK on all touched files; shell suites match master; ASan clean (capi3, tkt trio, tkt3718, savepoint, trans2, schema).

First real-org (SDO) end-to-end validation of the nort loop, plus the hardening it surfaced.

## What this does
- **Agent invocation seam**: unwrap the live `generateAiAgentResponse` `{"type":"Text","value":...}` envelope; run the agent callout **before** any DML (was failing live with "pending uncommitted work") and replace the per-record soft lock with a singleton dispatch guard; surface the action's `getErrors()`.

- **Parsing resilience (headline)**: parsing is now a graceful-degradation optimization, not a hard gate. Parse failure with a non-blank body → coarse body-only fingerprint + `Parse_Degraded__c` + still flows to the agent (which reads `Raw_Sample__c`) instead of dead-ending at `ParseError`. Fixed `RE_FLOW_API`/`RE_FLOW_ELEMENT` for the real Salesforce flow-email format. author: jayanaka-98
body:
## Why

For a structured return type, a weak or distracted model sometimes emits empty
content, prose, or malformed JSON. `parse_response` then either raises
`OutputConversionError` or, for an empty response, hands back the raw string,
which downstream code treats as the typed object and crashes. A single bad
generation shouldn't fail the call when a quick regeneration usually recovers.

## What

**Retry loop** — On a non-streaming typed (non-`str`) call, byLLM now regenerates
when the output is empty or unparseable. Between attempts it resets to the
original prompt and injects a corrective message that restates the failure,
**echoes the rejected output**, and re-shows the JSON schema, demanding a raw
JSON object. `str` returns are never retried.

**`max_output_retries` knob** — Retries *after* the first attempt (total =
`1 + n`); default `3`, `0` disables. Resolves per-call > per-object > `jac.toml`
`[plugins.byllm.call_params]` > default. On exhaustion, the raised
`OutputConversionError` reports the attempt count and chains the last error;
`raw_output` is preserved.

**MockLLM test primitives** — `MockRawResponse` routes text through the real
`parse_response` (so malformed JSON raises naturally), `MockError` raises a
wrapped exception, and `MockLLM.seen_prompts` records the prompt per attempt.
All additive; existing MockLLM behavior is unchanged.

**Tests** — Retry behavior is covered end-to-end through real `by llm()` calls
(recover, exhaust, limit, regression) in `test_byllm.jac` + a fixture.

**Docs** — New *Typed-Output Retry* section in the byLLM reference, plus the
config/invocation tables and the MockLLM testing section.

author: erskingardner
body: ## Problem Audit-log files were never reaching the Goggles tracker API. One host-side cause: iOS had **no dedicated audit-log token** — `TelemetryBuildConfig.auditTrackerConfig()` reused `bearerToken`, the OTLP/relay-telemetry token. Goggles is a different service, so once audit logging is enabled, uploads authenticate with the wrong credential (or skip silently when no OTLP token is configured). ## Fix Add a dedicated audit-log bearer token wired through the same build chain as the OTLP token: | Layer | Key | | --- | --- | | xcconfig secret (empty default) | `AUDIT_LOG_TOKEN_DARKMATTER_IOS` | | Build setting (Debug + Release) | `DARKMATTER_AUDIT_LOG_BEARER_TOKEN = $(AUDIT_LOG_TOKEN_DARKMATTER_IOS)` | | Info.plist | `DarkmatterAuditLogBearerToken` | | Swift | `TelemetryBuildConfig.auditLogBearerToken` → `auditTrackerConfig()` | There is **no fallback to the OTLP token** — an unset audit token skips uploads rather than sending the wrong credential. ## Deploy note Provision `AUDIT_LOG_TOKEN_DARKMATTER_IOS` in CI (and locally in `Config/TelemetrySecrets.xcconfig`, which is gitignored) for uploads to run. Audit logging itself remains an opt-in Settings toggle — this PR does not change that. ## Tests - Reworked `auditTrackerConfigDefersEndpointToMarmotAndCarriesCredentialsAndSource` to assert the audit token (not the OTLP token) is carried. - Added tests that the audit token is read from its own keys and does **not** fall back to the OTLP token. - `xcodebuild build-for-testing` (iPhone 17 Pro simulator): `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit # Release Notes * **New Features** * Added media attachments: send photos directly from camera or photo library. * Added group image editing: group administrators can now set custom group avatars. * Enhanced avatar display in chat list with improved avatar URL handling. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved timeline scroll pinning behavior with better bottom-inset handling. * Fixed group change notifications across conversation views. * **Chores** * Updated camera permission description to reflect new photo capture functionality. * Updated vendored library components and telemetry audit logging configuration.

author: mrseanr
body:
Slice P3 (final) of the pagination work — wires the mobile lists to the keyset
cursor contract from #194/#195. Each list loads page 1 on focus and pulls the
next page via FlatList onEndReached, appending until the cursor is exhausted.

- lib/use-paginated-list.ts: shared hook (PAGE_SIZE 25 + pageQuery) that owns
  the cursor, the focus refetch, loadMore/append, an imperative reload, and a
  hasMore flag. The in-flight guard is a useRef (not state-in-deps) so a fast
  scroll can't fire overlapping loadMore() calls or stomp the focus refetch —
  the M3 once-only-bootstrap caution generalized.
- customers / invoices / estimates / expenses / recurring / items: FlatList
  onEndReached + a footer spinner. invoices/estimates/recurring drop their
  client-side customer fetch and read the LEFT JOINed customerName from #195
  (fetching every customer to name rows doesn't survive pagination).
- items keeps the show-archived toggle (flipping changes fetchPage, which
  re-runs page 1) and archive/restore (calls the hook's reload()).
- activity: AuditHistory renders the feed as one block, so it uses a "Load
  more" button (mirroring web) against the audit-events cursor, 50/page.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean (confirms customerName resolves on the joined
endpoints through @thalermark/api-contract) and biome clean. No new route
files, so no router.d.ts regen. On-device Expo Go scroll-through is the one
manual step left.
