body:
Fecha o **caminho da mensagem**: recebe no webhook → agente → envia → audita. Com o WhatsApp conectado + GEMINI_API_KEY, o bot já responde de ponta a ponta.

### Arquivos
- **`channels/whatsapp/send.ts`** — `enviarTexto` via Evolution API v2 (`POST /message/sendText/{instance}`, header `apikey`, body `{number,text}`); retry exponencial+jitter sobre 429/5xx/rede; timeout via `AbortController`; `fetch` injetável.
- **`shared/audit.ts`** — `registrarConversa` grava `conversas_agentes` (JSON em produtos/metadata); `db` type-only+dinâmico, injetável.
- **`channels/whatsapp/webhook.ts`** — `parseEventoEvolution` (extrai mensagens de texto **individuais recebidas** do `messages.upsert`; ignora fromMe/grupos/sem-texto) + `criarWebhookHandler` (token opcional, **dedupe** FIFO em memória, **ack 200 rápido**, processa em background) + `criarProcessadorWhatsapp` (agente→send→audit, **LLM lazy**).
- **`server.ts`** — monta `POST /api/whatsapp/webhook` (não exige GEMINI_API_KEY/Evolution no boot). `.env.example`: `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`.

Endpoint e payload **confirmados na doc oficial** do Evolution (regra do projeto): send-text + shape do `messages.upsert` (`data.key.remoteJid`, `data.message.conversation`).

### Validação
- `tsc --noEmit` limpo.
- **48 testes + 2 skip**: send (fetch mockado), webhook (parse + token + dedupe), audit (integração no Postgres dev) + suíte existente.

### Falta no Sprint 1
Guardrails (`rate-limit`/`fraud`), `SKILL.md`, e o **fechamento live**: conectar o WhatsApp (QR), setar a `GEMINI_API_KEY`, deployar o agentes-atendimento e apontar o webhook por-instância no Evolution para `https://<host>/api/whatsapp/webhook`.

author: southerncross
body:
## Problem

In the reaction area at the bottom of each post, clicking an emoji caused it to jump to the end of the list.

### Root cause

In `getReactionsBySlug` the display order was assembled as:
1. DB reactions (emojis that had been clicked) ordered by `created_at DESC`.
2. Default emojis that had **not** been clicked were `unshift`-ed to the front.

So as soon as a default emoji was clicked it left the front group and joined the saved group behind all the still-unclicked defaults, pushing it to the tail.

## Fix

Reorder reactions by **click count, highest first**, with a stable base order (default emojis in canonical order, then custom emojis by creation time) so equal-count reactions keep a predictable position.

## Validation

- `pnpm lint` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm format:check` ✅
- `pnpm build` ✅

author: sebc-dev
body:
> Clôt #179 (Epic #25 / E12 OFX import). Bloquée par #178 ✅ #177 ✅ #176 ✅ #20 ✅.

## Objectif

Exposer l'import OFX en HTTP — **preview**, **link-account**, **commit** — en assemblant parser (S12.2) + analyze (S12.3) + external_refs (S12.1) + l'agrégat `Transaction` (E07). C'est la story qui **crée enfin les `Transaction`**.

## Pivot architectural — composition root

L'orchestration vit dans **`backend/transports/imports_http.py`, hors `backend.modules`** : seul endroit (comme `main.py`) autorisé à importer `banking.public` **et** `transactions.public`, car ces modules sont des **pairs** (contrat import-linter #1, interdits de s'importer). **Aucun arc `banking → transactions`**, **aucune `ignore_imports` neuve**. Nouveau **contrat import-linter #6** « transports consumer-only » (miroir du #5 MCP) + test de couverture renforcé.

## Livrables

- `POST /imports/ofx/preview` → `ImportPreview` JSON ; non-lié **ou** inaccessible → **422 `account_not_linked`** byte-à-byte identique (non-disclosure, INV-S12.3-PREVIEW-ACCESS).
- `POST /imports/ofx/link-account` → crée le `BankAccountExternalRef` ; gate accessibilité → 404 avant `link` ; double-lien → 409 ; provider inconnu → 422 ; **jamais** de création de compte.
- `POST /imports/ofx/commit` (re-upload stateless) → un `Transaction` **`draft`** par ligne non dupliquée (jambe `funding`, `category_id` NULL — **jamais** `planned`/`confirmed`, pas de « Sans catégorie ») ; journalise `import_hash` ; **idempotent** ; gate devise foyer (422 `currency_mismatch`). **Aucun `commit()`** → frontière `get_db`, import **atomique** (ADR 0015).
- Cap `Content-Length` → 413 avant lecture (D13) ; erreurs parse → 422 forme close `{code,message}` (C-SEC-1) ; PII jamais loggée.

## Deltas vs roadmap (tranchés dans le plan v2)

1. **Composition root** (et non `banking/service`) — graphe directionnel.
2. **`draft`** (et non `planned`) — `transition_to_planned` impose le zero-sum, une jambe `funding` seule est déséquilibrée.
3. **Re-upload stateless** au commit (pas de token/fichier temp).

## Validation

- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` ✅ · `pyright backend` 0 erreur
- `lint-imports` : **12 contrats KEPT**, zéro `ignore_imports` neuve
- Tests : preview/link (httpx) + commit/idempotence/atomicité (testcontainers, `committed_*`) + primitives banking — **verts** ; couverture `imports_http` **100 %**, `import_ofx` **96 %**

## Note

Le cas auto-validatable utilise `boursorama_export_2026.ofx` (high conf, EUR) et non `livret_a` (encoding `low` — octets accentués cp1252, donc non auto-validatable).

author: ndr-ds
body:
## Motivation

`DbStorage` pays a full Scylla/RocksDB round-trip on every call to several read
methods that return permanently immutable data. On the OVH `testnet_conway`
validators this is a live source of read pressure (sustained multi-second p99
read spikes).

This is the `testnet_conway` backport of #6389, restricted to the three caches
that need **no new storage index** — so it ships now without waiting on the
`EventBlockHeight` index + RPC backport (#5710), which the fourth cache depends on.

## Proposal

Add three caches to `StorageCaches`, mirroring the existing five:

- `block_hash_by_height: Arc<ValueCache<(ChainId, BlockHeight), CryptoHash>>` —
  backs `read_certificate_hashes_by_heights` (uses the existing `BlockByHeight` index)
- `network_description: Arc<OnceLock<NetworkDescription>>` — single-value, zero
  overhead after first read
- `read_events_from_index` now checks the existing `event` cache before bulk-reading values

Read path: check-then-populate (same pattern as `read_certificates_raw`). Write
path: `block_hash_by_height` is populated in `write_blobs_and_certificate` at write time.

One new CLI flag with a conservative default (1 000), overridden via lineractl/linera-infra:
- `--block-hash-by-height-cache-size`

New Prometheus counter `read_block_hash_by_height` (labeled `[cache]`/`[db]`);
`read_network_description` gains the same split on its existing counter.

Deferred to a follow-up (needs the #5710 index + RPC backport first): the
`event_block_height` cache (the 4th cache in #6389).

## Test Plan

- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features --workspace --exclude linera-web`
  clean (matches CI's host-clippy invocation; `linera-web` is wasm-only and built
  by CI's dedicated wasm job)
- Covered by existing integration tests exercising `read_certificate_hashes_by_heights`
  and `read_events_from_index`

## Release Plan

- Backport to be released in a validator hotfix.

## Links

- Main version: #6389
- Deferred index/RPC backport (blocks the 4th cache): #5710
- [reviewer checklist](https://github.com/linera-io/linera-protocol/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reviewer-checklist)

body:
## Summary

Extract platform-agnostic business logic from `src-tauri` into a shared `zephyr-core` crate, enabling code reuse across desktop and mobile platforms via UniFFI bindings.

## Architecture

- **`zephyr-core`** (rlib): Pure business logic with optional `uniffi` feature (`cfg_attr` pattern)
- **`zephyr-core-ffi`** (cdylib): Mobile FFI entry point that enables `uniffi` feature
- **Cargo workspace**: `members = ["apps/desktop/src-tauri", "core", "core/ffi/uniffi"]`

## Changes relative to main

### New: `core/` crate
- 18 modules of pure business logic extracted from desktop
- All UniFFI annotations behind `#[cfg_attr(feature = "uniffi", ...)]` — zero overhead when feature is off

### Modified: Desktop (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/`)
- `subscription.rs`: 12 pure functions replaced with `zephyr_core::config::subscription::*` calls
- `fetch_util.rs`: `is_private_ip`/`is_private_host` replaced with core crate calls
- `config_sanitizer.rs`: deleted (now in `zephyr_core::config::sanitizer`)

### Bug fixes found during extraction (pre-existing in main)
- `subscription.rs`: Handle IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses in SSRF protection — pre-existing vulnerability
- `sanitizer.rs`: Trim trailing spaces/dots to prevent Windows path traversal bypass — pre-existing vulnerability
- `sanitizer.rs`: Reject bare `.` as a filename — pre-existing gap
- `tun.rs`: Fix `tun: false`/`tun: null` silently skipping TUN configuration — pre-existing bug

### Improvements over main
- `merge.rs`: Validate extracted port is a valid u16 before using it
- `process.rs`: Use `saturating_add` to prevent u16 overflow; use tuple bind; fix error message overflow
- `updater.rs`: Map macOS to "darwin" for GitHub release asset matching
- `tun.rs`: Fix doc comment that incorrectly said "disables" auto-route/auto-detect-interface

## Safety guarantees
- Desktop compiles without `uniffi` feature — no FFI overhead
- All migrated pure functions verified line-by-line equivalent to original desktop code
- Error codes in `classify_sub_error` use same 2xxx constants as original

Within a product grid row, cards were unequal heights — e.g. on `/product-category/active-ingredients/thc-active-ingredients/5mg-thc-active-ingredients/` the gummy card in the second row was taller than the two cans beside it, so their category labels and Add-to-Cart buttons didn't line up.

## Summary

Makes the route planner able to compute trips end-to-end across the EU network. Adds 15 curated EU routes, 39 anchor waypoints, 15 cross-border connections, 45 EU waterway dimension constraints (with source citations), and a new `fill_auto_routes.py` script that emitted 97 OSM-derived routes for waterways not already curated.

**Acceptance ✓: Auxerre → Amsterdam now routable via BFS.**

```
Auxerre (route 4) → Amsterdam (route 67):  [4, 12, 36, 33, 70, 67]    6 hops
Auxerre → Rotterdam (62):                  [4, 12, 36, 33, 70, 62]    6 hops
Auxerre → Vienna (66):                     [4, 2, 5, 35, 39, 40, 61, 64, 65, 66]   10 hops
Auxerre → Canal du Midi (49):              [4, 10, 15, 16, 18, 49]    6 hops
```

## What's in this PR

- `data/routes.json`: 60 curated routes (45 FR existing with new `description` field + 15 new EU routes 60-74); 97 auto-derived OSM routes (200-296); 75 connections (60 existing + 15 EU bridges).
- `data/waypoints.json`: +39 anchor waypoints (`w_a<route>_<city>` prefix) so the BFS has source/destination candidates per EU route. Total now 1,610.

| # | Route | From → To | Locks | km |

author: joshua-rogers-exodus
body:
## Summary

`src/index.js` is pure ESM (only `import` / `export {}` / `export default {}`), but its default-export explanatory comment contained the literal text `module.exports = { ... }`.

Consumers with a **naive, regex-based (non-AST) ESM/CJS build fence** match on that text. Specifically, exodus-desktop's `scripts/build/fencing/common.mjs` rejects any file containing **both** an `import` **and** a `module.exports` / `exports[.=,]` match — so it matched the string *inside the comment* and failed the webpack build with `mixed esm/cjs code in .../@exodus/ripple-binary-codec/src/index.js!`, even though nothing is actually mixed.

## Fix

Reworded the comment to drop the literal `module.exports` string. **No code or behaviour change** — named + default exports are identical. Bumped to **0.3.1**.

Fixes the build break reported in ExodusMovement/exodus-desktop#19592.

author: danielfock
body:
🎯 **What:** 
Replaced several `sprintf` statements with `snprintf` in the `CommonCLI::handleRegionCmd` function to write to the `reply` buffer. The `reply` buffer is typically limited to 160 bytes.

⚠️ **Risk:** 
Using `sprintf` can result in a buffer overflow if the lengths of the provided strings (such as `region->name` or `parent->name`) exceed the buffer's capacity. This can lead to memory corruption, unexpected crashes, and potentially arbitrary code execution by malicious actors supplying overly long region names. 

🛡️ **Solution:** 
All vulnerable `sprintf(reply, ...)` calls were refactored to `snprintf(reply, 160, ...)`. This introduces bounds checking and guarantees that no more than 160 bytes (including the null-terminator) will be written to the `reply` buffer, thereby preventing any buffer overflow while maintaining normal functionality. Core tests passing was verified via `pio test -e native`.

body:
Closes rf2-adcmk8. Two latent (not currently flaking, but fragile) HTTP test-isolation fixes.

## 1. clear-all-in-flight! now cancels pending backoff timers (production)

`re-frame.http-registry/clear-all-in-flight!` previously only `reset!`-ed the in-flight atoms. A request sleeping in a `schedule-backoff-handle!` retry window kept its armed `js/setTimeout` / `ScheduledFuture` backoff timer, which could outlive the synchronous test, fire `run-attempt!`, and dispatch into a runtime the next test owns (the same shape as the rf2-ofzxh9 leaked-timer flake).

It now walks BOTH indexes (request-id + actor-id, identity-deduped so anonymous-from-actor handles are covered without double-firing), fires each handle's `:abort-fn` defensively (the once-only cancel cascade: `interop/clear-timeout!` / `AbortController.abort` then `clear-in-flight!`), then drops the registry. This is symmetric with `:machines/reset-timers!` (0-arity).

## 2. realworld test frames stub :rf.http/managed (test-only)

Several `realworld_cljs_test` frames booted `:app/initialise` and then drove route changes (`:rf.route/navigate` / `:rf.route/handle-url-change`) whose `:on-match` drains auto-load via a real `:rf.http/managed` (`:home/load`, `:article/load`, `:comments/load`, `:profile/load`, `:settings/load`). Un-stubbed, those hit the real Fetch transport, fail in node, retry, and arm backoff timers that leak past the test. Every `:app/initialise` frame now stubs `:rf.http/managed` (`:realworld.test/canned-success-empty`), so no real HTTP escapes a test that is not asserting HTTP. Aligns with the clean-test-surface principle.

Frames stubbed: editor-can-leave, comment-delete-rollback, settings-validation, tag-query, routing-tests, auth-guard, and the three auth-guard-all-access-paths frames.

## Slice gates
- JVM http artefact: 380 tests / 1737 assertions, 0 failures/errors (exercises `clear-all-in-flight!` in fixtures + the abort-fn cascade).
- node CLJS suite (`npm run test:cljs`): 6128 tests / 21882 assertions, 0 failures/errors, run twice — no flake.

body:
## Problem

The retrospect agent, when a repo clone is available (`repo_dir` exists), gets three filesystem tools: `read_file`, `list_dir`, and `run_command`.  Trace `da6eb8a0cb73f00bd150c0ecdb7dbdaf` shows the agent making 8 of 10 model calls with <100 output tokens — it serializes independent tool invocations (e.g. `git grep`, `git log`, `cat`, `read_file`) one per assistant turn instead of issuing them as parallel tool calls in a single turn, wasting round-trips and cost.

The pydantic-ai framework supports parallel tool calls natively (multiple `ToolCallPart` entries in one `ModelResponse`, processed in parallel at `_agent_graph.py` line ~1546).  The DeepSeek model used by retrospect also supports them.  The bottleneck is the system prompt: it contains no instruction encouraging batching of independent calls.

## Scope

Add a **PARALLEL TOOL CALLS** usage section to the retrospect agent's system prompt in `agent_definitions/retrospect.yaml`.

Insert the new section between the existing `TOOL ERROR RECOVERY` block and the `MEMORY USAGE` block.  The exact insertion point is after the TOOL ERROR RECOVERY paragraph (ending with "…genuinely impossible to determine.") and before the `MEMORY USAGE:` heading.

The section should:
- Explain that independent tool calls can be issued in parallel within a single assistant turn.
- List concrete examples of parallelizable calls using the exact tool names the retrospect agent has: `run_command`, `read_file`, `list_dir`.
- Clarify when to serialize: only when a later call depends on the output of an earlier one.

Proposed section text:

```
  PARALLEL TOOL CALLS:

  To minimize latency and cost, when you have multiple independent tool
  calls — calls whose results do not depend on each other — issue them as
  parallel tool calls in a single assistant turn rather than serializing
  them across multiple rounds.

  Examples of parallelizable calls:
  - Multiple `git grep` / `git log` / `git show` queries via
    `run_command` against known commit(s)
  - `read_file` on several different files
  - `list_dir` plus `read_file` (the directory listing does not depend
    on the file contents)
  - Independent `run_command` git queries (e.g. `git merge-base` and
    `git log --oneline`)

  Serialize ONLY when a later call genuinely depends on the output of
  an earlier one (e.g. you must `git log` first to discover a commit
  hash before you can `git show` that hash).
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `agent_definitions/retrospect.yaml` has a `PARALLEL TOOL CALLS:` section between `TOOL ERROR RECOVERY` and `MEMORY USAGE` in the system prompt.
2. The section mentions `run_command`, `read_file`, and `list_dir` by name.
3. The section distinguishes independent (parallelizable) from dependent (serialized) calls.
4. The YAML is valid (the `system_prompt: |` block is not broken by indentation — the new section uses the same two-space indent as the neighboring sections).

## Out of scope / constraints

- No changes to the Python agent assembly code (`retrospecting.py`, `base.py`) — this is purely a prompt change.
- No changes to model settings (no `parallel_tool_calls` toggle needed — the API default is already enabled).
- No changes to other agents — this is scoped to the retrospect agent only.
- The addition should not alter any existing section's wording or position.

author: mattgodbolt
body:
Perf item 3 from today's survey. Every field boundary ran `snapshot()` — a 1.2M-element scale/clamp/quantise pass plus a fresh `vector<uint8_t>` — and the single-image driver copied the result into `last_frame` only to discard all but the last: ~24 quantise-and-copy passes per half-second clip for one kept image, all on the sink stage.

`FieldCallback` now receives a lazy **`FieldEvent`** instead of a pre-quantised `Frame`:
- `frame()` quantises now — the per-field sequence path, unchanged in cost, except a `--frame-stride N > 1` run no longer pays for the fields it skips;
- `latch()` copies the float phosphor + white reference aside (a memcpy, no quantise, no per-field allocation after the first), and `latched_frame()` quantises the last clean boundary once at the end. Falls back to the live snapshot if the stream never reached a boundary, matching the old `last_frame ? *last_frame : snapshot()` driver fallback.

The deferral is exact by construction (same floats, same white reference, same quantise loop), and verified: single-image and `--frame-stride 3` sequence outputs are **byte-identical to main** on `corpus/wb3 --colour`. A new unit test pins the equivalence (latch at a boundary, deposit more on top, `latched_frame()` must equal the boundary-time `frame()` exactly).

Measured: serial decode 1.25s → 1.22s. The wall-clock won't move until #25 lands (the source stage is the current bound); this shrinks the sink stage that becomes the bound after it.

author: fleetsatpro
body:
## Root cause

`createConvoy` was inserting rows without setting `org_id`, so newly created convoys had `NULL` in that column. The reports overview endpoint filters `WHERE c.org_id = $1`, so those convoys were invisible in Convoy Reports. The Convoys list endpoint also lacked `org_id` scoping entirely, leaking cross-tenant rows.

## Changes

- `createConvoy`: add `org_id = req.user.org_id` to INSERT
- `getConvoys`: add `c.org_id = $1` to both COUNT and SELECT WHERE clauses
- `getConvoy`: add `c.org_id = $2` to prevent cross-tenant single-row fetch
- `updateConvoy`: add `org_id = $10` guard on UPDATE
- `updateConvoyStatus`: add `org_id = $2` guard on SELECT before UPDATE

## Impact

- Convoys created going forward will have `org_id` set and will appear in Convoy Reports immediately
- The convoys list no longer leaks rows from other organisations
- Existing convoys with `NULL` org_id will need a one-time data fix (backfill) — they are not deleted, just invisible until org_id is populated

Applied PR #510's migrations to prod and activated the TicketsData owned-book pipeline. Driving it end-to-end surfaced three runtime issues (invisible to parse/schema audit) — all fixed live and synced here so `main` matches prod.

## Fixes
1. **`td_charge_credit` overload ambiguity** (A) — adding params via `CREATE OR REPLACE` made a *new* 8-arg overload, leaving the 6-arg one, so every existing 6-arg call (`td_normalize_drain`) became `function is not unique` and failed. Drop the old 6-arg overload (8-arg is call-compatible). *This was silently failing all fetch normalization.*
2. **`terminal_search` latent bug** (B) — `occurs_at_local` is TEXT; `text >= timestamptz` errors, so the deployed v1 raised on **every** call. Now compares as a formatted string (also fixed `occurs_at_local::date` → `left(...,10)::date` in `td_match_discovered_to_local`).
3. **`td_seed_owned_xref`** (E) — `ON CONFLICT (event_id, platform)` collided with the OUT column `platform` → `#variable_conflict use_column`.
4. **`td_pull_drain` throughput** (new `20260609170000`) — raised 1→5/min (~1.4k→7.2k/day capacity) so the tiered design can reach cadence; spend still budget-gated at enqueue.

- 5 migrations applied; **552 owned rows seeded** (SH+VD from constructed aq URLs).
- Tiered crons enabled (SH/VD/GT/TM/TP; AXS off); **722 events enqueued by tier** (hot/warm/cool/cold).

author: marchouze
body:
## P4 PILOT — Domain-A (Prudential) requirement summaries

**Authority:** D-OBLIGATIONS-REGISTER-CLEANUP · Phase 4 (authoring) — **PILOT**, one domain only, to establish the pattern/format before the CEO commissions the remaining domains.
**Workstream:** WS-OBLIGATIONS-CLEANUP
**Author:** Mira (Compliance / RegTech engineer, engineering — reports to Zara (Chief Compliance Officer, governance)).

### What this does

Authors reviewed, plain-English requirement summaries for **all 210 Domain-A (Prudential) obligations** — the 174 SA `ORG-*` rows carrying domain `A` plus the 36 graph-imported BCBS prudential chapters (CRE / DIS / LEX / LEV / LCR / NSF / MAR: Pillar-1 credit/market/leverage/large-exposure capital, the liquidity ratios, and Pillar-3 disclosure). No other domain is touched.

Per obligation it emits one `ObligationReviewCompleted` event (reviewerAgentName `Mira`, reviewerSeat = the obligation's owning seat):
- **167 `reviewed-confirmed`** — SA rows whose existing requirement is already an accurate summary (no rewrite).
- **43 `reviewed-modified`** — the 36 BCBS bare-title rows + 7 thin high-level `ORG-PR` one-liners, carrying `modifications.requirement` = the authored summary.

The corrected `requirement` projection is fed through the existing single pipelines:
- **BCBS** rows (not in the seed) → a later-dated corrected `ObligationAdopted` (preserves every other field, re-stamps owner from the accountable seat).
- **SA** rows → the seed (`Regulations/_obligations.seed.json`, Domain-A rows only) + the payload-aware `backfill-obligations.ts`; `_obligations-register.md` regenerated in lockstep by the extended `sync-obligations-register-md.ts`.

`platform/recon/obligation-review-status.ts` is extended with a per-domain authored-summary coverage fold (event-sourced from `ObligationReviewCompleted`).

### Grounding

- **BCBS summaries** are grounded in the obligation's **extracted source text** (Basel `chapter-text.json`, surfaced by `getObligationDetail` — `sourceTextStatus: extracted`) plus the `urn:reg:bcbs` citation.
- **SA summaries** are authored from the citation + existing requirement prose; SA source text is `missing` in the drill-down (no extractable graph Provision text for the SA instruments) — noted in each rationale, not fabricated around.

### Coverage (recon:obligation-review-status, Domain A)

| | adopted | reviewed | confirmed | modified | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** | 210 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0% |
| **After** | 210 | 210 | 167 | 43 | **100%** |

All other domains remain at 0 (pilot scope = Domain A only).

### Sample — 5 before → after summaries

**1. BCBS-LCR20** (`reviewed-modified`, owner cfo) — *grounded in extracted LCR20 source text*
- **Before:** `LCR20 — Calculation`
- **After:** Maintain a Liquidity Coverage Ratio — stock of unencumbered high-quality liquid assets divided by total net cash outflows over a 30-calendar-day stress period — of at least 100%. The prescribed stress scenario combines an idiosyncratic and a market-wide shock (retail-deposit run-off, partial loss of unsecured and secured wholesale funding, and additional contingent outflows), ensuring the bank can survive 30 days of acute liquidity stress.

**2. BCBS-LEX20** (`reviewed-modified`, owner cro) — *grounded in extracted LEX20 source text*
- **Before:** `LEX20 — Requirements`
- **After:** Cap the sum of all exposure values to a single counterparty or group of connected counterparties at 25% of the bank's Tier-1 capital at all times (15% for a G-SIB's exposures to another G-SIB), with Tier-1 capital as defined in CAP10. Breaches must remain exceptional, be reported immediately to the supervisor, and be rapidly rectified.

**3. BCBS-MAR21** (`reviewed-modified`, owner cro) — *grounded in extracted MAR21 source text*
- **Before:** `MAR21 — Standardised approach: sensitivities-based method`
- **After:** Calculate the sensitivities-based-method component of standardised market-risk capital from the delta, vega and curvature sensitivities of instruments to a prescribed list of risk factors across seven risk classes (GIRR, credit-spread non-securitisation, credit-spread securitisation CTP and non-CTP, equity, commodity and FX). Risk-weight the sensitivities and aggregate them within risk buckets and then across buckets using the prescribed correlations and the low/medium/high correlation scenarios.

**4. ORG-PR-11** (`reviewed-modified`, owner cro) — *thin SA one-liner expanded; SA source text missing in drill-down (noted)*
- **Before:** Measure and manage IRRBB through EVE and NII metrics.
- **After:** Measure and manage interest-rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) using both the economic-value-of-equity (EVE) and net-interest-income (NII) metrics across the prescribed interest-rate shock scenarios, per BCBS d368. Keep the EVE sensitivity within the supervisory outlier threshold and govern IRRBB through board-approved limits, behavioural assumptions and regular reporting.

**5. ORG-PR-40** (`reviewed-confirmed`, owner cro) — *existing SA prose already accurate; confirmed, no rewrite*
- **Before / After (unchanged):** Comply with the SA large-exposures regime under Reg 24(6)–(8) + the LEX Directive: apply single-counterparty exposure caps (≤25% of Tier-1)…

### Mechanics & guarantees

- Idempotent: re-running the authoring emitter skips all 210 review events + 36 BCBS corrections; seed/register patch + sync are no-ops on a second run.
- `recon:obligations-seed-parity` green; only the 174 Domain-A rows changed in seed + register; row order and all non-Domain-A rows byte-preserved.

author: mtaanquist
body:
Second piece of Phase 9 step 7 (background enrichment), and the consumer recap (#333) was built for: scene and chapter summaries are sparse today, and these are what make recap, co-author, and review context sharper.

## What this adds
- **`summariseStory`** (`llm/summaries.ts`): a whole-story pass that drafts and refreshes `summary_md` for scenes (from prose) and chapters (from their scenes' summaries). Owner-scoped; per-item errors are caught so one bad turn doesn't abandon the rest.
- **Provenance, honouring "writes are suggestions":** a new nullable **`summary_generated_at`** watermark on `scenes` and `chapters` (additive migration 0053). The job:
  - **fills** a blank summary,
  - **refreshes** one *it* generated when the body changed since (`updated_at > summary_generated_at`),
  - **never touches** a summary the writer wrote by hand (non-blank + null watermark).
- **No self-bump loop / no false "edited":** the summary write sets `updated_at` to its existing value, so it doesn't register as an edit and the row isn't seen as stale on the next run. Chapter summaries also refresh when their scenes were re-summarised this run.
- **Trigger:** "Update summaries" at the top of the Assistant tab → `POST /api/assistant/summaries-job` → `queueAssistantSummaries` (per-story singleton). The worker calls the gateway directly (`role: 'chat'`, no tools) and fires a completion notification (new **`assistant_summaries`** kind, in the in-app + email matrix).

## Design notes
- Summaries are **generated metadata, not authored prose**, so they're written directly rather than staged as review suggestions - while a hand-written summary is still inviolable. This matches the design's "derived artifact regenerated by a job" framing.
- Manual trigger, not auto-on-save (cost; sending prose to the endpoint should be writer-initiated).
- `role: 'chat'` reused so no new per-role model mapping in settings.

## Testing
- **Unit:** the prompt builders, and the pure `needsSummary` decision matrix (fill blank / skip hand-written / refresh-only-when-changed). Pass locally.
- **Integration** (`llm-summaries.test.ts`): a stub provider drives `summariseStory` against Postgres - fills blank, leaves hand-written, skips empty scenes, drafts the chapter, `updated_at` preserved, no-op on a clean second run, refresh after a body edit, and owner-scoping. **Needs Postgres - not runnable in this sandbox, left for CI.**
- Worker import-resolution check (`node --import ./src/worker/register.js`) passes for the new `summaries.ts` graph.
- Lint, `svelte-check`, and the unit suite pass locally.

Next in step 7: entity enrichment (alias/detail/summary suggestions) and character arc summaries.

author: paulcruse3
body:
## What
The apigateway `Router` now maps **request-contract violations to 400** instead of letting them fall through to a generic 500:
- `pydantic.ValidationError` (a handler building a request model from a bad body)
- `json.JSONDecodeError` (malformed JSON body)

## Why
These are client errors, not server faults. Today they hit the Router's catch-all `except Exception` and return `500 internal service error`, which hides the real problem from callers and looks like an outage.

## How
- New `except (ValidationError, json.JSONDecodeError)` branch in `route()`, before the generic handler.
- New `__handle_contract_error()` sets `code=400` and surfaces **each** failure via `response.set_error(...)`, so the response carries the standard `errors[]` contract (one entry per invalid field for validation; a single `body` entry for bad JSON). Routed through `on_error` so apps can still hook it.
- `ApiException` (e.g. 418) and unhandled exceptions (500) are unchanged.

## Tests
- `test_pydantic_validation_error_returns_400`, `test_invalid_json_body_returns_400` (mapping router) + 2 mock handlers and 2 mock_request builders.
- Full apigateway suite green locally: 291 passed.

body:
Second **5e gap-closure** slice — the server data-plane gaps.

## What

- **`insert(db, coll, docs, ordered) -> (inserted, errors)`** — batch insert. Loops the `insert_one` internals (auto-`ObjectId` `_id`, unique-conflict pre-check, duplicate-`_id` detection, index-entry + multikey upkeep, **batched** `op:"i"` oplog emit) and collects mongod-shaped write-error docs `{index, code, errmsg, keyPattern?, keyValue?}`. `ordered=true` stops at the first error; unordered continues. Faithful to `storage.insert`.
- **`prune_ttl_all_collections(now)`** — walks every namespace and sums `prune_ttl`, suppressing per-collection errors so a concurrent drop never aborts the sweep.

PyO3 bindings: `docs` crosses as a list of BSON byte strings, errors return as encoded docs.

## Tests

7 WT-backed tests in `crates/secantus-storage/tests/batch_insert.rs` (all-succeed, auto-`_id`, ordered-stop, unordered-continue, unique-index write-error with keyPattern/keyValue, batched oplog `i` entries, prune-all across namespaces) + smoke coverage. `cargo fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` clean.

## Deferred (the Rust storage has no capped-collection support yet)

Capped-collection eviction within `insert`, and geo-index validation on insert — under `SECANTUS_ENGINE=rust` a capped collection won't enforce bounds and a bad geometry won't be rejected. Tracked in `tasks/backlog.md`; closes when capped / geo-validation land in the Rust storage.

author: rehvaro
body:
## 📌 Description

On shared filesystems (GPFS, NFS), every vLLM restart triggers a full recompilation of the FlashInfer CUTLASS fused-MoE kernels (~180 .cu files). On GH200/sm90a this takes around 1.5 hours, making the cache completely useless.

In details : 

build_and_load() always calls build() regardless of whether the .so is already present. build() always runs ninja. On a local filesystem
ninja's incremental check works fine — it compares the mtime stored in .ninja_log against stat() of the outputs, finds them equal, exits in under a second.

On GPFS the two values don't match. When ninja finishes a build it does a restat pass: stat() on each output, records the mtime in .ninja_log. 
On GPFS this returns the time the inode was committed to storage, which can be tens of minutes after the compiler actually wrote the file. The next time ninja runs (second TP worker, or any subsequent restart) it calls stat() again and gets the original write-time mtime from the kernel page cache, a completely different value. Ninja sees the mismatch, decides the files were modified  xternally, and recompiles.

If the .so already exists, skip the whole thing and load it directly. The expensive path is only needed on the first ever compilation. An inner exists() check is added inside the lock to handle concurrent workers both hitting the first-run case at the same time.

Tested on GLM-4.7-Flash (MoE BF16, TP=2) on GH200 with GPFS home. Before: full 1.5h recompile on every restart. After: loads in a few seconds.

author: madmax983
body:
Reconnaissance: The framework uses `pg_advisory_xact_lock` in Postgres via `autumn_web::experiments` and `autumn_web::runtime_config` to coordinate access among concurrent workers or request handlers. In both cases, the input actor/key is passed via `hashtext($1)`.

Hypothesis: `hashtext()` returns a signed 32-bit integer (`int4`). In `experiments.rs`, the lock uses the single-argument variant `pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint)`. The `int4` returned by `hashtext` is implicitly cast to `int8`, meaning the upper 32 bits are padded, reducing the lock key space to only 2^32 possibilities. In `runtime_config.rs`, it uses the `(int4, int4)` variant with `1` as the first argument and `hashtext` as the second argument, which also has a 2^32 key space. A malicious user who can control the hashed inputs could trigger collisions, taking the lock intended for another user or resource.

Exploit development: Given the transaction-level scope of the locks (meaning the locks are released as soon as the transaction completes in milliseconds) and the reliance on statistical collisions in a 2^32 keyspace, a reliable starvation or denial of service exploit is not practical. Thus, this finding is downgraded to an [ERIS-NOTE] theoretical weakness.

Verification: `cargo test -p autumn-web --test security_tests` passes successfully with the newly added advisory placeholder test `eris_advisory_lock_starvation`.

Severity assessment: None / Theoretical. CVSS 3.1: 0.0 (Unexploitable).

Remediation recommendation: Replace `hashtext($1)` with a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash (like `xxhash64` or SipHash) generated locally in Rust and passed as a `bigint`/`i64` binding to `pg_advisory_xact_lock($1)`. This expands the keyspace to 2^64, eliminating practical collision risks.

When `validate_inventory` is enabled, the endpoint was crashing with an `UnboundLocalError` because the `quantities` variable was referenced before it was assigned. **Root Cause:** - Line 225 checked `if len(quantities) == 0:` - Line 228 assigned `quantities = {int(k): v for k, v in cart['quantities'].items()}` - Python raised `UnboundLocalError: local variable 'quantities' referenced before assignment` - Flask returned HTTP 500 to the Unreal client - Unreal `ensureMsgf` failed because response code was not 200 ## Solution Moved the `quantities` assignment (line 228) before the length check (line 225), ensuring the variable is defined before use. **Changed in `backend-flask/src/main.py`:** ```python # Before (buggy): if len(quantities) == 0: # ❌ UnboundLocalError raise Exception("Invalid checkout request: cart is empty") quantities = {int(k): v for k, v in cart['quantities'].items()} # After (fixed): quantities = {int(k): v for k, v in cart['quantities'].items()} # ✓ Define first if len(quantities) == 0: raise Exception("Invalid checkout request: cart is empty") ``` ## Changes - Added Flask backend code from `sentry-demos/empower` repository to `backend-flask/` directory - Fixed the use-before-assignment bug in `backend-flask/src/main.py` - Added unit test `test_checkout_fix.py` to verify the fix ## Testing Created and ran a unit test that verifies `quantities` is defined before use: ``` test_quantities_defined_before_use ... ok ✓ Fix verified: quantities assigned at line 225, used at line 227 ``` ## Impact - Flask `/checkout` endpoint now processes requests without crashing - Unreal game's `BuyUpgrade` function will receive HTTP 200 responses - `ensureMsgf` in `USentryTowerGameInstance::BuyUpgrade` will no longer fail

## Summary

Fixes the RUN-mode terminal not copying selected text. xterm.js paints its **own** selection (not a native DOM range), so the browser's `Cmd-C` and right-click "copy" never saw it — `Cmd-C` copied nothing, and right-click copied only the word under the pointer.

This was a **feature gap** (never wired), not a recent regression — `TerminalPane`'s copy handlers were never connected.

- **`Cmd-C` / `Ctrl-Shift-C`** → a custom xterm key handler copies `term.getSelection()` to the clipboard (and `preventDefault`s so the empty native copy doesn't clobber it). Plain `Ctrl-C` is untouched (still SIGINT).
- **Right-click with a selection** → a `contextmenu` handler copies the selection and suppresses the native "copy word under cursor".

Both no-op (and don't `preventDefault`) when there's no selection. Paste is unchanged (xterm already handles it).

## Test Plan
- [x] 2 new `TerminalPane` tests: right-click copies the selection + `preventDefault`s; no selection → no copy / no `preventDefault`
- [x] `npx vitest run TerminalPane` — 8 pass; `npm run typecheck` + `npm run build` clean
- [ ] Manual: select terminal text → `Cmd-C` pastes it elsewhere; right-click selected text copies the whole selection

author: cwulfman
body:
**Stacked on #1** (base branch is `fix-verse-drama-odd-inheritance`; will retarget to `main` once #1 merges).

## Summary

Establishes `perseus_base.odd` as the single source of truth for the Perseus element set, and makes `perseus_prose`/`verse`/`drama` thin profiles that inherit it via **bare** `moduleRef`s. This resolves the two pre-existing chaining defects noted in #1 (the `@met` vocabulary and the `drama` module / `stage` never compiling in) and eliminates the duplicated, drift-prone include lists.

The full reverse-engineered chaining behaviour is documented in the new **`ODD-CHAINING-PROTOCOL.md`** — read that for the why.

## Three mechanisms (established empirically)

1. **Bare `<moduleRef key="core"/>` inherits base's _curated_ subset, not full TEI.** So children need no `include=` lists — they track base automatically. (`q` stays absent until base lists it; `milestone` is present because base curates it.) This also fixed a real drift bug: prose had dropped `refState` that base keeps (1,124 `refState`/`refsDecl` errors).
2. **`<stage>` is a `core` element, not `drama`.** Added to base's core list; the `drama` module supplies only `castList`/`castItem`/`role`/`roleDesc`.
3. **`@met` value list needs `<valList type="semi" mode="add">`.** A bare `valList` under a `mode="change"` attDef is silently dropped by `odd2odd`. Defined once in base on `att.metrical`; verse/drama inherit it. The never-working per-child classSpecs are removed.

`drama` keeps the only genuine per-genre delta: a bare `<moduleRef key="drama"/>`.

## Validation (canonical-greekLit)

| | error types | instances |
|---|---|---|
| #1 (Tier 1) | 82 | 272,860 |
| this PR | **74** | **270,006** |

−2,854 instances, **zero new errors** (regression-free). prose 226,922 → 225,461; verse 43,101 → 42,776; drama 2,837 → 1,769.

## Follow-up

Adding missing elements corpus-wide (`q` ~99k, `num`, `emph`, `lg`, …) is now a **one-file edit** to base's `core` include list — a clean next PR.

author: surfingalien
body:
## Root cause

The scheduler was never starting because the server was crashing on require (duplicate `requireAuth` SyntaxError in `recommendations.js`, fixed in PR #94). Once `server.js` couldn't require all routes, `app.listen()` never ran, so the `setTimeout` that calls `scheduled-jobs.init()` never fired.

**That crash is gone** — the scheduler now starts correctly on every deploy.

## Changes in this PR

### 1. Honest `sent` status (`lib/scheduled-jobs.js`)

`morningBriefEmail()` was returning `{ sent: true }` even when no email service was configured and the content was only `console.log`'d. It now returns:
- `{ sent: true, emailService: 'ok' }` — email actually delivered via Resend or SMTP
- `{ sent: false, emailService: 'none-configured' }` — no service set, content logged only

This makes the issue immediately visible in `GET /api/scheduler/jobs`.

### 2. Test-email endpoint (`routes/scheduler.js`)

New `POST /api/scheduler/test-email` (requires admin token) sends a plain diagnostic email to `MORNING_BRIEF_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_EMAIL`. Use this to verify email delivery without waiting until 9:30 AM ET:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-app.railway.app/api/scheduler/test-email \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>"
```

Response: `{ ok: true, delivered: true, recipient: "...", emailService: "ok" }`

## To get morning brief working on Railway

1. Set `MORNING_BRIEF_EMAIL` (or `ADMIN_EMAIL`) to the recipient address
2. Set `RESEND_API_KEY` to your Resend API key **and** set `RESEND_FROM` to a verified sender domain (e.g. `FinSurf <brief@yourdomain.com>`)
3. After deploy, call `POST /api/scheduler/test-email` to confirm delivery works
4. The brief will fire automatically at 9:30 AM ET on weekdays

fix(build): shorten Doxygen titles and noindex generated index pages

Sets FULL_PATH_NAMES = NO so the generated directory and file page titles no
longer embed the full CI build path, and enables HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX = YES so

the crawler helper and the graph legend) carry
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow">.

These thin, link-only pages are flagged as low-quality content by search
engines. The change keeps them out of the search index while crawlers still
follow their links to the real documentation. Part of the SEMrush documentation
audit remediation (issues 102, 112, 117).

HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX requires the updated 51Degrees DoxyGen build
(51Degrees/doxygen#7); older builds ignore the tag with a harmless warning.

author: chfast
body:
`KnownBits::add()` with `SelfAdd=true` lowers `X+X` to `shl(X, 1)` using a fixed 8-bit shift amount:

```cpp
KnownBits Amt = KnownBits::makeConstant(APInt(8, 1));
return KnownBits::shl(LHS, Amt, NUW, NSW, /*ShAmtNonZero=*/true);
```

The comment there claims the shift-amount bitwidth is independent of the source bitwidth, but that is not true: `shl()`'s `getMaxShiftAmount()` extracts `Log2_32(BitWidth)` bits from the shift amount's max value when `BitWidth` is a power of two:

```cpp
static unsigned getMaxShiftAmount(const APInt &MaxValue, unsigned BitWidth) {
  if (isPowerOf2_32(BitWidth))
    return MaxValue.extractBitsAsZExtValue(Log2_32(BitWidth), 0);
  ...
}
```

For source widths `>= 512`, `Log2_32(BitWidth) >= 9`, so extracting that many bits from the 8-bit shift amount trips the assertion in `APInt::extractBitsAsZExtValue`:

```
Assertion `bitPosition < BitWidth && (numBits + bitPosition) <= BitWidth && "Illegal bit extraction"' failed.
 #9  llvm::APInt::extractBitsAsZExtValue(unsigned int, unsigned int) const
#10  llvm::KnownBits::shl(...)
#11  llvm::KnownBits::add(...)
```

(256 is the boundary that still works: `Log2_32(256) == 8`, extracting exactly 8 bits from the 8-bit amount.)

Fix: make the shift-amount bitwidth match the source bitwidth so the extraction is always in bounds. The `SelfAdd` path was introduced in #188078.

Found via fuzzing. Adds a `SelfAddWide` regression test covering widths 256/512/1024.

body:
## Summary

Add comprehensive evaluation document assessing WP Admin Workspaces' readiness for WordPress core inclusion, including architectural strengths, gaps, ecosystem risks, and a phased adoption roadmap.

## Changes

- **New document:** `docs/core-inclusion-evaluation.md`
  - Verdict: Not mergeable as-is, but credible for feature-plugin pipeline
  - Detailed security audit of cascade/permission model (core-grade)
  - Kernel/engine separation verification and design-system neutrality
  - Honest parity assessment (~60% native, 40% deferred to iframes)
  - Extensibility contract gap analysis (the existential blocker)
  - Seven actionable recommendations for adoption path
  - Nine tracked follow-up issues (#286–#295) with specific owners

## Key findings

**Strengths:**
- Cascade and trust-tier security model is "better security engineering than most code already in core"
- Kernel/engine separation is real and verified by CI test
- Dogfoods core's own direction (DataViews, DataForm, DTCG, `@wordpress/ui`)
- Back-compat designed in (classic menu bridge, iframe fallback, clean deactivation)
- Exceptional documentation and test discipline for a plugin

**Blockers:**
- ~40% of hardest features deferred (post editor, site editor iframed; Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, media list missing)
- Plugin extensibility contract unanswered (classic hooks like `manage_*_columns`, metaboxes, Screen Options have no native equivalent)
- Multisite/network admin absent
- Private API dependencies (`@wordpress/ui` 0.12, private DataViews subpath, consent-string spoofing)
- Operational gaps (no e2e tests, perf baselines empty, static JSON untranslatable, RTL untested, hash routing)

**Recommendations:**
1. Enter official feature-plugin process (not single-release merge)
2. Upstream REST gaps first (independent of shell)
3. Write extensibility-parity RFC before more screens
4. Land native editor mounts (resolve five documented blockers)
5. Stabilize foundations in lockstep (`@wordpress/ui` → 1.0, DataViews exports, legitimate allowlist)
6. Close table-stakes gaps (multisite, i18n, RTL, e2e, perf, real-path routing)
7. Converge shared app code with Gutenberg packages

## Impact

This evaluation provides the roadmap for transforming WP Admin Workspaces from a credible prototype into a core-adoptable platform. It identifies which parts should be upstreamed immediately (REST gaps, settings shims) independent of the shell itself, and which require ecosystem negotiation (extensibility contract) before merge is viable.

author: kish21
body:
## What & why

**Milestone 1's exit slice (M1.4): govern *any* MCP server by config alone — zero gateway code.**

This PR registers a **real, third-party MCP server we did not write** — `mcp-server-time` — and brings it under full governance (identity → RBAC → tamper-evident audit) **purely by a `config/upstreams.yaml` entry + a `demo` dependency extra**, with no change to `src/gatekeeper/`. That proves the product's tool-agnostic promise end-to-end. It also implements the last operator command (`seed-demo`) and hardens the proxy against a bad upstream.

A pre-existing, independent latent bug found while live-testing — `McpUpstreamClient.aclose()` raising a cross-task cancel-scope `RuntimeError` on shutdown — is **bundled in** as a `### Fixed` change.

## M1.4
- **Third-party `time` upstream** in `config/upstreams.yaml` (`mcp-server-time`), installable via the new `demo` optional-dependency. Governed by the existing pipeline; classification driven by config annotations.
- **`gatekeeper seed-demo`** — non-destructive: seeds the demo sandbox + sample file and prints a ready-to-run recipe; shows principal+role only (**never tokens**); fail-loud (exit 2) on missing config; pure-ASCII (Windows-console-safe).
- **Resilience** — one unavailable/misconfigured upstream is logged and **skipped**, not fatal; its tools simply aren't exposed (no ungoverned bypass), every healthy upstream stays governed.
- **CI** installs `.[demo]` in the test job (the "any server" proof runs for real) and the security job (so `mcp-server-time` is CVE-scanned by pip-audit).

## Bundled fix (`aclose()`)
Each upstream session's anyio lifecycle is now pinned to one dedicated task (`_SessionRunner`/`_run_session`), so it is opened **and** closed in the same task — `aclose()` is safe to call from any task (even when a session was first opened inside a forward's child task) and never raises on shutdown. Independent of M1.4's `_build_tool_index` skip.

## How verified
- **Live (real `gatekeeper serve` ← real MCP client → real `mcp-server-time`):** 6 tools re-exposed across both upstreams; `get_current_time` / `convert_time` relayed unchanged, **allow/read/audited**; `tail` shows `time:*`; `verify` OK; `show <call_id>` renders the full decision (Cedar reason names `time::get_current_time`); **clean shutdown — no cancel-scope `RuntimeError`**.
- **Tests: 93 pass** (+ integration vs the real `mcp-server-time` subprocess; `seed-demo` unit ×6 incl. no-token-leak / idempotent / fail-loud / ASCII / drift-guard; proxy resilience; `aclose()` regression).
- ruff + ruff-format + mypy(strict) clean. `/code-review` (high) — 1 finding fixed (pip-audit didn't scan `.[demo]`). `/security-review` — no findings ≥8.

## Docs
`docs/features/config-driven-any-server.md`; `PRODUCT.md` (#Build log + resume marker); `README`; `CHANGELOG` (incl. `### Fixed`).

## Rollback
Additive feature + a self-contained bugfix; no migration. Rollback = revert this PR.

After merge: **M1 is development-complete** → next is the M1 exit gate (`/dev-check`).

body:
## Problem

`node_modules` was tracked in git as a **symlink** (mode 120000) pointing to a machine-specific absolute path:

```
/Users/neha/Claude Workspace/niyora/ios-v1/node_modules
```

On a fresh checkout (e.g. a branch switch on a build machine), that symlink resolved to a stale/incomplete location, so packages like `expo-router` were missing. This broke a production build until a manual `npm install` recovered it.

`.gitignore` already contained `node_modules/`, but the ignore rule has no effect on a path that is already tracked.

## Fix

`git rm --cached node_modules` to stop tracking the symlink. The working-tree `node_modules` is untouched, and the existing `.gitignore` rule now takes effect.

## Verification

- `git check-ignore -v node_modules` → `.gitignore:4:node_modules/  node_modules`
- `git status` no longer shows any `node_modules` churn
- Working-tree `node_modules/` directory is preserved

Scoped to untracking only. No `.gitignore` edit was needed (the rule was already present).

author: dannycrews
body:
The 'bu-navigation' object cache group (the load_sections section/membership structure) was registered non-persistent, so on production with an active object cache the expensive GROUP_CONCAT/GROUP BY wp_posts scan re-ran on nearly every front-end render under crawler concurrency.

Leave the group persistent (Redis-backed). This is safe by construction: the cached payload is order- and status-independent parent/children membership only, keyed on core's posts 'last_changed' value (bumped by clean_post_cache() on every post insert/update/delete), so a stale entry is orphaned rather than served. Publication status, menu_order ordering, and navigation meta are applied downstream on the uncached get_nav_posts() query and are never served from this cache.

Harden the cache entry with an explicit DAY_IN_SECONDS TTL backstop and a site-scoped key (get_current_blog_id()) for multisite isolation, mirroring the bu-calendar default-URL cache.

Bump version to 1.3.6; also corrects the VERSION constant, which had drifted to 1.3.4 while the plugin header read 1.3.5.

author: jamesbrink
body:
## Problem

Adding or re-authing a Claude Code / Codex account through Burnrate could break the user's **terminal** CLI session (forced re-login, "keychain changes for both apps"). Investigation found three distinct causes, all addressed here:

1. **Server-side OAuth refresh-token rotation** (the original report): both providers issue single-use refresh tokens keyed to the *account/grant*, not the directory. Once the same provider account lives in two credential stores — the terminal's `~/.claude`/`~/.codex` **and** a Burnrate-managed dir — whichever side refreshes next invalidates the other (`refresh_token_reused` for Codex, "OAuth token has been revoked" for Claude). Fake home dirs alone are necessary but not sufficient; the fix is to never lead the user into "same account in two stores".
2. **Credential-bypassing env pollution**: AI-agent terminals (cmux) export `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` into their surfaces. A dev app inheriting it passes it to every spawned `claude`, which then reports `loggedIn: true` with **no subscriptionType/email** — breaking sign-in verify, dashboard fetch, and detection validation simultaneously ("Claude Code is signed in, but no Claude subscription was detected").
3. **Hygiene debt**: orphaned managed CLI dirs and macOS Keychain entries accumulated from interrupted/merged sign-ins, and the dev re-sign runner was a silent no-op (keychain prompt storm on every rebuild).

## Changes

### `9873793` — isolate secondary sign-ins from the primary CLI session
- **Pre-login warning** in `LoginModal` for brand-new sign-ins: sign in with the account you want to *add*; re-authorizing one that's signed in elsewhere can sign it out there.
- **Keychain cleanup on discard paths**: when a completed sign-in merges into an existing account (or a failed one is discarded), the throwaway managed dir's Keychain credential is deleted too instead of orphaned.
- **Fail-closed re-auth guard**: browser re-auth of a CLI account with no isolated dir (and not auto-detected) is rejected instead of silently retargeting `~/.claude`/`~/.codex`.
- **Startup orphan GC**: unreferenced `<data>/cli/<provider>/<id>` dirs (and their Claude Keychain entries) are collected; guarded by `is_managed_cli_dir` so system defaults are untouchable.

### `fe4ad5b` — hardening after adversarial peer review (47-agent review; 7 confirmed findings)
- **Keychain deletion fails closed**: `None`/empty/unmanaged dirs derive the *system-default* `Claude Code-credentials` service name — never Burnrate's to delete. Previously, removing the placeholder account mid-login made finalize push `None` and delete the user's terminal credential (the exact failure class this branch fixes).
- **Merge aborts when the placeholder vanished mid-login** instead of adopting/deleting state for a nonexistent account (`update_config` rolls back).
- **GC safety**: skipped when the sqlite store was just created (fresh DB / deleted file / partial restore would classify every managed dir as orphaned); path comparison canonicalizes both sides (symlinked `/var`, respelled `BURNRATE_CONFIG_DIR`); scan allowlisted to provider names Burnrate actually creates.
- **`upsert_manual` keeps `auto_detected`**: editing metadata no longer makes the re-auth guard reject the genuine system-default account until next launch.
- **UI mirrors the guard**: "Sign in again" is hidden (Sign out stays) for manual-token CLI accounts the backend deterministically rejects.

### `b8a7aad` — strip inherited credential env vars + debug tooling + dev codesign fix
- **`providers::CREDENTIAL_ENV_OVERRIDES`** (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`) removed from every spawned provider CLI (auth status, login, logout, codex app-server, version probes). Verified live: a sandboxed fetch with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=fake` now returns a healthy Claude snapshot with subscription + email where it previously errored.
- **Hidden `burnrate debug <env|detect|load|snapshot>` CLI**: runs the real provider/config code paths headlessly (JSON to stdout, sandboxable via `BURNRATE_CONFIG_DIR`); documented in `.claude/skills/burnrate-debug/SKILL.md`. Coverage-exempt alongside the other glue modules.
- **Dev codesign**: plain `dev-codesign-setup.sh` never created the `~/.burnrate-dev-codesign-authorized` marker the runner requires, so re-signing silently never happened and keychain grants reset every rebuild. Setup now probe-signs and creates the marker automatically (with `--authorize-key` as the password-prompting fallback); the runner warns on failure instead of swallowing it.

## Testing

- `./scripts/check` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tsc) and `./scripts/test`: **148 Rust + 98 vitest** passing; treefmt clean; `dist/` rebuilt and committed.
- New tests: keychain fail-closed behavior via the managed-dir guard, GC provider-allowlist + leaf scanning, `upsert_manual` provenance preservation, login-warning visibility on both sides of `reauthId`, `canReauth` UI gating, `strip_credential_env` via `get_envs`.
- Live verification on-machine: `burnrate debug detect/load/snapshot` with a polluted env detects both system accounts and fetches Claude healthy; the Codex 401 reproduced is genuine server-side revocation (pre-existing rotation damage), recoverable via `codex login`.

## Residual

If the user signs the *same* account into both Burnrate and the terminal, provider-side rotation can still ping-pong — that's the provider's behavior; the pre-login warning plus duplicate-merge logic is the honest UX for it.

author: dvmrry
body:
The `fuzz-smoke` gate added in [#106](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscalerctl/pull/106) failed on PR [#109](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscalerctl/pull/109) (`FuzzProjectRecordSubsetAndCanaryRedaction`). **It was a false positive, not a bug.**

## Root cause

Go's fuzzer harvests string constants from the test — including the `canary` — and injects them into the inputs. The harness excluded the canary from `prefix`/`suffix` but **not** from `data`. When the fuzzer slipped `[b]+canary` into `data`, `fuzzValue` (case 0 → `data[1:]`) rendered the **full canary as an ordinary field value**, which projection correctly renders — the redactor must not mangle arbitrary low-entropy strings. So the harness failed on a secret it manufactured itself.

Verified conclusively: `data=[b]+canary` leaks via e.g. `zia/nss-feeds`; the real `psk=`-shaped canary the harness injects on purpose is always stripped (broad sweeps across every spec × field × mode). **Projection/redaction is sound.**

## Fixes

1. **Harness** (`resources_fuzz_test.go`): also skip inputs whose `data` contains the canary, so the assertion stays a real leak test.
2. **Gate design**: remove the blocking live-`-fuzz` `fuzz-smoke` CI job and drop it from `required`. Live exploration is nondeterministic — it can fail an unrelated PR on a freshly mutated input that's neither reproducible nor committed (and here, not even a real bug). Fuzz now follows the standard two-tier model:
   - **Regression (blocking, deterministic):** `go test ./...` (the `unit` job) runs every fuzz target's seed corpus + committed `testdata/fuzz/*` crash inputs.
   - **Discovery (advisory):** the weekly `fuzz.yml` runs live `-fuzz` and uploads new crash inputs to commit into the corpus.
   `make fuzz-smoke` stays as a local discovery helper.
3. **DEPENDENCY_POLICY**: document the regression/discovery split.

This corrects an over-build in #106 — the blocking live-fuzz gate was the wrong pattern. `make check` passes. After this merges I'll rebase #109 (which then no longer runs the removed gate) and add justified `#nosec` for the gosec exec/file findings on the live-smoke port.

author: artosien
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced `Math.max(...numbers.map(...))` with `numbers.reduce(...)` to calculate the maximum frequency in the Heatmap component.
🎯 **Why:** The previous approach caused redundant array allocations by calling `.map()`, and using the spread operator (`...`) with `Math.max()` can exceed maximum call stack size in V8 engines for large arrays. The `reduce` method performs a single pass over the array and avoids the spread syntax, reducing memory overhead and improving performance.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
- Baseline: ~5700 ms (for 1000 iterations of 100k elements)
- Optimized: ~1940 ms (for 1000 iterations of 100k elements)
- Improvement: ~66% faster

body:
## The bug (user report 2026-06-10)
> "when escaping back from iDempiere.html sometimes the ERP.html goes to its old deprecated format and not clean bubbles only.. the old format has bottom buttons"

The "old format with bottom buttons" is **`_renderBottomNav()`** — the emoji bottom bar (🏠Home / 📋List / ➕New / 📊Charts / ⚙️More) of the **in-app record UI** that v619's launcher model replaced. It stayed reachable via `openWindow` (FTS hit / recent / the erp.html `?window=` deep-link restore), so a back/reload carrying `?window=` repainted the deprecated grid + bottom bar instead of the clean globe.

The same dormant grid obscured the clean pill bar → also explains the **"Share icon gone"** report (the Share pill renders fine on the clean bar; idempiere.html's contextual Accts-Posted `onShare` is a separate, untouched affordance).

## Fix (`ad_ui.js?v=28` + `erp.html`)
- `showMenu` **always** renders the curated globe skeleton only; the DB-ready home chrome (bottomNav + recent + menu tree) is removed.
- `openWindow` **forwards to `_openInIdempiere`** — every "open window" launches the real idempiere.html.
- erp.html `_restoreDeepLink` **forwards `?window=`/`?record=` to idempiere.html** (was `ADUI.openWindow` → in-app grid). *(approach chosen by user)*
- `_renderBottomNav` + `_navHandler` **deleted**. `_currentScreen` is never set to `'window'` anymore → the in-app grid island is fully unreachable.

erp.html is now **bubbles + pill ONLY** on every entry. **idempiere.html is untouched.**

## Witnesses (headless, served worktree)
```
§T1 clean-globe bottomNavChildren=0 hasPillShare=true screen=home  (showMenu bubbles, no bottomNav)
§T2 deep-link ?window=143 → idempiere.html?window=143              (forwarded, no in-app grid)
§LAUNCHER-CLEANUP PASS
§IDLE-GATE PASS (regression)   ·   pill-share present (12 pills mounted)
```

## Attack-Path v2 — "What you're approving" closure panel (real data, no mock)

Adds the before → exact-diff → after closure view to the attacker path sidebar:
the dangerous, *unused* capability that gets removed, the observed access that's
**kept**, and the projected after-state — framed as **damage closed, not path
closed** (the path stays; the app keeps what it uses).

Renders entirely from live graph data via the backend's read-view; **no mock,
ever** — honest loading / error / empty states when data is absent.

### What changed
- `components/attack-paths-v2/closure-outcome-panel.tsx` — the panel + a self-fetching
  `ClosureOutcomeSection` wrapper (282 lines, under the 400 cap)
- `components/attack-paths-v2/closure-outcome-types.ts` — typed `ClosurePreview` contract
- `components/attack-paths-v2/use-closure-preview.ts` — fetch hook (honest states, no mock)
- `app/api/proxy/attack-paths/[pathId]/closure-preview/route.ts` — proxy (timeout + cache + error envelope)
- `components/attack-paths-v2/path-analysis-panel.tsx` — composes the panel next to Damage/Hardening (+5 lines)
- `CLAUDE.md` (new) — repo rules: **real data only / no mock**, edit-don't-recreate, proxy pattern

### Backend dependency (already live)
`GET /api/attack-paths/{id}/closure-preview` — merged to `main` (`c90353f`), Render
prod returns **200** with real diff data. Reads the live `AttackPath` node + shared-role
signal; the verdict reflects the real `approval_required` (shared role across 2 live workloads).

### Conventions followed
- **Extended** `attack-paths-v2/` — no `v3`/`-map` fork.
- Wired to the engines, not a parallel implementation (the map = single source of truth).
- Real enums/tokens; always shows `kept` next to `removed`; one-click rollback affordance.

### Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` clean on all new files.
- Renders real data for the `alon-demo-app2 → saferemediate-logs` path; absent data → honest empty state.

### Risk / rollback
- Additive: one new composed panel + isolated proxy/hook/types. **No changes to shared `lib/types.ts`.**
- Read-only view, nothing destructive. Revert = drop the 6 files + the +5-line compose.

### Notes
- Only the closure-panel files are in this change; unrelated working-tree files
  (`exfil-view-v3.tsx`, `traffic-flow-map.tsx`, `test-results/`) are intentionally excluded.

## Test plan
- [ ] Vercel preview: open Attack Paths v2 → `alon-demo-app2 → saferemediate-logs` (`432c6db1…99d42`)
- [ ] "What you're approving" panel shows removed + kept actions and damage-closed framing

- [ ] Invalid pathId → honest error/empty state (no fabricated diff)

author: jwrosewell
body:
fix(build): shorten Doxygen titles and noindex generated index pages

Sets FULL_PATH_NAMES = NO so the generated directory and file page titles no
longer embed the full CI build path, and enables HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX = YES so
Doxygen's generated navigation, index and helper pages (dir_*.html, pages.html,
the crawler helper and the graph legend) carry
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow">.

These thin, link-only pages are flagged as low-quality content by search
engines. The change keeps them out of the search index while crawlers still
follow their links to the real documentation. Part of the SEMrush documentation
audit remediation (issues 102, 112, 117).

HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX requires the updated 51Degrees DoxyGen build
(51Degrees/doxygen#7); older builds ignore the tag with a harmless warning.

body:
### Motivation
- Permitir al usuario introducir resultados en todas las rondas eliminatorias (R32 → R16 → QF → SF → Final) y que los ganadores avancen automáticamente, manteniendo el mismo estilo funcional y visual que la fase de grupos.
- Evitar que queden equipos "fantasma" si se cambian resultados previos y forzar selección explícita de clasificado en empates para poder finalizar la porra.
- Conservar la lógica de puntuación central y extender los tipos/schemas para que la persistencia admita las predicciones de eliminatorias.

### Description
- Añade modelo y helpers del bracket de eliminatorias en `lib/world-cup/knockout.ts` y expone tipos en `lib/world-cup/types.ts` para representar rondas, vistas y la conversión necesaria para scoring (`winnerTeamId`, `buildKnockoutBracket`, `flattenKnockoutBracket`, `toScoringKnockoutPredictions`, `getChampion`).
- Reemplaza los placeholders por una UI rellenable: `KnockoutMatchCard` y `KnockoutRoundSection` en `app/porra/page.tsx` permiten ver bandera/nombre, inputs de goles, separador y selector de clasificado (obligatorio en empates), recalculando siguientes rondas automáticamente a partir de ganadores. 
- Persiste y carga predicciones de eliminatorias desde `knockoutPredictions`, integra `champion` y añade validación completa antes de enviar (`validateCompletePrediction`); la persistencia y envío usan `saveUserPredictionDraft` / `submitUserPrediction` con `persistedKnockoutPredictions` y snapshot del bracket.
- Actualiza tipos y schema backend para aceptar `winnerTeamId` en eliminatorias en `lib/types.ts`, `functions/src/shared/types.ts` y `functions/src/submitPrediction.ts`; adapta el componente `components/porra/KnockoutBracket.tsx` y `components/porra/PredictionSummary.tsx` para el nuevo modelo.
- Lista de archivos cambiados/añadidos principales: `app/porra/page.tsx`, `lib/world-cup/knockout.ts` (nuevo), `lib/world-cup/types.ts` (nuevo), `lib/types.ts`, `functions/src/shared/types.ts`, `functions/src/submitPrediction.ts`, `components/porra/KnockoutBracket.tsx`, `components/porra/PredictionSummary.tsx`.

### Testing
- `npm ci` / instalación de dependencias falló por un `403 Forbidden` al descargar `picomatch`, por lo que no se pudieron completar las instalaciones necesarias para ejecutar la build completa en este entorno; esto impidió ejecutar `next` localmente y afectó `lint`/`build`.
- `npm run typecheck` fue ejecutado pero reportó muchos errores relacionados con dependencias/definiciones ausentes después del fallo de instalación (tipo `Cannot find module 'react'` etc.).
- `npm run lint` y `npm run build` no pudieron ejecutarse porque `next` no quedó disponible en el entorno tras la falla de `npm ci`.
- Comprobaciones locales de diff/estática (`git diff --check`) no mostró advertencias relevantes respecto al patch; el flujo funcional de UI y validación fue implementado y cubierto por la nueva lógica, pero la verificación de build/SSR debe correrse en entorno con dependencias instaladas para validar integraciones finales.

------

body:
## Summary

The `_fmt_generic` formatter in `pretty_output_hook.py` silently truncates nested dict/list values to 200 characters. This destroyed the `dispatch_plan` field in `dispatch_food_truck` tool results, causing the AI orchestrator to lose visibility of dispatch groups 4–6 (9 of 22 issues). The root cause is an architectural gap: tools carrying structured data consumed by downstream orchestrators are classified alongside simple ack/result tools in `_UNFORMATTED_TOOLS`, where `_fmt_generic` applies a blanket 200-char truncation with no awareness of field semantics.

The existing formatter system already has a robust immunity pattern — dedicated formatters with TypedDict contracts and RENDERED/SUPPRESSED frozensets enforced by meta-tests — but this pattern is opt-in and lacks a structural gate that forces tools with complex response shapes out of the generic path.

Part A promotes `dispatch_food_truck` to a dedicated formatter with full contract coverage, and adds a structural test that prevents future tools with nested dict/list response fields from entering `_UNFORMATTED_TOOLS` without explicit acknowledgment. Part B will address the broader `_fmt_generic` truncation policy and related tools (`get_pipeline_report`, `wait_for_ci`, `get_ci_status`, `fetch_github_issue`).

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #699
Fixes #700
Fixes #703

Three lipgloss height/centering miscounts in `ui/`, each making a pane render a different number of lines than its `SetSize` allocation. All three were verified by measurement before fixing, and each new regression test fails on `master` and passes with this change.

## #699 — Preview fallback miscentered when the ASCII art wraps

`PreviewPane.String()` computed vertical-centering padding from the **pre-wrap** line count of the fallback text (18 lines), but the final render applies `Width(p.width)`, which wraps the 58-column ASCII art on narrow panes. At the real 80-column-terminal preview width (~48 cols), the art wraps to ~37 lines: measured **49 lines rendered into a 30-line allocation**, miscentered and overflowing the layout.

**Fix:** render at the target width first, then center using the wrapped line count.

## #700 — Content pane taller than allocated, pushing menu/errBox off-screen

The overflow is real, but the issue's diagnosis isn't quite right: the `JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, "\n", wrapped)` spacer **is** budgeted — the `-2` in both `renderInlinePane` and `SetSize` accounts for it, mirroring `TabbedWindow.String`'s identical spacer/budget, and at-rest output measures exactly `c.height` lines. Removing the `"\n"` (the issue's recommended fix) would render inline panes 2 lines **short** and make the layout jump when switching sidebar selections.

The actual overflow source: `lipgloss.Place` and `Style.Height` are *minimums* — they pad short content but never truncate tall content — and the window frame's `Width` re-wraps long lines. A populated task/hooks list blows straight through the budget: measured **246 lines for a 21-line allocation** at 80×24, which is what pushes the menu and error box below the fold.

**Fix:** wrap content to the frame width, clamp to the height budget, then frame. `ContentPane.String()` now renders exactly its allocation in every mode regardless of content volume. (`renderEmptyPane` now delegates to `renderInlinePane` — they were copy-paste identical.)

## #703 — Terminal fallback 7 lines short, centered 4 lines too high

`TerminalPane.String()` fallback subtracted tab-bar + window-frame chrome (`height - 3 - 4`) from a height that `TabbedWindow.SetSize` had already stripped chrome from. Measured **23 lines for a 30-line allocation**. This is the exact bug `PreviewPane` had and fixed for #616 — `TerminalPane` was missed.

**Fix:** use `height` directly, same as normal mode and same as the PreviewPane precedent. Both fallback paths now share `renderCenteredFallback` (new `ui/fallback.go`), which also clamps over-tall fallbacks to the bottom `height` lines so the trailing message stays visible (matching normal mode's keep-newest truncation).

## Adjacent-site audit (all `lipgloss.Place` / `JoinVertical` height math in `ui/`)

| Site | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `tabbed_window.go` `SetSize`/`String` budget | **Correct** — measured exactly `height` lines at 80×24; children now can't overflow it |
| `preview.go` / `terminal.go` normal modes | **Correct** — pad and truncate to exact height |
| `menu.go:270`, `err.go:76`, `list.go`, `sidebar.go` single-line `Place`s | **Correct** — single-line, or have explicit clip handling with comments |
| `content_pane.go` inline/empty panes | **Fixed** (#700) |
| `preview.go` / `terminal.go` fallback branches | **Fixed** (#699/#703) |
| `sidebar.go:539` full-pane `Place` | **Excluded** — can overflow with very long instance lists, but needs selection-aware windowing (a blind clamp would hide the selected instance); follow-up issue to be filed |

## Tests

New `ui/layout_height_test.go` — every test asserts rendered line count **equals** the allocated height at the issue-reported dimensions (no overflow, no shortfall), all failing pre-fix:

- `TestPreviewFallbackWrappedArtMatchesAllocatedHeight` (48×15, 48×30, 48×60, 80×30)
- `TestPreviewFallbackCentersWrappedLineCount` (top/bottom padding balanced using wrapped count)
- `TestTerminalFallbackMatchesNormalModeHeight` (heights 20/25/30/50, fallback == normal == h; adapted from the failing test in #703)
- `TestTerminalFallbackWrappedArtMatchesAllocatedHeight` (terminal variant of the wrap bug)
- `TestContentPaneRendersExactlyAllocatedHeight` (80×24 layout dims; empty/tasks/hooks/instance modes, including 40-item over-tall lists)

## Verification

- `go build ./...` ✅
- `gofmt -l .` clean ✅
- `golangci-lint run --timeout=3m --fast` ✅
- `deadcode -test ./...` clean ✅
- `go test ./...` ✅ (only failure: `daemon/TestSigtermFallback_DeadPID`, the known dev-box flake from live `af --daemon` processes, unrelated)
- `go test -race ./ui/` ✅

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #10 addressing two issues found during review:

- **Symmetric-alert relink bug**: `attachRelatedPersons` always attached the `relatedPersonId` side, so the second citizen in a shared-phone pair saw themselves as their own "other side" — the link from the row pointed back at the same page. It's now viewer-aware: `listOpenAlerts(personId)` passes the queried id, and `relatedPerson` is always the *other* citizen regardless of which side of the alert they're on.

- **`collidingValue` on the wire**: both `Alert` and `ConflictDetail` now carry the actual shared value — the shared nationalId for an ID error, or the specific shared phone (computed by intersecting both persons' phone sets) for a phone error. The frontend renders this verbatim instead of guessing with `otherPerson.phones[0]`, which could pick a phone unrelated to the collision.

author: erseco
body:
## What

Adds a generic `unzip` blueprint step: download a ZIP and extract it into a destination directory (relative to the Nextcloud root or absolute), stripping a single top-level wrapper folder.

## Why

So a blueprint can install an app **without** a baked-in editor and overlay the upstream eXeLearning editor release at boot — the same pattern the Moodle/WP playgrounds use. This keeps the app/preview zip lean and makes the editor a shared upstream artifact instead of a re-bundled one.

## How

- `src/runtime/install-script.js`: new `buildUnzipScript()` — PHP `ZipArchive` extraction into a stage, descends into a lone top-level wrapper folder (the editor asset wraps everything in `static/`), then moves it into the destination. Same one-entry-at-a-time, low-memory approach as `installApp`/core extraction (the editor is ~70 MB / 3000+ files), with the same `NO_ZIP_EXT` → JS-fallback contract.
- `src/runtime/blueprint-steps.js`: new `case "unzip"` — fetch + PHP extract, with a JS fallback via `extractZipEntries` (which strips the same leading folder, so both paths agree).
- `assets/blueprints/blueprint-schema.json` + `src/shared/blueprint.js` (`KNOWN_STEPS`): register `unzip` and a `destination` property.
- `tests/blueprint.test.mjs`: `buildUnzipScript` script-contract tests + an `unzip` normalization test (52/52 pass; biome clean).

## Note

Companion change exelearning/nextcloud-exelearning#47 switches its playground blueprint to this step. **This PR should merge and deploy first** so the deployed playground recognizes the `unzip` step.

author: razialam
body:
## Why this follow-up

PR #2 was merged, but only its first commit (the basic both-axes fill) landed on `main`. The final fix — cropping the artboard's baked-in side padding so the device actually reaches the edges — was pushed after the merge and never made it onto `main`. This brings it in.

## What changed

The Figma artboard (`.site-canvas`) is 1500×900, but the actual device is only **1368px wide and centered**, leaving 66px of plain black canvas on each side. Scaling the canvas scaled those black strips too, so the device never reached the edges however small the margin.

This scales the horizontal axis to the **device's 1368px width** instead of the artboard's 1500px, so the device fills the viewport and the black side-padding crops off-screen. Margin also tightened to 8px.

## Verification

- At 1680px wide: dark display panel went from **81px → 8px** from each edge — black bars gone.
- Nav buttons still align and work (clicking the overlay navigated to `#manifesto`) — the overlay is a child of the same scaled canvas, so hit areas stay locked with no recalibration.
