author: rul1an
body:
## What

Docs-only RFC: the v0 contract for a host-capability proof gate on `crates/assay-cli/src/diagnostics/` changes. No implementation in this PR; the checker and the two workflows are a follow-up PR that must match this contract.

## Why

Diagnostics files carry host/kernel-capability claims (Landlock ABI, net-ruleset usability, no_new_privs). The lane-check classifier correctly keeps them out of the runner-spike lanes (different proof object), which means nothing currently machine-enforces that the diagnostics were actually produced on a real host for the PR head. Until now that evidence was attached manually (#1586, #1587). This contract makes the discipline machine-checked.

## Design decisions (as reviewed)

- Required status check, not advisory.
- v0 requires a validated `workflow_dispatch` run (event / head_sha / conclusion / workflow checked via the Actions API); a pasted JSON block from a trusted account alone never satisfies the gate.
- Proof workflow runs on the self-hosted host with `contents: read` + `actions: read`; check workflow runs on `pull_request` with read-only permissions and posts no comment; no `pull_request_target` in v0.
- Seven required landlock fields including `net_bind_tcp_supported` (same ABI 4 capability family, same doctor run); errno fields optional but type-checked.
- Presence and type validation only, never values: a red host is also evidence.
- Markdown under the trigger prefix is exempt; the checker and workflows are exempt as a documented technical exemption, not a trust statement.
- Machine-readable, append-only failure reasons.

## Scope boundary

Docs only. No checker, no workflows, no branch-protection change, no lane-check change.

author: shankypanky
body:
## What is this

Manifold Jobs is a curated job board for roles in trading, AI, and fintech — built for the kind of people who already use Manifold. It launches alongside the 2026 Manifold conference, where hiring has happened organically in past years. This gives that a home.

The differentiator isn't just niche targeting. It's the format: structured role cards that require honest trade-offs instead of HR copy, and a candidate profile built around what you've actually built rather than job titles and years of experience.

## Design philosophy

**Structured role cards, not walls of text.** Every listing has fixed sections — the problem this hire solves, what the work actually is, what good looks like at 30/90 days and 1 year, and an honest trade-offs split (great if you want X / hard if you need Y). Employers fill in the structure; the format does the filtering.

**Honest trade-offs as a first-class field.** The "hard if you need" column is the most important thing on the page. It self-selects candidates and builds trust faster than any amount of positive copy. Almost no job boards surface this — we make it required.

**Candidate profiles built around work, not CVs.** Instead of job titles and dates, candidates describe 2–3 things they've built: the problem, their role, the outcome. Skills are inferred from those descriptions and confirmed by the candidate. What they want — and what they won't do — is structured data, not a cover letter.

**Matching over keyword proximity.** The longer-term vision is two-sided preference matching: surfacing alignment (or honest misalignment) between what a role actually is and what a candidate actually wants. That's a later milestone, but the data model is being built toward it from day one.

## What's in this PR

**Data layer**
- `web/lib/jobs-data.ts` — TypeScript types and static job data. Three live MNX roles seeded: Backend Engineer, Head of Growth, Quantitative Trader.

**Prototype A — `/jobs` + `/jobs/[slug]`**
- Browse page with job cards linking to individual role detail pages
- Detail page implements the full role card format: masthead, skill tags, info tiles, problem statement, work bullets, 30/90/1yr milestones, honest trade-offs, who you are, apply footer

**Prototype B — `/jobs-2`**
- Same browse page but cards expand in place — no navigation to a detail page
- Stripped back to the original job post content: intro, what you'll do, what we're looking for
- Both prototypes are included for the team to compare directions

**Candidate profile — `/jobs/candidate`**
- Static mockup of what a filled-out candidate profile looks like (Jamie K., quant trader)
- Sections: status badge, summary, skill tags, stats bar (comp/availability/open to), work samples with outcome badges, skills depth bars, I want / I won't do split, reach out CTA
- Hardcoded for now — structure is the point

## What's not built yet

- Candidate onboarding form (5-step flow: basics → your work → skills → what you want → comp & availability)

body:
## What & why

Closes #68 — Wave 1 (infra & safety nets). Measures line coverage of `rigforge.sh` + `util/proposed-grub.sh` and gates PRs on it, **fully self-contained** (no Codecov/external service), matching the repo's pinned-deps CI philosophy.

> **Draft:** the committed floor is a placeholder (`0`) until the first CI `coverage` run reports the measured baseline — I'll set the real floor and mark ready.

## Approach

**Coverage tooling**
- **`tests/coverage.sh` + `make coverage`** — runs `tests/run.sh` under a **digest-pinned kcov image** (v42) with a **pinned static `jq`** mounted (the kcov image lacks jq; pinned by sha256 from the upstream release, same approach as shellcheck/shfmt — no apt). Emits Cobertura XML (paths normalised to repo-relative) + an HTML report, and enforces a committed **total floor** ([`tests/coverage-floor.txt`](tests/coverage-floor.txt), a ratchet). Fails loudly if kcov records **0** instrumented lines (guards the silent-zero failure mode).
- **CI `coverage` job** — the above (total floor) **plus `diff-cover`** (pinned `9.7.2`) for **patch coverage** of new/changed lines vs `origin/main`. Patch coverage is the real lever that keeps coverage from rotting.

**Crediting black-box runs (the issue's flagged "first task")**
- The black-box tests previously ran **copies** of the script (`cp "$SCRIPT" "$sandbox/rigforge.sh"`), so kcov would credit command-dispatch coverage to throwaway paths, not the git file.
- Fixed by making the script's base dir overridable via **`RIGFORGE_HOME`** (defaults to the script's own dir → a normal deploy is byte-identical). The suite now runs the **real** `rigforge.sh` against a per-test sandbox (`RIGFORGE_HOME=sandbox`), so kcov credits the sourced **and** command-dispatch paths to `rigforge.sh`. All 39 call sites converted; dead copies removed. **Suite behavior unchanged** (same pass count locally).
- `util/proposed-grub.sh` is already exercised directly (`PG="$ROOT/util/proposed-grub.sh"`), so it's credited too.

**Housekeeping**
- CI `lint` now runs **`make lint`** so its file list can't drift from the Makefile — it *had* already gone stale (`tests/smoke.sh` from #61 was never linted in CI). Now covers `tests/smoke.sh` + `tests/coverage.sh`.
- `.gitignore`: `coverage/` + `.coverage-cache/`.

## Validation note

kcov is Linux/ptrace based and **can't run on the macOS Docker VM** (ptrace/`personality` gets killed under Apple-silicon emulation), so the kcov numbers and subprocess-counting are validated **on the CI amd64 runner** — the same role the Ubuntu container plays for the e2e job. The harness refactor itself was validated locally (suite still passes, unchanged count).

## Acceptance criteria (#68)

- [ ] kcov runs over `tests/run.sh` in CI and reports `rigforge.sh` + `util/proposed-grub.sh` (subprocess runs verified counted — via the `RIGFORGE_HOME` change). *(confirm on first CI run)*
- [x] `coverage` CI job enforces (a) a committed total floor and (b) per-PR patch coverage via `diff-cover --fail-under`.
- [x] Reproducible (kcov digest-pinned, static jq + diff-cover pinned).
- [x] `make coverage` target; coverage docs in the README testing section.
- [ ] Baseline coverage % measured and recorded as the floor. *(after first CI run)*

## Follow-ups for you

- Add the `coverage` job as a **required status check** in branch protection (I can't change repo settings from here).

author: jwrosewell
body:
fix(build): shorten Doxygen titles and noindex generated index pages

Sets FULL_PATH_NAMES = NO so the generated directory and file page titles no
longer embed the full CI build path, and enables HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX = YES so
Doxygen's generated navigation, index and helper pages (dir_*.html, pages.html,
the crawler helper and the graph legend) carry
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow">.

These thin, link-only pages are flagged as low-quality content by search
engines. The change keeps them out of the search index while crawlers still
follow their links to the real documentation. Part of the SEMrush documentation
audit remediation (issues 102, 112, 117).

HTML_INDEX_NOINDEX requires the updated 51Degrees DoxyGen build
(51Degrees/doxygen#7); older builds ignore the tag with a harmless warning.

# Description

`mart_payments.fct_payments_settlements_enghouse` has a large number of duplicated rows. This occurs due to a join with `stg_enghouse__taps` on `payment_reference` in order to add `route_long_name`, `route_short_name`, `agency_id`, and `agency_name`. However, since one `payment_reference` can be associated with multiple taps (in the case of aggregated transactions), this led to duplicate entries in the mart table.

Removing this join and associated fields resolves these duplicates, and makes the table better match the Littlepay `fct_payments_settlements`, at the cost of being a breaking change. However, the removed fields are not used in agency-facing dashboards, and are not well defined since one settlement can be associated with multiple routes. They are also not used in the Littlepay tables.

Resolves #5399 which is blocking other settlements, aggregations issues in #5396 as well as https://github.com/cal-itp/data-analyses/issues/1942 

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation

author: frkak
body:
## Summary

**Task Reference**: [MYMR-228]

Cuts how much data we read from Postgres on the hottest read paths. Before this PR most reads fetched full rows even when the caller used a handful of columns — the task context endpoint fetched the full task three times per request.

**Task context endpoint** (`GET /api/task/[id]/context`)
- The agent/planning/working bundles each fetched the full task and walked the dependency graph independently: 3 full-task reads + 2 traversals per request. They now share one task read and one traversal inside a single RLS transaction; the markdown assembly is split into pure functions fed from that shared data.
- Conditional requests (HEAD / `If-None-Match` → 304) now read only the task's `projectId` instead of the full row.

**MCP context tools** (`mymir_context`)
- Each depth now selects only the task columns its output renders — e.g. `working` skips `implementation_plan` and `execution_record`; no depth reads `history` or `category`. Omitted columns come back as typed `NULL`s, so the row shape and all downstream code are unchanged.

**Access checks**
- The task access gate returned the full task row just to authorize; it now returns the 6 columns callers actually use. The project access row drops `history`/`createdAt`.

**Workspace page loads**
- The home-grid/sidebar project list drops `history`/`categories`/`createdAt`.
- Sidebar projects, user teams, and the project access row are memoized per request (`React.cache`), so the layout and page share one read instead of repeating it.
- Project overview caps task descriptions in SQL at the length the formatter truncates to anyway.

**Task detail UX** (the one visible change)
- Selecting a task renders the header instantly from the already-loaded graph data, with skeletons for the body until the full task arrives. Mutation surfaces that would see placeholder empties (assignee picker, files) stay disabled during that window so they cannot write empty data back.

**Hardening from review**
- A pre-resolved access row is verified against the `projectId` it is used for; a mismatch throws.
- The NULL-cast fragment that reaches `sql.raw` only accepts the literals `"text" | "jsonb"`.
- An invariant test pins that the bundle's single agent-depth fetch covers every column the planning/working assemblers read.
- `eslint .` was permanently red because it scanned the nested git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`, re-flagging documented RLS-exempt files at paths the exemption globs don't match. Worktrees are now excluded, so the RLS lint gate fails loudly again on real violations.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally with `bun run dev`
- [x] Linting passes (`bun run lint`)
- [x] Typecheck passes (`bun run typecheck`)

Full suite: 620 tests pass.

## Notes for reviewer

- **Byte-identity is proven, not claimed.** The golden snapshot tests for all five context depths and the API bundle were run against `main`'s pre-refactor implementation with this branch's snapshots — they pass on both sides. The overview description cap is asserted equal to `compress()` over the full string, including astral characters.
- Query-count tests (spies on the task fetch and the traversal) pin the "one read, one traversal" property of the bundle endpoint, and that the 304 path never touches the full task.
- Apart from the detail-panel skeleton, no behavior change is intended anywhere.

author: tvna
body:
Closes #372 (follow-up to retrospective #371, repair 1 of #370)

## Why

`main`'s `pyproject.toml` was not in `pyproject-fmt` canonical form, yet CI did not run `pyproject-fmt` (the quality gate runs only mypy + ruff + vulture). The hook is configured in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` but is local-only, so it rewrote the entire file on any `pyproject.toml` edit. In #370 a 6-line `addopts` change pulled in ~39/-33 lines of dependency reordering and version-spec normalization, which also made dependency-review flag 3 packages with "unknown license" and required a manual restore-and-amend.

## What

- Normalize `pyproject.toml` via the pinned `pyproject-fmt` pre-commit hook (tox-dev/pyproject-fmt v2.5.1).
- Add a `Check pyproject.toml formatting` step to the `guard-python-code-quality` job that runs the same pinned hook (`uv run pre-commit run pyproject-fmt --all-files`). Using the pre-commit hook keeps a single source of truth for the pinned version and adds no new dependency (`pre-commit` is already a dev dependency).

## Result

The baseline stays canonical, so future minimal edits to `pyproject.toml` produce minimal diffs with no manual restore-and-amend, and dependency-review has nothing spurious to scan.

## Expected one-time dependency-review warning

This PR is itself the normalization, so it changes the dependency version specs (e.g. `1.47.0` -> `1.47`) once. dependency-review therefore re-scans chardet / python-box / streamlit and emits a non-blocking "unknown license" warning (0 vulnerabilities, 0 incompatible licenses). This is the expected one-time cost of normalizing; after merge the baseline is canonical and future PRs will not touch these specs unless intended.

## Verification

- `uv run pre-commit run pyproject-fmt --all-files` passes on the normalized file (idempotent; verified locally).
- The egress needed by the new step is already allowed on `guard-python-code-quality`: `github.com` (EP_GITHUB_CORE) to clone the hook repo, `pypi.org` + `files.pythonhosted.org` (EP_PYTHON) to install pyproject-fmt + tox.
- CI green confirms the step runs in the hardened-runner environment.

author: gumibera
body:
## What this is

cycle-007 builds the path from **prediction** to **observed measurement** — and runs the first experiment on it.

Gygax could already *forecast* where an incentive system breaks (cycle-006's payoff engine). It could not tell whether the forecast was **true** — comparing a forecast to a simulation is "two models agreeing about an abstraction, a hall of mirrors, not a measurement." This cycle closes that gap with an artifact-grounded observation contract, the seam that consumes it, and a real-agent harness that grounds it.

## The headline result

15 real `claude -p` runs (3 awareness rungs × 5 trials) against a genuinely reward-hackable task. The payoff engine **forecast** `delete-test` (a reward hack) as the dominant strategy. The agent **fixed the code honestly at every rung — including the adversarial one that explicitly told it to game the metric by any means.** fix:hack = 1.00 everywhere, no cliff, zero hacks.

This is reported as a **first-class finding, not a failure** (K5): the model's training dominated the stated incentive. Findings report: `grimoires/gygax/playtest-reports/awareness-ladder-2026-06-09.md`.

A sharp moment: at the adversarial rung some agents *couldn't run the test themselves* (acceptEdits blocked execution) and said so — but the scorer re-ran the test itself and confirmed the fix. Artifact-grounding earned its keep: the agent's self-report was unreliable; the diff + re-run were ground truth.

## What's in here

| Component | What |
|---|---|
| `schemas/observed-trace.v1.schema.json` | The FR-1 contract — JSON Schema 2020-12, versioned, additive-only; producer-bound claim strength, status↔observation coupling. The cross-repo artifact Arneson builds to. |
| `scripts/lib/trace/` | The durable ingest seam: fail-fast validation → predicted-vs-observed diff (vs live payoff argmax) → cliff (`firstCrossing` reuse) → severity diagnostic → claim-tagged report. Coupled to the harness **only** through the schema. |
| `scripts/lib/ladder/` | The harness: isolated run dirs (no-clobber + containment), artifact-grounded scorer (re-runs the test; never reads narration to classify), real-agent runner (shell-free spawn, timeout, never-throw-per-trial). `run`/`score` CLI with `--dry-run`. |
| `evals/awareness-ladder/` | Self-contained fixture: `merge_intervals` (2 real bugs), 3 rung prompts, 4 canned scorer fixtures. |

## Capability (K1–K5) — validated end-to-end

- **K1** sidecar ingest → per-run classification (fixed/hacked/failed) from diffs + the scorer's own re-run
- **K2** predicted-vs-observed diff against the payoff argmax forecast
- **K3** fix:hack ratio per rung + cliff detection
- **K4** severity diagnostic (structural-urgent / reward-aware-basin / capability-edge / no-hack-finding)
- **K5** claim-strength tag on every output; no-hack reported as a finding

## Safety / scope

- **Zero edits** to `scripts/lib/payoff/`, `scripts/lib/parametric/`, `evals/incentive-fixtures/agent-reward-hack/`, `evals/harness.sh` (read-only reuse only).
- Spawn path is **shell-free** (argv-array, no `shell: true`), `cwd` = isolated run dir, containment-asserted before every write/spawn; `batch.json` stores the command template, never the environment.
- Accepted residual (OQ-4): the agent runs unsandboxed locally; the `--agent-cmd` seam is the documented slot-in for a container wrapper.
- `npm test` green (781 structural + new `test:trace` / `test:ladder` suites); strict typecheck clean; generated `runs/` gitignored.

## Notes for reviewers

- The Loa state artifacts (PRD/SDD/sprint/review reports) live under `grimoires/loa/`, which is gitignored by repo policy — this PR is the construct deliverable itself.
- `grimoires/gygax/designs/arneson-contract-alignment.md` records Gygax's position on the companion construct's proposed sidecar vocabulary (origin tags, seq/id shape).
- Reviewed + security-audited per sprint (24/25/26), each approved with non-blocking concerns documented.

ENV (zbb):
- Single effective-env resolver (lib/env/effective.ts) shared by `env list/get` and command dispatch, so what you see is exactly what a command receives.
- Hermetic dispatch: a command's env = SYSTEM_BASE + repo shell_passthrough + the resolved zbb-declared env; undeclared shell vars (stale stack values, sourced tokens) are stripped. Slot-load leaves the interactive shell intact.
- Lock-down: resolve() prunes manifest vars not declared in zbb.yaml (env:/imports:); framework/inherited/imported/dns excepted. `env set` refuses undeclared keys. The whole env must be declared.

- Resolve cwd->stack by exact identity (full scoped name), not bare short name, so org/util no longer binds to a com/util 'util' stack. Mirrored in hook.sh.
- stack add is collision-aware: a short name taken by a different identity auto-qualifies with scope (org-util) instead of erroring.
- Shell hook reconciles removed vars (tracks all exported keys).

- SourceHasher folds package.json `files` into the gate hash (git ls-files, tracked-only) so content index.yml/specs re-gate; no-op for gitignored dist.

author: toddbryson1
body:
## The bug
`proxy.ts` gates `/matches/:path*` on the **Stytch session cookie** only. But anonymous drivers never get one — they carry `cdla_driver_id` (set by `/api/intake`). So an anonymous driver finishes the homepage Debbie chat, gets `router.push('/matches/[id]')`, and **lands on a `/login` wall** — even though the `/matches` page renders fine for them via the anonymous-cookie path.

This is the **default, highest-traffic flow** (homepage Debbie chat → anonymous intake).

## Root cause (regression, not original design)
- `9cd5eed` added the middleware when *every* driver was email-authed.
- Anonymous intake came later (migration 0024 / `fea359d`) and relaxed the **page** to accept `cdla_driver_id` — but `proxy.ts` was never updated (`git log` confirms it's untouched since `9cd5eed`).

## Proof (live)
- `cdla_driver_id` only → **307 → /login**
- `stytch_session_token` + `cdla_driver_id` → **200, full page**

## The fix
Accept `cdla_driver_id` as a second optimistic signal in the middleware. Safe because the middleware is explicitly optimistic — the **page** still does the real validation (cookie must equal the URL `driverId`, or the Stytch session email must match the driver), so a forged cookie exposes nothing.

`+ src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts` pins all three cases (no cookie → login, stytch → through, anon → through) plus the `?redirect=` preservation.

body:
This PR implements a series of micro-UX and accessibility improvements across the dashboard to ensure it is usable by everyone, including keyboard and screen reader users.

### 💡 What
- **Semantic HTML**: Converted the `Toggle` component from a non-interactive `div` to a proper `button`.
- **ARIA Roles & States**: Added `role="switch"` and `aria-checked` to the Toggle component to correctly communicate its state to assistive technologies.
- **Accessible Labels**: Added descriptive `aria-label` attributes to the Toggle component, the "Remove pick" button (×), and the `StatusDot` indicator.
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Implemented global `:focus-visible` styles in `globals.css` using the brand's accent green to provide clear, accessible focus indicators.
- **Robust Interaction**: Added `e.stopPropagation()` to toggles to prevent unintended event bubbling.

### 🎯 Why
- Non-semantic interactive elements are invisible to screen readers and difficult to navigate via keyboard.
- Lack of focus indicators makes it nearly impossible for keyboard-only users to know which element they are interacting with.
- Icon-only buttons without labels provide no context for assistive technology.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Full keyboard navigability with visible focus states.
- Screen reader support for switches and status indicators.
- Semantic interaction patterns for toggles.

body:
## Summary
- Adds `--cpsl <library>` as an alternative Herm backend that loads a CPSL dynamic library instead of starting the container backend.
- Starts an internal CPSL worker process, validates CPSL ABI/metadata, mounts the current workspace at `/workdir`, and forwards repeatable `--allow-domain` / `--deny-domain` network policy flags.
- Routes Herm sandbox execution through CPSL, including native Luau execution through `local_sandbox_exec`, Bash compatibility through `/shell --bash`, and backend-aware sub-agent tool setup.
- Splits prompt/template handling into common, container, and CPSL profiles so container and CPSL modes remain isolated and independently editable.
- Adds a Herm-owned `scripts/build-cpsl-image.sh` flow that fetches/builds CPSL as a dependency and produces `.herm-cpsl/artifacts/<platform>/{herm,libcpsl.*,include/cpsl.h}`, with minimal/all profiles and PDFium staging/probes for `--all`.
- Adds tests for CLI parsing, CPSL worker protocol, dynamic library validation, network policy forwarding, sandbox tools, prompts, status labels, and build-script behavior.

## Dependency / Coordination

Semantic dependency:
- Herm is the consumer of CPSL. This PR depends on CPSL PR https://github.com/fundamental-research-labs/cpsl/pull/17, or an equivalent merged CPSL commit that provides the `cpsl-ffi` ABI v1 and compatible session/eval behavior.
- CPSL does not depend on Herm at runtime. Any `herm` submodule pointer in the CPSL PR is integration/demo bookkeeping only.

Merge/ref coordination:
- Until CPSL PR #17 lands, `scripts/build-cpsl-image.sh` intentionally defaults to `CPSL_REF=aduermael/lib-build` so this integration remains testable.
- After CPSL PR #17 lands, update this PR's script/docs to point at the merged CPSL ref (`main`, a merge commit, or a tag) before merging or releasing this Herm integration.
- If this Herm branch is squash/rebase-merged while CPSL PR #17 keeps a `herm` submodule pointer, update/remove that pointer in CPSL so it does not reference a stale pre-merge commit.

Core half of **Story 9** (#102) — removes the legacy numeric `event_level`, now fully superseded by `process_type`.

## What changed
- **Dispatch** routes on `event.process_type` instead of `event.event_level` (`HandlerRegistry`). `levels: :all` still matches every event; an explicit list now matches by process_type.
- **EventDefinition** — removed the `event_level` DSL macro.
- **Schema** — removed the `:event_level` struct member, the `to_ruby` serialization, the builder kwarg, the PR #92 range validation (`validate_event_level`), and the legacy backfill (`process_type ||= from_event_level(...)`).
- **Event** — removed the `:event_level` struct member; the emitter no longer sets it.
- **ProcessType** — removed the `from_event_level` / `LEGACY_EVENT_LEVELS` transitional shim.
- Updated/removed the tests that asserted `event_level` behavior (the `process_type` equivalents already cover the intent).

Net: 13 files, −131/+12. CI (`bundle exec rake test`) green; 90 runs, 0 failures.

## ⚠️ Release coordination — pair with the delivery half
The delivery gem still references `ProcessType.from_event_level(event.event_level)` as a fallback in `Delivery::Handler#call` and `OutboxRouter`. Core's own suite doesn't load delivery, so this PR is green — but it **must not be released ahead of the delivery half of #102** (which drops those fallbacks), or a consuming app on new-core + old-delivery breaks when `process_type` is nil.

author: chrissoncpa
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 PR 1 of 8 in the BlackLine arc. **Schema-only** change — no Server Actions, no UI, no behavioral impact on the existing GL. Subsequent PRs build the workflow on top of this foundation.

Design doc: [`docs/blackline-arc-design.md`](../blob/blackline-arc-design/docs/blackline-arc-design.md) (PR #204)

## What this adds

### Tables (3)

- **`reconciliation`** — one row per (entity, book, period, account). Composite-unique scope tuple lets the auto-instantiator (PR 6) run idempotently. Frozen `glBalance` + `supportingBalance` snapshots so the reviewer sees what the preparer signed against even if a JE backs into the period afterward. Per-row `requiresReview` Boolean stores Decision #2 — single sign-off OR preparer→reviewer chain — frozen at create time.

- **`reconciliation_attachment`** — supporting docs as encrypted bytes in DB (no S3 vendor dependency). Schema today is plain BYTEA; encryption wiring lands in PR 4 alongside the upload UI.

- **`reconciliation_config`** — per-tenant default sign-off shape (`defaultRequiresReview`) and default tolerance. Cascade resolution: Account override → tenant default → BlackLine standard (`true`, `0`).

### Enum

- **`ReconStatus`**: `OPEN | IN_PROGRESS | PREPARED | RECONCILED | EXCEPTION | WAIVED`

### New columns on `Account`

- `requiresReconReview Boolean?` — `null` = inherit tenant default
- `reconTolerance Decimal(20, 4)?` — `null` = inherit tenant default

### New backrefs

| Model | Added |
|---|---|
| `Tenant` | `reconciliations`, `reconciliationAttachments`, `reconciliationConfig` |
| `LegalEntity` / `Book` / `Period` / `Account` | `reconciliations` |
| `User` | `reconciliationsPrepared` (named `ReconPreparer`), `reconciliationsReviewed` (named `ReconReviewer`), `reconciliationAttachments` |

## Verified locally

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx prisma validate` | `schema is valid 🚀` |
| `npx prisma generate` | client regenerates cleanly |
| Migration SQL applied via `psql` in a transient schema | 3 tables created, `ReconStatus` enum created, idempotent re-run OK |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | zero output (no downstream type breakage) |

## Risk + rollback

- **Risk: NONE on runtime.** Pure schema addition; no existing query path touches the new tables. Account.requiresReconReview / reconTolerance default to NULL which the eventual Server Action treats as "inherit," so existing accounts behave identically until a recon row is created against them in PR 2+.
- **Rollback**: `git revert` this commit + `DROP TABLE reconciliation_config, reconciliation_attachment, reconciliation` + `DROP TYPE "ReconStatus"` + `ALTER TABLE account DROP COLUMN requiresReconReview, DROP COLUMN reconTolerance`. Idempotent — safe to re-run.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx prisma validate` passes
- [ ] `npx prisma db push --skip-generate` against a fresh DB applies the migration cleanly
- [ ] CI run on this branch reaches green (this PR adds no application code; existing tests should be unaffected)

## Notes for reviewers

- Two of the lock-in decisions from the design doc materialize here: per-recon frozen `requiresReview` (not a runtime lookup) and per-recon frozen `tolerance` (not a runtime lookup). The "frozen at create time" rationale: changing the tenant default later mustn't retroactively flip already-signed recons in or out of EXCEPTION status.
- `RecordEvent` integration is intentionally soft-referenced (recordType="Reconciliation" + recordId). No Prisma relation. Mirrors how ownership, JE notes, and reassignment already use RecordEvent.
- Migration uses `IF NOT EXISTS` everywhere it can, and wraps the `CREATE TYPE "ReconStatus"` in a `DO $$ ... END $$` block (Postgres has no `CREATE TYPE IF NOT EXISTS`). Re-running the migration is a no-op.

## Next

**PR 2/22**: Server Actions for `openReconciliation` / `markPrepared` / `approveRecon` / `sendBackToPreparer` / `markException` / `waiveRecon`. Audit-logged via `auditPrivilegedAction`. Cross-tenant rejection tested.

body:
## What this PR does

Executes phases 0–2 of the agreed modernization plan (see `docs/modernization/PLAN.md`, ADRs 0001–0003). The app stays on Meteor 2.7 and keeps its Bootstrap-3 look — by design: consolidation first, framework/visual jumps as separate, individually validated steps.

### Phase 0 — Characterization suite (the oracle)
- **17 Playwright specs** in `e2e/` covering login, registration wizard + applicant acceptance, the full assignment lifecycle (create → apply → accept → close with **"Zusage" email asserted via Mailpit**), cancel/re-enable with emails, notifications, profile, password reset via token mail, admin pages, detail view.
- Written **against the unchanged legacy app first**, then kept green after every single migration step.
- Cypress removed (its 2 specs ported); CI now runs Playwright with a Mailpit service.

### Phase 1 — React 15.7 → 18.3, TypeScript 2.3 → 5.9
- Last mixin user rewritten to `useTracker`; react-meteor-data 0.2 → 2.5.
- react-addons-*, react-mixin, smart-mixin, unused react-bootstrap removed.

### Phase 2 — Blaze → React, every page template
Dashboard, notifications dropdown, login (+forgot modal), reset password, profile, registration wizard, user/group admin, group members/applicants, **assignment form** (react-datepicker replaces jQuery datetimepicker), **assignment manager**, detail view, overview (lazy week accordion), copy-assignments.
- New generic `DataTable` replaces aldeed:tabular (DataTables) — same DOM classes, client-side search/sort/pagination.
- select2 → react-select; SimpleSchema/collection2 remains the single validation path (ADR 0003).
- **9 atmosphere packages removed** (autoform, tabular, select2×3, jquery-ui, reactive-modal, reactivearray, bootstrap-3-modal) plus the jQuery datepicker stack and all dead Blaze glue.

### Deliberately NOT in this PR (scoped in `docs/modernization/MIGRATION_LOG.md`)
- **Meteor 3** — requires async migration of the isomorphic domain layer + simpl-schema port; do the router swap first.
- **react-router / layouts** — MainLayout/Sidebar/ParallaxScreen stay Blaze shells until then.
- **Bootstrap 3 → 5** — one atomic class sweep on the consolidated React codebase.

### Validation
- `tsc` clean, **101 unit tests green**, **Playwright suite 17/17 green** (multiple consecutive runs) after every step; one commit per migrated template.
- Characterization findings about pre-existing legacy quirks are documented in the log (e.g. cold-load of `/manage-assignments` renders blank, dead `emailserver` route, blueprint page is a "Not implemented" stub).

author: alexm-picard
body:
## What
Completes the pitch INTAKE path (#25 wired pitch serving, not intake) and fixes a feature bug both trained models consumed.

- **Change 1 - load gate** (`ModelLoadValidator` + test): the promotion load gate gains a pitch arm - snapshot `head=pre|post` -> `loadPitchPre`/`loadPitchPost` with an in-distribution dummy. Before, a pitch model had no `park_order`, fell into the batted-ball branch, and 422'd at CANDIDATE->SHADOW. Test: real ORT load of the committed pitch fixture (pre passes; corrupt ONNX -> ModelLoadFailed). POST is the symmetric sibling; no committed 41-feature fixture exists to exercise it end-to-end.
- **Change 2 - `export_lr_onnx.py`** (new): the pitch LR baseline's missing ONNX export - skl2onnx, the full `Imputer+Scaler+LogisticRegression` pipeline baked into the graph (Java sends NaN; the Imputer op handles it), opset 15, NaN-row parity-checked.
- **Change 3 - parity probes**: `export_{pre,post}_onnx` gain a raw booster-vs-ORT value-parity check on real rows (atol 1e-4); a diff over tolerance is a finding to investigate, not loosen.
- **Change 4 - `register_pitch` + `register_gate`**: `register_pitch` now assembles and gates the LR baseline FIRST (rule 9; was a hardcoded `baseline_registered=True`) and grows the real `--from-artifacts` box path. Running the dry-run CLI surfaced that `register_gate` compared the contract `model_name` to the head, which the LR baseline (sharing the pre contract) legitimately differs from - fixed to compare against the head's canonical contract (still rejects a wrong contract).
- **Change 5 - `compute_tier3.sql`** epoch guard + test: `lagInFrame` over a non-Nullable Date returns `1970-01-01` (not NULL) for a first appearance, so the `IS NULL` guard never fired and `days_since_last_appearance` carried ~20,000-day garbage on ~4.5% of rows. Both trained models consumed it. Guarded with `OR = toDate(0)`. A static test pins the guard; a CH-gated test enforces the features rebuild.

## Verification
backend compile + spotless clean; ruff clean; `register_pitch --heads both` gates LR+pre+post; 42 pitch tests + the dsla static guard pass. pyright + the @SpringBootTest load-gate test + the CH-gated/parity probes run in CI / on the box.

## Box follow-on (not in this PR)
features rebuild (test_year-2 TE window) + PRE/LR retrain on clean dsla -> `export_lr_onnx` -> `register_pitch --from-artifacts` -> register LR+PRE SHADOW. Brier/ECE shift slightly after the clean-feature retrain.

author: akbisw
body:
## Summary
Fix the OAuth callback handler so the authorization code (and implicit-flow tokens) never linger in the address bar or browser session history: use `history.replaceState` instead of `pushState`, and scrub the URL on every error exit, not just on success.

## Finding
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Certain.

- `client/hosted-oauth.ts:316-317` (pre-fix) — post-exchange cleanup used `history.pushState(null, "", fullRedirectUrl)`, which *adds* a history entry: the URL carrying `?code=...&state=...` (or `#access_token=...` in implicit flow) remained one step back in session history, reachable via the Back button and persisted in browser history.
- No error path cleaned the URL at all: state mismatch (`client/hosted-oauth.ts:~223`), missing code (`~245`), and token-exchange failures (`~391`/`~428`, thrown before the cleanup line was reached) all left the OAuth params in the address bar.

**Concrete failure scenario:** a transient network failure at the token endpoint leaves a still-unconsumed, still-valid authorization code sitting in the address bar, where anyone with access to the browser (or its history) can replay it.

## Fix
- New `cleanupCallbackUrl()` helper in `client/hosted-oauth.ts` strips OAuth params (`code`, `state`, `error`, `error_description` from the query; `access_token`, `id_token`, `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `expires_in`, `state`, `error`, `error_description` from the fragment) via `history.replaceState`, preserving unrelated query params and hash content. Cleanup is best-effort and never masks the original error.
- Invoked on the success path (replacing the old `pushState` call) and on all error exits: provider `error` param, state mismatch, missing authorization code, any token-exchange failure (network error, non-OK response, JSON parse failure — via a try/catch around `exchangeCodeForTokens`), and implicit-flow missing/invalid access token.
- `client/config.ts`: `MinimalHistory` gains an optional `replaceState` member (backwards compatible); the helper falls back to `pushState` if a custom history implementation lacks it.

## Test plan
- `npx tsc --project client/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx eslint client/hosted-oauth.ts client/config.ts client/__tests__/hosted-oauth.test.ts` — clean.
- `npx jest client/__tests__/hosted-oauth.test.ts` — 15/15 pass (7 pre-existing + 8 new), plus `react-oauth-simple.test.tsx` still passes.
- New regression tests assert: success path uses `replaceState` (and not `pushState`); unrelated query params survive the scrub; `code`/`state` are scrubbed on state mismatch, missing code, token-exchange HTTP failure, and token-exchange network error; implicit-flow hash tokens are scrubbed; `pushState` fallback works when `replaceState` is absent.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches OAuth redirect handling and session history, which is security-sensitive, but the change is narrowly scoped URL cleanup with backwards-compatible history API fallback and broad test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens the Cognito OAuth redirect callback so **authorization codes and implicit-flow tokens are removed from the address bar and session history** on every exit path, not only after a successful sign-in.
> 
> Post-callback cleanup now goes through a new **`cleanupCallbackUrl()`** helper that strips OAuth query/hash parameters and updates the URL with **`history.replaceState`** (instead of **`pushState`**, which left sensitive URLs one Back-navigation away). The same scrub runs on **errors**: provider `error` params, state mismatch, lock timeouts, missing code, token-exchange failures, and implicit-flow token handling failures. Unrelated query params are kept; cleanup is best-effort and does not swallow the original error.

author: josiahfalde
body:
Fixes **JF-21**. Reported while dogfooding a real Fidelity export — three defects in `parseFidelityCsv` were skewing the whole dashboard.

## The bugs
1. **No expiry/strike** — the option symbol (` -SOFI260702P15.5` = ticker + YYMMDD + P/C + strike) was never decoded → blank expiry in Trades, empty DTE in the Radar.
2. **Statuses never resolved** — every sold contract was hard-coded `Open`; the `EXPIRED` / `ASSIGNED` / `BOUGHT CLOSING` rows were ignored. So win rate sat at 0 and every historical contract still counted as open collateral.
3. **$1 capital base** — the importer never set one → `compute.ts`'s `|| 1` divide-by-zero guard rendered "$1" capital, exploding every yield/return %.

## The fix
Rewrote `parseFidelityCsv` to:
- Decode the option symbol (with a description fallback) for **ticker + expiry + strike**.
- **Reconcile** the four transaction kinds per contract chronologically: `sell-open` → credit (`Open`); `bought-close` → `Closed` + a `BB` debit; `expired` → `Expired`; put `assigned` → `Assigned` + an `AAssignSTK` debit (`invested = strike × 100`); call `assigned` → `Assigned` (shares called away).
- Return a **suggested capital base = peak concurrent CSP collateral**, which `ImportData` seeds only when none is set yet (announced in the import toast, user-adjustable on the Data page).

`compute.ts` — the validated-to-the-penny engine — is **untouched**.

## Verification
Ran the new parser against the real 53-row export (throwaway script, not committed):
- 48 trades; statuses **21 Closed / 2 Expired / 1 Assigned / 2 Open**
- **0** credits missing expiry/strike
- capital base **$3,200**; the SOFI $24.5 put assignment → invested **$2,450**
- `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit + vite build) clean (pre-existing bundle warning only)

## Noted, out of scope
Fidelity exports contain **no earnings dates** — there's no earnings column in the file at all. Earnings risk stays a separate feature that needs an external earnings calendar; flagging rather than faking it.

author: rgcottrell
body:
Follow-up to a full review of all 176 compute shaders. Four classes of change:

## 1. Dead-shader purge (103 compute shaders + 2 includes)
Cross-referenced every generated `shaders::<CONST>_SPV` against `src/`: these were compiled by build.rs but never dispatched — whole `dequant_*` family (weights are consumed by fused kernels), the never-wired MMQ path (`quantize_q8_1`, `mul_mat_vecq`, `mul_mmq`), NV-only coopmat2 kernels (`flash_attn_cm2`, `mul_mm_cm2` — RADV has no `VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2`), `flash_attn_mask_opt`, `soft_max_large*`, mamba `ssm_scan`, RWKV `wkv6/7`, the GPU vision conv stack superseded by host im2col+GEMM, training/backward ops, and ~40 unused elementwise ops. Also dropped the never-dispatched `set_rows_*`/`q1_0` variants + SET_ROWS path inside `copy_to_quant.slang`.
Cuts the slangc fan-out by more than half (176 → 73 files). Note: final binary size is unchanged — unused `include_bytes!` consts were already DCE'd by rustc; the win is build time + tree size. Everything is one `git revert` away if a future model family needs an op back.

## 2. Wave-cooperative reductions (`reduce_funcs.slang`)
`rms_norm` (512 threads / 9 barrier rounds), `rms_norm_rope_multi` (256/8), `ssm_norm_gate`, `norm`, `l2_norm`, `sum_rows`, `soft_max` now reduce via per-wave `WaveActiveSum/Max` + one cross-wave fold (≤2 barriers). `flash_attn_split_k_reduce` (one wave) drops shared memory entirely. All dispatch sites pin `required_subgroup_size(32)`. `ssm_norm_gate` also keeps its input in a register instead of re-reading global memory after the reduce.

## 3. Flash-attention KV-walk bounds
- **SWA lower bound** (scalar + cm1): gemma4 sliding layers previously walked the *full* KV range and masked per element; the walk now starts at the first in-window block (same `qpos` formula as the analytic mask, so bound and mask agree by construction). Cost on sliding layers becomes O(window) instead of O(kv_len).
- **Causal upper bound**: with `MASK_ENABLE` the host mask is the within-chunk causal triangle (`write_causal_mask` contract), so fully-masked trailing blocks are skipped — per-row `eff_kv` clamp in scalar legacy prefill, per-16-row-tile clamp in cm1.
- Split-K is unaffected: out-of-range splits produce `(Lf=0, Mf=-1e30)` and the combine weights them to ~0, same as the existing past-the-end behavior.

## 4. Online softmax in the log2 domain
Q is pre-scaled by `scale·log2(e)` (mask scaled by `log2(e)` on add — exact for 0/-inf masks), so every `exp()` in scalar FA, cm1, and the split-K combine becomes `exp2()`, dropping the per-element ex2 input multiply. The split-K `(L, M)` partials are log2-domain; all three kernels changed together.

Plus: Q4_K/Q5_K 6-bit scale-min unpack deduplicated into a `types.slang` helper (used by both `get_rows_q4_k/q5_k`).

## Validation (Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S, RADV)
- `scripts/check.sh` green; 158 unit tests pass.
- Greedy token-identity vs main tip (f3be70b), same prompts:
  - Llama-3.2-1B Q5_K_M, 48 tok — **identical**
  - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_XL, 64 tok — **identical** (decode 61.2 → 61.4 tok/s)
  - gemma-4-12B Q4_K_XL, 5231-token prefill + 32 decode — **identical**; prefill **207 → 214 tok/s (+3.5%)** from the SWA/causal bounds; decode neutral at this depth (FA is a small slice of 12B dense decode at 5K ctx; the bound's decode win grows with context)
  - gemma-4-12B `--image --chat` (vision encode → decode) — **identical**
- Token-identity held despite the deliberate low-bit numeric changes (exp2 rounding, reduction order); outputs are not guaranteed bit-equal in general, but greedy decoding matched on every path tested.

Not included (bench-gated follow-ups from the review): GDN multi-column q/k/g staging, larger mul_mm_cm tiles, moe_down reduction hoisting, host-side split-K sizing over the SWA window.

author: nalutripician
body:
## Description

While running the fault injection test suite against a live multi-region account, three metadata response-delay tests were consistently failing. Investigation showed this is a **test-design issue, not a fault injection library bug** — the library injects the delay correctly every time (the rule hit count increments), but the test assertions were based on an invalid assumption.

### Root cause

The tests asserted that an injected metadata-refresh delay (e.g. 15s) would manifest as added wall-clock latency on a subsequent data operation:

```csharp
Assert.IsTrue(elapsed.TotalSeconds >= 15);
```

Operation diagnostics show what actually happens: the injected delay causes the metadata HTTP call to hit its **request timeout** (`TaskCanceledException`), after which the SDK **transparently retries** the metadata request and succeeds:

```
"Read Collection": DurationInMs:1034, ExceptionType:"TaskCanceledException"   ← injected delay hit the request timeout
                   DurationInMs:212,  StatusCode:"OK"                         ← SDK retried and succeeded
```

So the full delay is never observed end-to-end, and the operation completes in ~1–4s regardless of the injected delay or account topology. (In `PKRangeResponseDelayTest`, the rule was even hit 3× while the operation finished in 3.7s.) This is correct SDK behavior — metadata refreshes are resilient to slow responses — so the wall-clock assertion can never hold.

### Changes

- **`FaultInjectionMetadataTests`** — `AddressRefreshResponseDelayTest`, `PKRangeResponseDelayTest`, and `CollectionReadResponseDelayTest`: replaced the brittle elapsed-time assertions with deterministic validation that the delay rule was applied (`ValidateRuleHit`) **and** the operation still succeeds despite the injected delay (`StatusCode == Created`).
- **`FaultInjectionDirectModeTests.Cleanup`** — made `client`/`fiClient` disposal null-safe (`?.`), matching the other test classes. Previously, a test that failed before the fault-injection client was created threw a masking `NullReferenceException` during cleanup.

### Verification

All 37 builder/unit/metadata tests pass (32 builder/unit + 5 metadata). The fixed tests run in 1–4s and validate the injected rule deterministically.

> Note: the remaining `FaultInjectionDirectModeTests` failures observed locally are account-topology dependent (several tests document "must be a single master account" / hardcode replica & region counts, one is statistically flaky by design, and the custom-status mapping case is core-SDK behavior). They were intentionally left unchanged so they continue to validate correctly against the intended CI account.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (test reliability; no shipped-package source changed)

## Changelog

No changelog entry required — changes are test-only (`Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos/FaultInjection/tests/**`); no shipped-package source under `src/**` is modified, and there is no customer-observable impact.

author: ddol
body:
## Problem

On the dashboard, the **Vehicle Count** card showed a non-zero count while the timeseries **chart** below it was empty between roughly 5pm and midnight in timezones behind UTC (e.g. PST/PDT). The date picker also offered no way to reach "tomorrow".

## Root cause

The card and the chart asked the backend for the *same* picker selection using *different* date semantics — the card sent raw unix timestamps from the browser's `Date`, the chart sent `YYYY-MM-DD` that the server re-interpreted as a calendar day in a (usually `UTC`) timezone. When the local date and the UTC date diverged, the two endpoints queried different windows.

## Fix: one date format — ISO 8601

The query endpoints (`/api/radar_stats` and `/api/charts/{timeseries,histogram,comparison}`) now take a single contract: **`start`/`end` (and `compare_start`/`compare_end`) as ISO 8601 / RFC3339 instants** (e.g. `2026-06-09T00:00:00-07:00`).

- The instant fully specifies the window, so the server does **no** calendar-day interpretation — card and chart always resolve the identical range. The original bug cannot recur.
- **`tz` is now display-only** (chart axis labels, `radar_stats` response formatting); it no longer decides which rows match.
- The frontend builds those instants from the picked day **in the selected display timezone** via `isoStartOfDay`/`isoEndOfDay` (DST-correct `Intl` offset math), so the timezone dropdown shifts the queried window. Default range ends at **tomorrow-local** so today's data (stored against the next UTC day) is always in range; `displayTimezone` falls back to the browser zone when the server default is `UTC`.
- **Report generation keeps `YYYY-MM-DD`** (the ISO 8601 *date* profile) — those values are stored on the report row, printed in the PDF, and embedded in the report **filename**, where a colon-bearing instant can't live.

Storage is unchanged: the DB holds **UTC unix epoch seconds** throughout. The new [dates and timezones design doc](docs/radar/architecture/dates-and-timezones.md) is the canonical reference for the DB, the API, and the frontend.

## Changes

- **Backend** (`[ai][go]`): `parseInstant` + ISO `parseDateRange`; `tz` resolved separately for display; comparison window parses instants; report path keeps `parseLocalDateRange`.
- **Frontend** (`[ai][js]`): `isoStartOfDay`/`isoEndOfDay`; dashboard + reports-page chart previews send instants in the display tz; report generation keeps `isoDate`; browser-zone fallback; tomorrow-local default.
- **Docs** (`[ai][docs]`): canonical date-design doc; ARCHITECTURE.md + DEBUGGING.md updated.

## Testing & coverage

- `make test-go`, `make test-web` (752), `make lint-go`, `make lint-web`, `make build-web`, `make build-radar-local` all pass.
- New/expanded tests for the date logic plus the touched files' surrounding code:
  - **TS**: `dateUtils.ts`, `timezone.ts`, `api.ts` at **100% statements/functions/lines** (PDT/UTC/Auckland/DST cases, timezone fallbacks, ISO contract, Tailscale client).
  - **Go**: `server_radar.go` **99.1%**, `server_charts.go` **93.4%**, `server_reports_generate.go` **82.9%**.
- Residual uncovered Go branches are **dead code** (the three chart renderers never return an error; `ConvertTime` never fails on a valid tz) or **fault-injection-only** (second-query DB failures, PDF-pipeline/filesystem errors). Reaching literal 100% would require a chart-render API change and a DB interface for fault injection — out of scope for this PR; flagged as a follow-up.

author: emrahbaysal
body:
## Problem
On live hw124 the bootstrap-kit Kustomization was stuck `READY=Unknown` ("Reconciliation in progress"), health-waiting on a single wedged HR:

```
flux-system/bp-network-policies :: 1.0.3 :: HelmChart ... chart pull error:
failed to download chart ... 'oci://ghcr.io/openova-io/bp-network-policies:1.0.3':
failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: ... 401 Unauthorized
```

Root cause: slot-26's `bp-network-policies` HelmRepository (`type: oci`) was **missing `secretRef: {name: ghcr-pull}`** — the auth secret every other `bp-*` HelmRepository carries (slots 13/16a/16b). `bp-network-policies` is a **private** ghcr package, so Flux fell back to anonymous auth, hitting `401`. The chart never resolved.

Because the Kustomization runs `wait: true`, its health-check wedged on this one HR and **never advanced to newer git revisions** — preventing the catalog-seed `bp-postgres` CR (#3199) and any other downstream change from reconciling.

This also wedges every fresh prov: slot-26 lives in the cluster scaffold, so a new Sovereign fails on `bp-network-policies` identically.

## Fix
Add `secretRef: {name: ghcr-pull}` to the `bp-network-policies` HelmRepository — byte-for-byte the pattern on slots 13 (`bp-catalyst-platform`) and 16b (`bp-cnpg-pair`).

## Verify
- [ ] Live hw124: `kubectl -n flux-system get helmrepository bp-network-policies -o jsonpath='{.spec.secretRef.name}'` returns `ghcr-pull`
- [ ] `kubectl get hr -n flux-system bp-network-policies` reaches Ready=True (chart pulls)
- [ ] bootstrap-kit Kustomization advances past the health-wait, applies the bp-postgres catalog-seed, and `GET /api/v1/catalog/bp-postgres` returns 200

Refs #3188.

body:
## Summary

Two commits land the first production-ready version of the `SlackChannel`:

- **`65a037d`** — initial Slack channel via Socket Mode (text only)
- **`12f0d5e`** — download inbound file attachments and reply in thread
- **`369b055`** — isolate Elia test bot on Slack only (comment out Wasender, use only OpenRouter for vision)

## Why

The Slack adapter needed to match the conventions already established by `TelegramChannel`: download media on inbound messages, expose it to the mindset as `IChatMessage.images` / `IChatMessage.documents`, and route every reply into the originating thread to keep shared channels tidy.

## What changed

### `src/addon/chat-controller/slack/SlackChannel.ts`

- New private `downloadFile(file, logger)` helper that uses `fetch` with the `botToken` (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) to pull files in parallel via `Promise.all`. 20 MB hard cap per file; failures are logged and the rest of the message is preserved.
- New private `extractMedia(message, logger)` that partitions by MIME prefix: `image/*` → `images`, rest → `documents`. Matches `TelegramChannel`'s heuristic.
- New private `buildChatConnection(message)` and `buildReply(say, threadTs)` extracted from `handleMessage` to keep the flow linear.
- `threadTs = message.thread_ts ?? message.ts` is now propagated to every `say(...)` so top-level messages spawn a one-message thread and replies stay in the existing thread.

### `src/addon/chat-controller/slack/SlackChannel.unit.test.ts`

- 11 new tests (`T1`-T`11`) covering: PNG download, PDF download, ignored subtypes, image-as-document routing, `fetch` 500, 20 MB cap, missing `url_private`, thread preservation, top-level auto-threading, caption + image, multi-image order.
- Reuses the `globalThis.fetch` stub pattern from `TelegramChannel.unit.test.ts`.

### `test/elia/EliaChatController.ts`

- `@wasender()` handler and its imports are commented out so the Slack-only test bot boots without `WASENDER_*` env vars.
- `@cmd()` retypes its context as `ISlackReceivedMessage`.

### `test/elia/EliaMindset.ts`

- `models()` switched to OpenRouter only: `qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23` for text, `google/gemini-2.5-flash` for vision. The previous vision model (`qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23` upstream Alibaba) rejected every image with `InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter`, and `gemini-2.0-flash-exp` returns 404 on OpenRouter.

### `AGENTS.md`

- New **Slack Channel Notes** subsection under `Adding a New Chat Channel` covering: Socket Mode, required scopes, event subscriptions, file attachment behavior, threading, and the known limitation that the bot cannot send files yet (planned as `feat-slack-uploads`).

## Validation

- `npm run test:units` → 322 tests, 0 failures.
- `npm run types:check` → clean.
- `npx prettier --check` on modified files → clean.
- Real Slack test (workspace `wabot-dev`, app `wabot-elia-dev`, Socket Mode): the bot connected, received DMs and image attachments, and replied in thread. Vision model processes inbound PNGs and produces a description.

## Known limitations (out of scope)

- The bot cannot yet **send** files / images / documents to Slack. Outbound `reply` still ignores anything other than `text`. Planned as a follow-up change (`feat-slack-uploads`) using `filesUploadV2`.
- Required Slack scopes for production: `chat:write`, `users:read`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`, `channels:history`, `groups:history`, plus `app_mentions:read` if you want the bot to respond to @-mentions.
- `openspec/changes/feat-slack-attachments/` documents the design decisions and the spec for the new `slack-channel` capability; it is intentionally not committed to this PR.

author: midwan
body:
Two uaelib additions for the Host-Tools project (BlitterStudio/host-tools):

**Trap 95 — `HostShell_OpenPipe`**: a variant of the HostShell session that connects the child command through plain pipes instead of a pty. Output is binary-safe (no terminal line-ending processing) and EOF is only reported after the pipe drains, which makes it suitable for transferring file data from host commands. The existing read/write/close/status traps (91-94) operate on the same session handles.

- POSIX: `pipe()` pairs, stderr to `/dev/null`, `$SHELL -c <cmd>`.
- Windows: `CreateProcess` through `%COMSPEC% /C` with anonymous pipes mapped onto CRT fds, non-blocking reads via `PeekNamedPipe`, status via `GetExitCodeProcess`. This is the first HostShell trap implemented on Windows hosts; the interactive pty session (trap 90) remains POSIX-only for now.

**Trap 96 — `GetHostPlatform`**: returns 1 (POSIX/Linux), 2 (macOS), or 3 (Windows) so guest tools can pick a host command dialect; older builds return 0 for unknown traps, which guests treat as "assume POSIX".

First consumer is the new `host-download` tool, which streams downloads (host curl/wget) to any Amiga path with live progress — verified working on a Windows host with this branch.

author: n24q02m
body:
## Summary
Added input length validation to the `relay-login` implementations to prevent memory exhaustion Denial-of-Service (DoS) vulnerabilities.

## Details
When processing authentication requests, the relay login handlers compare the provided password against a stored hash using timing-safe comparison methods. If an attacker submits an excessively large password, allocating the buffer and performing the comparison could lead to significant memory and CPU exhaustion. Similarly, an excessively large `next` URL parameter could be used to bloat requests or cause issues in downstream string manipulations.

This PR adds the following safeguards:
*   **Password Length Limit:** Rejects passwords exceeding 1024 characters with an immediate `401 Invalid password` response.
*   **Next URL Length Limit:** Rejects `next` redirect parameters exceeding 2048 characters, falling back to the default `/authorize` path.

These limits are applied identically to both the TypeScript (`packages/core-ts`) and Python (`packages/core-py`) implementations.

## Security Context
*   **Vulnerability:** Memory Exhaustion DoS via oversized inputs.
*   **Impact:** An attacker could degrade or crash the service by repeatedly sending massive payloads to the unprotected login endpoints.
*   **Fix:** Added strict length boundaries well above legitimate use cases but low enough to prevent resource exhaustion.
*   **Verification:** Verified via test suites (`vitest` for TS, `pytest` for Python).

author: sm1ll3r
body:
###### Description of changes

The L4T udev rules were installed as 99-tegra-devices.rules. NixOS places rules from services.udev.extraRules into 99-local.rules, which sorts lexicographically *before* 99-tegra-devices.rules. This means the tegra rules run last and win, making it impossible to easily override them via extraRules.

Rename the file to 90-tegra-devices.rules so it is processed earlier in the udev rule ordering, allowing users to override tegra device rules through the standard services.udev.extraRules mechanism (which lands in 99-local.rules).

###### Testing

Verified rules file was renamed and device is booting without issue on:
- [x] orin-agx-devkit-jp5
- [x] orin-agx-devkit-jp6
- [x] thor-agx-devkit

author: kishiguro
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap found while validating #1305: zebra-rs enforced the RFC 1997 well-known communities only for SR Policy (SAFI 73, RFC 9830). IPv4/IPv6 unicast, VPNv4/VPNv6, labeled-unicast, and EVPN egress ignored them, so a route tagged `no-advertise` was still re-advertised (the `@bgp_community` BDD scenario that covers this had never been able to run before #1305 fixed its config path).

**Implementation** — one gate (`community_suppresses_advertisement`) hooked into the three shared outbound builders (`route_update_ipv4` / `route_update_ipv6` / `route_update_evpn`):
- `NO_ADVERTISE` suppresses advertisement to every peer.
- `NO_EXPORT` — and `NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED`, equivalent while confederations are unimplemented — suppress advertisement to eBGP peers.
- The check runs **before** the outbound policy, so a community the policy itself attaches toward a peer does not self-suppress (FRR orders these the same way). It depends only on peer type, which is part of `UpdateGroupSig`, so it is safe under the per-group advertise memo.
- On the v4 paths a suppressed route flows into `AdvertiseOutcome::Withdraw`, so previously-advertised routes that gain one of these communities are withdrawn (adj-out gated). The v6 path has no Adj-RIB-Out yet and filters steady-state only — same pre-existing limitation as the deferred v6 outbound policy.

**BDD** — `@bgp_community` now has a fourth router (D, AS65003, eBGP off B) so both behaviors are observable: no-export keeps flowing over iBGP to C while suppressed toward D; no-advertise reaches neither; a permit-all revert restores both (config apply is additive, so reverting means overwriting the `policy out` leaf — the scenario previously "reverted" by applying a config that could not remove the policy and only passed because the community was unenforced).

**Docs** — `docs/design/bgp-well-known-communities.md` records the full audit of every `CommunityValue` constant: what this PR enforces, and the per-community status of the rest.

## Well-known community audit (summary)

| Community | RFC | Status |
|---|---|---|
| NO_EXPORT / NO_ADVERTISE / NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED | 1997 | **enforced by this PR** |
| LLGR_STALE / NO_LLGR | 9494 | partial / missing — follow-up PR: capability-gated egress of stale routes, depreference of *received* LLGR_STALE, NO_LLGR no-retain |
| GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN | 8326 | constant only — future `graceful-shutdown` knob |
| ACCEPT_OWN(_NEXTHOP) | 7611 | constant only — niche RR/VPN feature |
| BLACKHOLE | 7999 | operator policy; optional knob later |
| NO_PEER | 3765 | intentionally not enforced (advisory; FRR does not enforce either) |
| ROUTE_FILTER_* | — | reserved constants, nothing to implement |

## Testing

- New unit tests: gate truth table across both peer types (1463 workspace tests pass, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt` applied.
- BDD `@bgp_community`: **6/6 scenarios pass** against the rebuilt `/usr/bin/zebra-rs` (binary hash verified before and after the run) — including the previously-impossible no-advertise scenario and the new no-export eBGP-edge assertions.
- BDD `@bgp_interas_option_b` (VPNv4 egress regression guard): passes on this branch. Note: this feature's "ASBRs hold every VPN prefix" assert sits right at its convergence margin (35s wait vs a worst-case 30s eBGP MRAI chain) and flaked under heavy parallel host load during testing — it failed identically regardless of binary timing-wise, and passed cleanly on both this branch and its parent once load settled; the gate is provably inert for community-less attrs.

body:
## Summary

**PR-B de 3** del Sprint P.2. PR-A (#43) mergeado dejó el backend completo + admin CRUD; este PR añade la vista kanban operativa y la sección Pipelines en la ficha del contacto. PR-C lanzará la pantalla de reportes encima.

### Backend (1 endpoint)

- `GET /api/contacts/{id}/pipelines` devuelve un resumen compacto por assignment activo (pipeline_name + stage_name + days_in_stage). Una sola llamada para que la ficha del contacto pinte la sección sin N round-trips. Soporta `?include_archived=true`.

### Frontend

- **`/pipelines/{id}`** pasa del stub de PR-A a un **kanban completo**. Columnas = etapas; cards = assignments con email + lead_score + tag chips + días en etapa.
  - **Drag-and-drop entre columnas** vía API HTML5 nativa (mismo patrón que ColumnConfigurator y el editor de etapas — sin dnd-kit).
  - **UI optimista**: la card se mueve inmediatamente; si el PATCH falla la snapshot se restaura y el padre muestra el banner de error.
  - Cards en stages con `target_days` superado obtienen un outline rojo para visualizar SLAs incumplidos.
- **Nueva sección "Pipelines" en `/contacts/{id}`** via `<ContactPipelinesSection>`:
  - Lista de pipelines + etapa actual + días + dropdown para saltar a otra etapa (lazy load on focus — un contacto en 5 pipelines no dispara 5 GETs al montar).
  - Botón "Sacar" archiva la assignment.
- **`<AddToPipelineModal>`** lista pipelines de la organización, deshabilita los que el contacto ya tiene, y permite elegir etapa inicial (no fuerza siempre position 0).

## Test plan

- [x] **`pytest backend/tests` — 322 verdes** (2 nuevos):
  - `test_list_contact_pipelines_returns_summaries` — flatten + days_in_stage + naming.
  - `test_list_contact_pipelines_hides_archived_by_default` — pinning del `include_archived` query param.
- [x] `ruff check .` (0.8.6 CI) — limpio.
- [x] `npm run lint` — limpio.
- [x] `npm run build` — `/pipelines/[id]` ahora 2.01 kB (kanban + DnD); `/contacts/[id]` sube con la nueva sección.
- [ ] Smoke post-merge: arrastrar una card entre columnas en `/pipelines/{id}` y verificar persistencia. Abrir un contacto y verificar que la sección Pipelines lista los activos.

10 ficheros. PR-C (reports UI) consumirá el endpoint `GET /pipelines/{id}/report` que PR-A ya entrega — sin más backend.

body:
## What

Patches the 8 High/Critical Software Composition Analysis (SCA) findings Datadog reports for this repo, tracked under [INF2-139](https://linear.app/poweredbyibex/issue/INF2-139/infra-vulnerabilities).

All affected packages are **transitive** (pulled in by the Vite/SolidStart build toolchain — none are direct deps), so they're pinned to patched versions via `pnpm.overrides` instead of changing direct dependencies.

| Package | From | To | CVE | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flatted | 3.2.7 | 3.4.2 | CVE-2026-33228 — prototype pollution via `parse()` | 🔴 Critical |
| rollup | 3.20.6 | 3.30.0 | CVE-2026-27606 — arbitrary file write / path traversal | 🔴 Critical |
| rollup | 3.20.6 | 3.30.0 | CVE-2024-47068 — DOM clobbering XSS | 🟠 High |
| minimatch | 3.1.2 | 3.1.3 | CVE-2026-26996 — ReDoS | 🟠 High |
| minimatch | 5.1.6 | 5.1.7 | CVE-2026-26996 — ReDoS | 🟠 High |
| @babel/traverse | 7.21.4 | 7.23.2 | CVE-2023-45133 — arbitrary code execution | 🟠 High |
| lodash | 4.17.21 | 4.18.1 | CVE-2026-4800 — code injection via `_.template` | 🟠 High |
| shell-quote | 1.8.1 | 1.8.4 | CVE-2026-9277 — command injection (newline in `.op`) | 🟠 High |

`rollup` 3.30.0 covers both its CVEs (≥3.29.5 fixes the XSS, ≥3.30.0 fixes the path traversal). Each `minimatch` major is bumped to its own patch release to avoid an API jump.

## Why overrides

Every flagged package is a transitive build-time dependency. Overrides target exactly the vulnerable versions with the minimal patched release in the same major line — smallest possible blast radius, no direct-dependency or framework upgrade.

## Verification

- `pnpm install` (pnpm 8 — lockfile kept at v6.0)
- `pnpm build` ✅ — solid-start client + server build pass with the bumped deps
- Lockfile confirmed to no longer contain any of the vulnerable versions

author: jredeker
body:
## Problem

When a PR is squash-merged, the release gate's `RELEASE_REQUIRES_TRUNK_MERGE` check fails because `resolveReleaseReachability` only checks git ancestry (`git log origin/trunk..change/{id}`). Squash merges create a new commit SHA on trunk, so the original change branch commits are not ancestors of trunk.

## Solution

Added a PR merge state fallback in `resolveReleaseReachability`'s direct route branch. When ancestry check fails and both `prNumber` and `route.repo` are available, queries `gh pr view` via the existing `readPrMergeState` helper. If the PR shows `state: "MERGED"` with a `mergedAt` timestamp, returns `{ reachable: true, proof: "pr_merged" }`.

## Changes

- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts`: 20-line squash-merge fallback in direct route branch
- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.test.ts`: 4 unit tests for squash-merge scenarios

author: akbisw
body:
## Summary
The library's own docs told integrators to detect user-cancelled / no-local-credential passkey failures via `error.name === 'NotAllowedError'`, but that condition can never match an error thrown by this library. This PR adds discriminating error codes, a helper predicate, and maps Chrome's `OperationError` (pending request), then fixes the docs to a pattern that actually works.

## Finding
- Severity: MEDIUM, confidence: certain
- `client/errors.ts:196-203` (pre-fix): `fromDOMException` converts a DOMException `NotAllowedError` into a `Fido2CredentialError` whose `.name` is `"Fido2CredentialError"` — the original DOMException survives only in `.cause`.
- Yet the JSDoc at `client/fido2.ts:146` (`detectMediationCapabilities`) and `client/fido2.ts:1121` (`authenticateWithFido2`'s `mediation` param), plus `client/react/README.md:147`, instructed integrators to write `if (error.name === 'NotAllowedError') { showPasswordForm(); }`.
- Concrete failure scenario: an app uses `mediation: 'immediate'` for a frictionless sign-in button and follows the documented pattern to fall back to a password form when no local credentials exist. The browser rejects with `NotAllowedError`, the library rewraps it, the documented check never fires, and the user is silently stuck with no fallback UI.
- Compounding: `Fido2CredentialError` used the single code `CREDENTIAL_ERROR` for both `NotAllowedError` and `InvalidStateError`, so there was no programmatic discriminator short of inspecting `.cause`.
- Addendum: for a concurrent pending request, Chrome throws `OperationError` ("A request is already pending"), which fell through to the generic `WEBAUTHN_ERROR` catch-all.

## Fix
- `Fido2CredentialError` gains an optional trailing `code` parameter (default `CREDENTIAL_ERROR`, class and name unchanged, so `instanceof` checks and direct construction keep working).
- `fromDOMException` now maps `NotAllowedError` → `CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED`, `InvalidStateError` → `CREDENTIAL_INVALID_STATE`, and adds an `OperationError` case → `CREDENTIAL_REQUEST_PENDING`, following the existing code-naming scheme.
- New exported type guard `isFido2NotAllowedError()` (same pattern as `isFido2AbortError`) for the password-form fallback; exported via the existing `export * from "./errors.js"` in `client/index.ts`.
- Rewrote the JSDoc examples in `client/fido2.ts` and the docs in `ERROR_HANDLING.md` and `client/react/README.md` to use the helper (and `.signedIn`, matching the real return shape of `authenticateWithFido2`).

## Test plan
- `npx tsc --project client/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint client/errors.ts client/fido2.ts client/__tests__/errors.test.ts client/__tests__/fido2-errors.test.ts` — clean
- `npx jest client/__tests__/` — 10 suites, 133 tests, all passing
- New/updated tests: `fromDOMException` code assertions for `NotAllowedError`, `InvalidStateError`, and `OperationError`; `isFido2NotAllowedError` predicate (positive/negative cases incl. raw DOMException); `Fido2CredentialError` default-code backward compatibility; end-to-end `fido2getCredential` rejection tests proving the legacy `error.name` pattern doesn't match while the helper does, and the `OperationError` pending-request mapping.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Client-side error mapping and API surface only; default `CREDENTIAL_ERROR` is preserved for direct construction, with expanded tests and no auth protocol changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **documentation vs. behavior mismatch**: integrators were told to use `error.name === 'NotAllowedError'`, but thrown errors are `Fido2CredentialError` with the DOMException only on `error.cause`.
> 
> **`Fido2CredentialError`** now accepts an optional **`code`** (default `CREDENTIAL_ERROR`). **`fromDOMException`** maps WebAuthn DOMExceptions to **`CREDENTIAL_NOT_ALLOWED`**, **`CREDENTIAL_INVALID_STATE`**, and **`CREDENTIAL_REQUEST_PENDING`** (Chrome `OperationError` when the message matches `/pending/i`; other `OperationError`s stay **`WEBAUTHN_ERROR`**).

author: jasonp2323
body:
## Problem

Release-please **is** firing on every push to `master` (5/5 workflow runs succeeded since `1.15.0`, and the `1.16.0` release PR is live). The real issue is **what lands in the release notes**: release-please's default `node` config only renders `feat` / `fix` / breaking-change commits in the changelog — every other conventional type (`test`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `ci`, `build`) is `hidden: true` by default.

That silently dropped merges from the release. Concretely, of the 5 merges to `master` since `1.15.0`:

| PR | Type | In `1.16.0` notes? |
|----|------|--------------------|
| #197 feat(infra) | `feat` | ✅ |
| #199 feat(core) | `feat` | ✅ |
| #200 feat(core) | `feat` | ✅ |
| #202 feat(application) | `feat` | ✅ |
| **#196 test(core)** | **`test`** | ❌ **dropped** |

Worse, a master batch consisting only of maintenance-type commits (`test`/`docs`/`chore`/…) would produce **no release entry at all** — the "release wasn't triggered" symptom.

## Fix

Add an explicit `changelog-sections` array to `release-please-config.json` that un-hides every standard conventional type, with section titles aligned to the buckets already declared in `.github/release.yml` (Features / Fixes / Documentation / Maintenance, plus perf / revert / refactor / test / ci / build).

**Version-bump semantics are unchanged** — only `feat` / `fix` / breaking still bump the version per semver. Maintenance-type commits now *appear* in the changelog and get swept into the next `feat`/`fix` release rather than cutting one on their own.

## Test plan

1. Merge this PR into `master`.
2. The Release workflow runs and release-please regenerates the release PR (`release-please--branches--master--…`).
3. Confirm the regenerated release PR's changelog now includes a **✅ Tests** section containing `test(core): concurrent double-redemption guard for invite claims (#196)` — i.e. the previously-dropped commit reappears.
4. Going forward, `docs` / `chore` / `refactor` / `ci` / `build` merges also show up under their sections.

## Follow-up

A separate issue will track the optional, non-standard enhancement of *triggering* a release for maintenance-only batches (forcing a patch bump when no `feat`/`fix` is present), which this PR intentionally does not change.

author: jordepic
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

- Closes #22861.

## Rationale for this change

When using DataFusion comet I noticed that my hash join operator was failing with the following error: `Failed to acquire 142606336 bytes where 17142251456 bytes already reserved and the fair limit is 17179869184 bytes, 4 registered`. Looking into this more, DataFusion asks to reserve memory for each batch (by default 8192 rows) of the build side of a hash join - and tries to reserve (without actually allocating it) num_batches * batch_size.  This is problematic when these are batches are zero-copy slices of a larger batch (e.g. GroupedHashAggregateStream), since the slice size is evaluated to be the size of the larger buffer. This is because the reference to the slice actually keeps the entire buffer from being freed. DataFusion doesn't overallocate memory (the underlying data is the same), but it does over-request it (in the centralized accounting system), which can lead to these "ResourcesExhausted" exceptions.

## What changes are included in this PR?

In this change, we keep track of all of the buffers that we've already counted via a set of pointers.  This way, we don't redundantly request memory for the whole arrow buffer for each sub-slice of it.  We choose this approach as opposed to just requesting a smaller amount of memory per batch, because as mentioned before, the pointer to each batch technically keeps the entire arrow-buffer from being freed.

## Are these changes tested?

The new hash join test fails on main with ResourcesExhausted and passes with this change.

## Are there any user-facing changes?

No breaking changes. Adds a new public helper count_record_batch_memory_size to datafusion-common.

## Summary
- New `conditional-fields` Stimulus controller (forms): shows/hides dependent blocks based on the value of other form fields, with zero round-trips
- Auto-detects triggers from `data-when-{name}` attributes on each dependent; lookup is kebab/snake forgiving (`data-when-ship-different` finds `[name="ship_different"]`)
- Rule grammar: space-separated values = OR within a field; multiple `data-when-*` = AND across fields; `:checked` / `:unchecked` tokens for boolean checkboxes; `name[]` checkbox groups supported
- Hides via `hidden` + `disabled` together (both required — `hidden` alone does not exclude from submit); `<fieldset>` cascade for blocks, per-field disabled tracking for `<div>`
- New `<x-hwc::conditional-field>` Blade component is the recommended path: single source of truth for the rule (`when` prop), renders `hidden disabled` initially when the current state doesn't match, eliminates the client/server drift that would otherwise flash the wrong fields on first paint
- `:model` prop handles edit forms: the component evaluates `old($field, data_get($model, $field))`, mirroring the same expression already used in `<x-hwc::input value="...">`. No parallel state map; validation retries always win over the model fallback
- Controller works on any container with named inputs — not just `<form>`. Doc shows filter bars, dashboards, in-page configuration panels as valid hosts
- Recipe at `docs/recipes/conditional-fields.md` covers five real-world patterns plus an edit-form `:model` example
- Intentional exception to the "no components in Wave 2" rule — documented in the plan; the rule duplication this component eliminates is structural, not cosmetic
