author: krixon-bot
body:
No-issue: maintainer-directed one-line doc fix surfaced while landing — merge strategy must come from the repo, not be hard-coded.

A `gh pr merge --squash` against this repo fails: the `main` ruleset allows rebase only, while the repo-level `allow_squash_merge` flag still reads true, and the docs hard-coded `--squash` as the merge command. The merge step in `skills/GITHUB.md` now starts by discovering the allowed merge methods — the base branch's `pull_request` rule's `allowed_merge_methods` when present, the repo flags otherwise — and picks from that set: squash preferred, rebase after reducing to logical commits, never a merge commit (skip with reason if neither is allowed). `skills/land/SKILL.md` step 3 names the concept and links to it.

body:
## Summary
- Shared profile-picture uploader (square-crop + downscale + JPEG compress) used on two surfaces: admins set any member's photo in the member drawer; members set their own on `/me`. Built once in `@luminova/ui`, two entry points.
- New `@luminova/ui` `Avatar` (photo + initials fallback) and `ImageUploader` (cropper lazy-loaded — `react-easy-crop@5.5.7`, vetted; stays out of the initial chunk, ~6.6kB gzip deferred to file-pick).
- `@luminova/firebase` exposes a storage accessor + `uploadMemberPhoto`/`deleteMemberPhoto`. Path `members/{memberId}/profile.jpg` (fixed name → overwrites, no orphans). Photo write is its own action, decoupled from the member-form Zod submit.
- **Security (rules):**
  - `storage.rules` scoped: Admin/Membership write any member; owning member (`firestore.get(member).uid == auth.uid`) writes own; any authed user reads; `image/jpeg` + ≤5MB enforced; literal `profile.jpg` only.
  - `firestore.rules` gains an owner-only `members` update branch scoped to `profilePicture` via `diff().affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` — **required for `/me` self-upload to work** (storage allowed the upload but the field write was previously denied).

Specs/plans: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-h1-profile-picture-upload-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-09-h1-profile-picture-upload.md`

author: oobabooga
body:
The unsloth Gemma 4 GGUF repos (e.g. `unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF`) ship the MTP speculative-decoding head as a separate file: a root `mtp-*.gguf`, plus higher-precision copies under `MTP/`. This is unlike Qwen, where the head is baked into the main GGUF. 

Studio didn't know about these files; the fix is to treat the drafter like mmproj: a companion file that is downloaded with the model and excluded from variant selection everywhere.

## What changed

- HF loads auto-download the root `mtp-*.gguf` and pass it to llama-server via `--model-draft`. Local loads detect the sibling next to the weights. A separate drafter counts as an MTP model for auto promotion and VRAM fitting, same as a baked-in head.
- The download manager fetches the drafter with every quant (like mmproj), so the download-then-load path gets MTP too. Reported download sizes include it.
- Drafter paths are excluded from variant lists, best-quant picks, quant-matched file lookups, and inventory scans, in both the hub utils and the `model_config` copies of that logic.
- `extract_model_size_b` now understands Gemma effective sizes (`E2B`, `E4B`), so the sub-3B no-MTP policy applies to E2B, and auto mode skips the drafter download there.
- **Graceful fallback on old binaries:** if llama-server dies while loading the drafter (prebuilts that predate the `gemma4-assistant` arch), the load retries once with `--spec-default` so the main model still comes up, and logs a warning to run `unsloth studio update`.
- Fixed the already-loaded check coercing vision models' spec mode to "off". Switching speculative decoding on a vision model never triggered a reload.

## Results

Measured on `gemma-4-12b-it` (`UD-Q4_K_XL`): 43.6 -> 63.4 tok/s on a fresh reply, 43.3 -> 66.2 tok/s on repeated text (draft acceptance 73% / 97%).

author: alliedtoasters
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6.

`_extract_all_model_events` (`src/control_tower/trajectories/timing_utils.py`) skipped any model event whose `working_time` was `None`. Ollama-provider events — our production rollout path (`unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q5_K_M`) — carry `working_start` but `working_time=None`, so the guard silently dropped **all** model events: every `action.timing.model_calls` list came out empty and the captured `raw_input`/`raw_output` never reached the `Trajectory`, even though the data is present in the `.eval` file.

This is issue option 1 (best-effort timing rather than dropping the event):

- Skip only when `working_start` is missing (there is then no anchor on the working-time axis).
- When `working_time` is `None`, keep the event with a zero-duration fallback (`end_time = start_time`) and a new `ModelEventInfo.duration_known=False` flag.
- `_build_model_call_timing` reports `inspect_cache_hit=None` (unknown) for fallback-timed calls instead of misreading the 0ms duration as a sub-500ms inspect disk-cache hit.

The `working_time`-present path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Verification

Against the exact log from the issue (`logs/2026-06-09T03-52-33-00-00_onboard-ollama-honest-parse-links-304d70ca_*.eval`, 18 model events, all `working_time=None`):

- **Before:** 0 model calls attached, no raw I/O.
- **After:** all 12 trajectory actions carry their model calls (12/12 with `raw_input`+`raw_output`), the 5 orphan reasoning events associate via the existing orphan logic, and `inspect_cache_hit` is `None` throughout. The remaining 6 of 18 events attach to a `ready_to_plan` harness tool call that the converter intentionally excludes from trajectory actions (pre-existing behavior).
- An Anthropic run (`onboard-opus-honest-parse-links-pure-5944d2a3`) — whose events it turns out also have `working_time=None`, so this was never Ollama-only — now recovers 28/28 model calls with raw I/O as well.
- `make pr-checks` green (2535 passed, 29 skipped, 1 xfailed).

No new test per repo testing guidelines (no mocks, no unit tests pinning internals); verified end-to-end against the real eval logs above.
